text: So I took my husband here for breakfast on a Saturday morning. I had loved lunch and read the great reviews on breakfast, and they didn't disappoint. We arrived between 9:30 and 10:00 and there was no wait, plenty of open tables. Since I knew we were in for a leisurely meal, we took in the paper, read and chatted while waiting. I had the pomegranate mimosa before the meal, and it was served in a regular-sized beverage class - no teeny-tiny champagne flute here! For the meal, husband had the scrambled eggs with parmesan cheese, french bread toast, and fresh fruit. I had the french bread eggs in the hole with sauteed tomatoes and olives, sweet potato donuts, fresh fruit and bacon. I didn't even know where to start eating! Every single thing on both of our plates was delicious, and as usual, the freshness of the produce just added to the great tastes. I had never had tomatoes sauteed and was a little unsure of how it would taste; well, they were sweet and wonderful! I doubt I would take my kids as this is no basic bacon and eggs, but if anyone wants that, they can go to IHOP. This place is definitely becoming my selfish pleasure, and as I saw several other breakfast items to try, I know I'll be back!

text: We "tried" to have a Birthday Party get together at Patterson House. They cannot handle more than 10 guests at a seating area. We had twenty coming. Silly me... I thought I would bring them business in this rough economy. They did everything they could to discourage us from coming in. We decided to have one round before the embarrassment of too many guests with no seating started. Talk about stuffy. They claim their motif is "Prohibition Era Speakeasy". More like an L.A. "Look at me, I'm important" trendy haircut of the week type joint. Drinks - inventive. Tasty - NO! All 10 guests at our table were making choking faces after they tried their drinks. OK... one guy liked it. He's from... LA! Rude, pushy, and not very accommodating staff. I have no prior experience with this place. Have only heard good things. All I can tell you about is my own personal experience. No axe to grind here... I just don't want anyone else to feel as unwelcome as I did. My guests all felt the same way. So, if you're the type of person who needs to be "seen", this place is PERFECT for you. If you just wanna hang with real people and great friends, try Rebar. We went down there and were treated like they actually appreciated our business. Imagine that? Great staff! Patterson House - I believe you should read this at your next meeting. BTW... the folks in attendance: Head of a large Insurance Firm, Realtors, Rock Stars, Blue collar workers, Studio musicians, and a teacher. Congratulations, you managed to alienate across the board! Doubt they'll be back soon, or anyone they talk too this week. Signed, Disappointed and humiliated.

text: If only I could rate this place negative stars. Absolutely terrible in every way imaginable. First, the apartments are made out of incredibly cheap materials, and it shows. The walls are so thin you can always hear your neighbors, whether they are next door, underneath you, or even outside. If someone next door slams their door, expect all of your windows to rattle. The appliances are old and cheap, and in a two bedroom apartment they provided us with one cable outlet, and refused to install another (when we offered to pay!). But, the biggest complaints are reserved for management. They are completely incompetent. Some examples: -On the first day we moved in, they provided us with no stove, a broken fridge, and two walls were painted bright blue and purple. We had to call, repeatedly, to get them to give us a stove and working fridge. - When we first moved in, there was a mistake and they were trying to charge us for something. When we tried to find out what it was, they would not explain what the charge was for. The manager told us we weren't making a very good "impression". -When we moved in, free water was included in our lease. During our lease, they decided to start charging residents. Even though we still had 3 months on our lease (and legally entitled to free water), they would send us water bills every month. We had to take our copy of the lease to the front office to get them to stop, and after that they sent another. Each time we went, the person we spoke to seemed to have NO IDEA what we were talking about. -We had a neighbor who had a friend living there who was not on the lease. This person was a nightmare- loud music, involved in drugs, and physically threatening. After 9 months of weekly complaints, they finally did something, but not before they (the assistant manager) told us WE needed to be "better" neighbors. This person had the police called on him multiple times (by other residents), and wasn't even on the lease. This was beyond insulting. -We were once served with a 5 day eviction notice...2 days before the rent was due. They thought it was a funny mix-up. I could go on and on. I implore you, don't move here. The residents they accept are a nightmare, the apartments are crappy, and the management is stupid. Feel free to email me with any questions about my experience.

text: I went to Christie's last Saturday afternoon, because my feet were screaming for a pedicure. It was my first time there, and I had a great experience. I didn't have an appointment set up when I arrived, so I added my name to the wait list, picked out a color, and took a seat. The salon is small, but they have 5 pedicure chairs, and 4 manicure stations. There was a woman on line ahead of me when I arrived, but I still waited for less than 10 minutes for a chair to open up. The salon is very sanitary, and they clean everything between customers. They all also wear rubber gloves, and sanitize their tools. I pay attention to all of this stuff, because you can never be too careful with your toes, of course! The girls (and one guy!) all worked very efficiently, and I was able to sit back and relax in my high-powered, Shiatsu massage, leather, reclining chair. The girl that did my pedicure was great. She asked me before cutting my nails, and checked the length with me before proceeding. This really made my day, because I'm a total weirdo and I cannot stand when my toenails are too short. What can I say? It just grosses me out. I didn't venture upstairs, but I know that's where they do waxings, and tanning too, I assume. Christie herself was also there, and you can tell she knows what goes on in her shop. I was sitting next to her and she knew that I had never been there before, and was nice enough to ask me how my experience was going. I'll definitely be going back.

text: Stopped into Three Dog after having been to a few other dog bakeries around town. I think Three Dog is the original, and I'm going to vote for it as the best. Mostly, that is because the girl working when I went in on Sunday was AWESOME. As I've found out, people at holistic pet supply stores have a tendency to sometimes be a little judgmental if you don't have your pet on an all-natural diet. The girl working was super laid back, answered my questions, was friendly and didn't have any problem putting down the doggie treat batter she was mixing up to help me out. Besides that, they have a great location and it smells amazing in here! My dogs and cat have been getting a little spoiled lately with all of the treats I've been buying them and I don't want to have to put them on diets anytime soon, so I resisted the urge to buy some yummy snacks for them. Instead, I picked up something that could just be a lifesaver in our house-- HappyTails Dog Smog Remedy. It claims to rid your doggie of bad breath and "gaseous emissions." I don't think I've used it enough times to know if it works or not yet, but let's hope it does! Of course, you can take your dogs in here with you and they'll give him or her a free treat. And if you are lucky, you will go in on the right day and get to meet Olive, a beautiful & friendly pit bull, who accompanies her owner to work.

text: Before Coldstone or Maggie Moo's, there was Scoop De Ville. It absolutely stands out in the category of "Fold in" ice cream. Like an ice cream parlor from a different era, this place serves the softest of ice cream with baked goods, herbs, fruits, chocolates, and all kinds of toppings blended in. No one comes close to providing the topping options that they do. You can create any ice cream combination that you ever dreamed of! Using an automated grinder, the various toppings are brought together perfect, and not uneven --- as is the case in the coldstones where the server's disinterest or lack of attention to detail can detract from the quality of the ice cream that is supposed to be custom blended. Scoop De Ville has such a warm, fun feel to it that you just enjoy being in the place. None of the contrived "sing every few minutes with no enthusiasm or soul" that you see in some of the Coldstone outlets (Times Square, anyone?). From the fuzzy, hand drawn menus to the cheerful and helpful staff...this is exactly what creates a wonderful dessert experience. Even though Scoop De Ville has been around 20 years, the family that runs it has been in business in Philadelphia since 1850 producing candies and chocolates. They just moved from their 90 year old location to a nearby, roomier location --- but the quality, the ambience is all there. Be prepared to be absolutely delighted!

text: Came in on a recommendation from some vegan family members, and I was not disappointed! My gf is a meat-eater, so we both had a chance to try what we wanted, and both of us did great. We shared the hummus sampler, which came with 4 different types of hummus, and they were all fantastic. I especially like the jalapeño variety, as it was light, fresh, and almost dancing on my tongue, and we both agreed that the fresh basil hummus was the best we'd ever had. I expressed my interest in spicy foods, and our waitress (very sweet, friendly, and all around cool) totally hooked me up with some spicy chili sauce that was friggen awesome. For our main course, I had the falafel plate, and the gf had the gyro plate. She had never had spit-fired steak before, and she was very impressed. She said the meat was flavored great, and very juicy. She slammed it all down without even taking time to burp :P My falafel were really good. Really. I try making falafel and it never, ever turns out this good. They were served with house hummus, a tahini sauce of sorts, and praise god, my awesome server brought out a couple of roasted (HOT) jalapeños. We were so stuffed that there was no room for any of the awesome looking deserts, but alas, that means next time we'll make sure to leave some room, and take the rest to go. That may be a challenge, though, cause they keep bringing oven-toasted bread to the table, which sits for about 30 seconds before being devoured. For our two meals and appetizer, we only spent $25, and the $5 tip was well earned... The hummus sampler was only $4!! On a side note, the head chef, Maurice, made a few rounds, checking on customers, making sure everything was up to snuff, and generally adding an atmosphere of friendly caring to the place. It was really nice. Umm... what else? The music was good, the service was fast, caring, intuitive, the decor was groovy... All in all, a great place to eat!

text: Located in the heart of Santa Barbara, this store has a lot of potential for doing well. It's surrounded by a great array of shopping choices, sure to attract potential customers. When you walk inside, it's clean (though smells a bit *too* much like nail polish, comparatively speaking) and on first glance everything looks pretty nice. However, my girl friends got both manicures and pedicures, and the job seemed really rushed. While waiting, I stopped into the bathroom to find it very dirty (making me wonder how sanitary the rest of the place really was), with a mop and bucket hanging against the doorway, and foil wrapped loosely around the pipes (does that fix leaks now?). The nail jobs themselves weren't all that great - the filing was lopsided on more than a couple of the nails, and the polish wasn't even across the surface. They even missed some spots close to the skin, leaving the nail bare. Within 24 hours, some of the polish had started to come off, and within a week most of it was gone, to the point that my friends just had to use remover and go with bare nails instead. I hope this place can turn itself around, but it just doesn't seem like they're really putting in the effort where it counts. Spend some more quality time with your customers, make sure you're doing a good job, and put some extra money into your supplies. You'll be much better off if you get returning customers.

text: Coming from Seattle, it's not a great surprise that I would pick a hotel that was affiliated with coffee. And yes, the packets of coffee for the room coffeemakers were Maxwell House. But as a legacy of the coffee scions, this hotel suffers a bit. There are some nice points, however. The hotel comes with a bar and restaurant that aren't too bad (karaoke night was a bit tragic though). There are free shuttles to the airport and downtown and the beds are comfortable. A small pool is present in the back with a number of nice shady trees around. So me giving it two stars makes it sound like a dive, right? Now I've stayed in hotels where the room was just a mattress on the floor with a few roaches crawling around. I've stayed in a hotel where I was propositioned by the front desk staff ("Do ya wanna go?"). Those places were dives. The Maxwell House is not a dive, it's actually a reasonably nice hotel. But I give it two stars from a value perspective. I was here for a half marathon and they were charging $250/night. It doesn't come close to that sort of value. The rooms are okay, but not specifically deluxe. You can find a similar room in any given Sleep Inn. They have Wifi, but you have to pay for it. The location is in the suburbs next to a gas station and the interstate. There were very few open outlets in the room. I had to charge my iPod with an outlet in the bathroom (leaving it in the sink). And about the bathrooms. These were curiously designed. The shower stall is open to the rest of the bathroom with a large drain in the center of the floor. So when you take a shower, the entire bathroom is filled with 1-2" of standing water. Now I've seen a similar set up in a hotel in Austria. I asked the innkeeper about it and his answer was: "It's usually the Americans who ask for rooms with showers. They tend to drink to much and puke in the bathrooms. With the center drain, it lets us clean them easier." It's possible they're using the same concept here, but it doesn't say much about what they think of visitors to Nashville. As a bonus, there was no place to set the shampoo or soap. I laid these on the floor of the shower. On the bright side, they did provide these with the room. Overall, it's not a terrible place and the staff was fairly helpful and friendly throughout my stay. The shuttle drivers were very good about trying to fit people in despite a crush of runners. But I wouldn't suggest staying here unless you're getting a bargain deal.
label: NEG

text: Do you remember that quick scene in "Broadway Danny Rose" where Woody Allen and a bottle-blonde Mia Farrow are being chased by a mobster in a warehouse filled with the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade floats? The bullets hit the helium tanks, and their nasty barbs to each other sound like Mickey and Minnie having a domestic squabble. That's what Blaine Kern's massive warehouse feels like. You could easily hide among the dozens upon dozens of floats and celebrity figures parked here, all in varying states of readiness for the next Mardi Gras parade in February. At first, the $18.50 admission feels rather stiff, but you really need to get to this place if you want some sense of what it takes to mount the Mardi Gras festivities. It's a long warehouse at the southern end of the convention center. Jamie W. and I drove here, but they provide free hotel shuttles if you make plans in advance. It's quite a sight once you enter with all the big-headed cartoon characters staring out in sometimes disturbing ways. You wait in the huge gift shop for the next tour at which point you're taken to a screening room where you see a vintage featurette on the parade. Linda was our guide, and she took us through the workshop where several craftsmen (and craftswomen) work on the characters and the floats year-round. Papier-mache and fiberglass heads and figures are recycled into new characters with each parade, which may explain why Dorothy looks like she's from Tokyo on her way to Oz. Heads are placed randomly on the floor. The Three Stooges over here, the Marx Brothers over there. A black-and-white two-face of Michael Jackson. Full-fledged figure stand waiting for their turn in the spotlight. King King and his bride. Elvis. Captain America. Yoda. The Potato Heads. The V-Day lovers kissing in Time Square. It's easy to get lost in this alternate reality where everyone's heads are proportionally bigger than their bodies. Linda took us back to the screening room where we were given slices of Louisiana-Style King Cake, probably the most inedible cinnamon roll I've ever tasted. Then we were given free rein to try on various celebrity heads of which only one looked familiar. How do I look as Marilyn, Mr. President (see photo)? All in all, this is an amusing diversion on any trip to New Orleans, and frankly the bacchanalia and debauchery of the real event doesn't hold that much appeal to me. Personally this is enough.

text: Boy my Dad would have loved this place, and there's very little not to love about the Pub. Located at the end of Admiral Wilson Blvd at the junction of Camden and Pennsauken, most people zoom by at about 60 miles an hour as they flee the Camden wastelands on the way to AC. Such a shame. The place is huge, from the parking lot to the bar to the main dining room. As you are brought down on the main floor looking at the seven huge wood fired hearths, it seems like they could seat 1000 people. (they probably have!) Yes, the place is old school, it's been in business for 57 years and maintains that old school combo diner steakhouse feel, and there's no good reason that should dissuade you, think of it as 'kitsch'. As for being dark, I've been in many lounge style restaurants where I've needed my cell to read the menu, Vetri included, so don't think they escort you with flashlights. I'll also point out that as we usually go early for dinner, there are plenty of older folks there and they seem to get along just fine. So let's get down to why you're coming. Huge steaks, charcoal grilled and darn tasty for a reasonable price. The 'Relish Bar' (salad bar) is also a nice touch, and is always being restocked with fresh ingredients. Don't miss the cheese or date nut bread at the end, they're my favorites. I've included some pictures of our food, I had the bone in ribeye and a cup of snapper soup, my son has the 12oz strip, and our guest has the boneless ribeye. We all enjoyed our meal, and it was perfectly cooked. The snapper soup was strangely thick, almost seeming to have a bean base, and the meat, although plentiful, didn't actually taste like turtle. The accompanying sherry also was pretty weak, but that was the exception. Normally it's all top notch, and I suspect someone new was making the soup and a busboy was nipping at the sherry and refilling it with water. Did I mention the 1/2 basketball size loaf of bread that hits your table as you're being seated? How about the airplane style service carts that your food is delivered in, each equipped with a gallon of fresh made au-jus for those that like some extra sauce. Seriously. Want some extra on your steak, of course. Your potato too? Certainly. Directly into your mouth. Open wider hon. A glass to drink after I leave? Here you are. Yum. Huge potatos, some baked, some stuffed, and some double stuffed, accompany your platter. Double stuffed resembles a potato skin on steroids and is pretty much a meal in itself. I wish they had a sweet potato option. We've never made it to dessert, but I can say they make a darn good cup of coffee. The desserts sit spinning in a cold case as you walk in, and are tempting, but there's just no room left! Our server, The meticulous Maureen, kept our sodas full and stopped by at least five times to make sure all was going well. We'll request her again for sure. Three huge steak dinners for three, with take home extras, all for less than breakfast at Max Brenner's. How can you beat it!!

text: This place was recommended to me by a Japanese (born & raised in Japan) friend living in the area. I finally tried it out last week & had to go back within a few days, I loved it so much! I'll update my review as I try more menu items. The decor is simple & attractive; I don't recall music playing, but it doesn't feel empty in its quietness. It's rather tranquil. There are a number of booths & a few tables with chairs; the bathroom was pretty barren (not fancy) but clean -- no complaints. - Soy sauce flavor ramen: Delicious! Not quite up to par with the ramen stands I frequented in Japan, but that's to be expected from a restaurant like this. The noodles are perfectly al dente, the soup has just the right flavor & consistency, & the chashu (pork) topping just melts in your mouth. & for the price ($7? 8?), unbeatable. It's a HUGE serving. - Kaki fry (fried oysters): Amaaaaazing. This is one of my favorite izakaya dishes, & they make it PERFECTLY. It's not a permanent menu item (right now). At $4.50 for 4 oysters, it's maybe a LITTLE bit on the pricy side of average, but trust me, they're well worth it. - Katsu-curry (curry with breaded fried pork cutlet): Also delicious! For $8.50 you get a large plate 2/3-filled with rice & 1/2-filled with curry sauce, half-ladled over the sliced cutlet. It's a rather thin piece of tonkatsu, but that's how it's supposed to be for katsu-curry. I can make tastier curry myself at home... but the katsu is harder (& more trouble), & for $8.50 I'm definitely content to let someone else do the cooking on this one for me, especially since they make it so well. If you've never had Japanese curry before, I HIGHLY recommend trying the katsu-curry. It's GREAT! - Vegetable tempura: My fiance had this on our 2nd trip, & I have to say I was a little bit less than impressed. It was just barely on the soggy side; not as light as good tempura is supposed to be. But I give them major points for putting daikon-oroshi (grated daikon radish) into the dipping sauce automatically; it's not tempura without daikon! & the serving size is quite respectable. However, unless tempura is a staple for you & you just can't live without it, I wouldn't order it here. Edited 11/13/08: We went again last week with the Japanese friend who recommended I Ai to us, & her fiance, & had a LOT of food. I won't update about all of it, but I will say this: - Tuna Yamakake (Tuna sashimi with grated yama-imo) is REALLY REALLY GOOD. If you're into trying new things, definitely give it a try.

text: It's been years since I first stepped into Rusty's and, over those years, I've been several times and, each time, saying that it would be my last. I've been anticipating this place closing down for years, because this area could use a decent bar/restaurant, but have been long disappointed. Rusty's is really two places: the bar and the restaurant. The bar gets crowded and rowdy, especially in the early evenings and on weekend nights. The parking lot is tiny and, particularly during those times, don't even bother with the main lot and just park down the street a little bit and walk. That is, if you really want to come. My first experience was with that bar, which is a two-story loft style structure, features a pretty mediocre draft beer list, no happy hour (at least, not that I know of) and, probably because of the high ceiling is LOUD when there are a lot of people in there. The bar, honestly, is not that bad, but this would probably be my 20th or 25th choice of a place in town to spend an evening drinking with friends. The restaurant is really what sucks here. My first time inside, I was shocked with how many TVs there are in here. I mean, holy crap, how many do you need? Not only are they pretty much in every, available space, each table has its OWN INDIVIDUAL TV. I guess if you like that, then this is your place, but I think they would do better with keeping a couple of table TV-free (if possible). The food definitely sucks. Lots of frozen and Sysco stuff with a really generic, uninteresting menu. It's not expensive, but definitely not particularly cheap either. I've always had terrible service here, but maybe that's just luck of the draw. I came here years ago as my good-bye lunch from my employer at the time (not my choice) and can recall being annoyed that it took almost an hour for our food to come out, even though there was really nothing complex about it. And, yeah, it was terrible when it came out. The next time I went there was a couple of years later (like I said, I really dislike this place) as part of a group of 6 or 7 (again, not my choice). The waitress was unattentive until she randomly came up to us, crying, saying that she had to leave because so-and-so had been in a car wreck or something. Weird, but okay... But the replacement waiter never showed up. The food took well over an hour and we could never get more drinks. This may have been because of the mandatory gratuity. I didn't stick around to hear the ensuing argument though. I came back a year or so later, with a group again, and had a similarly bad service experience when cordoned off in the back room. We were put there and then forgotten about. The food, again, took a ridiculous amount of time, and I was just reminded of why I hated the place. The most recent time I came here, there was a UFC fight going on. The first thing that came back to me when I walked in, that I had forgotten about, was the douchebag bouncer. Sure, it's often just comes with the territory, but they're just such jerks here. Why is it necessary? I don't know. It's not like they get a bunch of frat boys in here. So, anyway, the bar had a $5 cover for the UFC, but the dining room was free. In a group again, we were again sent to the back room where no less than three TVs were BLARING the UFC fight. We were jammed in there with two other parties, so there was no just turning the TVs off. If you really like the whole sweaty men dry humping each other, that's cool, but it's just not for me, nor was it of interest to anyone in the group. Again, the food was slow (although not as slow), but the service was a bit better, and they actually had an interesting beer on tap. The waiter also gave us some free nachos, which were pretty bad, and were the only food that I ate for the night. I got out after one beer and now am, again, vowing never to return. I'd like to point out that there is a Famous Sam's location maybe a block away, on Silverbell. I'm not exactly big into Famous Sam's but, as far as food, atmosphere, bar selection and service go, they've got way more over this place, which is the main reason why I've always been confounded as to why Rusty's remains open. I'm okay with sports bars, but this place just sucks.

text: A group of 15 of us went there last night for a friends birthday party. Upon being sat, two waitresses immediately took our drink orders and were very helpful to those who were pondering their large and delightful drink menu. "Madras Mojito - delicious, but not what you might think of as a mojito." "Capa "Caipirinha? Its a drink made from a sugar cane liquor called Cachaca..." Always nice to have wait staff that actually know their drinks. We started with some satay appetizers, which were good, and which came with dipping sauces that were delicious. My wife ordered the White Pizza (a strange item on a place that seems to have a much more tropical flair), which I thought was fair but she seemed to like OK. I opted for a trio of sides: courve - a kale dish with lemon juice and tomatoes that was amazing, corn salad - a dish that was more reminiscent of a succotash than anything and while good, didnt hold a candle to the kale, and a broccoli item that was delicious and nicely spicy. Again complimenting the wait staff, they were amazing. They kept us in drinks without hovering, they brought the cake when we were ready and got us in and out without a hitch - quite a feat with 15 people who were cruising downtown in a limo. All in, a solid place that I will be happy to go back to soon.

text: So when my husband's brother told me we were going to a place that was a frozen yogurt/coffee house/wine bar with great food, I was like, "Say WHAT?!?" Seriously, no one could possibly do all of that in one space and do it well... Of course, now I'm going to have to eat my words... just a little. Live Culture is a funky dark-ish, cozy-ish place that has at least 80 wines by the glass, an interesting collection of beers and a nice-looking menu of things that can be made with bread, meat, cheese and salad. I say nice-looking because the plates looked nice, but I'd just had dinner and didn't have a chance to try out the food... yet. What I DID have, was the Real Beer Float. That's right... because this establishment serves frozen yogurt as well as beer and wine, you can get a real-beer float. I opted for the Framboise Lambic with vanilla fro yo. Can I just say... DELICIOUS! The creamy and sweet vanilla contrasting with the sweet-tart lambic... ahh! Another suggestion was an oatmeal stout with the chocolate kiss fro yo, but they ran out of the stout. I could have gotten Guiness with the chocolate, but that seemed a bit heavy after our dinner. If you think that sounds weird, you should think of the flavor profiles of Guiness and chocolate. It's practically a match made in heaven! It would be very much like having a chocolate affogato, but with alcoholic coffee! My brother-in-law had a Polish beer (I don't remember the marque) and then proceeded to have tart-plain and peanut-butter yogurt. I'll definitely go back to try their food since a bresaola or mortadella panino sounds right up my alley. I also want to curl up on the high, semi-banquettes that line one wall. They look nice enough to curl-up on and just web-surf with dinner (which is what one patron was doing). Oh, and I want to meet Derek, because his real-beer floats are genius.

MGR: I need to see the physical card Me: Ok, I guess not even a faxed copy of the front and back of my card will do? I know other places... text: I've been coming to Great Basin off and on for years. It's in Sparks, which makes it a little bit farther away than I usually want to travel for a mid-week meal. The bartender, while keeping up with all the table drink orders, had beers in our hands in seconds flat. Not much later we were seated. I have always enjoyed the food here at Great Basin. They have great burgers -- fiancee is a fan of the black and bleu burger that is smothered in crumbly bleu cheese. I like the chicken skewers usually, but went with the delectable shepherd's pie last night. Someone in Great Basin's kitchen knows what they are doing. This is a good spot for all the pub favorites. The waitress, who was also extremely busy, made sure our food was served hot and came to check on us a couple of times. I can't remember the last time I was actually offered more rounds of drinks at restaurant; usually the server drops off the food and bails for the rest of the meal. Not this gal. The best kind of service is the kind that you don't really remember because the server is doing their job so well they become unremarkable. Which is what this waitress was, and I mean that as a high compliment. Lastly, this is easily the best microbrew in town. Nothing against Silver Peak or anything, but Great Basin's beer is on another level. I don't even like beer as a general rule and I found myself ordering two pints of the seasonal Red Nose Wassail last night. It tasted like Christmas in a beer, if that makes any sense. Solid and highly recommended!

text: Let me preface this by saying I was dragged to this place after a 10 hour sales meeting in a hot and steamy conference room. I was starving--and in need of several adult beverages. As this place was described to me I had imagined I'd be embarking on a historical and cultural culinary adventure back through time. You know--chunky bar maids dressed in corseted dresses that functioned for centuries as silicon enhancements holding 8 lead pints in each hand, rogues in the corner laughing and fighting, massive boars heads served on mountainous piles of meat, bards telling their tales of old. And I guess in some demented way this place was just like that....only without the embellishment. Instead of the boar's head we got a small handful of roast beef placed lovingly on a plain bun that was, in turn, placed lovingly on a paper plate of the same size (are we at white castle?). Those Rubenesque hostesses I was imagining turned out to be a friendly--if not forgetful--unceremonious woman who could carry not 8, but 1 pint in each hand. But we did get our Bard. Instead of striking tales of dragons and knights, Mr. J. Alfred Prufrock relinquished a long, tiresome soliloquy on the struggles, tragedies and triumphs that you would expect from a lifetime devoted to being a basketball referee. Now I understand the difference between being captivated with times of yore and being held captive by them.

text: I gotta give the Factory some credit...it makes the Troc look like a classy venue. That, my friends, is some true wizardry. Well, there is a lot that would satisfy about half of the staff on a slow night, otherwise, you get to pay an ever-shifting amount to park on what appears to be a public street/alley/lot/toxic dump around the venue. You get to polish your street cred, at least...toss the bum/security guard a few bucks when you park, and promise to toss even more when you get back so long as your car is still in one piece (and make sure you follow through...bums are like elephants when it comes to remembering things). Hey, it works. Ok, you make it inside. If the show skews more towards an "adult" audience, make sure you show up several hours early so you can get a good spot upstairs. Otherwise, hang out downstairs with the kids. Sound...sound??? Put a boombox inside of a heating duct and blast it...you have just been to a concert at the Electric Factory. It always, always sucks. Always. I saw the Mr. Show...show here, which had no music, and the sound still sucked. How does this happen? You simply need a mic that doesn't a-splode when spoken into. Didn't happen. It boggles the mind. A gang of stray cats could run a better venue. I truly hate this place and everything about it. I would normally not waste any time writing about it, but I figured I'd play a little game...I dropped a reference to the last band I ever saw (and will ever see) somewhere in my rantings...name them and you win scene points. Now, excuse me...I'm going to rent a helicopter just so I can pee on this dump.

text: Eh. The drinks are in a bucket of ice, but they're mostly warm and when I tried to dig down to the bottom for a cold one, a few bottles fell out of the bucket. The free chips and salsa were decent, but after a few minutes of munching on them, I realized the red sauce was super hot and my eyes were burning before the food ever even came out. Now granted, I have a low tolerance for heat, I've never been sweating at a Mexican joint before the entree even came out. One of the good things about Taco Riendo is it's one of the few places where you can get a fish taco. text: Chinese is not really my thing - not since I was a teenager eating sweet-and-sour chicken balls on mall dates like they were escargot and coming home reeking like food court. These days, I generally prefer a cleaner palette and most Chinese food (correction: American Chinese food) is greasy, slimy, over-fried, and leaves you feeling bloated and sloven, like a mall rat with baby fat sticking like glue. Wok n' go is express Chinese that I can dial up when I don't feel like cooking and feel fantastic after I've eaten. They're programmed into my cell phone and have a presence in our home like a Portuguese mama who still comes over to cook for you but, alas, thankfully lives a full block away around the corner! The food is fresh and cooked right in front of you. The sauces are savoury and not slimy (which I've learned is the result of a marinating process called velveting that adds egg whites and cornstarch to change the texture of meats - an authentic eastern technique that, in my opinion, doesn't quite translate). So I can still stay awake and function without heartburn after I eat Wok n' go, but granted I don't go for the sumo meal; I stick with the tofu and veggies on rice and the green onion cakes and hot and sour soup. When I want to indulge, I go for the lemon chicken which is breaded but has quality chicken; and it's not your typical 70% breading 30% meat-morsel mix. There's more meat than fatty coating - so you can still enjoy, but not fall colluding victim to the revenge of baby fat (called obesity) that's sweeping our fast-food nation...faster than you can say, uh, "sweet and sour chicken balls," (which aren't, btw, even Chinese food!!) Baby fat belongs in the baby books. Wok n' go is a short walk from my house and I haven't derailed my body by eating their express fare on the fly. Thank you, Wok n' go, for the integrity of your food, and your fast, friendly service. I enjoy reading trashy mags in your store front while waiting for my take-out order to be called. You even know my name.

text: In the past year, Banh Mi had become the latest food fad that everyone seems to enjoy and being in Philly, we benefit from a respectable size of Vietnamese population residing in South Philly. All I did is comparing a few bakeries in Chinatown, Ba Le, O Sandwiches and Ziet Cafe in South Philly as well as Sampan around 13th and Walnut, so I'm open to suggestions on places that I should try. But as of now, I'm sticking with Q.T. Two friendly ladies behind the counter made up the Q.T. sandwich team. They make each sandwich to the order to guarantee maximum bread crispiness and freshness. The prices here are slightly more expensive than conventional Chinatown standards and since it's made to order, there is a 5-10 minutes waiting time but it's quite worth it. Like other reviewers have mentioned, each Banh Mi has slightly sweet and sour pickled carrots and cucumbers, fresh cilantro for spice and jalapeno pepper for heat. The non-vegetarian ones are smeared with pate. I usually get the special Banh Mi which contains a combination of three different meats. The bread is toasted and crunchy which compliments the crispy vegetables, the creamy pate and the meat. The storefront can be slightly improved and it'd be great if they can speed up some in the sandwich making department but other than that Q.T. is definitely a welcomed addition to the Philadelphia Banh Mi scene.

text: Every once in a while, as a former big-city dweller, I get a craving for cheap, greasy Chinese take-out. You know -- big battered nuggets of chicken in unidentifiable pink syrup, pan-fried dumplings, and mysteriously salty egg rolls. Maybe I'm alone in this, I don't know. Anyhow, though, my one experience with New Golden Buffet has convinced me that this is not the place to satisfy those cravings. For about thirty bucks, I got a take-out meal consisting of Moo Shu Vegetables, a slightly spicy dish called Ma Pu Tofu, General Tso's Chicken, along with dumplings, pork fried rice, and an egg roll. The dumplings were fine, and the Moo Shu vegetables weren't too bad, but everything else was, frankly, terrible, and as you can see from my other reviews, my standards aren't exactly high. The chicken was almost too hard to chew; the egg roll tasted like it hadn't been completely defrosted before they heated it up, and the tofu dish consisted only of chunks of mushy, flavorless tofu floating in copious amounts of gloppy "sauce" (which appeared to be soy sauce thickened with cornstarch, plus sweetener and hot sauce). The dumplings tasted identical to the dumplings I've eaten in hole-in-the-wall Chinese take-outs around the United States, so they were fine. The Moo Shu vegetables were reasonably good; they tasted fresh, and the flavorings weren't too salty or sweet. Now, most folks go there for the buffet, and there was a bit of a crowd there, so maybe the buffet offerings are better. But for thirty bucks I expected something a little better than this. To top it off, the service was incredibly slow. I'm still looking for that cheap Chinese fix. Website (which features a take-out menu, as well as -- oddly enough -- a list of current quotes from financial markets): http://newgoldenbuffet.com

text: Freshii is sort of like Mongolian barbecue, but for salads and wraps and with more paperwork. On that little clipboard is a little form that looks like a W2, no matter what you order you're going to have to fill this thing out. If something on the posted menu sounds good, write the name of the menu item in the upper left-hand corner of the form and mark the box next to the sauce or dressing you would like. You can also build your own meal--the fun way to order--by selecting salad, wrap, soup, noodle or rice bowl and customizing with toppings and sauces. After you've filled out your form, make sure to write your name in the upper right-hand corner of and then hand the entire clipboard to one of the employees in the back of the shop, at the end of the line. They'll do a quick check of your order, highlighting your choices as they go, and then give you a carbon copy. Now, all you have to do is briefly leave Freshii to have the carbon reproduced in triplicate and notarized. Just kidding, you can actually just give it to the cashier along with any of the impulse-buy chips or Cliff bars you've picked up while in line. Whew! That's it, your work is done. After you pay, you can ponder the unusual assortment of deli-case and packaged bulk food items--flax seeds, anyone? A custom-built lunch and a drink will set you back about $10.00, a stock selection with chips and a drink will be about the same. They also sell the, suddenly ubiquitous in Nashville, tart froyo. I haven't tried any yet, but it looks tasty!

text: Johnny's Po-Boys is a great little place with a HUGE menu. Their menu has something for everyone and it's a great place to try something new! Johnny's is small and a little plain, but the quality of food and the price definitely make up for it. The menu has an extensive variety of po-boy's as well as other items like seafood gumbo or subs; they also have weekly or daily specials listed somewhere off to the side. For those of you unfamiliar with a po-boy, it's a large sandwich consisting of a meat or seafood served on half a french baguette typically with lettuce, tomato and mayo. If you've never had a po-boy or never had a certain type of po-boy, this is THE place to try it out. You can choose from the traditional seafood pb's like soft-shell crab and shrimp, or you can pick an exotic one such as alligator! They also have the tried and true chicken tender, hot dog or tuna salad pb's for those feeling a little less adventurous. You can get just a sandwich or a combo, and everything is available as take out too. Some of the meals came out a little quicker than others, and if you end up being one of the lucky ones waiting on your food, don't sweat it! I ordered the special of the week, the half order soft-shell crab po-boy with a bowl of seafood gumbo on the side, all for about 15 bucks! I ended up waiting about 15 to 20 minutes for my food, so that did not make me too happy.....especially since I saw the others in my group getting their food very quickly. Well let me tell you, it was definitely worth the wait! I got my po-boy plain (no lettuce, tomato or mayo); a whole order must contain 2 soft-shell crabs as mine was the half and I only got one, but that was more than enough! I was served a baguette split down the middle with a deliciously crispy fried whole soft-shell crab sitting on top. They prepared the crab by removing the inside of the crab (guts, etc...), dipping it in breading and frying the entire thing. The sandwich was hard to eat in one piece, so I ate it open faced. The seafood gumbo was fan-TASTIC! Made with entire pieces of soft-shell crabs, large shrimp and crawfish and plenty of veggies and hot sauce, it made the perfect side dish. It came with a piece of toasted baguette as well and when I used that up, I used the rest of my sandwich baguette to sop up what little gumbo was left. I dipped the crab in there too; the entire meal was one to remember.......in fact, I'm not gonna lie.....I may day dream about it time and again when I get a craving for some good creole food......and you would too if you tried it!! So, in conclusion: Johnny's Po-boy's =legendary experience!

text: Jacque-Imo's is the place to be. If you ever visit New Orleans, you MUST make this one of your dining destinations. Trust me on this one. Jacque-Imo's is tucked away from the French Quarter. Hop on the Charles Streetcar and enjoy a nice 15-20 min ride from the French Quarter to Jacque's and you're sure to be in for a treat. The place is a great reflection of what the south is all about: friendly, down-to-earth folks & solid Cajun/Creole cookin'. There are 2 picnic tables set outside + a colorful truck w/ a plant on top & a prized table & chair set up on the bed of it! The small 2 story building is bustling w/ folks having a good time and the casual interior filled w/ lots of personality. It's impossible to not feel comfortable here. Jacque himself can be found checking in on all the tables, making sure everyone is having a good time and sportin' his chef's jacket, pair of shorts and of course... Birkenstocks. He's quite the party animal and I love it! The wait was a good half hour, but w/ a bar just next door and a hostess that offered to come in and round us up when our table was ready, the time just flew by. Once we were brought to our table, I couldn't help but grin from ear to ear as I came to find out that we were lucky enough to score the table on the truck! SWEET! The highlights of the evening were the... -Watermelon Mojitos: These come complete w/ chunks of fresh watermelon. What a treat! I love how they come in plastic cups; perfect for toting em' along on our stroll back to the streetcar stop. -Alligator Cheesecake: Don't let the name fool you. My bf was turned off by the name, but once we bit into this quiche-like app, we were both sold! This is a signature dish at Jacque's, and it makes perfect sense why. Welcome to the South. -Fried Green Tomatoes: An absolute favorite of the evening. These big, succulent slices w/ crispy skins are exactly what FGT should really be about. -Fish: ha! I forgot the type we got, but either way, it was cooked to perfection & we both gobbled it down. All in all, a unique, fun and delicious experience!

text: The horrid attitude and unfriendly overall aura of Mama Angelina's has made me finally resolve not to dine there. I live in the Arts Condos, which is LITERALLY directly across the street from Mama's, so it has always been a convenient place to get a slice of pizza at a good price. And the pizza IS good, if you like New York style, super thin, super greasy, super cheesy pizza. At $2.00 a slice for a piece as big as your arm, it's a decent sized meal at a totally reasonable price. But the staff is so abysmally rude that I won't put up with it anymore. I literally had my final straw today; I went in and ordered a cheesesteak with everything, two pieces of cheese and two pieces of sausage pizza. The guy wrote down my order and then another guy began making my sandwich. Pizza is normally given to you on a flimsy paper plate, and if you're taking it to go, they slide the whole thing inside an equally flimsy paper bag (the kind you might get a cookie in.) If you order four or more slices they will put it all in a pizza box for you, which makes sense because 4 slices is pretty much the size of a small pizza. Well today the guy pulls out some paper plates so I said "Could you please put them all in a box for me? I just have to walk across the street, but I don't think I can carry four paper plates and a sandwhich." And he said "We don't have a small box." So I said "Well, normally if I order four slices they put it in a box for me." So then he starts glaring at me and YELLS "What kind of pizza DO YOU WANT?" I said "Didn't you just take my order sixty seconds ago?" And he just repeated himself - "WHAT KIND OF PIZZA DO YOU WANT?" So I literally told him, to his face, "Look. I'm fed up of this. I have probably spent $1000 buying $2 pieces of pizza from you over the last 12 months, and every time I come in here I'm treated like dirt. You guys are so rude, I don't want anything to do with you anymore." And he actually had the nerve to be incredulous about it, as if it was news to him. Trust me, he's heard this before. So he points back to his coworker who is making my cheesesteak and says something about how he's already making it, and I said "No, forget it. I don't want anything to do with your food ever again." And then as I'm walking out the door, he had the audacity to say "God bless you." Don't put money into the pockets of people who have no consideration for you as a customer just because it is convenient. Give your hard earned dollars to people who make you feel like your business is appreciated. Mama Angelina's is staffed by two young men, an older man, and a woman who are incapable of gratitude, pleasantries or even social nicety. It isn't worth it.

text: Oh, those bastards! I take one of those "special" routes to work... the 37 that services my business park departs Broad and Snyder at 6:17am, 6:41am, 7:05am, and 7:29am, the last of which gets me to work around 7:45am. text: Going here was the worst restaurant experience of my life, no question. Sam runs this joint as a one man operation in Printer's Alley downtown. When I first walked into the tiny room (couldn't have been more than 250 sq ft), I was pleased at the sight of such an informal, distinctive, divey kind of hole in the wall. Horrible, yellowed posters as decor, cracks in the floor tiles, no air conditioning. I usually love little places like that (e.g. Edgefield in East Nashville). I was, however, sorely disappointed. Sam, who many people on this site and on City Search sympathize with for reasons unknown to me, is a complete jerk. The first greeting I received was "NO WRITE ON MENU". I was studying the small laminated menu, trying to decide what I wanted to order. I guess he assumed I was going to mark on it, the way a lot of sushi places have you order. I placed my order and specified what type of nigiri I wanted with my roll, as it didn't say on the menu what type came with the sushi combo plate. Instead of explaining things, he snapped again, "You no get to pick all three same! You get what I put on plate!" I took it and assumed it was my misunderstanding. I was careful to handle him with kid gloves and not get upset, as it's a relatively common occurrence for good restauranteurs and chefs to be prickly, neurotic, irregular characters. I have interacted with people like that before and had some of the best food I've ever eaten served by them - one of those "good artists are drug addicted and suicidally depressed" sort of phenomenon, except "good chefs are insane and total jerks". I figured his personality might just be the price to be paid for outstanding cuisine. I was so, so wrong. When our order was up, I went and grabbed it from the bar and sat down. The first thing I noticed was how sloppily it was assembled. Sushi is one of those culinary niches that takes pretty exacting technique and attention to detail. It takes practice and focus to make tight, neat maki, which is why it isn't something delegated in kitchens, but reserved for a specific sushi chef - a guy who knows what he's doing. Sam, with way too much rice spilling out of his maki and his loose wrapping, clearly does not know what he's doing. I picked up a piece of yellowtail nigiri, dressed it up with some wasabi and dunked it in soy sauce. I popped the nigiri in my mouth and the first thing that hit me was the soy sauce. I have never had such cheap tasting, horribly salty soy sauce. I know soy is salty, but this was terrible. Pretty much any sushi place I've ever been to, upscale or divey, usually goes with the standard - plain old Kikkoman. I dont know what horribly cheap brand he was buying, but the salt was all I could taste, which as it turns out, was not such a bad thing. I tried another piece of nigiri, no soy sauce this time. I nearly gagged. The fish was not only at room temperature (which was warm, considering the place had no a/c or circulation), but also was very, very obviously not fresh. Before I totally gave up (and because I was hungry), I tried a piece of crunchy shrimp roll. The shrimp was bland, the tempura not at all crispy or light and once again it was definitely not fresh seafood. The biggest offense with his roll, however, was the rice. The grains seemed bigger than they should be, making me think he was using regular long grain white rice, instead of the slightly more expensive sushi rice. Additionally, I found out part of the reason why his rolls are so sloppy, other than the over stuffing. When my roll fell to bits when picked up and when I tasted the rice, it was clear there was no vinegar in it, meaning it was not prepared correctly for sushi and therefore, not sticky rice in the least. Let me reiterate, this guy has no idea what he's doing. I only had one or two whole pieces of his stuff before surrendering. The friend I was with, however, wasn't quite as critical as I was (and also didnt order nigiri, the most offensive part of the meal) and said I should box it up and he would eat it later. We took our stuff to Sam to be wrapped. He drilled us for a while: "Where are you going after this? How far away is your house from here? Are you going to refrigerate this right away? You know this is RAW FISH, right?". At first, I thought it was cute that he would care, but he made it clear pretty quickly what his motivation was - "People get sick, they blame sushi restaurant. I not want to get sued! You could just go and leave in car all day. I have good restaurant! I not get in trouble for sick people!" It was hilarious. He was mad about us maybe getting sick and suing him after a 10 minute ride in an air conditioned car, but he wasnt worried enough with food safety to serve properly stored, fresh fish. Despite being a paying customer, I was treated as a nuisance and then given terrible food. Everyone says Sam's is the cheapest sushi it town. I wouldn't argue that. It's also pretty inexpensive.

Nestled firmly at the end of the 12 South shopping district, Las Paletas is arguably the best place in Nashville for desert. They have something for everyone. Like chocolate? No problem, they've got plenty of options. More of a fruit kind of person? Yep, they've got that covered. And for the bold, well, don't worry, you'll be sated too. Flavors can range from Mexican caramel (still my favorite) to hibiscus to chocolate wasabi. Parking is a little precarious sometimes, as they share the space with a salon that keeps similar hours, but its well worth it. Also, if the day's nice, you can park in one of the convenient street spots down 12th and just make the rounds, do a little shopping, then stop in at Las Paletas before heading back to your car. Whether you're a local or a tourist, there is absolutely no excuse for missing out on Las Paletas.

Why do everything okay, when you can do a few things GREAT? This should be the slogan of House, because it certainly is the way they designed their menu. The Jersey Joe, a wonderful panini on artisan rye bread. Crisp, fresh, delicious. The key to any sandwich is the bread, and House make's sure to use only the freshest locally baked bread (From a bakery whose name escapes me at the moment). The tomato soup is freshly made, with real organic tomatoes, served steaming hot. The place is literally a hole in the wall, but very cozy, especially on a cold, wet day. I wouldn't call it House, it's more like Home, because you feel right at home when eating there. The gentleman who served us was extremely gracious and courteous, and I could tell he was very proud of the work they were doing there. Small business pride is something that gets lost in the monstrosity of the big chain restaurants. What else can I say? This place rules.

text: One might assume that Indianapolis is incapable of offering fine cuisine in the Italian realm, however, we all know what can happen when we ASSuME. You will struggle to find better Italian food anywhere in Indiana, and now the locally-owned, northside spot is reaching out to a nightlife audience, as they have already established two regular weekly events (Flirt Wednesdays and Tantivy Thursdays) featuring local DJs, a sexy crowd, and in some cases, live art and fashion events. The restaurant also provides some of the best outdoor dining in the city. Here in the Midwest, dining enthusiasts race to the restaurants that feature decks and rooftop dining during the few months of the year where it can be comfortable to eat outside. Sangiovese's deck seats at least a few dozen tables, and is not adjacent to any busy street or noisy clutter. In fact, quite the opposite is true: the deck, located on the backside of the restaurant, faces a secluded section of the White River and provides a spectacular view, particularly as the sun sets during evening dining. This is another example of one of Sangiovese's best qualities: you can take a date, a group of friends, or your parents and be equally comfortable with the atmosphere and the service. As if eating, drinking and dancing weren't enough, Sangiovese also offers catering services and delivers (minimum order required) anywhere in the greater Indianapolis area. If you're a business needing a lunch catered, be sure to give them a shot. Located in between Keystone and Allisonville on 82nd Street. Do yourself a favor and grab dinner at Sangiovese. Stick around on Wednesday or Thursday for DJs (starting at 10pm). One meal at this place and you'll be booking your next reservation!

text: Came in for lunch. IMO they were not overly busy for a fast food place. Two people ahead of us, took 4 minutes to get to the head of the line. Gave the order including a 4 for $5 Sweet Deal. The guy on the cash register rang up each individual item, over charging four dollars. I pointed it out and he had to get another guy to fix it. Then we were given an order number and went and sat down. About 5 minutes later they brought some food out and asked if it was ours as they had mixed up the orders. For the next 5 minutes they kept bringing out food trying to figure out who ordered what. 15 minutes after we ordered our food it finally came, only to be wrong. I had to take back the burger and get the right one. Finally 30 minutes after we arrived we were able to start eating. Maybe this was a fluke but one I do not wish to repeat. It definitely was not a "fast food" experience. If I feel like D.Q. again I will try one of the others in Reno.

text: I saw the construction of this little cuppiecake shop over the past few weeks, and waited with bated breath for the grand opening... which was surprisingly underwhelming--no flags, no big affair, no anything. Maybe it's because the cupcakes are equally underwhelming--they look more appealing than they taste. At $2.50 a pop, it's not going to cost you an arm and a leg, but they really are just "ok" cupcakes. I tried the chai-flavored icing + chocolate cake cupcake (misleading-ly named "chai" for a cupcake that's just plain ole chocolate): chai frosting had a delicate flavor, but maybe borderline bland, and the cake itself wasn't soft or moist. Maaaybe I would give it another shot if More Than Just Ice Cream wasn't directly across the street...
label: NEG

text: Much like the writer who posted before me, I am a regular of Rittenhouse nails first at the location on 17th and Samson and now on 20th. I also am cheating on Helen, but not with Linda (though maybe I should give her a try), but with Susan. I just can't help it, the salon on 20th is larger, prettier and at off-peak times like mornings or weekday afternoons, very quiet. The owner Sunny actually cares about her customers unlike some other nail places in the city. If something you do not like happens, tell her! She will apologize and fix it, she is a savy business woman. I've been going to Rittenhouse Nails for over four years and only once was there a problem and she raced after me and brought me back in. She's the best! They now use the hot stones for the Pedicure massage and it's fabulous. Try to go during off-peak hours they open early usually 9:30, slow during the weekday mornings, and stay open fairly late, but be careful it gets pretty crowded late in the day. When they are not busy, you get a longer massage, but realize even when they are croweded, they do a great job and will give you a shortened down version of the royal treatment.
label: POS

text: Since Pudge's has been slowing (yet surely) going downhill, I've found myself going to Lee's more than a little often. Nothing against Lee's, but you must understand that years ago I would not betray Pudge's even under pain of death. But alas, they betrayed me, so I am but a nomad in the desert. The big plus with Lee's is that, golly gee, the people who work there are very friendly. "Cool", even. The food is pretty darn good too...really good. Flaws and all Pudge's still holds on the edge on steaks, but Lee's is right up there on the hoagie front. The tuna is better, for sure. I can't compare the other grill items (burgers, etc.) because I never even consider ordering them (does anybody?). Are you a Philly sports fan? Furthermore, a Flyers fan? Well you might as well move in, because this is will be your new home. The walls are literally covered with Flyers "stuff", mostly Daily News full pagers, plus all sorts of memorabilia. The TV, if on, is surely showing a game. There are a few tables to dine-in, but its all counter service, and does more takeout business anyway. In conclusion, Pudge's could very well win me back...fire the jerks ruining the place and conquer the difficult task of getting the orders right and they are back in the game. But until that happens (if it ever happens), I'll probably be spending more and more time (and money) at Lee's...and I ain't ashamed to admit it.
label: POS

text: H. Cue's is a hidden gem. It is above Pizza Perfect on 21st. You can actually order pizza from your bartender and it will be added to your bar tab...which is kind of awesome. The bartenders are incredibly friendly as are the regulars. This was actually the first bar in town that I felt totally comfortable showing up alone. Pool is by the hour, and girls get happy hour price (pool) all the time. So bring a lady along for the discount! Also, there are two dart boards and a slew of board games behind the bar. Add the killer jukebox to the mix and you've got an excellent bar.

text: I am very hard on my shoes and I wear through shoes faster than should be humanly possible. I was told by my last shoe repair guy, as he chuckled over the state of my heels, that I "must be a very aggressive walker". After moving, I was half-heartedly searching for a new shoe guy and when two pairs of heels were well-past wearing I took a gander at Yelp, saw the great reviews for Capa and took the sad little pairs in. Capa offered everything I was looking for in shoe repair. Quick, no nonsense service with fantastic results. My shoes look brand new - and that's a feat. On top of that, prices were fair ($28 for two pairs heeled and polished). Bravo Capa!

text: Maybe I've got my expectations set too high, but I was not at all impressed by 400 Olive. The service was sloooowww with long waits to place orders, get refills, or to have dishes bussed. I could overhear folks at neighboring tables complaining about the service as well. And there were only about 10 or 12 people in the entire restuarant. This was a consistent experience all three times I've come here (1x for dinner, 2x for breakfast). Food was pretty decent, but it feels overpriced. Maybe that's because when you get in on a late flight and don't have time to go offsite, eating at the hotel just leaves a bad taste in your mouth (pun intended). Dinner feels like less of a rip off despite the higher prices. Maybe that's because I've become desensitized to overpriced dinner salads and such. Breakfast is a total rip-off. $12 for an omlet, $10 for fruit, etc. My big complaint is that they don't open to 6:30. Hey, I'm from California and would LIKE to be having breakfast at a leisurely 8AM PACIFIC time (i.e. 10AM Central), but I'm working with the locals. They start at 5:30 and have been benovolent enough pick me up at a lethargic 7AM. Thanks. Seat me at 6:30 sharp. 25 minutes to get an omlet. 5 minutes to eat and pay. Just awsome. If I wasn't such a wus, I'd walk uphill both ways, in the snow, in 15 degree weather to another breakfast place. And yes, it really is "snowing" and really is 15 degrees and I really am a wus.

text: I DO NOT RECOMMEND HIRO'S IN TARPON SPRINGS. THE FOOD IS NOT GOOD, AND THE SERVICE IS POOR. Our waitress, who undoubtedly must have been new, was scattered. Our drinks took an unusually long time to arrive. The sushi appetizer we ordered was not the one we got. When we tried to waive our waitress down, she kept ducking in and out of sight. So we called to the waitress attending the table next to ours and let her know our appetizer was wrong, and she had the gall to question us about having ordered incorrectly. There was a lot of smoke accumulated inside Hiro's because they don't have the hoods above the table like Benihana. We had an emergency and had to leave before our chef had even arrived at the table to start cooking the meal. I asked for the check and could not believe they were charging me for the entire meal!!! I tried to complain to our waitress, but she just kept scurrying around and didn't even notice the incorrect bill. I finally got a manager's attention (a blond woman whose name I didn't get), and told her that we shouldn't be charged for a meal we didn't have. They grudgingly removed the items we never got to eat. Our waitress, possibly feeling a little guilty, packed up the other appetizer we had ordered (which was correct!) in a to-go box, and we ate that in the car. It was pretty much scallions rolled inside Steak-Ums and doused with teriyaki sauce. Perhaps we've been spoiled by our frequent (and excellent) dining experiences at Benihana. We are new to the Tampa Bay area and are still feeling out restaurants. But after having attempted to dine at Hiro's, we will now happily drive all the way to Orlando if we want teppanyaki. Hiro's wasn't that busy, so there was really no excuse for the poor service. We didn't even get an apology. NO DINING EXPERIENCE IS WORTH THE AGGRAVATION--I DO NOT RECOMMEND DINING AT HIRO'S IN TARPON SPRINGS.

text: I was really looking forward to finding a good Mexican restaurant in Reno, and was sorely disappointed in this place. I can think of at least 10 restaurants/taquerias in the Sacramento area (where I'm from) that top this place easily, including chains. My first impression of this place was really great, very busy and very friendly. My husband and I were greeted with chips and salsa like any other Mexican place would. Except this salsa tasted like tomato soup with chili powder in it. Well, I figured that was okay because at least I wouldn't gorge on chips and salsa and be too full to eat the entrée. Our waiter asked for our drink order. We asked what they had for soft drinks. He said Dr. Pepper and I was sold. When our drinks came back, I almost spat the soda out on my husband. It was Mr. Pibb. I don't mind Mr. Pibb in lieu of Dr. Pepper, but when my mind is expecting DP, Pibb tastes like cough syrup. Don't lie about your drink selection! Dr. Pepper does not equal Mr. Pibb. Not much later, our food came out. After a few bites, I asked my husband what he thought. He said, "Eh, I've had better." I said it was the blandest Mexican food I've ever tasted. We both agreed that we wouldn't be back. One thing I've got give to this place is their excellent service. We were seated immediately and had paid our check all in 35 minutes. When people came through the door, our waiter knew over half of them and greeted them with hugs. Unfortunately, I've just had better Mexican food.

text: I went to eat at Gallagher's for the first time recently, and I was sadly disappointed. If you are looking for an upscale steakhouse in the Tampa area, there are many other better options. The only thing that I was pleased about at Gallagher's was my dry aged 7oz filet mignon, which was delicious. However, my husband ordered the ny strip, and it was overcooked. My caesar salad was boring and unimpressive. The mashed potatoes were incredibly salty, the dessert was disappointing, and the service...well, I expected better. I saw one employee changing table linen right in front of us...3 tables at a time, leaving them bare while he hunted for new table cloths..it was just very unprofessional. I had heard good things about this restaurant, but I will not be returning.

text: I still for the life of me can't understand why this place does not get better reviews across the board; they are always crowded when I have been and the food is always amazing. Some of the menu items even include soup or salad at no extra charge, which is an increasing rarity these days. Their queso, in my opinion, ranks 3rd after San Antonio Taco and Chili's in that order. Then, out of every place I have been to, their onion rings are just flat out Amazing, the best in town. The mark of a good onion ring? The onion stays in the batter coating when you bite into it. Their batter, which is not crumbly or crumby like other places, is a very much like a tempura batter and oh so good. I have not yet tried on single bad thing on the menu, from their fried mushrooms with horseradish sauce, chicken n buttons and Monterrey Chicken breast. Then there is the amazing mac n cheese (only second to Cracker Barrel, still need to try Loveless and Rotier's on that) and their awesome burgers. There is the one dish that is sure to make any lover of Mac n Cheese outright soak themselves in drool... The Ultimate Pasta, which is so good; think mac n cheese on steroids and this is what you get. Also, if you are a fan of Chicken Parmesan and are really hungry, they have the largest serving of Chicken Parm anywhere I have seen. Now while it is not the best in town, it is still very good. Finally, I must say, they have the best Chicken Tortilla soup I have ever had anywhere (even back home in Texas), as it has the perfect amount of cheese, tortilla strips, chicken, corn and seasonings in it. As for there Caesar salad, it is consistently good every time I have had it. I could go on and on about all the tasty menu items there, but there are to many to name. However, I will say that they also have some very good shakes. Now, my only complaint is that I wish they would bring back their coupons! They used to have coupons where, among other things, when buying two entree's you got the lesser of the two (cost wise) for free.
label: POS

text: How I miss this place since I moved to th NYC! All you have to know is $18.99 all you can eat Churrascaria, Free Caparinhas (you bring lime and rum), and some of the tastiest desserts this side of Rio! The quality of meat is not up to par with Fogo however it is damn good! Juicy, salty, plenty of sauces to accompany the meats... makes the side dishes an after thought. The area is ghetto but the workers inside are friendly esp. the large motherly lady! Shes the best! (She bribed me and my friends with samples of all her deserts one time) Heres my tips for eating here: 1. When buying by the pound... put some light greens all over your plate so they don't charge you for the all meat price ($8-9/lb) vs the nl ($6-7). 2. Get the pinapple cake topped with condensed milk($3). It a wet cake with fresh fruits and cream throughout and topped with a sweet layer of condensed milk. 3. Bring antacid! esp if you go all you can eat. I couldn't sleep on my back for a whole night after one monster gorge fest! 4. Go on weekends only for prime selection of meats! Short rib/ flank / picanhna are on point!

text: I took a date here on a Saturday night. It was the day of a big college football game in the Dome so parking in Quarter was even more atrocious than normal. The Star Steak & Lobster House is a small joint right near the touristy Canal side of the Quarter and boy it shows. Now as a bit of backstory, when I was in highschool I worked with my grandfather on our cattle farm in Missouri. when I was leaving for New Orleans he told me that while they may be some of the best cooks there, if he remembers correctly they couldn't cook a steak to save their lives since there aren't much cattle farming opportunities on the swampland. Now, years later, his words ring truer than ever. While the service was acceptable, the food was sub-par, especially for the high price. The SS&LH is more of a gross parody of New Orleans food than an actual restaurant. The reason I frequented the joint was a deal I got through Groupon, so at least I had an excuse; I'm not sure about the other 4 people who were at the other tables. The atmosphere was dingy, the live musician was a mediocre flutist playing over some backing tracks, the whole thing was New Orleans gone wrong. For one, I am pretty sure my side of sauteed mushrooms were microwaved before they brought them out. Correct me if I am wrong, but I am pretty sure after a light treatment of butter in a frying pan it isn't proper to place the mushrooms in a bowl or water. I may have been born at night, but it wasn't last night; these mushrooms were nuked. The drink prices were ridiculous as well. $4.50 for Turbodog??? I can pick up a 6-pack at Win-Dixie for seven dollars after their markup. I know the quarter is expensive, but this may be criminal. To be frank, there is no reason to come to this restaurant, and tourists and locals alike should stay away. If you are really jonesing for a steak, just go to Applebee's. You will get better food, or at least comparable, for cheaper, plus you don't have to park in the quarter. You are in New Orleans, there is no excuse to go to an overpriced mediocre restaurant.
label: NEG

text: I was truly conflicted about how many stars to give Lounge One Two Five. My roommate and I debated on whether it should receive 5 or 1, and the truth is, it's so bad, its great. text: Ate there for the first time today... Same experience as Holly K.-- VERY fresh ingredients, everything cooked perfectly and obviously from scratch. Even the fried rice... nothing in it smacked of that cheap, hastily thrown together, sitting in some prep-table from hours ago impression you usually get from fried rice dishes in the more modestly priced Chinese restaurants. Nothing heavy at all, and not oily (of cheap bulk frying oils) either... All-around delicious and very satisfying meal. Full of REAL and beautifully balanced/composed flavors... Yum! I will be back there very soon again. Also, the owners (who do most of what goes on there themselves) ARE both sparklingly present, highly enthusiastic, and very sincerely friendly and outgoing people (but not intrusive or egotistically all-about-themselves either). After we'd eaten (and paid our check) I noticed a *very* large bowl of delicious-looking freshly steamed herbed clams waiting there in the kitchen window... I made a comment to the gentleman who is the owner (and he waits on tables as well) in high praise of how good they looked, and said that I definitely wanted to order THAT the next time I was there... He explained that it was actually his own lunch, and that, for a variety of reasons (which he elucidated a few of) it's not on the menu and they don't generally offer that in the restaurant. A couple of minutes later though, just before he did sit down to eat (I and my friend were the last couple to still be there at the end of their busy lunch session and were about to leave), he walked over and, with a big sincere smile, set down a plate in front of me with five or six of those beautiful clams on it. Mmmmmm delicious! Gosh they were good. The point is, these people don't see their customers as strangers or as not mattering. Lots of places say that, and sometimes you run into the odd restaurant owner or host/hostess who does try to adopt that "service-with-a-smile, you're-our-friends" kind of attitude (some more sincerely than others), but these people are the real deal. Nothing even slightly forced or artificial about that whole exchange (and the rest of our interaction with them as well). I liked the food, for sure. But I liked them even more. The kind of business and people I definitely wish there were more of, and want to support with my own money and "dining vote" by going there as much as possible in the future. text: I'm usually too lazy and unmotivated to write reviews longer than a couple sentences, but I'll make an exception here.
