There were at least a few empty tables with half-full glasses and used napkins still on them which should have been the first clue that the restaurant was understaffed. We were offered an outside table in what appeared to be an alley where the Prince of Demons and his minions lived. No thanks. After being seated, we realized that the greeter was also the only waitress working that night. And the music? It was coming from a clock radio at the rear of the restaurant w the time blinking. WTF? I had to resist my OCD tendency to set the clock. We waited at least 10 minutes before the greeter/waitress returned to pour water into our glasses and offered to open our bottle of wine. By now, my friend and I had discussed leaving for another restaurant because we were both starved and presumed it would take hours, if not days for our food to come out. We were reassured that they were no longer seating new customers and that it wouldn't take too long for our food. After placing our order (two apps - dumplings, chicken nachos; two entrees - pork tacos, burger), she began to open our bottle of wine. We saw her struggling w it and then she came back to inform us that her corkscrew had probably broken and that she was still trying to open it. By now, the cork was at least a centimeter into the neck and appeared to have been mauled by cheetahs. She returned to inform us that her corkscrew was officially broken and asked whether she could filter our wine so that we did not drink the cork residue. Why yes, we responded, that would be quite nice. What a generous offer from the person who had just mangled the cork w a broken corkscrew. Fortunately, our (inexpensive) wine was salvaged. But why she poured the filtered wine into a metal pitcher intended for ice water was beyond me. The food was unremarkable, but not awful. No offer to somehow compensate us for destroying the cork, but that's alright because I'm letting everyone know what happened on Yelp. Shame on you, Paul. Here is an unsolicited, but short list of small steps you can take to improve: - At least set the correct time on your clock radio so it doesn't blink. - Provide your staff w corkscrews that work. - Update your lame website. As it is right now, it's an embarrassment to the World Wide Web. Otherwise, I wish you all the best keeping your restaurant in business during this recession.

text: I am excited to taste truly authentic, perfectly seasoned specialities of Middle Eastern foods. This is food representing the best that can be had. The humidity affects the amount of liquid, the strength of that days' lemon- all of these variables are so significant. In a hurry? You can't rush excellent. You can't whip up a great Hummus, and you can't re-trim the lamb in your shish kebab. The prep work is enormous and takes a long time to get right. This is very very high quality in a modest, clean and cheery setting. Oh, did I mention the rice? Believe me, families' reputation is built on something as simple ( to us) as how the rice is prepared. Fish, chicken, beef, and lamb on the menu- and outstanding vegetarian offerings too. text: I wouldn't waste your time dining here with all of the other great options in the Big Easy. Everything from the service to the food was lackluster and unimpressive. My boyfriend and I decided to dine here for his birthday dinner on our weekend trip in New Orleans, and this happened to be our last dinner in the city. We went out with I'm sorry to report not a "bang" but a "bust." We first arrived over 20 minutes before our reservation and were not seated until 15 minutes after, and frankly, they were not that busy at 8.45 that we should have been waiting that long. When we finally sat down we waited 10 minutes just to receive menu's. Our server literally greeted our table and said "happy birthday" to my boyfriend (I had told the host to let our server know we were celebrating) and then walked away and never brought us menus. We had to ask another server. We then decided we were both going to share an appetizer, salad, entree, and dessert. Our first course was angel hair with crawfish in a creole cream sauce. We waited close to 20 minutes for our appetizer to arrive and when it did, we both wished it had stayed in the kitchen. It was literally one small scoop of pasta that wasn't event cooked right ( it was all stuck together in one small blob, looked unappetizing and was in a a sauce that was utterly bland. We were so hungry by this point we just ate all 2 bites hoping the next few courses would redeem it. Our next course was a salad with scottish salmon, watermelon, frisee, ricotta salata in a chili lime vinaigrette. This dish was so bad I didn't eat it, I gave it to my boyfriend who was reduced to eating it without breathing saying all the while he felt he was in a tough man competition just trying to get it down. The salmon had a terrible texture and looked like it was out of a can and as my boyfriend put it, it looked like salmon cole slaw. Not something you would expect to see at a restaurant of this caliber. Then we shared the Pork Chop in the Tamarind and Mole sauce with sweet potatoes. The dish was huge! They split it for us in the kitchen and it still was massive! Th pork chop was cooked well although a little fatty and the sauce was very thick but tasted alright. The sweet potatoes were ehh. It's a pretty scary thought that after all this we still took the chance with dessert, but I am glad we did. The banana cream pie was delicious, and although not a saving grace for the terrible food that came before it, we were glad we finally had something tasty to eat. However, we were very disappointed that I had mentioned it was my boyfriends birthday and they didn't even put a candle in the pie, or offer us a complimentary dessert or anything. We have been to many other fine dining establishments that go that little extra mile to make you feel special and I feel that our server did not go out of his way to make our evening memorable. A handshake and "happy birthday" just doesn't cut it. We did have to wait an extremely long time for everything from being seated to receiving our menus, to waiting for the food and then waiting for the check way after we had finished our meal. Our server was busy chatting with some ladies who we assumed worked there and were dining on their night off. The highlights of the evening would have be my glass of wine was pretty good although overpriced at 13 a glass, and the busboy who took care of us throughout the evening was great! He was always there to mark our table, clear our plates and refill our water. However, I think its pretty pathetic that we went to a supposed excellent restaurant with a renowned chef and the best thing we can say about the whole experience was the busboy. Needless to say, we will not be back on our next visit to New Orleans.

text: "Dirty Country" Crusted meats: ok. Crusted cheeses: sure. Crusted placemats? Welcome to Carman's, where country and cleanliness are but two forks in a filthy wood. Cream for your coffee? Let it flow briskly from a breast-shaped pitcher complete with mother's crusting 'round the nip. Time to order? No need to commit to sweet or savory, because with lush fillings like goat cheese (or was it ricotta?) blended with cinnamon and red peppers, you get it all. Visual diversions while you wait? So many to choose from! Say, for example, the bold ceramic penis cup broken at the base, then reglued for - perhaps - another round at the rodeo. Or, the terrifying, tiny Venetian glitter mask, placed dead center on the main wall. In a horror movie its eye sockets would be threaded with fishing line, and like the blackest flesh-tearing raven, it would swoop toward you until your mouth wobbles open to a Sissy Spacek scream. BUT DON'T LOOK DOWN. Because your food has just arrived, and that's the scariest thing of all. In an homage to a post-Katrina world, it's an overweight mass of thick, tomato-strewn egg, submerged in bilge water. The extra water splashed up from the dish sink over the counter and onto your plate is entirely complementary. Feeling ill? Perhaps you'd like a moment alone, say in the bathroom. Or perhaps you'd prefer the kitchen. Good news - no need to choose! Because sanitary sakes alive, they're more or less the same room. Next time I want dirty country I'll skip Carman's and ... actually, I'm too much of a lady to tell.
label: NEG

text: I know, I know. It seems really weird to give Winners only 2 stars. Let me explain. I have loved winners since it opened up in Edmonton (or since I could shop.. whichever came first) and I have never had trouble finding things at Winners, but for the last 3 Christmas's and birthday's, I have received a Winners gift certificate, and I think this location is starting to loose some merit. My first issue-- this store is filthy. I have noticed that if my clothes drag on the floor while I am searching through racks, that they quickly become covered in a layer of dust and dirt. The other thing I have noticed is that when I get the the change room and put down my items, that my hands are black from holding the hangers. Yuck! Once a welcome addition to the area for Non Chain supporters. It's become more of a bar and less of fast casual dining. Hanley's Pie remains on the menu, good pizza. text: The most strange experience dining out I've had in years. We sat down at our table and then was informed that after waiting for our booth we had to go wait in a separate line to order our food. There were no waitresses at Famoso's, instead you go and order your food and pay, then someone brings you your pizza. You get your own forks and knifes and napkins. You pay everything upfront so you have to decide if you want desert before you order or if you want 2 or 3 beers with your meal. I guess you could keep running up and waiting in line to order them but I don't understand the system here at Famoso's. When our pizzas came they were okay I suppose. Thin crust like I expected but very wet & soggy. Everything was made fresh though so I can't complain about the taste, just getting it into your mouth is the hard part as it sags just below the crust. Also the place is very small and a lot of people are just kinda hanging around the place like its some club. They were waiting for take out pizza and for tables, and at one point I had a few people hanging around my booth actually leaning on my seat and his buddy was staring at me trying to get the soggy mess into my mouth. I don't understand why this place was so much money for a pizza if it's mostly just self serve. The personal pizzas range from $11-15, and for a bottle of beer you are looking at $5 domestic $6 imported.

text: A great place for people watching! Ok, our real reason for coming here was to find a matching rose for a desk pull, and we were close. There's a vendor under the main structure who sells door knobs, drawer pulls (metal, ceramic), antique keys...and what we found was really close. Most items are $1, so we scored with 2 rose pulls that are likely the closest match we could find. Towards the end of the structure is a woman with antique and old children's books such as more Oz adventures, Mother Goose, etc., but what caught my eye this time was "Fanny at Chez Panisse" for $5, a children's introduction to cooking book. :) Melamine rotary phones, a Springtime in Tokyo Barbie (I might kick myself for not picking this up as it was a 60's style Barbie made in 1999), a plant lady in front of Fast Eddies, lamps, books on Erotic massage, Nazi memorbilia, bayonet spears, Civil War portraits and coats, records, lace, silver and costume jewelry, dolls, coins, magazines, lighters, and stuff, lots of stuff. Including Rosie O'Donnell as Barbie's Friend (her special friend, I'm sure). We didn't see much that we needed (do you ever NEED anything from a flea market?), but also didn't have much room having found a woven bentwood rocking chair en route to the market (yeah!). If you go, wear shoes that can easily wander over rocks and gravel that can get dusty.

text: One thing I've learned growing up in Philadelphia: Sometimes, the best places for food (I'm *not* talking about fine dining, I'm talking about FOOD) can look like crap from the outside. The best Cheesesteaks I've had was from a place I can't remember (and has since closed down) from when I was a kid in Juniata, across the street from Acme. Anyway, this brings me to Jimmy's. It occupies a corner of a strip mall, and the only sign it has outside is a vinyl banner hooked up to the front. It would be VERY easy to miss. However, BBQ - good BBQ - Is something in short supply out in the Exton area. So, the family and I decided to give it a try. Simply put, this is the best BBQ I've had in a long time. The brisket was OK, a little on the drier side but still pull-apart tender. The pork BBQ is extremely good, as is the chicken. The Mac and Cheese is also the way its supposed to be, as are the BBQ beans. The inside is pretty minimal. They have a big screen TV and some picnic tables and chairs - To me, that's a good thing. Its a BBQ joint, and I get the feel, smell, and taste of one inside. Just be careful - If you like BBQ, you may find yourself over there every couple of weeks needing a fix... :)

I prefer to have my work done in one sitting and Anna worked straight through (5 hrs.) so I didn't have to come back. I can't comment on the other people who work there since I didn't really interact with them. But I can't say anyone went out of their way to be rude. I would definitely recommend this place.

text: When we arrived at SpringHill, the fella who'd been watching TV on a couch in the lounge (in like a polo and khakis?) popped over behind the front desk and spouted, "What's going on, man?" to my husband and me. Phil: "Uhm, I'm checking in?" The trouble was we were sharing a suite with my brother- and sister-in-law, but our flight had arrived first. Unfortunately, our names had not been added to the reservation, so technically we shouldn't have been let in. But the brothers do share the same last name. As we were explaining this, the very cavalier front-desk dude beckoned over a young woman in a suit, presumably someone with more authority and said to us, "Woah, now tell her what the deal is again." We explained again. But he interjected with, "HOW many people exactly do you have staying in there?" -- which had already been explained in our multiple re-tellings -- "Four." Scoff. "You realize it's a one bedroom?!" "But there's a pull-out couch. And it's 11pm and we're just here for tonight." And moreover, WHY do I have to explain myself to YOU -- FIVE times??! We then had to explain to the guy what we would do when the other couple arrived. (Let them in, of course.) Anyway this finally did lead to us getting room keys, which I realize is against policy and they told us this, and I appreciate the exception being made. But it was handled in the most unprofessional manner. Then, the room. There were food crumbs on the floor in the living room still. There was a HEAPING trash can, full of food waste and all manner of things under the sink. The beds are the sort that don't have fitted sheets. And as an FYI, the "suite" is more of a studio -- a partition separates the bedroom from the living room. Not impressed. Though the bathrooms were a nice size and had modern fixtures. The buffet breakfast was decent: Belgian waffle maker, hardboiled eggs, yogurt, fruit, pastries, biscuits, and sausage gravy. Some cereals and breads, OJ and pretty good coffee. I'm told the gym was small but pretty nice. And they do offer an airport shuttle, runs till 10:30, but they were nice enough to pick up our family a little later than that. At $100 a night, and not all :that: close to the airport, I think you can do much better.

text: What a disappointing experience. This week my husband "surprised" me with a 5 year anniversary trip to Rancho Oso. The draw was the opportunity to give our dog a lesson to herd sheep. We were very full of anticipation for that opportunity. When we first arrived at the Ranch, they directed us to a trailer that would be our accommodation. Now at $120 a night, you expect decent but not spectacular. When we opened the door to the trailer, I felt physically sick. I told my husband there was no way I would even sit on the sofa much less sleep in the bed - the place was disgusting and it was about 120 degrees inside. And if we could not get our money back, I would sleep in our vehicle for the night. When we explained our displeasure to the guard at the gate, he showed us a cabin that we could move into. The cabin is new and very nice and we were pleased that they were able to accommodate us. (Beware - most of their accommodations are trailers - not cabins - so be sure to ask exactly what you are getting. If you are okay with grungy accommodations, the trailer will suit your needs just fine. If you want a clean place with a decent bed, ask for a cabin.) After two nights there, I turned to my husband and said I could actually come back to this place (but only if we stayed in a cabin). It is beautiful country. But then today we had our "herding" experience with Adrian Lopez, and I knew I'd never return. Adrian was obnoxious and rude from the beginning. Mind you the lesson - if you could call it that - was all of about 10 minutes long - at a cost of $20. He took great pleasure in making you feel like an idiot because you didn't understand what he wanted you to do at the moment he told you to do it. He barked commands rather than talk you through what he wanted the dog to do. And when I didn't immediately do what he told me to do he hurled insults such as, "Do you understand English?" "You don't speak English do you?" "Do you know what your rear-end is? I told you to move your rear-end against the fence. You obviously don't know what your rear-end is." In between, he made some rude comments about women and "liberals". I would have walked out of the ring after his first round of nastiness but my dog was clearly enjoying the opportunity to herd. If you enjoy being continually ridiculed while you're trying to learn something new, take Adrian's "class". He's guaranteed to ruin your day. Otherwise, spend your money somewhere where they don't take your business for granted. I would never go back to Rancho Oso and I cannot recommend it.
label: NEG

text: Is it cliche to complain about how some auto mechanic ripped you off? This place pissed me off so bad that I will take it to the grave with me. Even sans the smug owner who talked about me in a hushed voice right in front of me, I feel like the level of ondescension I received from him when trying to ask about the 2200 dollars I paid him was only on par with the catch and release scam that seems all too common from reading other reviews. I took my car here to get it checked out as it was leaking oil. Upon inspection, I was told that I needed a new transmission for 2500 dollars. When I told him that I considered the car a loss and would rather not have work done to it, he informed me that I can pick up my broken car for 500 dollars as this was the cost of the mechanic having examined it. Now, the average cost of mechanic work is 80 dollars an hour. This insinuates that the mechanic had done roughly 6 hours of work on my car. 6 hours to remove a transmikssion from a car? Maybe he and 5 of his peers examined it for 15 minutes and rounded it up. But somehow I doubt it. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this place.
label: NEG

text: Room was filthy. Probably hadn't been stayed in for months. A thin layer of dust was everywhere. I called to have it re-cleaned while we were out... and returned to the tables/shelves being dusted and the comforter changed. The pillows still had dust on them. The windows for the view were so dirty you could not see out of them (wasn't expecting the poor maid to climb out on a ledge). Toiletries were quality, along with the linen (when cleaned). Good walking distance to all museums and restaurants.

text: We visited Enzo's last night based on the sterling reviews we read on line. I can't tell you how disappointed my family was. We arrived at 5pm last evening which was a Sunday. We were the first table seated. The waiter promptly took our order. We got the salad which was nothing out of the ordinary. In fact I have had better salads at the local diners. Then the four of us proceeded to wait one hour to be served our entrees. If the food was extraordinary or even good, it would have been worth the wait. But it was mediocre at best. My daughter opted for chicken piccata. It was rather tasteless but the chicken was tender. My husband, chicken with mushrooms which he described as Ok. My other daughter ordered the eggplant parmesan which tasted good with the first couple of bites but as she ate it, she liked it less and less. I had the same experience eating my chicken capri which was chicken with eggplant, capicola and cheese. As we ate our food, we liked it less and less. For me, there was an odd taste to the tomato sauce. I could not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

text: Put down your chips and cards, the Harrah Collection is a must see!!!! I too didn't see any Volvo's. But going there, I knew this museum was not about having every single car manufacture in their museum. Historically, Volvo was indeed an important element of the history of automobiles, but it wasn't just wasn't part of Bill Harrah's car collection at this time. I love the exhibit spaces with lots of adoration towards momentous personal transportation appearances, including Porsche, Ferrari, Dela Hayes, Mercedes, Ford and so many others. Cars were separated in a cute replicated town as eras, Vintage Early, Early, Pre-War (Art Deco), Post War, and 60s-70s. It seemed all do run and are impeccably maintained. There is some kind of way one can "adopt" a car and restore it as needed. I didn't inquire how that is done, but if you have some time with some handy ways to restore cars, give them a call.
label: POS

text: Aerial is one of those secret clubs that often gets forgotten. It is not a winter venue and is located on top of the big bang and consists of literally being on top of the roof with an open sky and a few couches....which makes it particularly a summer hotspot. To my knowledge, it was only open on Sunday nights and was so packed it was hard to get in. To get to the top floor, you have to enter into the Big Bang and ride the elevator up to the fourth floor. The only horrible thing about this place is the bathroom. There is one stall for women and one stall for men. If you really have to go, the chances are you are going to wait a loooonnnggg time. But other than that, is super fun. I have met a lot of really classy people there and always usually have ended up debating the law or some political matter--but hey, for me that is a good night :)

text: Roberts is located downtown by Hollywood Bar and Filmworks. Somehow I found this place and thank goodness I did. If you are a Herron student or an art student for the matter, it is important to know where this place is if you are taking a Photography class -great prices on photo paper and film (which is expensive). Kinda hard to find parking so expect that. Has other great stuff inside besides just cameras, film and paper -also printers, jewerly and more!

text: Catered office lunches are a lot like checking out new music. You borrow a disc, try it out with no commitment, see if you like it. If it's good, you rip that one and hit up itunes to find more tracks. If it's really good you say, "damn I gotta see that sh*t live!" Thus was my experience with Smile Cafe. They've delivered lunch to the office a couple of times. Tried a little bit of everything. Each time I'd say, "I gotta go check this place out." Any place that can deliver Pad See Ew and have it be delicious and not all stuck together despite being carried across town has to be pretty good. I was not disappointed. The Pad See Ew was even better at the restaurant, as one would expect, and the red curry was spicy and delicious, not to mention the place is a quaint hole-in-the-wall. Service was friendly and fast. Definitely glad I checked the place out for dinner. Smile Cafe is now my no-frills, go-to Thai place in town. And the gallery upstairs is cool.

text: I'm actually delighted that Capogiro is so pricey. Or rather, the part of me that cares about fitting into my clothes is delighted. Otherwise, I might be tempted to visit every day. The space is inviting, with plenty of seating and fun old family photos decorating the walls. It looks like there's an outdoor area as well? I have yet to adventure much beyond a vanilla chocolate flavor combo. It's just the right amount of creamy, sweet, nice to look at... why mess with success, right?
label: POS

text: I WANT to like this place. It has the great bones of an old hotel, it's beautiful inside and out, the desk service was always very helpful and friendly, and the rooms are comfortable, clean, and quaint. But the noise and location (downtown) are hard to overcome. They warn you about the noise, but the scope of the noise is hard to fathom. It's not just the loud club, which they do caution you about and I was fine with. Far worse was the racket the staff makes dragging stuff around the patio when closing and opening up (both occur in the very wee hours), the hipster crowd on the patio late, and the mysterious LOUD banging in the restaurant (I think). Location: Downtown Tucson is supposedly back on upswing, but is still desolate at night, with few dining options open past 8pm.

text: I had a wonderful time with my husband and sister-in-law while visiting SB. We all had massages. My massage therapist, Ava, was excellent. The women's changing area is small but meticulously maintained. A bonus is being able to use the sauna, shower and all the wonderful products, including salon blow dryer after the service. They do not rush you out and provide healthy drinks, teas and snacks. The waiting area for before & after treatment is small but it is a clever use of space with a waterfall and "massage huts". It was a pleasant way to unwind with family. We all really enjoyed it. My sister had the Ayurvedic warm oil massage while we enjoyed a deep tissue massage. We would love to go back next time we are in town. It is, however, pricey even for Santa Barbara.

It is my husbands fav place to eat now. We have been in about five times now and have nothing to complain about.

Dolmas was served warm, which was a nice suprise, but also had very good flavor. It's a good place for fairly fast middle eastern food.

text: Any visit to Rami's is sure to be a great experience. Rami, himself, is nothing short of a delight. Always courteous and thankful for your business. If you're female, he'll probably greet you with, "hello beautiful lady." And you'll smile because he's just so cute, with his accent and all. Moist isn't typically a desirable descriptive, it actually evokes gross-worthy thoughts, BUT when it comes to Rami's falafels, I wouldn't have them any other way. Where other falafel spots dry their chickpeas to the heavens, Rami's is right on. The falafels are the truck's claim to fame, but it's not what I go for. I prefer the chicken sandwich with hummus, feta, tabouli and hot sauce. It's not on the menu, but it's the way to go. Before you choose Greek Lady, give Rami's a try.

text: Love this Pub! There's such a cozy atmosphere and the food is really good! I find the Fish and Chips and the sweet potato fries to be my favorites!! The breakfast and brunch are also prepared just right. During the warmer months there's outdoor seating. My friends and I always get wonderful service.

text: I didn't think I liked peanut-butter milkshakes (sacrilege, I know) until visiting Natural Cafe with a friend last weekend, who vouched for the reliability of the place. A few nibbles of her portabello mushroom sandwich, coupled with the vast Natural Platter (feat. beans, rice, cornbread, cheddar cheese, and the list goes on...), had me hooked. Amid Santa Barbara's humdrum chain stores disguised in Spanish-style architecture, this was a true gem, with its airy atmosphere and high ceilings. With so many things to try on the menu, I'll have to make a return trip someday.

text: Generally speaking, I am a big fan of Whole Foods, but this visit left a sour taste in my mouth. So I wasn't too thrilled with my initial visit to Clay Terrace, but I figured if there would be any saving grace to that place, it would be the Whole Foods, right? Wrong. The set up of this store is pretty similar to any other Whole Foods. The selection, prices, etc... all of that was the same. Here are the things that bothered me: 1. Free samples- who doesn't love free samples? It would have been nice if they had toothpicks/utensils to eat them. And some of that stuff looked like it had been sitting there for hours. 2. Cashiers- generally speaking, I think this is where Whole Foods (and Trader Joes) really differentiates themselves from other grocery stores. As we approached the cash registers, 3 of them were open, but didn't have anyone working them. Evidently all of them were having a rousing conversation at the third person's station. When we finally managed to get the attention of one of them, we got down to business. After my wife had paid, the cashier handed her the receipt, but began takling to the bagger (who showed up after the fact) about an order she needed processed. My wife stood there, not sure if she needed to sign, or if she was all good. The bagger actually had to ask the cashier if we were good to go, to which she replied a hasty "oh, yeah." OVERALL- Whole Foods- you really let me down on this one. I didn't knock you too hard, but I don't think I'll be coming to this location anytime soon. Celebrity Rating- Sheryl Crow

text: I'm in shock as well kim d. I just don't get it. Have these reviewers never eaten quality BBQ before!?? This joint is Mediocre, AT BEST. Ordered from here (based on all the Hype) for our family get together this past Mother's Day. What. A. Disaster. First off, they screwed up our order. Unfortunately we didn't realize this until we were home and it was too late. We ordered two of the supposed "E-Z CARRY-OUT SPECIALS". Which meant we get 4 quarts of sides with our order. We ordered 2 quarts of beans, and 2 quarts of potato salad. Guess what we got? FOUR QUARTS OF SLAW! Not even CLOSE to correct. Our fault for not checking before leaving; their fault for simply not including what we ordered. Well, what we did get was shockingly bad for a place as overly Hyped as this. Brisket was dried out and bland. Totally tasteless. Worst meat of the order. I have cooked and carved hundreds of pounds of brisket at the NYC BBQ festival a few years back and it's a shame to call what we were served brisket. The chicken was marginally better. Not at all great, but simply passable. But still, far FAR short of what one would expect based on all the raving mad Hype this place has. Pulled pork was the the 'best', and I use that adjective loosely. Wasn't great by any means. It simply was the least offensive of the three meats we ordered, and I'll leave it at that. I love, eat and RESPECT great 'cue. I've eaten it all over America. I've eaten at most of the BBQ joints here in nYc (Daisy May's, Virgil's, RUB, Hill Country, et al.) and any one of them will DESTROY Pappy's Smokehouse. It's a shame...I was really hoping this place would be great, since I was venturing into what I thought was the BBQ heart of the country, if you will. There was one saving grace of my visit and that was the t-shirt I bought. It's really funny. BTW, as we were leaving with our order I took a few photos for this entry on Yelp. A guy who worked there was standing next to me by the door and asked if I was taking spy photos for a competing BBQ joint. I said no, I was just getting pics for my review on Yelp, and he replied "Oh...it better be a good one." Sorry dude...

text: My first review, and its a bad one. Trailhead Brewing Company, which will here on be referred to as THBC was great the first time I ate there about 6 years ago. December 2010??? Not so much. From the outside the place is appealing, its a brewery in a great building in quaint downtown St. Chuck. Going inside I was greated by a hostess dressed in a sweatshirt which if we were at the Flying J diner we would be on par. To keep up the truck stop experience, THBC was very smokey as well. We were eventually swept away into the room with the dated decor. Whats really cool about THBC is that this place has a dumbwaiter, what sucks is that we ended up with a dumb waiter. Our server had zero personality, and by his lack of enthusiasm of the eats at THBC we should have took the hint and went elsewhere, but we didn't and here's where my last two days went... After the server with the personality of a gray crayon acknowledged us I decided that since they had the greatest pumpkin beer 6 years ago, I would order their specialty seasonal beer which was the scotch ale. The description was something like golden brown ale, with a strong alcohol taste and maybe a smokey scotch after taste. Beer # 1, was a stout, hands down. Golden Brown does not = Black. Just to make sure it wasn't me, I ordered a 2nd beer after I finished #1... completely different beer which was more like their brown ale. I didn't complain because both beers were drinkable, but either my waiter, or bartender was a complete idiot when it came to serving up the suds. Food... I should have stopped at beer... for goodness sakes why didn't I just stop at beer? We place our orders, I ordered a salad and the bacon cheddar burger because the rest of the menu consisted of bland dishes all covered with BBQ sauce. The others at my table couldn't find anything enticing, so they all went with apps, and one other salad. Thats a total of 2 salads... remember this... I ordered a salad, and one other person did as well. Got it? When my burger arrived it was okay, nothing special, a little under cooked, but not that bad. The salad was tasty... maybe a little too tasty... Someone ordered wings which were way too spicy, and when we asked the gray crayon he said, "yeah they're really hot." Why the hell wouldn't you tell someone if the wings were that hot. They were nearly inedible. Most places have Hot, Medium, and Mild.. not THBC. The other person at the table liked their salad btw. Finally after wasting 84 bucks on apps, and sub par micro brew (compared to Schafly, BLVD, and others in MO THBC shouldn't be considered a good brew) we went home. Hours later, I thought I was dying, or just got back from drinking a toilet full of water in Mexico. All the symptoms of food born illness without going into too much detail. I was laid up for an entire day. FYI, I ate the salad... the other person who ate theirs, had the same thing as well, and they were down for the count for almost 48 hours. If you want a lamo waiter, a glass of Mr. Beer brew, and food poisoning go here, otherwise keep walking by.

text: The first time that I went to SLeeK some of my friends and I stumbled in there because we were bored one Friday night and decided to check out the new casino in town. We came up SLeeK and from looking at it from the outside the place looked rather cool. The design was reminiscent of the 1950's and early 60's with woodwork for the wall and clean flowing lines shaping up the restaurant. Since we were not ordering food that night we sat ourselves down at the bar and had our drinks. They were nice and the bartender knew how to make our drinks with no problem. That night the crowd was rather thin as the place had just opened and they had yet to advertise their existence to the world, so we drank and talked in relative comfort while easily ordering a couple of drinks from the bar. The next time I was at SLeeK I actually at a meal there. Being a steak place I had just that. The steak was wonderful and everything came out perfecting. They actually knew when we had finished our appetizers because each table has a camera above in order for the cooks to know when they should start to prepare the next dish so it is not sitting under a heat lamp. I really like that aspect, even though it is a little like Big Brother watching. SLeeK is a nice place to go for a drink.

text: The best possible way for me to metaphor Silk City, is to say it's akin to a lover you're not right for. Things start out great but progressively decline as your lovers nature and nuances wear on you. It's tolerated because there's a reservoir of goodwill from which to draw. But slowly that deteriorates and you decide the relationship needs "a break." Well, within that break you date around and start to remember about some of the good times you had with your former flame. You think to yourself..."maybe they've changed..." but when you go back to them it's the same old story. Last night we ventured back to our old stomping grounds to be met with a higher cover. ( $6 for guys ) They also now have a cover on Thursdays which was never the case. This is blasphemy imo due to the fact that local similar venues 700 club, PYT, Lucy's all with similar drink specials and music ( well i'll get to that) have no cover on either night...the nerve. That being said, I plunked down my six dollars and entered anything you can shake your hips to. I WAS actually enjoying myself given the scenic eye candy and the passable music. My buzz was extinguished when out of the blue DJ DeeJay decided to come on to the mic and announce that for the final 45 minutes he would be commemorating John Lennon for the rest of the night. Boredom ensued and I was no longer interested in shaking my hips. Apparently I wasn't the only one who felt the betrayal, as people awkwardly attempted to adjust to the remixed music not originally made for hip shaking, and eventually had downsized to about half capacity with 15 minutes to go. DJing is not about implementing your own personal agenda into your music repertoire, rather giving the paying patrons what they want, and not playing interminable dross. Once again cut deep, I'm breaking it off...
label: NEG

text: The high prices here are a major turnoff. The regulars must be making a good chunk of change in town. Their small sandwiches don't fill me up, so I have to go for a large sandwich (18"), which will run you around $13. Having Baguette Deli in town now makes me ponder sandwich scenarios like this: Baguette Deli's footlong house special (which can fill me up): $3.25 Cobby's 18-inch sub with a couple small bags of chips and a small piece of fruit: $13+ Basically I would need to grab at least 20 bags of chips for me to feel like I got equal value. The thought of me speedwalking out of Cobby's with 20 bags of chips (with a friend hopefully flanking me for security) is amusing but unrealistic. But I do wonder what happens when someone grabs what could be construed as an excessive amount. The sandwich quality is not bad beyond any stretch of the imagination, but I've never said to myself "This is a really good sandwich" either. And you think you would get more than what you actually get given the price. I tried the clam chowder once, and I won't be trying it again. The customer service is quite good though. Even when the line is huge and things are hectic, the servers stay friendly and pleasant. I'm not sure I get the popularity either other than supporting a local establishment with friendly employees, but better Cobby's than the chain sandwich shops. Just be prepared for a significantly bigger hit in your wallet.

So for a number of years I have also been a model helping out my friend teach her classes. While sitting there over and over again, I have learned a lot about hair, texture, color, wave, face shape, and how to hold the shears properly. Needless to say, my standards were set very high when I came out here, and had to find the perfect place. I used to have blonde hair down to the middle of my back, but finally cut it all off and went back to my natural color, dark. I had gone to three other salons and I always came out either looking like a man, or Florence Henderson, not good! I was drawn to Rocket Science because of the great reviews and cool name. I even wanted it shorter a few days later, and she had no problem with my request. Dara has by far surpassed any expectations I had as a stylists and her training and experience shows in her work. The trust was build up enough for me to have her do my eyebrows too, perfect once again. I can honestly say, the girls at Rocket Science are excellent at their craft! text: Isaac and I went to Mels for date night last week...Yes, we still have date night...let it go. I was excited (for many reasons, but that's for a different kind of site). Anyway, it had been several years since my last trek over the river and up the hill. I remember Mels being a gaudy, grease ball hangout. You know...guys who watch The Godfather, Donnie Brasco, or Scarface EVERY NIGHT! To my surprise when we walked in the place was looking kind of good. It is now furnished in what I would call contemporary style. Although, they do still have the mirror wall, reminiscent of a South Philly row home whose owner wants to make the living room seem expansive (or should that be expensive, either way). As soon as we sat down an older gentleman, pinky ring and all, approached the table. He was a nice guy, but really pushy. The type of server that wants to sell you the overpriced specials, the bottle of wine, the add-on lobster tail. Anything to increase the check, in hope of increasing the tip. We did end up ordering a bottle of wine, for fear that if we hadn't we might end up "sleepin' wit the fishes". Seriously, Mels has a fairly decent wine list. They carry a nice variety...Actually, they advertise a nice variety, whether or not the bottle is in house, well that is a different story. We struck out on our first two bottles, but we hit a home run on our third choice. It was a nice Argentinian Melbec. The price was just right, only $27!!! The prices on the bottles of wine might be the best thing Mels has going, very reasonable. However, what you save on the bottle they make up in glass pours. It took me forever to decide what I wanted, it just one of those night, where nothing sounded good. I didn't get the stuffed chicken special that the server was force feeding me. I settled on chicken Italiano. Not much to say, it was completely bland. Isaac had shrimp scampi...again not much to say. I commented about how bland and flavorless everything was, and then I looked around the room putting two and two together...it looked like a night trip out for the Sunny-Dale Geriatric Ward. Seems to me like they have that demographic nailed. At the end of the night, I would have rather have spent my money on another bottle or two of wine.

You must come here during strawberry season, because they have the most amazing strawberry shortcake and milkshakes. AMAZING. They also have some kind of strawberry girl pageant and there's a giant strawberry you can sit inside and take your own photo. Out back they sell plants, other fruits and a few knick-knacks. Worth the stop! I even noticed on their website that Barack Obama made a stop here when he was campaigning.

text: Wasabi used to be the only spot for sushi for me but for some reason this past year they have been disappointing me. It started on New Years, where I usually order a tray or two and just chill out at home instead of doing the whole 'party' thing, but for the first time in three years the sushi just wasn't up to par. It was lacking the usual freshness and flavor I had come to know from Wasabi and in general was quite dry. I also think they forgot to put a few dozen pieces in there but by the time I was preparing the servings the place was already closed for the evening. I did lunch there a few times since and still wasn't leaving feeling satisfied with the food and especially the service. I'm beginning to wonder if they've gotten new owners, chefs, or something. I know it's just a corner Sushi spot, but I feel as if it is going downhill. I did take out from their South Street location once and although it was quite good the place quickly changed names so I was assuming it had tanked. Now they're moving to the old taco house location just east on Pine Street so I'm wondering if a fresh start is something they need. I am going to miss the cute set up with the bamboo curtains, though. Even though they have been disappointing me as of late I would still recommend the place to someone looking for a quaint little Japanese spot without the trendy crowd or prices.

text: We came to Mesa for lunch on a rainy day while on a visit to SB. We had our doggie (chocolab) with us and heard this place was dog friendly in the patio. It really was! It was HUGE, and pretty good, except for me there was too much cheese. Which is unusual because i LOVE cheese! The cheese was a little overpowering. Also the avocado comes on top, not in the omelet so be aware of that. My boyfriend had the chicken fried steak and that was also HUGE. He liked it a lot but couldn't eat it all (which is unusual, because he can eat a LOT). He asked for hashbrowns as his side but they accidentally brought out homefries. He said it was fine, but they insisted on giving him an extra order of hashbrowns for free anyway! Awesome! The service is great, friendly and attentive. No attitude or rushing us, even though they were busy. It was a very nice experience overall with hearty food and a nice atmosphere. text: I have a major axe to grind with said establishment and how poorly they handled a snafu from way back when. (If only Yelp had existed back in the day!) It was a typically crowded Saturday night, and parking was of course at a premium. So instead of circling around for parking for 30 minutes, I caved and decided to hand my keys over to the valet. Fast-forward to the end of our meal, where our waiter told us to give him my claim check when we were ready to settle the bill so he could give the valet a heads up to bring our car around. We did so, which would have worked fine, except for the fact that it took a good 20 minutes for our waiter to bring my credit card back so I could sign the bill and leave. This triggered a most frustrating chain of events. Under the assumption that we would be out in a few minutes, the valet brought my car around in a timely manner, but when I didn't show up soon after (because the waiter was moving at a snail's pace), he left my car in the middle of the dark street with the keys in the ignition and the driver's door partially open. WOW - you might as well have put a sign on it that said, "Please steal me." Knowing how New Orleans is, I'm frankly shocked that the car didn't get stolen. But it gets worse: not only was my car abandoned and ready to be stolen at any time, but it was also blocking traffic (darn narrow Warehouse District streets), so I got a parking ticket. As I'm finally leaving the restaurant, someone outside informed me of what just happened with my car, and of course, I'm furious. (I was a broke college student at the time, so a parking ticket was certainly not a welcome added expense for the evening's activities.) The brilliant valet who ditched my car resurfaced and made excuses for why he left it. I soon realized that I was going to have to escalate the matter to management to get any sort of resolution and was irritated enough, so decided to go home, regroup and try to get this resolved the next day. I first started with calling the restaurant, who so adroitly played the blame game and said that it's not their fault (even though it was their waiter who delayed me getting out the door) and that the valets are from another company that I would have to contact. I then reached out to the valet company, who pretty much said they couldn't do anything about what happened. Nice. As a last resort, I tried contesting the parking ticket with the city of New Orleans (It's all about the principle of the situation!), which, in their infinite wisdom, they rejected my claim. Being the tenacious one, I decided to go back to square one and approach the restaurant again, but in person this time. I showed up during a quiet afternoon and politely asked to speak to the manager. He showed up soon after, and listened as I calmly explained what happened. After I finished my story, I was appalled by how he responded, talking to me as if he were calming an upset child and using such platitudes as "oh baby" and " sweetie, I'm so sorry." I did not appreciate being talked down to like that, and that was the last straw. (As Ms. Janet says, "No, my name ain't baby!") The smarmy manager said that he would refund my money once I mailed in the documentation, but after being talked to in such a manner, I was done. At that point, I was happy to take a financial hit from the parking ticket just so I wouldn't have to deal with that awful manager again. And, this incident aside, your sushi ain't all that.
label: NEG

text: I have been craving a (vegetarian) muffuletta from Central Grocery for weeks now, and every time I've tried to go I've failed to obtain one. First of all, they're only open 5 days a week, from 9-5, so you have to make sure you show up when they're actually open. Then, I realized they observe the New Orleans Sabbath (i.e. they're closed on Monday), and are not in fact open Monday-Friday during business hours but rather Tuesday-Saturday. Fair enough. (But the limited hours are the reason I'm not giving them 5 stars. Just sayin'). The one time I actually showed up at Central Grocery on a day they were open, I wondered why there wasn't a line out the door. Optimistic, I went inside to *finally* satisfy my craving. Unfortunately for me, they'd run out of bread, so once again I left disappointed. (Pro tip: Don't show up at 4:30 in the afternoon and expect to get a muffuletta.) If it were up to me, Central Grocery would be open 24 hours, 7 days a week, or at the very least they'd be open past 5 o'clock and perhaps (gasp!) have a website. In an ideal world, I could go to their website right now and have a muffuletta delivered. Even having it mailed to me would be awesome. (They do ship, by the way, so you can send one to friends and family who are out of town. I recommend doing this if you want them to love you.)

text: I had (have) a small chip in my windshield, so I called AOK to see if they could repair it. They said no problem - $50 and you're set. So I take it in and they say it'll take about 2 hours. I finally get a call after sitting in Dunkin Donuts for 3 hours, so I walked back. The guy said he wasn't charging me because it "leaked" a little. Not only was the chip still visible, but there were permanent streaks on both sides of it. He made it worse than it was when I brought it in. So I thought whatever, I'll try to get it fixed somewhere else. I go to another glass repair shop right after and he says they can't repair it because once you try to repair a chip and it's done wrong, it's over. PLUS he said it will almost definitely not pass inspection now - you need a new windshield. So not only did they make the chip worse and not repairable, but now I have no choice but to buy a new windshield just to legally drive my car. $50 turned into $300 and a big headache because I chose the wrong shop. I went back to AOK right after and asked the owner what they can do about since they basically ruined my windshield. They said they can give me the $50 off a new windshield if I buy it from them. text: Hey Smoke'n Dudes you have finally hit the yelp scene! I have been noticing your very colorful and highly decorated vans driving around for years! I adore barbecue, one of my very favorite comfort foods and hubby has been dieing to check you out., so he downloaded a buy one entree, get one entree free from your website and off we went. I understand that it was around 3:00pm, but almost one half hour for take out when we were the only order was a bit much. Hubby noticed they kept inserting a meat thermometer into his stuffed pork loin and you giving it more time. That is cool, get it to the right temp, but it was your daily special and you open at 11:00am! His other entree for tomorrow night is the half smoked rotisserie chicken and between the two meals for his sides he chose mashed red skinned potatoes that were quite tasty, baked beans that could have came from a can, they were very thin and nothing wonderful, canned corn and a corn muffin that was good. I had to snag a bite of the chicken to yelp about of course and I liked the smoky flavor and it was very moist. His pork was not cooked and it was on the tough side. For my entree I had the House Sampler of two ribs ( you gave me four, thank you), BBQ pulled pork, BBQ beef brisket and my sides were mac & cheese and red skin potato salad I love when I pick up my ribs and they fall apart, this did not happen and could not happen because they should have cooked a lot longer than they did. The meat was flavorful enough but fatty. They were meaty so there is potential in them. Certainly not the best I have had. The pulled pork was good and the brisket was uneventful. Check out Tommy DeNic's the next time you are at the Terminal and ask him for a few tips and bites. I just love his passion and watching him check the brisket and pass out free bites with so much pride. The mac and cheese is the same mac and cheese you can get at Popeye's, KFC or Cracker Barrel. I liked your potato salad but I had a real problem with how it was handled in your store. The gallon tub of potato salad was down to probably one fifth full at the most. Kathryn used her bare hands to pick out a plastic teaspoon, which she laid on the counter. She then put on one plastic glove which she used to stir the salad and to use as a scoop to fill the cup. This was cool, but then she took off the glove and used her bare hand to pick up the dirty teaspoon and threw it back into the container of the remaining potato salad, why? Why was it even in there? For tasting? I then made it a point to watch her and she is fidgety and I am picky! She reached under her shirt to scratch her back, swiped her nose a few times, scratched her head, answered the phone and used the register and then just dove into baskets of uncovered plastic ware to throw in my bag! The best part of this whole scene is I hate most potato salads I order out and yours was very good, very good indeed. I just wished that I had felt better about eating it. On a good note I had a half pint of some of the best chili I have ever eaten, with chunks of beef plus ground beef and I loved those chunks of green pepper, onions and tomatoes! The flavor was outstanding and I enjoyed each and every bite! Kudos to you on that. The rum raisin bread pudding that you won first place in the Pennsylvania State Championship has wonderful flavor, but I shall bake it more tomorrow because it was 70% uncooked raw dough. I understand that you cater pig roasts and have won state championship awards but you are prepared for those, your restaurant was not ready for us at 3pm and this is what we got. Folks you can dine in at one of their five red checkered clothed tables, call in ahead for take out or have it delivered and as mentioned they do have catering. I feel bad and I wanted to say 5 oinks and that I am stuffed like a pig, but this little piggy is crying wee wee wee all the way home. Oink... 2.5 oinks.

text: Who could have ever imagined that food served at this orange double-wide with hand-painted "Thai Food" signs (with the last few letters crammed on the plywood HA!) leaning up against the porch would be so delicious?? text: I have not eaten the dim sum but ate here for dinner. "Ban Kau" is one term to describe a sautéed fish. This is the Sautéed Fillet Grouper With Yellow Chives. $15.95. Hong Wan Zha Ji Gai - This is the Cantonese styled Crispy Fried Chicken. $9.00. Tong Yun Gai Lan Ngau Youk - This is the Sliced Beef with Chinese Vegetables. Approximately $10. Cheui Pei Zha Yeum Dau Fu - This is a fried tofu dish with broccoli doused in a brownish sauce. I think this is the Fried Crispy Stuffed Bean Curd. Approximately $10. Ju Yim Sin Yau - This is the Fried Crispy Squid with chili and spicy salt. Approximately $10. Some bowls of white rice. The Ju Yim Sin Yau was decent, the calamari had the right amount of crisp, doused with the right amount of salt, but I thought it kind of lacked some spice to it. Overall it was decently tasty. The Cantonese crispy chicken was also decent, most of the meat was kind of bony, but the chicken meat was decently tasty and the skin had some crisp to it but not much. The scallions made it tastier. The Beef with Chinese vegetables was pretty good despite the sauciness of the dish and it was served on a giant plate. They were really generous with the portions, one dish should be enough to feed 3-4 people. The beef strips were tasty and flavorful. The vegetables were freshly cooked just right and the Chinese broccoli had the right crisp to it. The fried tofu was also decently good, it was really crispy on the outside and very soft on the inside. Each piece was also reasonably sized. The brownish sauce made the tofu and the broccoli tastier. As for the Sautéed Fillet with Yellow Chives, it was probably the tastiest dish I had. The texture was really soft, and the chives brought more flavor to the fish, making it tastier. The restaurant was really quiet when we came, making the atmosphere relaxing despite the sounds from the plasma HDTVs. Overall, I had a solid and tasty dinner at this restaurant, and it has also changed my perceptions of Chinese food in Philadelphia somewhat. I would definitely come back for the Beef and Chinese Vegetables, and for the Sauteed Fillet Grouper with Yellow Chives.

text: Which is worse: a restaurant with terrible food and great service, or one with great food and terrible service? The former won't stay in business, so it's pretty harmless. The latter, however, will stick around for years to infuriate countless patrons. Why won't it close? People who have heard the promise of the cuisine will continue to seek out this establishment, assuming that the stories of poor service are overstated, or perhaps imagining that it's charming in a "Soup Nazi" sort of way. It will stay in business because nobody can quite comprehend how bad the service will be. Until they experience it. Again and again. And by the time they realize just how wretched and demoralizing each meal is, they've already contributed to the circle of life that keeps this restaurant afloat. This brings me to Siam in Lambertville. I will concede that it has some of the best Thai food around. However the service leaves more than a little to be desired. I will sum up my feelings about Siam with a couple examples of my experiences there over the years: 1. The Crying Vegetarian. Before I met my wife, I had a vegetarian girlfriend. She wasn't vegan, but she was veggie in a pretty serious way -- such that she would read all the product ingredients at the supermarket to make sure there wasn't a hint of anything meat-like (e.g. the picoliter of anchovy in a bottle of worcestershire sauce). We stopped into Siam on a sunny afternoon, and she was delighted to find one of the specials listed as "vegetarian". Halfway through eating it (nay, devouring it), she gave me a sour look that I knew couldn't be good news. She called over the waiter to inquire about the "vegetarian" status of her entree. Yes, of course it has fish sauce, explained the waiter rather matter-of-factly. But it's called a vegetarian dish! A vegetarian dish can't be made with fish sauce! So did this get an apology, perhaps an offer of at least a replacement meal, if not a free one? No, because it was HER fault, he explained: she didn't *explicitly* state that she wanted the vegetarian entree prepared without fish sauce. Cut to tearful girlfriend freaking out. Cut to my look of disbelief at what had just transpired. Cut to miserable, silent drive home from Lambertville. 2. Count the shrimp. Before we married, my wife and I went to Lambertville fairly often to visit friends who live there. On one such visit, somebody suggested that we hit Siam for dinner. Having put "the crying vegetarian" behind me, I went along with this plan. As luck would have it, three out of the four of us had Thai Basil Shrimp on the brain that evening. After the appetizers, out came the entrees... OK, out came two of the entrees. One Thai Basil Shrimp and one "other". Hmmm, that's funny, we ordered three Thai Basil Shrimp, not one. That IS three Thai Basil Shrimp, we were told -- all together on one plate. Now I'm all OK with family-style dining. But this was really ONE order of shrimp, maybe TWO if you stretch it, but no way was this THREE orders worth of shrimp. Of course our server insisted that it was, showing more than a little irritation with our gall to suggest otherwise. So the three of us began playing "count the shrimp" to make sure that we all got equally screwed by this miserly portion of food. Was it good? Of course it was, which makes it even more infuriating to watch the entire meal disappear in a matter of seconds. From the tab we split that night, you'd have thought we'd dined in style. But from the fact that both couples ended up ordering pizza later that night (no joke), I can't help but remember this as The Last Time I Will Ever Eat At Freakin' Siam!

Arriving, the first thing that I noticed is that It's got a neighborhood bar vibe going on. It was a Friday and they had a singer with an acoustic guitar singing 60s kind of music - nice. The place was smoky, but not of the tobacco kind. It was the kind of smoke you get from a great bbq pit - nice. The regular menu is printed on a heavy paper trifolded, not ostentatious at all, but the specials looked very good and not neighborhoody bar kinda food - both seafood risotto and pasta, duck or lobster salad - nice. But I knew something was not right when our server ask if we wanted drinks and when we hesitated, she was already gone before we could respond. And it went mostly down hill from there. The good: GREAT seafood pasta, VERY GOOD clam chowder (a few too many potatoes, but lots of flavor, it's the smoked salmon that they add to it), and a tasty manhattan (kind of peppery cinamonny flavor (like the "red hots" flavor (candy, not hot dog) you get in a really good Mexican horchata) - very nice. The bad: the service (they need one more server, or at least one server who would come over and pay attention for more than one minute), my steak (t-bone from the special menu, I ordered it because it came with fried potatoes, memory food from my mother's southern cooking, the steak was ordered medium rare and came out VERY rare, sent it back and it came out medium (better than rare), but also VERY salty), my friend's baked half-chicken (DRY and very old, with not very good mashed potatoes, come on, if you have risotto on the menu, you've got to be able to produce good mashed potatoes), and finally the service (again). The ugly: Also, they had a lot of children there when I was there. I don't particularly hate children, just the annoying ones, like when they kick on the door to the restroom when someone is in there (I know, it's the parents). From reading some of the other reviews, it's looks like they do somethings very well (is this a southern restaurant or a German one or a German southern hybrid?) - like spaetzle and schnitzel, and I would certainly recommend the pasta and the chowder. So, if you go, try those. Oh, and don't bother to try the caraway seed cole slaw either. Dry, tasteless, and ... oh so boring.

text: Perfect fried seafood Louisiana style Don't sleep on the drinks Front Street is rarely my first thought when planning a night out, and Catahoula is just far enough off the beaten South Street path that it seems off the radar. One look at the menu here and I figured I'd have to come back a few times. After eating, I knew for sure. The smaller eatery is all high tops, with two large televisions above the bar. It's a cozy feel, with big windows to let in the night and dimmed track lighting. Phoebe the bartender (more on that momentarily) mentioned that they're usually playing Pandora's Tom Waits Radio. There are a few great spots in Philly to grab a perfect cocktail, and Phoebe's drinks have definitely landed Catahoula on that list. Alongside the signature French 75's and Sazeracs, she offers a farmers market cocktail on Tuesdays. Recently it consisted of fig jam, bulleit and a few other magical ingredients that all added up to a sweet, bitter and savory drink I could have sipped on all night. She also obliged when I ordered 'something with rye,' creating the perfect post dinner cocktail. Don't sleep on the Sazerac too. It's just about perfect. So the drinks are deft and worth the price, but the food is solid too. Started out with a crawfish bisque which was smooth and spicy, followed by some oysters. There weren't any fancy frills, just oysters, a lemon wedge and a tangy green tabasco mignonette. The selection is different every day. I hate super salty oysters, which these were not. Ask if you don't know the lay of the seafloor. I followed with the catfish po-boy, not because it seemed 'safe' but because I wanted catfish and the big papa plate seemed a little much. The sandwich was perfect. There are few things more awful than seafood that's been ruined by breading and frying, but that wasn't the case here. The breading was fluffy and light, and uniformly thin all over, with no residual grease. The toasted bun and tomato were just sidekicks. The creole spiced fries didn't last long either! We finished with the roasted pear and crumb topping, of which a bite went uneaten between three of us because we were so packed from the rest of the fare. It's definitely a ride for me from Grad Hospital, but worth it. This is one of those places where I fully plan on eating my way through the entire menu sooner rather than later.

text: Here's the Deal... The Santa Barbara Bowl is the best outdoor venue to see a concert. Period. (that's why I put a period at the end) I've seen over thirty shows there, and it's not just the beauty of the place and the quality of the sound, but the fact that big acts that normally wouldn't play such a relatively small place love to come to Santa Barbara. In fact, they often say on stage that it is one their favorite places to play. The recent renovations, especially the bathrooms, and the gorgeous VIP deck make the Bowl a top-rate concert experience. Watching a full moon come up in the evening sky behind the Eagles, and looking around to see so many friends just fills you with a sense of well being and connectedness. The aforementioned VIP deck serves up a spread of delicious food; fruit, nuts, cheeses... and friendly bartenders offer up the drinks that lend to a California Cool... (but not TOO cool) atmosphere. Sometimes I miss standing in line at the ubiquitous porta-potties, smoking a cigarette, and talking to some cute blond in a tank top, listening to Steve Miller boom out fuzzily in the background... but not for long, The Bowl has grown up... and so have I. But we're both still rocking. Cheers, Bob

text: Having passed this place many times on (or under) the street I was blown away when I finally walked in and found the ultimate in intimate, European-vibed chillaxation. Copper-topped bar, esoteric old-world accoutrements, and more gourmet old-world beers and wines than you can sample in a lifetime. Throw in fondue of both the cheese and chocolate persuasions and everybody gets laid. Pros -Beers - they have small pours or big pours so you can try a bunch or just have a little or lot of one, and get your drink on however you like. We had the Unibroue nut brown which was delicious. -Vibe - there's a little Europe during the WWII resistance atmosphere, which is to say savvy, understated and strictly for those in the know. -Fondue - mostly a novelty act, but it felt appropriate and even cool here in the basement of Beneluxx. Not huge portions of it either, which is a good thing IMO. Cons -TV situation - you should come here anyway, and for reasons other than watching TV, but their TV (to the chagrin of our bartender) was stuck on whatever channel plays Friday Night Lights. Lame, in a word, made doubly lame when at the same time the Phils are rallying from a 7-1 deficit to beat the hated Reds of Cincinnati to win 9-2 in the 10th and I miss it.

text: Delassandros has had a change of ownership some time in 2009 and the steaks have gone WAY downhill, (not that they were anything special to begin with, just that now they've gone from mediocre to outright "I-can't-believe-I-just-paid-money-for-this!" bad.) The meat is extremely dry and they're now stingy on the cheese. The reason the meat is so dry and flavorless is twofold: 1) the cooks prepare a ton of meat in advance and then they let it sit in a huge pile on the side of the grill, and 2) they then chop the meat so fine that it's like tiny microscopic pieces of granular dried beef. The end result is that you have meat stripped of all the grease and fat and thus old and flavorless. As it stands, this place survives solely on its reputation that was established over a decade ago when it happened to earn a ranking in a Best Of Philly contest. Just about any corner deli in Philly will cook you a FRESH cheesesteak that is exponentially better than Delassandros. It's interesting to me that so many of the recent reviews are from people from out of the area. Many locals have stopped going here.

text: So ... I'm a New Yorker, recently visited Nashville, taken by old friend to Virago when we settled on wanting sushi. It's not the worst sushi I've ever had by far, & also not the best. I would give this place 3 or even 4 stars except for the fact that this was perhaps the very worst service I have received at any restaurant in my entire lifetime. And I am not exaggerating. The waitress (who looks somewhat like a young Meryl Streep) must be either new or just coming out of a coma. She suggested we get appetizers because we'd not ordered nearly enough for our main course. Wrong. The main courses we ordered were enough for at least FOUR adults (there were only 2 of us). Then (get this), the main courses arrive BEFORE the appetizers (which, in fact, were NEVER served ... waitress said they must've gotten accidentally taken to another table, wtf????). I got a bad feeling when I arrived about 15 min ahead of my friend & was seated & promptly IGNORED the entire time before my friend arrived ... no "can I get you something to drink?", nothing. Literally, I had to get up, go to the hostess & ask her to please send somebody to take my drink order ... and STILL it was several minutes of waiting. Then, as my friend & I are wrapping up our dinner, we glance over & see our waitress sitting at a nearby booth, patiently wrapping knives & forks in napkins even before we've finished our meal!! Um, check please???? (Any restaurant that takes service seriously does not have waiters wrapping silverware at a booth while diners are still present, good god, who doesn't know THAT?? Maybe at a diner that's acceptable, but not a serious restaurant.) Look, I know I'm from New York, where a place like this would go under in about 5 minutes w/ this kind of horrendous service. Yes, I get that it is important to "slow down" & be patient when visiting the South, & normally I LOVE that things there operate at a more relaxed pace... that is, in fact, part of its charm. But this place takes nightmare service to a whole new level. Plus, it seems to be a bit of a "scene," lots of loud, drunken, screaming girls at every other table. I felt like I was in some dive campus bar. Hope Meryl Streep's a better actor/singer/whatever than a waitress.

text: I have been a Toyota consumer for over ten years. I will continue to purchase Toyota's but I will never purchase or service any of my vehicles at this dealership. I initially came to this dealership because it was close to work. I should have gone elsewhere. This service department is the worst service department I have ever encountered. Service advisors have zero customer service skills - they are rude and dishonest. I came in for a safety inspection and they ended up fishing for a $1600 power steering rack repair. During my annual safety inspection they identified a "leak" in my truck's power steering and stated that a repair was needed in order to pass the safety inspection. This is a "leak" that I have had for three years! Leak is probably too strong of a word to identify this issue since I have only needed to add a couple of ounces of fluid throughout those last three years! There is absolutely no problem with the safe operation of my truck. It handles well and the steering displays zero signs of problems - it passes all 5 steering tests required by the state (Subchapter E 175.80). Two other independent shops that have inspected this truck have noticed this leak but they also recognize that it is extremely minimal and has no impact on the safe operation of the vehicle. Also, they understand the DOT criteria and know that this is not an issue for failing a safety inspection. Of course these independent shops have offered to replace the rack, but they never refused to pass me until I replaced it! Why does this truck pass elsewhere? Aside from honest practices, this issue is not listed as criteria for failing in PA DOT's inspection regulations. When I mentioned this to the service advisor, he said that he was told to fail any vehicle with any leak. Really? I only wish he was told to adhere to the regulations set forth by the DOT and not look for a way to land an unscrupulous and overpriced repair.

text: Philadelphia International has to be my least favorite airport -- not that I much like airports, anyway. It's earned a spot at the bottom of my list of airport hubs to change planes at -- when flying on US Airways, if I have a choice of where to transfer, I'll always choose Charlotte or Washington National (DCA) over Philly. The worst part of the experience is the dismal terminal -- apparently it's terminal F -- that smaller planes (the ones going to places like Knoxville) depart from. I'm don't think I'm being unreasonably picky. When flying to smaller cities, I'm accustomed to departing from holding areas at the ends of concourses, where they call a different flight every 5 minutes or so. Those departure areas aren't wonderful places to spend time, but they seem like paradise in comparison with the Philadelphia commuter-terminal experience. The commuter terminal always feels poorly lighted and dirty. Worse than that, there's nowhere to sit. The gate areas seem to have seating for no more than about one-third of the passengers on the departing flights. Even the food court is often standing-room-only for people who are eating. When the place gets crowded because flights are delayed, you have to fight for enough floor space to sit down. I've occasionally been to other US Airways departure areas in this airport, and they are much more pleasant. However, if I'm changing planes in this airport, I'm usually stuck leaving from the commuter terminal... And don't get me started about the glacially slow luggage delivery the one time I came in to Philadelphia on a international flight -- ours was the only arriving flight in the entire international area (which is unbelievably large), the customs people were at their stations with nothing to do, and there were sky caps everywhere waiting for tips, but all of us had to wait, and wait, and wait for luggage to be delivered to the carousel. (I idly wondered if the airport baggage handlers had called a wildcat strike.) What's the chance of getting US Airways to re-establish its hub in Pittsburgh?

text: I really wanted to like OTS. I've heard good things from people so I went there for dinner today for the first time with two girlfriends. I was really unimpressed. The ambiance was nice, with lots of flat screen TVs and loud music inside. We sat outside on the enclosed patio. There were several huge TVs outside too, but you couldn't see what was on them because it was light outside. Our bill was $25 for three burgers and a potato wedge appetizer (no drinks). First I was disappointed that our potato wedges didn't come out until after our burgers. I was starving when I got there and really wanted something to eat quickly. It took probably 20 minutes to get our burgers and another few for the wedges. I didn't think the potato wedges were good at all; they were really bland. I was expecting some seasoning or something but they were just fried and served with green onions and a bit of crumbled bleu cheese on top. My friend and I asked for our burgers well done and they came out very pink. By that time I was so hungry that I just ate it, but anywhere else I probably would have sent it back to be cooked longer. My friend's medium well burger was really really pink. I got the mushroom burger and the mushroom and swiss cheese topping was very good. It was served with a ranch sauce which was good but too runny, it slid straight off the burger. The burger was also really small. The menu said it was 1/3 pound, but it seemed much smaller. It was about half the size of the bun and I was still hungry after finishing it (which never happens; I eat like a bird). If you want waiter service this is one of the few places in IV you can go, and it's not terrible. I didn't have a bad experience, just was unimpressed. I'll probably try it again and hope it's better next time. It would probably be more fun on a weekend night to have a few (expensive) drinks with friends.
