text: An absolutely beautiful three story mansion where respectable ladies and gentlemen used to meet in the parlor before sitting down to dine on a fabulous meal and to share an eloquent dining experience. This Victorian mansion was built in 1895 and restoration began in 2000, Bella Tori, which means beautiful tower, opened it's door in 2005. This massive mansion has sixteen gables and four fireplaces! Entering from the wrap around porch, I felt naked without my parasol, corset and full long dress, as you immediately feel transported back in time it reminds you to be a lady and what it was like to relax, Gone With The Wind immediately came to mind. I pictured proper gentlemen smoking cigars and drinking brandy from snifters in the library while women gossiped and sipped tea in the parlor. From the high vaulted ceilings, to the beautiful molding, heavy drapes which are pulled back to view the very large and long framed windows, sconces hang on the walls and beautiful fireplaces are ready to light for that romantic dinner for two. The plush carpets and stairways stay true to maintaining the original era of the mansion. We dined here for Easter brunch and had to change our reservation time They were fully booked for the hour that we chose to dine and we were asked if we minded sitting on the deck, it was a gorgeous sunny day and even though I need to experience the ambiance of dining in the library or the beautiful master bedroom, we decided this would be delightful and away from all the hustle and bustle that dining out today brings. There were only four tables with umbrellas to shelter out the sun and we had our pick of three as there was only one other couple there when we arrived. My own problem with this delightful setting was the omelet station was set up there and soon the traffic in and out the door began as the lines formed. It is unbelievable how folks will stand and glare at you and what you are eating, glaring back let them know they needed to revert their attention. Hubby and I both noticed how the eggs were not cracked to make the omelets and how the ingredients were not kept chilled or on ice. The dessert station was set up inside the deck doors and the chocolate was melting and when trying to slice a piece of cake it stuck to the spatula. There was no where to set your plate down so this all had to be done with one hand which turned your slice into a mess and left half in a glob sticking to the spatula. The large antipasto table held a spring leek and potato soup which was okay, I'm hoping it was the potatoes which made it the wonderful consistency it was because I detected a flour taste to the soup. The Caesar salad was crisp and the dressing was perfect. The table had a variety of cheeses, brie, camembert, bleu's, cheddars and pepper, the smoked whole whitefish was wonderful and I could have eaten the entire fish myself. Cold dressed noodles, a roasted vegetable salad was so good, cherry wood house smoked salmon which will bring me back to have more, fresh fruits, jumbo poached shrimp and Joanna crab claws. This is the first time I have had these crab claws which were fully cleaned of the outer shell and ready to eat and hubby and I are still talking about how awesome they were. This same table also had a nice assortment of homemade salads, bagels, crackers and muffins. Fresh carved pit ham and slow roasted stuffed leg of lamb, which was medium to medium well at best, was being served along with the omelets on deck. Inside the buffet tables held a multitude of chaffing dishes filled with delightful foods, braised short ribs which were very meaty, tender and moist, broiled New England cod soaking in a milk broth was tender and delicious, thick sliced bacon, sausage patties and turkey bacon. To accompany these meats and fish they had pasta with a marinara and homemade meatballs, thinly sliced potatoes layered thick which tasted like an amazing cross between an au gratin and scalloped potato dish, ginger glazed baby carrots, homemade cheese blintzes with homemade strawberry preserves which were beyond heaven and oh Bella, Bella, the eggs Bella will stay etched in my memory forever. Beautifully poached eggs served on a thin sliced Canadian bacon and a homemade hash brown patty makes me wish that you were open for breakfast everyday. They do not skimp on anything, detail is their middle name. I can not wait to return for a relaxing sit down dinner. Be sure to tour this gorgeous mansion, any employee is eager to answer questions. They are open Tuesday through Sunday for dinner from 5:00 until 9:00 and brunch on Sundays from 11:00 until 2:00. It's an affordable luxury!

text: No, it's not swank and luxurious accomodation, but at $40.00 per night on weekdays (depends on when you go, and can be less with special deals in the mail when you join their OneClub) it doesn't need to be. Oh, and then I won $40 from said nickel machine and even got carded (I'm way beyond 21, trust me), so I had a good day at the casino. Results may vary. They have a bit of everything and even some low minimums like the $0.50 chips/$2.00 roulette. The circus acts and the midway are fun! You are never too old to be mesmerized at some of the crazy stuff people are capable of doing while balancing stuff on their heads. Of course, this does mean that you will see children. If you don't like them, go back to the casino part and have another free drink while you win/lose some more money, and then it will be like they were never there. Circus Circus lets you do a late check out so that if you have a flight out at like 8 or 9 at night (so that you can have another full day of fun before returning to your boring normal life), you can do a late check out. I don't remember the cost, but it seemed very fair at the time and was nice to still have a "home base" in between buffets. **Update Feb 2007** We opted for the until 4PM for another $20 because it got stupid any later - something like $60?! Speaking of buffets, the Courtyard Buffet inside Circus Circus isn't all that great, but it's not as horrible as I've seen some reviews in other places say. I didn't get sick, some of it was pretty good, some things I was glad to skip. Kind of like a lot of average buffets. **Update Feb 2007** Nope, not again. Not good. Still didn't get sick, but it might have been a relief just to be able to start over somewhere else. The Steakhouse has a $11.99 prime rib dinner weeknights from 5:00PM-6:00PM (was $9.99 in Feb 2006, but has gone up by Feb 2007 trip), so you know where I was during those hours. It was pretty good. Beware the Lobster Bisque - waiter came by and casually asked if we wanted any soup/salad with our meals, and when he said the soup was lobster bisque, we thought that sounded just wonderful. And it was! Very creamy, delicious and perfect in every way. But we had no idea it would be $9/bowl. Suddenly our $20 prime rib dinner for two turned into more like $40 (but the bisque is still in my memory - so good). If you want to rent a car to drive up to Tahoe, Dollar Rent a Car has a desk right inside of Circus Circus. The selection isn't quite as good as at the airport, especially if you decide to change reservation from compact car to SUV since it just occurred to you that it's winter and that you'll be driving uphill, but in that case, you can just take the free shuttle to the airport to rent whatever you want from there. The free shuttle was in desperate need of new shocks, but it got us to and from for free, so no complaints. I'm not quite sure about the schedule in terms of as stated every 30 minutes vs. when it actually comes, but again, free. And we never really had to wait terribly long. **Feb 2007 Update** I think they retired the shockless van because to and from were better vehicles with nice drivers. And so, we have planned another trip and did not hesitate to choose a Sky Tower room at Circus Circus again. (Still true looking toward a 2008 trip - won my heart twice).

text: I'm not telling you anything new by telling you that Whole Foods is expensive -- very expensive for most items. For example, I personally like to examine prices on regular skinless chicken breast when comparing supermarkets. At this Whole Foods location it goes for $6.99 per pound. Please begin your rant now on: A). Organic B). Locally grown C). Free range D). Growth hormones E). All of the above Finished? Now I'll proceed. Are you kidding me... $6.99 per pound for fucking chicken breast?!? Is this a joke? Or just simply white guilt? I mean, seriously, Wawa and 7-Eleven are cheaper than this store. That being stated, I do agree that quality costs more, and Whole Foods does provide quality products. Quality products and selective price gouging. You can find deals though. Their generic brand, 365 Organic, is comparably priced to other supermarkets. And their staff is generally young, vibrant, and friendly. Additionally, if you like your skinny jeans and ironic mustaches co-mingled with stuffy executive-level refinement, you'll find your fair share here. In all seriousness though, I do appreciate a clean supermarket and an attention to presentation. Whole Foods excels in these qualities. You like cheese? They have a fantastic cheese selection for a grocery store (but you'll pay $$$ for it). The prepared foods (also $$$) are excellent. If I was a squirrel, I would break into this store to feast upon the various assortment of nuts, grains, and all salt of the earth. And the produce section, it's a veggie lover's wet dream. In conclusion, if/when I become sustainably flushed with cash from a renewable source, I will come here every week. Until then, I will continue to only selectively shop at Whole Foods.

And if your main ingredient in your cheese dishes isn't allowed to be called cheese, I don't think you should be allowed to be called an Italian restaurant. And you can't call a dish Chicken Parmesan if there's no Parmesan in it. Aside from just the issue of cheese, the overall quality just didn't seem to be there. The Pasta Con Broccoli that I ordered was just plain bland. In fact the provel based cream sauce tasted almost exactly like the Alfredo sauce from Chicago Uno. The marinara on my wife's ravioli was also pretty sad. Now, when my Mom makes sauce, she takes an entire weekend. A pot simmers on the stove for three days and two nights. I learned from my mother that good Italian cooking is essentially simple, but requires quality ingredients and takes time. Concetta's marinara tasted remarkably like tomato sauce out of a can, with some herbs in it. I didn't hate the place, and if you live in the neighborhood, and it's convenient, it's not the worst place to eat, buy my experience was no better than I've had at Olive Garden.

text: I love Linvilla! I have to at least try and make it out once a year to an orchard and this year we wanted to stay local and tried Linvilla. What a great place! First we went to the food and had freshly made potato chips, which were so fresh and hot. The lines are long but they move pretty fast. We also saw tons of fancy caramel apples, funnel cake, apple cider, and more. Next, to the store for fresh apple doughnuts where we got half a dozen of them suckers. We also got a gallon of apple cider for $5. The store was a good size but everything and everyone seemed crammed in there. It didn't look like a good place for strollers, but people were still pushing them through. We stopped by the pumpkin barn but didn't end up getting one because they didn't seem like anything we couldn't get at the grocery store. I think they may have actually cost more there. We went back through the parking to the orchard and you can either pay $1.39 a pound or $25 if you fill this cardboard bucket them have. Not as cheap as the store but they are fresh and it's fun to pick your own! We picked about $18 worth after walking through the large orchard. It was really fun following their "map" to find the different varieties of apples and the further out into the orchard you get, the more quite/less busy it is. I had a great time here and appreciate the efficiency the staff moves at. Just remember it's a very crowded place so come with patience and you'll have a great time.

The saffron flavors were absent from the dish as well and there was a salty pool broth on the bottom of my dish (paella is not suppose to have broth, the seafood broth is suppose to be mixed with saffron and other spices and soaked up by the rice as the rice cooked). After my initial shock with the paella, i decided to try the beef wellington, the beef wellington looked delicious but that was about the only positive aspect to the dish. First of all, the foie gras pate that topped the steak was completely raw (for those who doesn't know what that is, essentially my dish had raw goose liver in it) and so was the pastry wrapping the steak. the steak in the middle was ok but it lacked character and flavor. imagine eating a flavorless piece of steak wrapped in raw dough and goose liver - not the best experience in the world. After tasting our horrible meals, we waited for the manager to drop by our table to check on us, after about 15 minutes of waiting, i decided to go ask for the manager myself. I found a server only to find out that there is NO MANAGER on duty and the most they could do for me is give me a comment card. I did not send the food back for fear of the cooks messing with my food (since there is no manager in charge) and the fact that I was already sick to my stomache for eating raw liver. After tip and tax, i spent about 110 dollars there and it was by far the worst 110 dollars i have ever spent on food. After further inquiry, I found that the owner made several racist comment towards Jose (the mastermind behind all of Criallos formerly wonderful dishes) and his family (something about how a mexican girl can't be a host and belong in the back of the kitchen when talking to Jose's daughter) then proceeded to fire the whole family. After the incident, the majority of the staff, including the manager at Criallos quit due to the new owner being rude and several inappropriately suggestive comments. text: If your out of town, reading yelp to find a good place to eat classic New Orleans (cajun food), come here instead of Acme. So you cant sample here, so I just got their most popular item, the Ferdi Special, which came with their house baked ham, roast beef, debri, and gravy (and I asked for extra gravy on the side - nods off to Adam Richmond). I also got the crawfish ettuffle since that was the only thing I did not get at the Acme Oyster House. OMG ettuffle is delicious. Not too salty, (which was a problem at Acme), it has a broth which probably has a ton of butter and flour (or some sort of thickener), the crawfish cooked delicately with the flavor of the sea from the crawfish influsing into the broth very distinctly. The crawfish was sweet, tender, and fell apart with minimal effort in your mouth. No tough overcooked crawfish here. The ettouffle comes served over white rice, which when you are paying $8.25 for a small cup seems kinda a cheap move. Why cant they give me a whole cup of ettoufle with a side of rice. There's also another meat, most likely a fish in it. Altogether, this is probably the best thing that I had in New Orleans so far. More than anything, this reminds me of a good thick clam chowder, except with crawfish instead of clams. The Ferdi Special was alright. The broth was kinda flavorless, and to be honest, the best part of the sandwich for me was the pickles and mustard, which was a good combination with the lightly salty meat and gravy. Correction, the best part is the free pepper oil on the side. It was absolutely awesome. Sweet, sour and spicy at the same time, I ended up killing my sandwich with it. Well the chicken and sausage.The jambalaya is a bit less salty than the jambalaya at Acme, it also has a bit more of a spicy kick to it. An interesting note is that the sausage here is sliced and the chicken is pulled. I feel that this is a bit better than the other way at Acme. The chicken stays tender and chewable, and the sausage (which naturally has more fat gives the jambalaya an additional component almost becoming a compliment to the dish rather than depending on the rice as a medium He jumbo however is better at Acme. The chicken in my jumbo is dry, and the jumbo just isn't as flavorful as the darker jumbo at Acme. There is also less meat in this jumbo. The soup is just thinner. It's not as salty or as spicy. Again, the sausage is sliced thick, but in this case, I like it better chopped up like at Acme. Overall, I would say that this place makes the Louisiana classics a lot better than Acme. So if you want good jambalaya, entouffe, or gumbo, come here. But dont get the Fergi special. its pretty overrated. sorry travel channel (and subsequently Man Vs Food)

It is clear that they either put it in a spicy brine or marinade prior to cooking, and it makes all the difference. As for the style of the fried chicken, it comes out crisp with a spicy wet finish on the outside. I got the 400 degrees level and it was hot, but not enough to make me sweat. As a matter of fact, I didn't take the first sip of my soda until I was done. Given that I am spicy freak, this should be plenty hot enough for mortals (for reference, I can eat the spiciest thing Prince's has without batting an eye, I frequently consider using pepper spray as a condiment). But all in all, damn good fried chicken. For sides, they have spicy crinkle fries (hit the spot), baked beans (the way they are supposed to be made), cole slaw and potato salad. As well, they have a couple of random things like a burger(?) and they have fresh cookies for dessert. Another nice perk about this joint is the people that run it are friendly - great customer service. So there is another way they have Prince's beat. Their hours are a little wonky,. 11AM-3PM M-F and 11AM-1AM Saturday. As well, they only take cash, so make sure you come prepared or you'll be washing dishes. My wait time was very reasonable, a little less than 20 minutes, and they recommend you call in your order in advance.

text: At long last, I finally took the plunge and tried the now Yelp-Infamous Hodaks. My friend has been going here for years and highly recommended the 1/2 Golden Chicken plate, so that's what I got. First let me say that the place was packed! We went around 2pm-ish and it was just wall to wall tables and people. The atmosphere could be described as a rustic Applebees. The walls are adorned with all manner of nostalgia inducing antique bric-a-brac. Service was great. Our waitress took our order promptly and kept our drinks full. And our food came out fast! I was surprised by just HOW fast considering the amount of food that came out. I had a wing, a breast, a thigh and a leg (duh, 1/2 a chicken!) a mountain of crinkle cut, oven-baked fries and vinegar based coleslaw. Everything was piping hot and was properly cooked. The fries were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. I tried a few bites of the coleslaw and it was ok, I guess.... which is an extremely positive remark considering I hate coleslaw. Of course the chicken was the star of the show! It was tender. Juicy, excellently prepared and had a rich, slow cooked chicken flavor. I will say that the breading was a little disappointing. It was more of a cornmeal/breadcrumb coating rather than more conventional flour batter. While the spicing was pretty good and added another level to the deliciously prepared chicken, the somewhat gritty texture left me yearning for Porter's flaky batter. Definitely not bad, but it seemed like a texture that would require getting used to. I also really enjoyed the flavor of the bbq sauce on the table, although it could have been nearly any kind of bbq sauce since it had been packaged into a blank, maroon squeeze bottle. A massive meal leaving me feeling weak and sickeningly full (a sure sign of an EXCELLENT meal!) all for $12 dollars including tip will have me coming back to try other items on the Hodak menu, despite my feelings about the breading.

text: You're in Philly. You want a cheesesteak. This place was near my hotel and rumor had it they have a $100.00 cheesesteak. Of course I had to swing by. By the time I ordered, I'd chickened out. The soup base was so velvety smooth, flavorful, with just a touch of heat (cayenne or Tabasco I guess). Oh Lord, I loved this soup. Then there was the lobster. It came out of the kitchen in a mini-tureen. OMG. The loveliness of keeping my steam in my bowl until it was in front of me. Let ME get the first whiffs of lobstery goodness. Wash it all down with a couple of dark & stormys, and life was good. Mmm. I wanted to return to this lovely spot. All warming and welcoming with the dark brown wood interior and single candles on each of the conversationally placed tables. Alas, the work people limited my restaurant choices. No worries. text: This place fell far short of good comfort food that you typically find in a quality family diner. The waitresses care about your experience and show they care quite a bit, however caring cannot make up for overcooked, poor quality food. I ordered the Meatloaf when I went there. What is more a measure of comfort food than meatloaf? It was overcooked and dry like a piece of burnt toast, and about as thick. It was about as tasty as salt and pepper and the run of the mill brown gravy could make it. I prefer ketchup with my meatloaf, but this came smothered in brown gravy. I'm confident that using ketchup or gravy would have made zero difference in the taste. No excuse for poor meatloaf. I had fried mushrooms and grilled zucchini as my included sides. The mushrooms were fried until they were slightly less hard than a walnut and the breading was standard; not home-cooking like at all. The grilled zucchini was so over-cooked, I would have guessed it was under a heat lamp for more than an hour or two. I had the bread pudding for dessert and it was standard stuff. Far from really great home cooking, but actually closer to a home recipe taste than many fine dining restaurants that I have had it. On the bright side, the portions were sizable and the price was very affordable. My bill for soup, salad, dinner, dessert, a roll, and an iced tea was just barely over $10, not including tip. All of this, except the drink, was included in the dinner price. A very fair bargain in terms of quantity. It's open 24 hours, so if you are starving and don't have a lot of money when other places in the area have long since closed, it's there and it's open. If you are looking for good home cooking food, you can probably skip this place. If cheap food, lots of it, and quality doesn't matter is what you want, then give it a try.

text: Totally shocked that this place exists in Southampton, PA. I am allowed to say that because I lived here for most of my life until I got married and moved away....hehe! This BYOB oozes with a city chic style. Mismatched tables, black and white high back leather chairs, low lighting and austere table settings give off a urban sophistication that most suburban establishments lack. The tantalizing aroma of Italian cuisine flows freely from the brightly lit open air kitchen. I am a connoisseur of vodka blush sauces and this place could be one of the best I have ever had! The pizzas look they should be on the cover of Food and Wine Magazine. text: The wildly varied responses to this place reflect one of two things: either people don't know what to expect from Texas BBQ, or the reviews are a result of a newly opened restaurant that's still working out its kinks. I didn't experience the kinks... nor, oddly enough, the BBQ. Because I don't eat meat (what?!). So what the hell kind o' business does a vegetarian have evaluating a BBQ joint? I walked away stuffed. So there. My boyfriend lived in west Texas for years, and was salivating when we saw the BBQ joint opening soon. I can make a meal out of side dishes, so I happily went along for the ride. They have vegan chili, which was tasty, and a baked mac & cheese that was quite delish as well (note: these, and the coleslaw are the only dishes that are truly vegetarian; the beans, mashed potatoes, german potato salad, collard greens are all made with meat and/or animal fat). Best part of the meal, though was the banana pudding (save room). BF had the pecan pie. mmmmmm. The atmosphere is inviting, and very well done--complete with movable walls that expand the restaurant when needed. The beer/wine/bourbon list is small but selective; the service was very attentive without being intrusive. I had a blast, and want to see this place succeed. text: This looks like a nice French bakery, but doesn't deliver on the promise at all. The unexpectedly grilled mozzarella and pesto sandwich was unbelievably greasy, and very light on *bread* for a bakery sandwich -- a sloppy, unappetizing disaster, even though the ingredients were all nice enough individually. (To be fair, the place's fresh bread, though pricey, is very good: they bake a nice, crusty, chewy loaf.) Rather than decorative art, the walls are covered with dozens of those weirdly passive-aggressive hand-painted signs that are proliferating around New Orleans, so everywhere you look is another pseudo-cheerful warning telling you to "be nice" (though the staff seem uninfluenced by that sign). At best this is an unsuccessful attempt to create a good neighborhood French bakery, at worst a tourist trap for locals; in any case, there are better bakeries elsewhere in uptown New Orleans -- like the great new Maple Street Patisserie, which is everything that the Boulangerie pretends to be.

text: I never made it inside the arch, but wanted to post a review anyway as a warning to would be visitors. My girlfriend and I were driving cross country and decided beforehand to make St. Louis a stop. We had heard that it could be a little rough there, and the rumor was seemingly confirmed when we arrived in town a little late and went to a bar next to our hotel. We were hungry and the bar didn't have any food, so we asked the bartender where we could get some grub. She looked us up and down then proceeded to tell us that she would not recommend two young girls walking the streets at night in the area we were in because of how bad it was and that her brother was a cop and hated the fact that she worked there. I told her we brought pepper spray and she said we should have it in hand, ready to go, at all times even in the daytime. Needless to say, she scared us half to death. This brings me to the arch. We had already purchased a ticket to go up to the top online. Standing in line for the security check I saw a sign that said no firearms, no knives, and also no pepper spray. When we got to the front I tried to give the security guard my pepper spray to hold on to until we got back down. He refused and told me I needed to remove the item from the park entirely. I never saw a sign when we entered the park saying that we weren't allowed to bring pepper spray into the park. We were holding up the line so we exited and tried to figure out what to do. Since we only had 10 minutes till our appointed tour time, we threw away the pepper spray in the garbage can and went back in line. Well I guess that was a totally bad idea. When we got to the front another security guy screamed at me from across the hall to get out of line, then proceeded to belittle me in front of the entire line of people saying that I was a danger to children, purposefully disobeyed the officers instructions, etc. Then they wrote me a ticket for "Disorderly Conduct" and "Creating a Hazardous Condition." I have never been more humiliated in all my life. I wasn't trying to break the law or endanger others. I was upfront about having the pepper spray and tried to give it to them so I wouldn't endanger people. Anyway, just wanted to give my fellow yelpers a heads up that they are really strict and inflexible about that stuff so beware. :(

text: Niche produce choices Every kind of oil you'll need Holy crap, live frogs! If you're looking for Cap'n Crunch or Honey Oat diet bars or some other major market fare, this probably isn't going to be your bag. If you're in the market for live frogs, fish, 10,000 kinds of noodles or a very very specific kind of spicy topping sold only in (insert country where you vacationed once and had an amazing sauce you've never seen again,) this is your spot. If you're a native English speaker with little to no knowledge of ingredients they don't use at Applebees, you're going to be lost here. Bring a friend, especially if you're trying to navigate noodles or produce. They have a huge selection of both, and most items you've probably never heard before (which would make two of us.) There is a whole aisle taken up with soy sauce, oil and other flavorings. If you're not careful it's easy to get lost trying to pick from among the chili-infused varieties. A word of caution: go to a mainstream grocery store if you want mainstream produce. Things like cucumbers, tomatoes, etc. can be hit or miss here because they're not as common in eastern fare. If you want fresh bok choy or other leafy veggies, this should be the first stop. The real draw here is the seafood. It's all fairly fresh, and some of it is still swimming. Feel free to order as much as you want, it's all fairly inexpensive. Last time here I got three salmon filets fresh off the fish for $10. They have all sorts of random seafood as well, including live frogs, crabs, and sea urchins. It's like Petco without all the cute kittens. There is also a selection of plates, bowls and cookwear to be had in case you're planning a full on dinner party and need just the right serving dishes. Again, it's all fairly inexpensive. The best part is the checkout, where if you bat your eyes nicely and smile a lot, they'll give you a free gift just because. I'm kidding, they give everyone a free gift. Usually crackers or some small pre packaged product. Look, I'll give you Superfresh for your run of the mill produce and everyday items. If you're looking to cook up something special or really need a random ingredient for which you've been scouring store after store, try Hung Vuong.

text: With a last name like mine, you'd probably never guess I'm Polish. But I am, on my mother's side. Thanks to my babcia and mamusia, I grew up on a steady diet of kielbasa, pierogies, golompki, borscht and bigos. So when my colleague told me about the New Wave Cafe, a Polish mom-and-pop joint in Port Richmond, I could hardly contain my excitement. "It was recommended by a friend of mine who knows his kielbasa," she said. After googling the place and reading a Philly Weekly review that deemed the food "like babcia used to make," I jumped at the chance to make the New Wave my first food group pick. As I drove into Port Richmond, I noted the Polish delis, bakeries and other family-owned businesses along the main drag, and I marveled at the Catholic church, which dwarfed them all. "This is gonna be great," I thought. "Some authentic Polish food in an authentic Polish restaurant in an authentic Polish neighborhood in Philadelphia." An unassuming little place on the corner of Alleghany, the New Wave resembles a bar more than a restaurant. Aside from the kitschy decor (which included neon wall paintings of various planets and a statue of an alien that appeared to be giving us the finger), I felt like I was in Poland as soon as I walked in. Four men sat at the bar chatting to the bartender in Polish, and a Polish newscast blared from the television in the corner. I was a bit concerned when I saw that there were only 3 or 4 tables that appeared to be for dining (drinking was obviously the primary purpose here), but my anxiety subsided as soon as I saw the authentic menu. We ordered some potato pancakes as an appetizer to share. I ordered the pierogies and borscht for my main course and some Polish beer (Okocim) to wash it all down. The Okocim was fabulous, no complaints there. But my disappointment set in as soon as I tasted the food. The potato pancakes had the right thickness and crispiness, but they needed more salt. I tried my friend's cucumber salad, which also needed more salt as well as some lemon and dill. My borscht was okay--for some reason it was lukewarm (there's nothing worse than lukewarm soup) and they forgot the sour cream. The pierogies were the most dissatisfying part of the meal. Granted, I shouldn't have ordered them fried (steamed is the traditional way), but there's really no excuse for how overdone and dry they were. Maybe that Philly Weekly review was outdated, or maybe it was just a bad night, I don't know. All I know is that our food wasn't fabulous. I appreciated the cultural experience and the opportunity to drink Polish beer, and I'd go back to Port Richmond for sure, but I'll be trying some other Polish mom-and-pop shops before I head back to the New Wave Cafe.

text: Preface: I've noticed some comparisons to Chipotle here. That's not completely off-base, as both places construct burritos assembly-line style. Beyond that, the two diverge. Though Chipotle is good for what it is, beside Freebirds it presents as a mass-produced, not-quite-as-good, unauthorized forgery of Freebirds. It's like the Starry Night poster in the UCSB Bookstore, while Freebirds is the original--and it is, having predated the Chipotle concept by almost a decade. The review: Freebirds solidly ranks as one of the west coast's elite burritos. Though it's easy to mistakenly dismiss as drunk food based on the core clientele, look a little deeper and you'll appreciate the unmatched quality of a Freebirds burrito. Let's start on the outside. The distinctive tortilla is so rich it's almost savory. Their tortillas are practically a meal unto themselves. And they're always grilled and flaky, yet still resilient- never gooey. Next: the meat. The most striking thing about all the meat at Freebirds is its astounding freshness, which is probably due in large part to their tremendous throughput- this place is busy 24-7, often with a line out the door, and no ingredient languishes more than a few minutes before it's served. At least one employee's full time job seems to be pulling meat off the grill and chopping it. The quality is also consistently high- no second-rate cuts here. Sauces and salsas are also above-average, but they're not Freebirds' greatest strength. A couple of things are worth noting, however: Guac will cost you about $1 extra (a little steep), but what you're paying for is freshly crushed, real avocados. Always important. And the flaky little grilled onions add some flavors that are unusual in burritos... I suggest trying them. Finally, the atmosphere: so lively, it could raise the dead. And the staff are always cool. All in all, an absolutely classic burrito, worthy of its reputation, and every penny you spent on it... even if prices have apparently climbed a bit in recent years.

text: My mother has a certain facial expression- my sister and I call it the "Tofu Face"- reserved for occasions involving bean curd. When she hears/says the word "tofu" (which she oddly calls 'taw-foo' with her Boston accent) her nostrils flare tightening her upper lip as her gaze ambiguously drifts. Thankfully when I bring her to Thoreau on mother's day weekend we can skip the unpleasantries. The menu here features exotic but recognizable vegetables. Some everyday ones too... but my point is that creative, eclectic and inspired dishes are highlighted. It offers entrees similar to, if not exactly matching, the parent restaurant (Blue Sage in Southampton) featuring kind and gracious servings that rarely contain 'weird ingredients'. I loved the Blue Plate, and often order the Cubano Supper as well. I have heard rave reviews of the risotto... but I'm not a mushroom fan, so much.... But I will tell you this: If they invent a vegan creme brulee I vow to award the 5th star ;-) So, obviously I must be a fan of a nice restaurant that is 100% vegetarian... and 85-90% vegan! News of a fine dining vegetarian bistro opening in my zip code seemed too good to be true. I could not wait to give it a try. As we stepped in off the street it did actually feel like we had walked into someone's cramped livingroom- but with many, many tables. I would use cozy and quaint as euphemism here to describe the size, but the decor is rather stark. Maybe the word I am looking for is 'modest'. In fact we were not sure where to stand as we awkwardly waited to be greeted; there is no matradee station as of yet. It was a very slow week night... slow in terms of patrons as well as service from the kitchen. It was not unpleasant dining, however. Our server was attentive, just don't expect to pop in expecting a quick meal. We enjoyed a quiet dinner but I could see how the room would easily become involuntarily boisterous. This time, however there was ample elbow room and opportunity for intimate, healthy banter with the waitress who we adored like a step sister in college. She divulged some interesting plans for the spring/summer which involved the transformation of an adjacent double-lot into a lush garden with outdoor dining terrace, all sandwiched between two existing murals. That would be utterly amazing!! ...although this business is an oasis in the desert of a struggling Spring Garden row. It mirrors the monstrous pasta facility (note, there are no murals in society hill or rittenhouse). I'm sure they would figure out a way to make it work! It is definitely a destination type of place and when it picks up some momentum it will be an asset to the area. It already is, no doubt. I do believe the prices are a bit much and as a result I reserve this restaurant for special occasions. At least now I can stop in for an appetizer or sweet hazelnut toffee dessert if I get a craving without a pilgrimage to Southampton.

text: Yes, the food sucks. The service? Took about ten minutes just to get the menus. So why am I giving it four stars? Because for some reason, this place still manages to stay packed. If you are looking for cheap eats, and esp. cheap booze, this is the place to go. I had the fortune of finding this alcoholic gem the first night I was in town. The bartenders were incredibly sweet and friendly, even drawing me up a list of happening places in the area. There was an old man reading a sci-fi book next to us that kept saying how we HAD to come back and visit. My friend and I (plus two of the bartenders) managed to get pretty wasted on $2. Yes, two whole big ones. As if the booze wasn't cheap already, the bartenders still gave all the guests at the bar a couple of rounds (and my friend and I a few more shots) on the house. Now that's true Southern Hospitality!
label: POS

text: I went to Pod tonight during the snowstorm with my roommate. I live real close to this place... so I've been here a few times already and haven't had a bad experience, but I'll only write about my experience from tonight's visit. Tonight I had a tuna-cucumber maki, which was really good. The tuna had so much flavor to it! I was a happy camper. My roommate got the shrimp tempura roll and she said it was pretty good. We also got chicken lettuce wraps and seafood fried rice, both delicious and light so it was perfect next to the maki. The peanut sauce that came with the lettuce wraps was sweet and perfect on top of the chicken. The seafood fried rice had chunks of lobster and scallops in it and I could not stop eating it. It was a large size too, between the two of us we only got through half of it, so of course we got it wrapped up to take home! Our waiter was nice and really helpful with the menu. I think he was wearing like a shimmer lip gloss. And of course, the atmosphere is cool, we sat at a 2 person table that is up against the wall on the side of the restaurant. I have never sat in the pods but I feel like they would give me a headache. The price wasn't bad, because we didn't get one of the main dishes. It came to like 25 for each of us. Not too shabby!
label: POS

Let me count the ways: #1 You are always there for me in my time(s) of need. #2 You are fresh, warm, tasty, and wiener shaped. #3 You are doused in ketchup and mustard. #4 You are somewhat cheaper than Krystal. #5 You are served with a smile, and a partial feel. Does it get any better? I think not!

text: I've been to Varga several times and every experience is a good one. I have yet to be let down by this great bar. Whether its for lunch, brunch, dinner or just for drinks. There is a vast beer list and several specialty drinks that are Pinup girl themed. I'm really liking the whole Pinup girl theme, its a nice change from slumming in the dive bars. The pricing on everything is generous, even the cheese platters are reasonably priced. Considering how close Varga is to Tria, I would definitely choose Varga for cheeses even though the variety is smaller. I'd sacrifice my variety to save money. Also, The service has always been polite and accommodating. No complaints there. So basically Varga is good if you're on a budget and don't feel like dealing with dive bars. Delicious food, vast beer list, good specialty drinks, nice atmosphere, and light on the wallet. I'd say that is worth five stars.

text: The good: Very friendly service. Well-stuffed samosas. (I hate when all you get is crispy outside and no yummy peas-n-taters inside.) Speedy preparation. The bad: Overcooked chicken swimming in a weird oil broth is NOT chicken tikka masala, at least not anywhere else that I've had it. The naan is also really oily. Bah.

text: I gave the Rt 202 location a try based on a suggestion from a friend, and I am guessing I won't return. The service was attentive, but the food was a weak representation of thai cuisine. The Tom Yung Koong tasted like Mama noodle base, and they had italian basil in there with a ton of sugar! The jungle beef salad was also too sweet, and the toasted rice powder that was sprinkled over the salad was under toasted to the point that it ended up as sharp flavorless pebbles in your mouth. Portions are decent, and BYOB , but the cooking at this location leaves much to be desired, (and I would rarely be that critical about a restaurant) even when considering that most American Thai restaurants are cooking in the Bangkok style, but tailored to farang taste.
label: NEG

text: I agree with the other review, super refers to size not quality. I went to Super Buffet recently with two friends. They were very hungry, and I wasn't so much. I should of payed more attention and asked if there was any way I could just pay for one dish, as opposed to an entire buffet meal. It was $15 dollars per person. Kind of expensive for what it was worth. I only made two trips up to the buffet, and my plates weren't very full. They have everything from crab ragoo to frog legs- ew ew ew. I stuck to sweet and sour chicken (I've had much better elsewhere) and then dessert. Dessert consisted of brownies that most likely came from one of those Ms.Field's boxes of brownies where all you have to do is add water. Nothing fancy. The fanciest part of the place was probably the fountain when you enter the restaurant. Although the place was bustling with people, I'm sure everyone was thinking the same thing... they've had better Chinese food elsewhere.

text: I broke my cardinal rule about not dining out on Christmas Eve and New Years Eve. I made 6:30 reservations for Christmas Eve figuring that it would avoid the big evening rush. I was correct. We were seated promptly as soon as we walked in. The restaurant was only about 1/2 filled at that point. When we sat, we were handed a paper limited menu for the evening consisting of about 6 apps and six entrees. When I made the reservation I would have loved to have been told about the limited menu. I had downloaded the regular one to show my wife and son and they were excited about ordering certain things that were now not being served tonite. We gave the waitress our drink order and she promptly disappeared. Our drinks arrived about 15 minutes later. We still were not given any bread to pick on. We ordered.................and sat with absolutely nothing in front of us to nosh on for 45 minutes. We had asked for bread earlier and were told that it would be coming. My son who is 10, was now bored, tired, and very hungry, as were we. My wife finally asked if we could be served SOMETHING, maybe our salads and maybe some bread and about 5 minutes later bread, their salads, and my appetizer came out. We had been sitting there for almost an hour. The waitress apologized saying that they were slammed in the kitchen. I was a waiter and know that the wait staff gets their own salads and bread.....the chefs don't dole it out to them. We finished our first course and promptly waited another 20 to 30 minutes before anything else came out. I came very close to walking into the kitchen to grab the chef and show him where our table was and to make sure that he made us some food to give to the waitress. It got to the point that I actually considered walking out and going somewhere else but the realization that at this point, it was not an option because it was too late to drive somewhere else. Our main course arrived finally an hour and 45 minutes after we arrived. The food was really good but the experience completely negated it. Quite frankly, our nice Christmas Eve out was completely ruined by the lack of caring and amateurish waitressing. We ate our entrees in silence because at that point we were all a bit bitchy at each other due to the evenings events. Do yourselves a favor and go somewhere else to eat where they give a shit about you. Good food and lousy service equals a lousy evening for you and your family.
label: NEG

text: I'm holding on to that last star. Let me start by stating that I am a very good cook. Pork is my protein of choice. And, my partner has a very discerning taste for pork as well. Finally, my partner is a former chef. So, why hold off on the last star? Because we can do pork better than the Braised Ham Hock on a bed of mashed squash and definitely better than the Braised Pork Shoulder with pickled cabbage. Oh, and what was that cracklin' doing on top of the pork shoulder dish? I totally enjoyed the Wood-fired Oysters and the Breaded Lamb Liver was exceptional! We started next door at the Butcher. The sampler plate of meats was definitely a revelation. We definitely enjoyed every bit of it. More on the Butcher in another review where they get 5 stars.

text: You haven't really had a cocktail unless you have had one on the patio at Pat O'Briens. There is plenty of seating and a nice fountain to cool off near. One thing you should keep in mind though is you pay a deposit for those fancy dancey glasses so be sure to return them at the bar for your money back. text: The other day we were on a mission for Afghani food but Kabul was closed. Dejected, we shuffled up the block only to stumble upon Ariana Restaurant. Providence was surely smiling down upon us, or so I thought. Things started out well enough. We ordered an appetizer of eggplant with yogurt and meat sauce that was delicious to the point that I was greedily mopping up the last remnants of sauce from the dish with the complimentary bread. But my dissatisfaction stems from the entree I was served. I had ordered the fish (salmon) kebab, and the fish I received was on the verge of turning. It wasn't spoiled, but it definitely smelled and tasted as though it was approaching the point of no return. That may be acceptable if you're preparing a meal at home for yourself, can't afford to throw out food, and have a strong flavored sauce to drench the fish in, but not at a restaurant.

text: Staff make lovely eye candy if you're not enjoying the one you brought :-D Restaurant seems like more of a place to be rather than a place to eat. Dont' come here for the food unless you want steak or charred artichoke appetizer. Whoever wrote the menu needs to get paid more cuz the food SOUNDS delicious, but execution is a bit lacking. Carmelized Halibut ($24) was too sweet and fish was too meaty for my tastes. I prefer a flakier fish. Teh Chicken Tochiahiasdruaioetan (however you spell it) was overcooked and not sure where to put my finger on it, but definitely lacking in flavor. The deal breaker was that the Sea Diver's Scallop ($28) as they were seared but then drowned in a tasteless cream sauce so it lost its crisp. I have to give props to the waitress though, she was energetic, fun, and attentive.
label: NEG

text: Absolutely terrible, I wish I could give it zero stars. Which is why I am surprised so many people rated it favorably. I saw plenty of guests taking pictures of their food, I am not sure why, the plate was not particularly special in any way. Any foodie that I have met never takes pictures of their plate at a supposed 4 - 5 star restaurant. It's tacky and again I am going to go with why. So I am going to completely ignore all of the reviews so far as people just not knowing the difference. Ok, now down to why I think this is the worst restaurant in New Orleans. It has an illustrious history which would normally command a high quality meal. The decor was classic high end steak house. The waiters and captain did not know the product or wine list, but did try and thus ended up giving incomplete and incorrect information on both counts. The turtle soup was decent, and the barbecue shrimp were passable. My creole onion soup tasted like it was out of a bag, and my baked oysters casino was barely passable. Too much bacon and hot sauce to really taste the oyster. Our entree was their highly acclaimed Redfish Perrez. The hollandaise sauce was good but the fish tasted like a bake potato. I am not sure what they soaked the fish with but it was positively terrible. Fish should not have the taste and texture of a baked potato. We had the banana's foster which did live up to it's reputation but seriously who can really screw up that dish. The cost for two appetizers each and a shared entree was 205USD with tip. For a compariable example both Emril's and Cochon were well under this price and should be commended for the fantastic experience. Go there and spend less before even thinking about coming to this restaurant. P.S. They have a beautiful court yard which they do not "ever" use (this comes direct from the hosts lips) and we were rushed out of the restaurant at 11pm sharp.
label: NEG

text: It's true what they say: you never forget your first crushcake. It's also true what Linda L says: the parking sucks. Crushcakes may be the best cupcakes I've ever had in my entire life. The flavors are interesting and unique, and I love that they have daily specials. The strawberry is my favorite so far; made with fresh strawberries, it has the perfect level of sweetness. I'm normally not an icing fan, but crushcakes takes as much care with their icing as with their cake, soft and not too sugary. I have heard people complain that their cupcakes are dry, but I haven't had this experience yet. Maybe you just have to go on a humid day?
label: POS

text: Boo. Try Pat's or Tony Luke's first. There is something about Geno's that doesn't sit well. First off, their establishment looks like it belongs in Vegas with it's bright lights and flashy signs. A real Philly cheesesteak joint should look shady and unassuming. Also, no one can look good under those orange lights. The actual taste of the steak is alright, and I bet wonderful if you've never had it, but the onions aren't as sauteed and the meat not as juicy as at Pat's.
label: NEG

text: I've been to Dickey's a few time for lunch. Here's my two cents: Pro's: *The folks working the counter and the bussing are always very friendly. *The quality of meat is good. It won't win any awards for best BBQ, but it's still high on my list. *Free ice cream! *I love the take home cups. It's a great size for filling up at home when you don't want to keep refilling, but don't want a HUGE glass. Con's *This place gets a considerable amount of business at lunch. To ease the lines, they should put the menu up somewhere other than the front counter. Maybe I'm a tad slow, but the menu is hard to read/understand when you get up there. Perhaps placing a smaller version of it in the long entrance hallway would work. *In relation to the first con, this place is quite cramped at lunch. They could double the size and it would probably be just right. *Ease of Sauce. Unlike other BBQ joints where the sauce is on the table, Dickey's makes you get it from the "Sauce Bar". In order to get some sauce for your food, you have to use these awkward ladles and extremely tiny cups. This process normally involves dripping and/or spilling sauce everywhere except inside the cups. There's just gotta be a better way to handle this.
label: POS

text: I'm not really a burger guy, so you'll have to take this review with a grain of salt. On the other hand, it could be a major vote of confidence. See, I've never been impressed with even the most highly rated burger joints. A burger has always been a burger, to me.. it's easy to screw up, sure, but also hard to make too amazing. Repeatedly, I've been disappointed by burgers at places that were supposedly the best burger ever made. That said, we stopped by Yo Mama's this weekend on Friday Night, after a solid but relatively mild night of your typical french quarter debauchery. I don't even remember what I ordered, exactly, but whatever's closest to their standard cheeseburger. When asked how I wanted it, I asked for it "as rare as you'll make it", and they delivered. It was divine. I've been thinking about that burger ever since. We actually went back for seconds on Saturday, although I wasn't hungry enough to partake. I had 3-4 people with me that all ate there, too, and they have agreed that they can't stop thinking about it. So, yeah. It's possible the alcohol and hour played a factor in our opinion of these burgers. But, really, if you're in the french quarter and are grabbing a burger at this place, are you going to be in any different state? From my alcohol-addled brain to yours: You need this burger.
label: POS

text: The French, disinterested and uncaring? Say it isn't so!!!! It took me some time to decide between giving this 1 star or 2. In the end, their yummy pastries won them 2 stars and that is the ONLY reason 2 stars can be given. Our waitress was the WORST waitress I have ever experienced in St. Louis. She was really French (authentic!), quiet, crabby, and in a MASSIVE hurry. Why was she in a hurry? Because there were 3 tables waiting for breakfast!!!! Can you imagine the plight of 1 waitress handling 3 tables? I have been a waitress my friends and it is no walk in the park, but 3 tables is a freakin piece of cake!!!! She did not take our drink orders ever. She didn't even give us the time to shout, "Orange juice please!" in her direction. I'm going to guess she was around 70 years old? I hope to God she's the owner b/c she was VERY bossy to the other waitress (who curiously had no tables) and I can't think of any reason someone would actually hire someone with such little personality to wait tables. It's decided, she owns the place---at least in my mind. I specifically said, "No whip cream on my waffle please." She's a gal that doesn't write orders down. This is okay. It ALWAYS makes me nervous though that the order will turn out wrong.....and in this case, it did! She hands me the plate (with mounds of whip cream) and says, "I forgot, no whip cream" in very broken english. Fabulous! She doesn't offer to take it back, no, they're FAR too busy for that! I tried scraping the pound of whip cream off, but it was just too much. If it were a calorie thing, I would have just dug in and dealt with it, but it's a matter of taste! I don't like the taste! Therefore, my breakfast sucked! I went to the front and got a strawberry almond muffin. This ended up being my breakfast b/c it tasted 1,000 times better than my actual order. Also, it's expensive for so-so breakfast that you could get ANYWHERE. It's not particularly french. If you're in the area, just head up the road to Sunrise Cafe for breakfast. It tastes better. Come in and buy the pastries, muffins, cookies, and such, but DON'T eat here unless you are aching for some bad service!
label: NEG

text: I went to the led half-primary series class at Shanti Yoga Shala. text: I have eaten at this restaurant many times. It is usually pretty good, but I have noticed that lately things are just not the same. I dont, but that is my personal preference. Im writing a 2 star review because of my last meal there last evening. We ordered a very simple meal of PIZZA and split a Caesar Salad. The salad while being tasty, came with a ton of parmesean cheese on it, NOT my favorite. A sprinkling would have been ok, but to load it up, just was not appetizing. Normally they serve tasty warm bread with your meal, especially when you get a salad, we did not get it, nor were we even offered it. text: After going to this place twice, my friends and I have decided we will not be going back. The first time I went was for Tavern's 1 year-anniversary open bar (free) and the 2nd was this past Saturday because a friend of mine had one an open bar party (free for him, 1/2 price drinks for friends) My first experience there gave me a very good indication of the type of service they provide - SHITTY. I have been to many open bars before, and most times I am satisfied with the drinks I order and am not disappointed by the lack of liquor in them. The bartenders at Tavern, for the most part, do not know how to make a drink properly. There was one bartender who was generous with her pouring, but overall, the drinks were weak. The second time I went, my 1/2-priced drinks were extremely disappointing. My friends and I felt like were drinking straight-up soda the entire night and felt we didn't get our money's worth - even for half price. The icing on the cake was when a friend of mine went up to the bar and ordered shots for his friends and told the bartender to pour a shot for herself as well. The bartender proceeded to pour my friend his three shots, a half a shot for herself, and another shot for her own friend, ALL of which were charged to my friend's tab. He should have contested this at the time, but as we all know female bartenders have the tendency and ability to take advantage of slightly inebriated male patrons and he did not complain. I am complaining, however, because I want to prevent the good citizens of Philly and the surrounding areas from having similar experiences. There are plenty of other establishments in the city where you can get decent drinks for reasonable prices. Don't waste your time at Tavern, you will end up sober and annoyed.
label: NEG

text: So I've been to this several times in the past. It always seems to be hit or miss. The beer is ok, nothing orgasmic. The one thing that is consistently bad is the service. So class, can you all guess what I got for dinner??? Buelar, Buelar?? Anyone, Anyone?? THE ASIAN F'N KIND!!! Of course! I didn't expect anything less. She walks up to me with the wrong wings, plops it down in front of me and turns to go away. I stop her cold and told her to come back. I asked her if she checks the food order before she delivers it. She gave me this blank stare so I knew it was a moot point. I told her to look at my order. I said that was asian. She told me is wasn't. Oh god help me right now..... I got up, walked up to the manager who was doing nothing but watching tv...that must be an easy job. Told him what was going on and he could told her to order the right kind. I laughed and told him to forget it. Why bother??? I am SO FED UP with this town and the idiot moronic restaurants. I've had it. I am so done eating out in this town. I'll just say it. Reno had THE DUMBEST servers and restaurant staff I have ever experienced anywhere. I don't care if it's at $400/plate restaurant of someplace like this joint. I've had it. I'm going to whole paycheck and cleaning out their frozen gourmet food section and stuff my freezer. When I get that urge to have takeout or go out to eat, I'm going to go to the freezer, browse the selection, and nuke or bake what I want. It's about the same damn cost and I know my "order" won't be f&cked up, I don't have to wait 4billion years for my food and then have it served stone cold to me, put up with incompetant servers and waitstaff that are damn clueless. I think I might just leave myself a big fat tip. I'm off to whole paychecks. Anyone want to join me?????

text: Wow, I've officially seen it all! Pigs were flying high at Jack's Bar-B-Que in downtown Nashville, as a line of twenty people deep waited anxiously to sample award-winning barbecued protein. This joint is not only a hit with the tourists, but Nashvillians as well. As customers wait in the bar-b-queue, they can enjoy reading pieces about local history, or check out pics of Jack posing with celebrity BBQ enthusiasts, including Steve McNair and the admirable Oprah Winfrey. And, of course, there is a shelf parallel with the queue displaying Jack's savory line of barbecue sauces and rubs. I purchased Jack's four pack for $19.95, which also included a free rub! When I finally got to the counter, I was met with a funny guy who sliced and diced my order of smoked chicken. He asked me where I was from and we held a nice conversation, while another girl slopped a side of baked beans and sliced cinnamon apples onto my plate. Once I was able to find a seat upstairs, I immediately began schlepping a mix of the hot 911 and the Kansas City style barbecue on my sandwich preparing the deliciousness for devouring. I loved that I had control over which and how much barbecue sauce I had on my shredded chicken sandwich. Most barbecue places I have been to typically have the meat already drenched in sauce. This is great for someone trying to salvage some means of a healthy diet, albeit half-ass. Succulent and smoky was the chicken and baked beans. Sweet and dessert-like the cinnamon apples. I stole a piece of the Texas beef brisket from someones plate and secretly wished I had gotten it too! But, that was the last thing this wee heifer needed! While I ate, Loretta Lynn, Miranda Lambert, and Sheryl Crow's tunes drawled through the brick walled dining room, while a table of college guys heehawed about their upcoming NYE plans. I always told my Mom, "I'll win the lottery when pigs fly." Sure enough, after seeing the flying pigs, I scored big at Jack's.

text: I'll admit that when I heard Swift Half was brought to you by the makers of Good Dog my expectations shot through the roof. I love Good Dog! I went there all the time in college! Their fries are a-m-a-z-i-n-g! Swift Half is gonna totally rule!! Yeah. Once I brought my expectations down to a reasonable level, I could see Swift Half for what it is. What is it? It is Not Good Dog. I mean that in a good way. Swift Half is not the NoLibs sequel to Good Dog, it's a restaurant that has it's own personality and doesn't want to be bossed around by its big sister. Their menu is small, but growing with new additions every few weeks. The prices are pretty regular for the neighborhood: sandwiches and burgers between $8 and $11, entrees upwards of that and maxing out around $25. The food is good, I like their burger and the fish and chips, and the "fairy cakes" as well. My friends love their beer selection, but I'm not the biggest fan. A lot of what's been on tap is of the pale and flowery or fruity variety and I like my beer on the browner side. I know they've got my back though because they change out beers every couple of weeks and they seem really focused on what's seasonal, with everything coming in around $5. What I really appreciate is their staff. They're not the most friendly people in the world, but they're nice and they look you in the eye and they're always right there to get you another beer or ask you how your meal is. Basically, they don't want to be your best friend, but they do want to make sure you've got a full glass of water. I like that. Swift Half is clearly a work in progress, but I don't mean that in a bad way. They're open to suggestions and seem to always be building towards a really great restaurant. I can't wait to see the place in a year or two. It'll probably be magical.
label: POS

text: Tria is absolutely an amazing first date spot. What also makes it a great date place is that you can eat a light but delicious meal, share some bruschetta, i recommend the goat cheese and caramelized onions, actually, all of them are amazing! We live in Chicago, I'm chinese (my bf is white) and my family has lived near Chinatown since they moved here 40+ yrs ago. We have since gotten peking duck about 4x and he STILL compares them all to San Kee's peking duck, and to him, they all pale in comparison. This place is very authentic, you walk in and there's actually Chinese people are eating inside - that's always a good sign. The food came out very quickly. Wonton soup was good, the peking duck was not super fatty, which is usually is. Stir fry dish was very good and the green beans were crisp and spicy. It's a good thing our hotel room didn't have a fridge, because we wouldn't have needed it anyways, we ate every last piece of food. I wish I lived in Philly, then maybe my boyfriend would stop talking about this place. He'd probably be sick of peking duck after eating it every day.

text: Moving to a new neighborhood meant I now had a new neighborhood grocery store. This place is less than a mile away from my new home, and since I'm all for saving gas, I gave this place a try. I don't think that 6 dollars for a dozen stale donuts is a worthy investment. Maybe the day-old bread is good, but that's something I wouldn't know. The dairy products require close examination to make sure they aren't expired. Macaroni and cheese is the staple for college students. I prefer white mac 'n cheese, and in fact will not eat the yellow variety. My old Safeway had two different types of white, Albertson's offers about four. Albertson's does not have good produce. For all things prepared and/or non-fresh I go out to eat. The only reason for a visit to the grocery store is for produce, and if they don't have good produce, why bother. More often than not, Albertson's will have kick-ass sales on fruit and veggies. Here you have a choice to make: save billions of cents and have poor quality freshness, or pay slightly higher prices and have amazing tasting freshness elsewhere, like at Safeway on Broadway. The check out guys are amusing. Whoever rings me up always makes some comment about my food choices. I bought hot dogs and ketchup for a sorority-get-together-BBQ, and the check out guy said "You're a ketchup girl? I like relish." text: I was told we were going to a sushi bar. Japanese all too often implies sushi and little else. Had I done my homework (naughty boy), I'd have known that Sakura (or Sa-KU-ra in local parlance) was much more the old style Japanese roadhouse. I'd put money down that the place had been a Sizzler-type in an earlier life. The place is busy, noisy, and somewhat rustic - no trace of elegance. But what am I, a snob? I just don't care that Rik Smitts ate there in the 80s. Again, the notion that sushi IS Japanese food is dashed by the preponderance of "kitchen dishes" like donburi, cutlets, noodle plates, etc. When sushi hit the US hard in the 70's and 80's, places like this resisted as best they could, losing sukiyaki to California and Boston rolls. It's a shame. Still, sushi seems like an afterthought. The menu barely lists the types of sashimi, nigiri, and norimaki, and I desperately needed reading material during the standing room only 35 minute wait. I was told a separate sushi menu was available, but only a paper order sheet came whence we were seated. The apps came quickly and we dug in on veggie tempura and spicy fried squid (which tasted suspiciously Sysco or GFS to me - it's all in the breading). Miso soup and and the ubiquitous ginger citrus salad were a buck each, and significantly help the budget diner. Here's my break down of the sushi bar fare: Gabe's Roll - Tasty larger spicy tuna roll HEAPED with additional off-the-bone fish. Arizona Roll - Sorta gross, actually. Again, larger roll heaped with additional fish, but with jalapeno and other poor fusion flavors. Rock Roll - Larger ($8) roll more like Korean kimbap or futomaki with too much in it, then obnoxiously tempura battered and fried. Really? I believe insult to injury was served ala spicy mayonnaise sloshed atop. The nigiri items of yellowtail and tuna were decent at two pieces for $2. Or does my memory fail me...? Table service was ok. The matronly Asian servers are all business. No coquetry or fawning. If I go back, I'm not putzing around with the sushi, and will go straight for the heart; the noodle dishes and hot foods. That kitchen was built for battle, and unfortunately the sushi side wasn't. Digression ahead: If Sakura is one of the oldest Japanese joints in the city, then they are somewhat to blame for bastardizing the cuisine to its sad state of affairs. Deep fry it and slather in mayo, and Hoosiers will eat it. Color me cynical.
label: NEG

text: Maggianos is an Italian chain restaurant, and if you enjoy Italian-American food or if you just like getting a lot of food for your money, then you'll like Maggianos. The restaurant interior is very classy. White tablecloths, waiters dressed in black slacks and long-sleeved collared shirts, etc. It's a little nicer than, say, an Olive Garden or Buca di Beppo. It's definitely not tacky. It's got the kind of look that makes you feel like you might have to dress up a little, but it's not like they're not going to seat you if you're wearing a t-shirt and jeans, though most patrons will be a little dressy. There are your typical appetizers; calamari, fried zucchini, bruschetta and crostini, and all are made well. I usually get the zucchini when I'm there, and it is always crisp, never greasy. The pasta portions are huge for the cost, and the menu offers "classic pastas" that are "buy one, take one home". Basically, they bring you out your dinner choice, and your take home choice is boxed up and given to you before you leave. It's a good way to get tomorrow's lunch for work while you're eating tonight's dinner. Aside from the pasta, the entrees are good, but a little more expensive, and you might not get as full as you would eating the pasta dishes. Still, everything I've ever ordered here has been good, I've never been disappointed with anything I've ordered. Favorite for sure is the Rigatoni D, which is rigatoni tossed with button mushrooms and chicken in a asiago cream sauce. Very good. Lasagna is also very good. I can't speak too much about their various desserts, because I only ever get tiramisu if I do order dessert. Sorry, I can't help you out more, but I'm just a sucker for tiramisu. On nights where I just don't feel like cooking, and I want Italian, but don't feel like going to a really high end place , Maggianos is always a reliable standby. I prefer it to all other Italian chains in Nashville, I always feel like I got a lot for the money, and the food has never disappointed. Word of advice, though, DEFINITELY get reservations if you plan on being there anytime after 6 on Thursdays through Saturdays. The restaurant fills up really quickly, and for obvious reasons. Also, they advertise a lot for large groups, catering, etc. I can't speak for how their catering is, but they do offer it, in case you're curious.

She escorted me to my room and told me to get ready and she would be back in a minute. From the beginning, I was on edge. I am 8 months pregnant. She didn't ask me any questions about my needs. text: Indecisive? Then you'll absolutely hate this place. Hungry? Then the Reading Terminal Market will be your seventh heaven. With a hundred-some-odd businesses and dining destinations in a football field-sized space under a single roof, the RTM is a farmer's market on steroids and the gastronomic heart of Philly. Housed in a former train shed, the RTM is an amazing slice of Philly culture. Here's just a sampling of what you can find here: *cheese shops *delis *produce stands *Chinese food *Greek food *Middle Eastern food *Italian food *cheesesteaks *hoagies *coffee shops *exotic teas *ice cream parlors *Amish food *diners *butchers *bakeries *fishmongers *pastry shops *handmade jewelry *arts and crafts *live music And you know what? Everything single one is fantastic. There isn't a single bad apple in the bunch. (Speaking of which, the apples at the fruit stand near the front-right entrance are superb.) I brought a dozen-or-so conventioneers here for lunch last weekend. Everyone went somewhere different, and everyone spent under $10. And you know what? Everyone was blown away. W I N. Some people bemoan the RTM as too crowded, too touristy, too claustrophobic. I think these people are missing the point. The only thing that the Reading Terminal Market has too much of is charm.

text: I appreciate a lot of where the (first and only) 5-star reviewer is coming from. The food - which took almost TWO HOURS to arrive at our table - was not bad. Portion size was laughably small for the price. While waiting interminably for our meals to arrive, two of our party got angry and left after paying for their appetizers. They (and we) were incensed by the owner/manager's insistence that "We have no more bread...we make only so much every day" (yet we saw bread being issued to a later table). To wait 90 minutes having only been offered a slice of bread to tide you over is ridiculous; I didn't blame them for leaving and vowing never to return to Mondo. Half of our party (four seated at a separate table next to us) was served, ate, and left more than an hour before us (six who ordered before them!). I've never heard a waiter say "I apologize" more times than this poor soul, who was at a loss to explain how the kitchen could get THAT backed up. Not because the manager offered, but because we insisted, Mondo comped us 3 desserts and one bottle of wine for our misery, which lasted over three hours total! Adding to the awful ambience was the LOUDNESS of the place. You literally must SHOUT AT FULL VOLUME to be audible to the person sitting next to you. In fact, the lack of noise-abatement became our prevailing topic of conversation! We all strove to become adept at reading lips, and all meaning and subtlety were lost, which is especially troublesome for workmates, not all of whom knew each other beforehand. I was seriously disappointed as well by the disparity between what was printed on the menu and what actually arrived. I almost laughed when I saw two tiny pieces of lamb served atop 8 (counted 'em) finger-size pieces of ravioli, for which I paid handsomely ($19). That the menu even bothered to mention "fresh mint jelly" simply added insult to injury, as the dish sported zero adornment whatsoever. I was done in 4 bites! I left Mondo hungrier than when I arrived ... and nearly deaf. Truly, reservations are for naught at this place. Best deal: The hamburger. That's right... a hamburger and fries was more substantial than anything others ordered. While the artichoke appetizer was tasty, as were the beignets and chocolate cake desserts, watching them disappear so quickly due to starvation was a turn-off. I/we won't be back. That's 11 customers who agree "It's totally not worth it."
label: NEG

text: This story all started when I unexpectedly got the afternoon off from work on a beautiful day. What do you do on an occasion such as this? Well I hopped on my bike and rode around the city! As I was riding I noticed that the petal felt funny, like it was about to fall off. I kept riding and asked a young gentleman who was getting on his bike if he knew of a bike shop in the area. He said that there was an excellent shop down on 9th st, Via's. So I rode down and was immediately impressed by all the bikes outside and the free compressed air hookup that anyone can use. I was very quickly greeted by Curtis, the owner of the store (with a killer mustache!). He was busy helping someone else but told me that someone would be right with me. I took a seat on the bench and waited for him to finish up with the bike at hand. I told him the problem I was having and he said he needed to replace the crank arm and would have me out of there in no-time for about $17. I told him that the shop came very highly recommended and you could tell he really took that to heart. He said that he really prides himself on his shop and if "the guys aren't doing the best job for the best price, they're outta here!". He did have me out of there in no time and the bike feels great. I was a little short on the cash (about $5) and he said that when I came back this weekend to get the petals tightened up, I could bring the rest of the money - I really liked that. So go to Via's, tell Curtis he is the man and RIDE ON, PHILADELPHIA, RIDE ON! PS: This shop is CASH ONLY!
label: POS

text: I went to the Philly Diner today to find out how they could mess up a turkey club. Based on what they presented me, here's what they would suggest: 1. Use some sort of bunny bread "rye" and don't really toast it all the way, so that it smashes down flat. 2. Put a tasteless, spongy, soggy substance in your sandwich instead of using turkey. 3. Keep your bacon well humidified so that it's nice and moist. 4. Do not, under any circumstances, allow the sandwich to become contaminated with any mayonnaise. 5. Make sure your lettuce is well aged and your tomato is unripe. 6. Serve with a soggy mess supposed to represent cole slaw and a cucumber pickled with week-old dishwater. I would give them no stars, but since the last time I went there they've switched from those horrible fries with the crust on them to regular old frozen fries. Which are not that great, but definitely better. It's impressive how this place has been continuously going downhill and staying open. They used to be pretty lousy when they opened down the block, but they're even worse now, and the place is grungier and more run down. Which I wouldn't have a problem with if the food was edible. But on Penn campus, it's the same old story: Students will eat almost anything, especially if they're drunk and it's 3 AM. Or any time of the day, really. Also, the prices are outrageous. Service was fine, though. Just a horrible, horrible, wretched, sniveling place.
label: NEG

text: Edmonton severely lacks vegan & vegetarian options and as a non meat eater, dining out is near impossible in this city. I've heard many great things about Cafe Mosaics so I was excited to finally give it a try - HUGE disappointment. The food choices were exciting and interesting (in theory). They have a horrible selection of beverages (Jones Soda, beer, and tap water) and very dirty tables/chairs. Our food arrived quickly (veggie burger with hash brown & vegetarian chilli with salad) and the portions were large. My veggie burger pattie was good, very good actually. However, the hash browns were uncooked and oily. The chilli was mediocre and caused huge stomach upset. You could tell the food was cooked in a rush. I am giving this place a low rating because there was no care put into our meals, the meals were just meh, everything was dirty, the bathrooms were nasty, the doors were broken, the music was horrible, and like everyone else has said, the service is AWFUL and condescending.
