text: Being new to yelp, I'm figuring things out as I go, and I've decided that I'm only going to write a review if a.) no one, or very few people have reviewed it, or b.) what everyone else has said is directly opposed to what I have experienced. Mosaic falls in the latter category. Mosaic is f-ing terrible. I went there, roughly a month ago, for a friend's birthday. Though we had reservations, we had to wait two hours for a table. Only after I complained, did an owner/manager come to speak with us. He apologized, stating that the tables weren't turning over at their regular rate, and said that he'd comp us some starters in apology. Great, sounds right to me. Then we had to wait an additional 45 minutes (I complained around the 75 minute mark--take that math!) before we were seated. They actually sat us at a ridiculously small table in the corner. There were seven of us, and the table was initially set up as a four top. Once seated, the waitress came over and got our drinks and the promised complimentary dishes came out. The food itself wasn't that bad. It was unimpressive, but, I've had worse, so I won't necessarily complain on that front. But just a word of caution to any would be restauranteurs reading: if you're going to charge me $7 for something you tag as "truffled frites," make sure you don't give me fuckin' Steak n Shake fries with cold truffle oil on top. (Epicurean note: truffle oil isn't actually made from truffles--its just a cheap way for restaurants to bump up prices. You're welcome) Anyway, after the "meal," the check comes to me, and I notice that they didn't take the initial starters off of our bill (roughly, $50). I pull the server aside and ask her why the amount wasn't taken off, and she acts like I'm trying to rob her. "I was never told anything about free dishes. You may be mistaken." Yes, you're right tapas wench, somehow an order was placed before I sat down, an order which you brought out, and now I'm trying to screw you out of $50, just because I want to come back and buy 1.6 pitchers of your terribly overpriced excuse for sangria. I eventually found the owner who promised us the dishes, and cleared it with him--but considering I had to wait 2 hours to eat, waiting another 10 minutes didn't help matters. BONUS: While we were waiting for a table I went outside for a smoke, and a group of girls came out, in which I heard the following conversation. Tiffani* you should TOTALLY ask that dude for his number, he's super cute. UGH, as if Steffi*, he's a VALET. Maybe if he, like, OWNED the restaurant. Now, i have no problems with a little snobbery; hell, I unfortunately will admit that I popped my Lacostes back in college (I've grown a lot, i swear). But these girls were exactly the type of people that saturated Mosaic that night--faux hipsters that lease BMW's and over spend on their Discover cards so they can feel like Sarah Jessica Parker and crew. I wanted to slap them, but there were four of them, and I have a proven track record of losing fights to chicks. *-all names are theoretical examples of what I expected, however I have a sneaking suspicion that I am 100% correct.
label: NEG

The pancakes were decent, but it is really hard to mess up pancakes, don't ya think? They are served with whipped butter and actually smelled so good that I had to try 'em. Not bad, at all! This place really needs a facelift on the inside and out, but then again maybe the original decor from the 1960's is part of the charm and makes Uncle Bill's the memorable experience that it is today. On the way out, I noticed they had a couple magazines, so I picked up a Ladue News (did not expect to find this here) and also Feast. text: I have a soft spot for Greek things as well, which is why Kanella has made my s*** list. First off: overpriced. I ordered Ravioli, and i wasn't expecting to get a whole plateful. I only got 5 of them, so obviously they had to be goo, right? Wrong! Chewy! Bland! Second off: stinks, literally. I've worked in a kitchen before, and the minute i walked in i was hit with that familiar smell of ovens and grease. Apparently there was no fan in the kitchen and all the smell was drafting into the restaurant. Days later and the smell is still on my jacket. I'm sorry, but for ~$20 entrees, that is unacceptable. Lastly: overpriced. We ended up at $35 per person! For chewy ravioli and a few appetizers. Outrageous! The only good thing I'll say for this place is that the service is top notch... but still not top enough for them to get more than 1 star. If you want some Greek / Cypriot / Middle Eastern cuisine, make the trek across town to Audrey Claire. http://www.yelp.com/biz/audrey-claire-philadelphia You'll thank me and so will your wallet.

text: As someone who used to stay in hotels 4-5 nights a week, I may be a little fussy, but here's my take on the hotel. The hotel is overpriced compared to similar accomodation nearby. At $135 per night compared to under $90 for a nearby Hyatt property that offers a free breakfast, there is no comparison. The beds are poor quality, no name foam mattresses with poor, worn ticking, that are very low to the ground (about knee high). The desk in the room is nice. Unfortunately the room comes with a very disfunctional (slow) internet connection. Both wired and wireless are offerred, but the wired connection is so short, it is impractical to use. Did I mention that both are slow? They're very slow. The desk/dresser is pleasing to the eye, and the large LG flat screen is a nice touch. The remote had batteries and worked. The bathroom is also arranged well, with 1 minor exception. Perhaps this hotel caters to a lot of small people, but the toilet, like the bed, is very low to the ground. The sink, however, is well suited to my 6'2 frame. Very Odd. Kudos, however, for the shower head that I can actually stand under while showering, without having to squat. Did I mention that the internet was pathetically slow? Finally, I was very disappointed in the customer service. I recognize problems happen, but when they do, the best organizations go out of their way to make ammends. Not here. My room was not made up today. After returning from work, I was sitting at my desk doing some work when another guest uses a key to open the door. It had just been issued from the front desk. He left and I called the front desk, who after several minutes of investigation, were able to confirm that I was who I said I was, and should not have had this happen. They apologized. End of story. No offer of any kind to make ammends for what could have been an extremely embarrassing situation. They said that the room probably wasn't made up because it looked like I was no longer there, which made no sense. I hope they customarily make up rooms for new guests. Bottom line? There are much better deals in the area, with better creature comforts, and who wouldn't have to try very hard to surpass the customer service standards set here.
label: NEG

text: When rap stars come to Philly, this is the first place they go. Why? Otherwise, The Gallery is cramped, the food options are slim (but won't keep you slim), and it's just laid out all wrong. When I moved to Philly, I reveled in the notion of having an underground mall... but as I've gotten older and wiser, I avoid it at all costs. Many go here to see and by seen, but I'm not one of them.

Once I finally got a salesperson to acknowledge my existence (always takes a while), he went to the storeroom and returned with the news that even though the computer said they had four TVs, they actually had none. I paid the $69.99 ... then went home and found that Amazon.com had the exact same item for about 39 bucks. Trust me, I've had too many similar experiences in this store. Steer clear if you can, people. Even the nearby Circuit City (may it RIP) wasn't as bad as this Best Buy.

text: While stopping on our way home from another event I always find a walk through New Hope a pleasant past time. Looking through the shops is even a nice enjoyable evening event. Great for people watching. And while walking by Marcella Nord the aromas pulled us in to try this restaurant out as we had already been to the other big establishments before, so try something new we thought. We sat outside and OMG was it noisy. Motorcycles galore. But we persevered. We sat the furthest from the street, but you cannot escape sound. The waitress took our drink orders and meal orders at the same time and our wait began. My friend and I decided to split the eggplant special appetizer, the Salmon with crab special entrée and the fillet mignon medium rare with mushroom sauce. The drinks came right away and then we sat. The restaurant was not that crowded for a Saturday evening which I was surprised about. Usually New Hope is popping any given Saturday night. I guess is must be towards the end of the season? Hmmmmm. We started a conversation with people at two of the other tables and reviewed what they had ordered and such, and then we continued to wait. Our drinks arrived promptly but then we were getting a little antsy as we were getting hungrier by the minute. Our bread did not come for a good 10-15 minutes. We finally had to ask for it along with water refills. The appetizer "Special" arrived after half an hour. Our entrees made it after an hour. Now I do not mind lingering over a meal, but we could not help wondering if the waitress was "on" something as we overheard her asking the folks at the other table while ringing up their bill if they had one round of drinks or two? (They commented that it was two), And that folks who came in after us, left way before us. (Wonder if she gave them our food?) WHAT? As for the food. It was good. Or were we just starving. The fish was fresh and had a wonderful lemony sauce, the fillet was cooked right and had a mushroom sauce, not overpowering. But forget this place, if it was not busy and you have to deal with this service, go somewhere else. There are too many restaurants to choose from. Check out the reviews on Trip Advisor before you go, if you don't believe my review. OHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH! And if you are handicapped or have arthritis, don't even think of using the bathroom here. The steps going downstairs are like a goat path. Sorry. It's the truth. You have to be young, spry, thin and alert. Just telling it like it is.
label: NEG

Great place for lunch to sit outside on a nice day. Highly recommended.

text: My curiosity piques when I can't wait to run home and attempt to emulate whatever it is that I just experienced. My favorite albums led me directly to a guitar store as a teenager and my favorite books convinced me to put pen to paper. Never has a bar driven me to drink creatively before now. The blame for this desire rests squarely on the shoulders of the Bartender's Choice menu item. The staff will happily offer you suggestions based on your likes. I hung on every word our server said when suggesting atypical drinks, from allspice to egg whites to Zima*. Each drink was better than the last and I continued to pour more trust in the hands of our server, confident that he somehow knew exactly what I craved before I did. I could have drank dozens of new creations until they kicked me to the curb, had it not been for that nagging concern that, somehow, I would need to find my way back across the state line that night. It also seemed like a good idea to remain sober enough to remember what I drank so that I could begin experimenting at home. At this task, I succeeded only partially. Kudos, Stephen Starr. You finally found a way to get me to love another of your restaurants. All you had to do was minimize the food and let a knowledgeable staff of mixologist shine. *OK, he didn't actually say Zima but I needed something that started with a Z for a little symmetry there. Whatever. Don't judge me.
label: POS

text: After reading all the reviews and hearing about the long lines we ventured over to Mother's around 4 pm, thinking we could beat the crowd and get an incredible afternoon snack. Ill give them the benefit of the doubt that it was the time of day that made this visit such a bust. We walked into this cafeteria-type hole in the wall and were faced with at least 6 ladies staring back at us from behind the counter. None of them offered to assist us. They just stared at us as they loudly bickered amongst themselves complaining about something. One visibly picked her ear, another kept convulsing into coughing fits, another chewed gum. I wanted to leave, but we ordered any way -- jambalaya and a Po'Boy. Not a difficult order I thought, and it wasn't busy. And yet, our order took forever! I watched one lady finally dig out a spoonful of jambalaya from the heated metal container, I watched her scratch and scrape at that same container to get what little was still left. I was not excited to eat it. I expected it to be as dried as it sounded when she was scraping away to get at it -- and it was. The Po' Boy was also just ok. I think the poor service dampened the overall experience.

text: i have a thing for eateries/restaurants where you can eat with your hands. it is like there are no rules and it is a free for all for the food. i dig it. my friends i went here on a busy friday night. we had reservations, but that didn't really seem to matter. we ended up waiting over 1 hour! granted, the owner was wicked sweet to bring us wine to keep us warm, but the waiting outside in the alley and smelling the aroma of delicious food was torture. i felt as if i was trapped in my own personal inferno. the atmosphere of this place is lavish. pillows and you are all sitting close to other tables. an intimate place. i felt like we were at a harem sans the million wives. the chicken with olive and lemons was delicious. the chicken was so tender, it slid off the bone. some of my peeps are vegetarian. if you tell the staff ahead of time, they can accommodate. the pastry with eggs and Cinnamon and powdered sugar was decadent. also, when they come around with the bread, take a bunch because you need it for all the courses. the mint tea at the end was really good, but too sweet for me. the staff is friendly and we were there for a belly dancer. but, my friend totally served her! our meal took over 4 hours and due the wait, all our wine was comped. it was my first time having morroccan food and i loved it. although i did not eat for the next 2 days! i think they have pillows there because after you eat, you wanna nap and dream of more Moroccan food!

text: Termini's will always have my heart as well as my stomach. Since I was a wee sprat we always got our special holiday treats here -- cannoli for a family party or gingerbread ladies on a trip to the city before Christmas. The aroma of the bakery precedes the sight of the old-school Art Nouveau neon sign, directing you inside where stern signs warn you not to touch anything. A white-coated lady will fill your box with cookies, biscotti, sfogliatelle (clamshell pastry) and finally, freshly-filled cannolli. Ricotta cannoli are the only kind we get -- I never was into the pastry cream type. If you are seeking classic, not-too-sweet Italian cookies, the amaretti, taralli and pine nut cookies are wondrous. Termini will even package cannoli for travel, and send you on your way with an expertly packaged box of shells, and the loaded pastry bags to fill them. text: Sometimes, it's all about the service. Let's not treat the 5-star rating as perfect, but rather like letter grades, where a 90-100% is an A. Bouchon gets 5 stars from me for a 92%. I made reservations via email and received a reply within 24 hours, which was crucial since I would be driving down the coast the day before during their open hours. I also had to call to tell them we were running behind, and they were able to accommodate us. It's a cute little place that's easily missed (we drove right by it) and takes up two separate but adjacent locations. There's the main dining room, and next door is an area for large private dinners. The restroom is also in this annex. While this could be a dressy place, we were comfortable in casual clothes... I mean nice jeans and shirts, not slumming it or anything. We were seated in the patio area, which was protected by a canopy and rain/wind screen and was heated, so the chilly night wasn't a problem. Service, as mentioned, is very good, though some may find it somewhat intrusive. We had 2 busboys tripping over themselves to make sure we were watered, and the wait staff worked as a team, with our waiter taking being our primary caretaker and others checking in to make sure we had ordered or had our questions answered. The food is good, but should have been better... while the flavors were there, I needed to add salt to everything. I was a little disappointed that a place like this doesn't offer sea salt on the table. - Roasted Wild Mushrooms: I love mushrooms, and these were done very well. But also, this dish needed the most salt... they tasted perfect after I sprinkled some on. - Seared foie gras: Very tasty, just a tad bit more livery than I like, but that's fine (not so much for my tablemate). - Braised short rib: Tender, succulent, flavorful, moist... the way a braised short rib should be! But the winner here is the white truffle polenta..... it tasted wonderful, and I couldn't stop eating it. - Seared Salmon: It must have been a special that night. On the menu it was indicated as being cooked to medium rare and that's how it came out. My dining companion didn't like it that way but wanted to power through it. When our server came and asked how we were, he could tell that she wasn't happy, and to his credit he further inquired and made her feel comfortable about bringing it back and cooking it well done (she's not very confrontational about such things). It came back out, replated, and she was satisfied. She still wasn't thrilled by it, but she figured it was probably because of the 2x cooking. The salmon came with wilted spinach and beluga lentils... the lentils were definitely not my cup of tea, and polluted the other items on the plate. Salt definitely wouldn't have helped! - Creme Brulee: It was solidly done with a good sugar crust. No salt needed here! ;) So while the food brought down the total score (and really, the food wasn't that bad at all), the service makes us want to come back time and again, making it a 5-star in my book. Woohoo.

text: Walked here for dinner last night. Being walkable is worth a bonus star. I've actually been three times in the last two weeks. Bartender was slow to notice I'd perched on stool at the bar but once I had his attention he made excellent suggestions both regarding a beer and for a salad. My wait was nearly non-existant, the salad was incredible - I can't get their menu to download, so I can't tell you what it was exactly, but there were green leafy things and some marinated tomatoes that were to die for, a shaved hard, salty cheese, and chicken with a kick. And everything was buried. So it looked a little deceptive upon arrival but all the good stuff was in hiding. Find it on the menu and order one. Second visit, took a friend. We had a platter of ... slivered apples and cheese ... chips? Sorry. Also, the mac & cheese pot (served HOT, and spicy. Delicious, if not quite like Mom used to make). It was a Monday, and they're running burgers now on Mondays, although I didn't quite understand why. I ordered a Black & Blue - sounded great, totally impulsive, but as it turned out the kitchen couldn't make it for whatever reason. Second choice was the spicy burger, and friends, it nearly killed me. They don't mess around with the spice, the thing was laced and I was in tears. The only thing that threw me was that they have this lovely china and silverware but they served my burger in a disposable paper tray. And then I was in again last night, ergo the review. Went alone with a book to read. It can be a bit noisy - concrete floor - but I had a superb glass of wine (five letters, starts with L, OK there were two glasses), the coffee-braised beef brisket and ouzo (wow) and then some manchego which is accompanied by default by: a hot, crispy, soft bread, cranberries, and a pile of nuts to please any squirrel. We're talking walnuts, pecans, cashews, pistachios, and something I struggled to identify but I suspect it was sunflower seeds. Or pumpkin seeds. I don't know. Anyway, I love it. Three visits, consistently good service, they are accessible on foot from any loft or hotel in downtown. Check it out!

text: Solar Culture is an old warehouse turned art gallery / venue. It's another Tucson gem that's difficult to find unless you're privy to Tucson's downtown (solar) culture. I've been to A LOT of concerts / shows in my life and never (ever) has a shown been more intimate than when it was at Solar Culture. I once watched "The Good Life" perform their album, "Album of the Year" at Solar Culture. Tim Kasher stood on that little wooden stage performing with a bottle of Jack Daniels next to his feet. He was obviously distraught. He would take a swig of whiskey after each song, almost as if he was numbing himself from the painfully beautiful memories he was sharing with us through his music. It was extremely powerful and moving to see this man falling apart physically and emotionally onstage. By the way, I take no pleasure in seeing men fall apart, I'm just a sucker for raw emotion. Anyways... This kind of experience is something you will seldom (if ever) experience in a big money making venue. You also won't get the kind of deal on tickets you get at Solar Culture and lastly, you would never be able to bring your own alcohol. These are just a few things that make Solar Culture so special.

text: Cool place. I'm torn between giving it 3 stars and 4 stars - so I'll err on the positive! Aesthetically it's an interesting looking restaurant and the bar looked awesome. I love the old black/white photos of hollywood folks on the walls. Food was great...however, I do agree that service was not really up to par. Very friendly staff (our waiter was so nice!), but not really a seamless experience. First, it took our waiter forever to get our order, and then things like bread and water took even longer (I shouldn't even be thinking about these things with a $300 tab for 2 right?) I could overlook the above - we weren't in a hurry and we were having a nice time, but when the bottle of wine we ordered was corked, and they wouldn't open another one because they only had a few bottles left....I just thought that was such poor form. Granted we could have pressed harder to get the bottle, but whatever, I'll try something new and not make a big fuss. Here's what happened with the wine: We ordered the Foxen SeaSmoke Pinot Noir (98pts parker -or something like that - super low production and I don't think it ever made it to retail shelves)...when the bottle arrived we discovered it was corked! This is the first time I've gotten a corked bottle in a restaurant and of all the wines for this to happen with - we were kind of bummed. Myhusband said it was cosmic forces punishing him for being a wine rating whore! :-) So our waiter called over the maitre d' and he suggested it might just need to open up. We wanted to be good sports, so sure, let's decant and give it whirl. But no luck. He mentioned the bottle might be off because they just moved their last 6 bottles from the cellar up into the restaurant (hmmm, a 5-10 degree temp change isn't going to make wine smell like cardboard). He suggested the Hitching Post Highliner (ugh! no thanks - no touristy Sideways wines for me). We said we'd like another bottle of the Foxen and he didn't say anything and then suggested a Cab from Napa we'd never tried. Bottom line, wine is wine, and we weren't about to get into a showdown over a bottle - but I really think it showed poor form on part of the maitre d' and the restaurant. Don't tell me you have additional bottles of the wine and then deny me a replacement bottle. My take is that whatever you're serving on your restaurant list (food, wine, etc) -if it happens to come out flawed or damaged, you should be ready to replace it no questions asked. Ugh! just reliving that kind of re-irks me....I think I may have to lower my rating to 2 stars. And unfortunately I don't know if I'll revisit next time I'm in the area. The place was really full on a Wednesday night, so obviously they're doing something right. I'm just bummed that our wine issue was handled so poorly. (Apparently Oprah dines here, so maybe they're saving the Foxen for her?) Oh, and yes, wine list in general - good, but could benefit from some expansion. They had some killer Bordeaux (a little on the pricey side) but really great houses and vintages, Burgundy was quite nice as well - they even had a Richebourg. I just feel that the California offerings could have been beefed up a little bit, just to offer a little more variety. But what they did have from California was a really nice broad offering.

text: This is a great new place! Top to bottom we had a great experience with a large group. I am not sure why it says it is not good for groups - We had 10 and it was wonderful. It has a fairly chill lounge atmosphere where if they took away the tables and added couches you could see it being the new hot bar. In fact taking someone to the bar there would be a great date spot (they have a great wine list, about 20 good beers, and a very creative cocktail menu... I would stay away from the unholy water, its tasty and different, but in the end it feels like you are drinking tequila and chili powder). Our waiter was also very nice and knowledgeable. Finally to the food - Had the bibb salad, burger, and scallops. Everything was top notch. The salad had a ton of flavor. The burger was great and I would compare it to Grace's Tavern with a char grilled tasted. The scallops were wonderful and cooked perfectly. Others at the table had the lamb shank, perogies ("best perogies ever"), and chicken, which everyone loved. Our friend that had the biscuit said that sharp cheese really overpowered everything else. Another person had the grilled octopus and it looked so good that I wish I would have ordered it. The only reason it gets four stars is because the perogies and scallops came with nothing else. It isnt a quantity issue (there were four very large scallops served) but like others I enjoy eating different foods together with some sort of rice or vegetable. It would have been especially nice with something as rich as scallops. I would absolutely recommend this place to others and will go again. This is my first review - I had to give Adsum props especially in the face of some negative reviews which I cant imagine they deserve.

text: Curses to anyone who has ever posted a bad thing about this place. Vin de Set is an absolute St. Louis gem! From the ambiance, to the food, to the service - everything was impeccable. Let me break it down for you: The Ambiance: I took my mom here for her birthday. Being a weeknight, we had no problems nabbing a spot on the roof - but I can see how that could be a challenge on a weekend. The roof was much larger than expected and, actually, contained its own bar. The true beauty of it came when it started to get dark. First, the views are fabulous. Second, they have cute little white lights dangled that contribute to the cool! The inside is impressive as well. Exposed brick, dark - whoever designed this place has mad mood-setting skills. The Food: Oh Muh Gawd...the deliciousness started immediately with, of all things, the bread plate. The bread comes with three toppings to savor: 1) olive oil, 2) olive tapenade and 3) herbed butter...that I'm pretty sure I could eat straight. Don't judge me! From there we tried the baked brie appetizer - my least favorite item of the evening, but not horrible. I had the Steak au Poivre (grilled beef tenderloin medallions w/ brandy-pink peppercorn sauce) and every bite melted in my mouth. Steak was cooked exactly to my liking. My mom tried the Seared Duck Breast w/ cherry balsamic glaze and loved it. I'm not much of a dessert person, but had to try something here b/c the offerings are ridiculous (in a good way). We split the Maple Mascarpone Cheesecake. This was eyes-rolling-in-the-back-of-my-head delicious! I venture to say...the best dessert I've EVER had. Bonus points that you can order your coffee in a French Press to go with it! The Service: Service was excellent from the minute we stepped off the elevator and were greeted. Our server was very good at explaining everything, being around but not overbearing and, generally, adding to our good experience. My only complaint is that their wine list doesn't provide any short descriptions to distinguish between the offerings. We told our server what type we were after and she didn't fail with her recommendation. My Jerry Springer Final Thought: This place costs much less that it could or should, considering the entire experience. Great value. It has the whole package and I'll certainly be back.

It was very handy, and was clearly sold at the Military Clothing and Sales Store at the bases we lived at. As I described this product (and my father had more than one), the manager told me it must have been something my father had assembled himself, as if I was too stupid to realize what was clearly a purchased item, and whatever it was, he never had anything like it. Now, regardless of whether he had it, I knew it was a product that could be had, and to be told otherwise was pretty insulting. As I had a little time to kill, I went to another military surplus place, and they knew exactly what I was talking about, but simply said they didn't have it. Well I am so happy that I did. We arrived early 7ish on a Wednesday and it was somewhat empty -- but we live around the corner, so we know that is not usually the case. Our waitress was so sweet ( I Wish I could remember her name). She was very knowledgeable about the menu (which was small, but incredible), and joked with us like an old friend. We have a bad habit of always wanting the same things, but usually one of us will sacrifice and order the second choice so that we can share both...buit not tonight! We both ordered the tartare and the flank steak. OHH but first we had the Oysters which were probably the best oysters that I have had in Philadelphia! Delcious Delicious Delicious! The tartare was great, served a little curried and with housemade chips. The steak was served with marrow...instead of butter...it was like heaven. I never wantde this meal to end. I kid you not. The cheese plate was alright..i wasn't entirely impressed, but I am kind of a snob when it comes to cheese. And to top it off, they brought a little piece of heavenly ganache out with a candle in it for my darling's birthday. Go Now. xooxox

text: I wanted to book a lovely stay for New Years Eve with my boyfriend and sadly our stay was dreadful. It all started with us being placed in a room with a mattress so hard and full of springs it reminded me of a youth hostel-they kindly moved us and apologized that many of their rooms still have old mattresses. As the day progressed, while trying to nap we kept being woken up to the clink clank clink of what sounded like dishes being laid out for an army. Opening the window we realized we were in a new room overlooking the restaurant's kitchen and the clinking and clanking would continue into the night and begin again at 7AM. The janky room heater kept sputtering loudly off and on, we had to turn it off (we'd rather be cold). We also had to completely dismantle the power chords to the entertainment console because the empty fridge turns off and on every five minutes. This "wonderful" night's rest was peppered with neighboring toilet flushing (agree with other reviewers), paper thin walls (ditto again) that do not keep out the noise, and the doorman who we could hear up to our 2nd floor room yelling, "GOOD MORNING" to every patron entering or exiting the Montecito Inn. When I finally fell asleep for the 100th time, I was woken up by a BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP, yep, the alarm was accidently set at an ungodly early morning hour. Thanks Montecito Inn for letting us off the hook for a second night! At least we have a funny story to have for the rest of our lives...alrighty, gotta take a nap, it's exhausting staying here. P.S. their free packet hot cocoa is fabulous! P.S.S. I'm so over the Charlie Chaplin theme.

text: We stayed here for a week. This is our second time staying in a Hotel Indigo - last year we stayed for a week in the West End location. I very very (very very, very very) very much prefer the downtown location (NOT West End) - we were on the 12th floor here and had no complaints about water pressure. The W.E. location had poor pressure, lukewarm water, toilets that refused to flush, sinks that drained slowly/not at all.. We had none of those issues here. The room was beautiful, modern and clean, our floor was quiet. The hotel restaurant was OK. I had a yogurt "parfait" which consisted of about a quarter cup of yogurt with two small pieces of pineapple topping .... .... .... and how much did we pay for it? argh! ..... But the drinks in the bar were tasty and they have nice desserts. The bar hosts writer's rounds nightly, which is a great Nashville touch. The staff is super friendly, attentive and quick. I did wish that we had a fridge/microwave in room, especially since we stayed for a longer period of time. No bathtub either, but I don't mind that so much. The bed was very comfortable (firm, not cushy, which is what I like) and the linens were very clean and fresh. This is a very insignificant thing to complain about, but is a pet peeve of mine: the in-room coffee came with powdered creamer. Not that the in-room coffee was that great to begin with, but powdered creamer just makes my eyeball twitch. A minor complaint, but it makes a difference to have the good liquid stuff, even if the good stuff is still fake chemical-ly milk. TV was fine, lots of channels. The parking blows, 22 bucks a day for valet or 20 for self-park. There is no street parking. They comped us on valet parking, maybe since we were staying with them for a decent length of time, but I'm not sure if that's the official policy or not. Our room was on Union Street, and traffic rarely was noisy enough to be distracting, although there were a couple of ambulances/fire trucks that would scream down the street. We had a nice view of the pretty new City Hall building. The hotel adjoins a somewhat mediocre Starbucks, but there are some decent dining options within walking distance - Varallo's and Provence are reasonably closeby, and then you have some tasties on 2nd avenue (nachos at Buffalo Billiards are my favorite on earth. Also, try the wings at Piranha's or the cozy Beer Sellar.. if you venture down to B'way, there's the BBQ at Jack's.. I could go on forever : ) We lived in Nashville for years before moving to Oregon and I miss the food more than I can communicate in words.) The walk to Broadway for touristy fun is quick and easy. Great experience at the Hotel Indigo downtown!!

text: To anyone from Burlington NJ, the Prince Diner was a staple to your social life. Prices were cheap, and it was always a fun atmosphere, and the vast majority of people who went there loved it, and the staff. On the day it closed, the place was packed until the very end. Some of us even loved it so much we bought shirts off of some of the servers (mine is hanging up in my closet). After months of renovations, the Poseidon Diner emerged, which didn't last long at all, and now it is the Dolphin Diner. The place has cleaned up a bit. It looks more like a restaurant than a diner. There are TVs and flashy interior decorating everywhere- not what a New Jersey diner is supposed to be. The food is expensive for diner food, and the portions are smaller than usual. The quality of the food is nothing to write home about, but it IS a diner. I rarely leave not hungry. The servers don't go the extra mile, and half of them barely speak english- not that it's a bad thing, it's just hard to build a relationship with english speaking customers if your servers don't speak english. They have free WifFi, but I assume most people are in a diner to eat, not surf the web. Long story short, I only go there if I have to, which is what I'd suggest to anyone else.

text: i am not a "mani-pedi" girl. mostly because I can't afford to get one more than twice a year. Spring and mid-summer, usually, as sandals make this a necessity. So the other day, I decided it was time. They weren't busy. It wasn't the end of the night when they'd be rushing to sweep me out the door hastily. I didn't look like a degenerate shmuck, nor an entitled primadonna expectantly reading an InTouch with a yorkie tucked under my arm. I was gracious, happy to be treating myself, and looking forward to that warm massaging chair. That thing NEVER gets tired. So they had no basis to judge me or resent me for being either poor and unable to pay, or rich with a sense of entitlement. My girl didn't look me in the eye, didn't smile, and i'm pretty sure didn't speak english. like AT ALL. not only did she not speak english, she spoke her native language into a cell phone while engrossed in conversation for the entire duration of the pedicure. she had perfected the art of holding the phone with her chin, which was, i admit, impressive. But it totally detracted from my experience. she blazed through all the motions, forgot the razor bit ENTIRELY, and when i asked if she was going to DO the razor (the biggest reason i can't do feet myself is because i need someone else to do all my thick, calloused dancers' feet) she hastily and weakly ran it along the pads on the bottom without even filing it smooth. I felt slighted from the getgo, and it only got worse and worser. my manicure was equally dissatisfying. she was off the phone now, thank god, but just rushing and not being diligent. the whole time i kept one eye on her coworkers, who were much more engaged and careful with their clients. A man had been getting a pedicure, and the woman was actually MASSAGING and scrubbing his whole calf, ankle and foot (there was an actual LATHER). I couldn't believe it. Now, you COULD argue that he bought a spa pedicure and i just bought a standard, but there ISN'T a spa option on the menu. he and i paid the same, and he was being treated like downright royalty. (I could lay a low blow and say something along the lines of "maybe they're just used to catering to men, uh washy washy", but I stay above the belt.) My tip I had planned to give was becoming more minimal with every mistake - and then she cut me to the quick while doing my cuticles - ON 2 NAILS. I bled. And that was the nail in the coffin. After i sat under the dryer, debating, I went to the bathroom and made my decision. I gathered my bags, stood up, put her tip back in my pocket - and walked out the door. I have never done this and at first felt terrible - but I was livid - and so so disappointed. I am never going here again - no matter how inexpensive. I took her tip money and bought myself a veggie chicken salad sandwich and a coffee. And then I was happy - even though my nails looked like poo.

text: Came here last night with my boyfriend after an open bar event a few blocks away. We stumbled our way through the CBD and luckily, Luke had a table ready for us (thank god for flash floods and rainstorms keeping the majority of people home). I'm a fan of the hotel/bank decor, but slippery stone floors and a tipsy rain-soaked me was not a good combination. We sat at a table and immediately ordered wine and appetizers: the rabbit and duck liver pate and a roast beet salad. My Bellini was great, with the fresh peach really resonating, but Daniel was unsatisfied with his wine (it came in a tumbler like Italian wine... weird). The pate was the hit of the night! So smooth and rich and buttery, accompanied with Creole mustard, tiny pickles, and 2 fruit relishes on buttery crisp toast. INCREDIBLE. We literally scraped the cute little glass container out. Restaurant August needs to take a tip on pate from Luke because this was seriously superior. For an entree we shared the moules and frites. Amazing fries, fresh and hot, and a great creamy buttery garlic broth with the mussels (although a few were shriveled and overcooked). At this point we were happily satiated and thus declined dessert... and still, dinner was only $60! I've come before for the oysters and they are great and ESPECIALLY reasonable for happy hour. Their house microbrewed beers are delicious, although the cochon de lait sandwich I tried before was somewhat dry and bland. One of my favorite mid-priced spots for a chill delicious dinner. Can't wait to come back.

text: I visited the park this Saturday with my 17 month old and husband. It was a hot day. We drove from New York City in a car that we paid by the hour to have for this trip. But it was worth it because our baby loves Sesame Street. EXCEPT our experience was BAD. There were some basic things that should be improved to make this a much nicer experience. For the huge expense we paid to visit, it should have been great. And great would have required very little. But instead it was "meh" at best, and I will never recommend this to any of our friends. Instead, I'm going out of my way to tell my friends that I would NOT recommend it. 1. WHERE WERE THE CHARACTERS??!!??!! We arrived at noon. We left at 5. In that time, we saw the Count walking away somewhere, Bert & Ernie with a long line that cut off before our turn, and Cookie Monster & Telly in a different long line that we were actually able to get through. Thats 1 sighting, 1 disappointment, and a mere 1 actual character meeting. There should have been characters everywhere. We should have been greeted by at least 3 characters at the entrance and there should have been so many characters wandering the park that we got to meet them all with ease. Instead, my toddler, who literally lights up with joy and fills with delighted babbles upon meeting a Sesame person, ended up shrieking and crying up and down the street because she got cut off from Ernie, only got to see cookie monster for 20 seconds because of the long line, and never met Abby, Zoey, Elmo, etc etc. Meeting the characters is literally the #1 reason to come to Sesame Place. Everything else they offer is available somewhere else. So disappointing customers in this way is totally unacceptable. 2. Food Access: Was literally horrific. They specifically cater to young children and do not allow food to be brought in to the park. Food should be everywhere and wait times should be nearly nonexistent. I saw a family with 5 kids going through hell. The kids were starving and dad was trying to keep them calm at the table, but mom didnt make it up with the macaroni and burgers for a good half hour. HALF HOUR! I waited a similar time, at least 20 minutes, to get a burger, chicken sandwich and 2 drinks. The workers are not hustling - they should be! Its a simple menu, they should be churning out the 6 options available like a well oiled machine. One of the registers on my side didnt bother to tell people he was open, just watched everyone assume he was closed and funnel into one line. I called him out on this, and he just sad "ooh." Ridiculous. Later we needed to buy milk for the baby's bottle, and I was told that instead of going to the refrigerated drink unit by the register to grab a drink and pay, I had to stand in the looooong food line. Why?! I just needed milk. My baby can't wait 20 to 30 minutes so I can stand in a Sesame Place food line that would put communist food ration lines to shame. Character Show: We were able to see the Elmo's Live Show. Elmo didn't stay after the show to meet the kids. I understand that pictures take time, but they can put a sign saying no pictures, and let the kids give him a high five or a hug as they leave. Again, this whole park is about kids getting to see their Sesame friends up close and personal. Total failure to make that happen. Clearly I'm a dissatisfied customer. If you have huge coupons and live nearby or if your kids dont really care about Sesame Street (just want to play on some jungle gyms and water slides) then its fine. But if you want to meet some characters, see shows and get access to reasonable concession options, skip it! The Sesame area at Busch Gardens Tampa is good though.

text: We had high expectations given the first impression upon walking in (and by the Yelp reviews), but E&E disappointed on almost every note. We went early on a Tuesday and were seated right away. The interior is modern and hip, with cozy tall (overhead) round booths. The service was friendly and not overbearing. We started with the ahi sashimi appetizer and iceberg wedge. The sashimi was well seared, but was drizzled with a wasabi based sauce and another mild chili red sauce. It looked great, but I could have done without the sauces. Ahi tuna is a delicate taste, and was washed out by the oversaucing. The seaweed salad and ginger on the side were a nice and proper touch. The iceberg wedge was simply an iceberg lettuce head, quartered, and served with a blue cheese dressing and some grape tomatoes. The dressing was notable, but otherwise the dish was not. Our dinner specials came with caesar salads (the house salad-- which I found odd). I ordered mine with dressing on the side, and I'm glad I did. What came out was some chopped lettuce (romaine), with a smattering of grated parmesan, and (inexplicably) some multicolored tortilla strips. The dressing in the side cup was unappetizing, looking like oil mixed with mayonnaise. We should have taken the salads as a bellwether. When the entrees arrived, they were plated well, but many little things added up to a hot (overcooked) mess. The lobster tail was chewy and overcooked. There was some kind of breaded chunk atop the lobster tail reminiscent of a "Rockefeller" treatment, which tasted fine, but I didn't get why it was there. The sweet potato mash had apples mixed in, and was cloying (sweet potatoes don't need another fruit to make them taste good; take a cue from the name, chef!) The crab cake was the best part, with lump crabmeat, but it had the same drizzle as the sashimi app. Most of the spices and flavors they used were just "off." Too much going on on the plate. The veg on both entrees was a mix of steamed broccoli, julienned carrots in some kind of sweet sauce, and edamame (flavorless and out of place on the plate). The flounder piccata, while simpler, was also overcooked. It had the piccata sauce, but also some kind of smoky barbeque sauce drizzled alongside it. The corn mashed potatoes had a similar "off" spice/seasoning. The burger was cooked medium well (correctly) and the fries reminded me of Checkers fries, with an extra crispiness to them (perhaps finished in a convection oven). The shift manager walked by once during the early part of the meal to ask how everything was. He barely broke his stride to actually wait for our reply, so at that time we did not have a composed answer. A few minutes later, we did let the server know about the overcooked dishes, and he offered one free dessert. We opted for the bread pudding, which was on the special menu. It was fine, but served in an overly sweet caramel sauce. To top it off, there is a compulsory 15% gratuity "for your convenience" (that was actually printed on the check). There aren't many places in the Langhorne area with a good beer selection. Hulmeville Inn and Isaac Newtons are the only ones I know of in the area that are worth visiting for the beer. Well you can add Miller's Ale House to the list! They have 35 taps and bottled beers too. They have tons of your usuals but they also have a good selection of local breweries and they do a great job on keeping seasonals on tap. They also have some really great deals on beer, $2.95 Leinenkugels all day! I think the only "full price" beer I had was a Hooegarden. They also had a really cheap deal on pitchers of Miller Lite ($5) or $2 bottles all day. If I still lived in the Levittown area this would be my new local sports bar. I'm out in Jamison now but when I'm back in the area I'll definitely be stopping into Miller's Ale House.

text: My wife had booked this room WAY in advance and had booked a double room, non smoking. When we got there to check in, all they had available was a smoking room. The beds were comfortable, the AC worked, it did the trick. The main problem was with house keeping during our stay. We stayed here for almost two weeks and our room was actually CLEANED once. Every other time, all they did was make the bed, pick up the towels and that was it. we had to request new towels several times because they would take ours and not replace them (or not leave enough), the drain in the tub was slow so it meant that it was clogged. I asked for it to be fixed but it never was, so I had to do it myself. They never replaced soap or shampoo unless we asked and the longer we stayed, the worse the smoke smell became. By the time we left, all the clean clothes in our bags smelled like cigarettes. They don't have room service and all the takeout spots nearby close early so make sure you make time to have dinner somewhere before you go back to your room. I had to work remotely the entire time we were in town and the wireless internet there (although it was free) was absolutely worthless. I had to go around the corner to the Marriott lobby to work from there. The pool was way too warm and salty for some reason. It was a bust. Long story short, stay somewhere else.

And if I had wanted cold mashed potatoes, I would have ordered them. The French onion soup was like someone put some vinegar in some water, cut some onions up in it, and cooked it for a little while. My apologies to the French for using their name in the same breath as that soup. I heard a rumor that the Reuben is edible. So, based on someone else's advice, if you have to go, and if you have to eat, apparently get a Reuben, the onion rings, and a milkshake. text: Breakfast is a passion of mine. For 92 straight weeks I only ate breakfast. I have had everything breakfast has to offer. I came. I saw. I kicked breakfast's ass. Breakfast is comfort food. I remember being six years old, and despite being locked in a steel box out in the sun for 3 days...it was my fault...I coughed during The 1.98 Beauty Pageant...an offense I wouldn't have taken so lightly, but my parents...well...not technically parents...were much more kind than I..and they would slip pancakes under the metal door. I would use half of them to sooth the heat blisters and half would be the sweet treat I craved to eat so badly. My only friend. Now as an old man I think back on those happy moments during breakfast and smile. When forcefully relocated to this area I searched out the best breakfast joints I could find. Most were not good. Most caused me great pain. Most were very quick to throw someone out for standing on their chair screaming "I'll never let you destroy my memories you bastards!" Some people are very sensitive. As I was being dragged screaming and foaming at the mouth out of a lesser eatery someone suggested I go to Nudy's...then the obligatory pinprick and complete darkness. A few weeks after my release I went to Nudy's for a hearty breakfast, and I was not disappointed. Since my first time eating there I have gone back several times. Everything from their omelets to their pancakes are terrific. They have an excellent selection geared towards virtually everyone. People who want the sweet pancakes with syrup and whipped cream will be in their own personal heaven...people who just want a great protein omelet with their choice of meat and cheese will be thrilled...and people who want something more sophisticated like eggs benedict or a great hollandaise sauce will be very, very happy. The best part of Nudy's, and the thing that keeps me coming back is the service. Sure, it is cheap. Sure, it is good, Sure, they use great ingredients...but the friendly and accomidating service is what will always keep me coming back.

text: What a fun restaurant! However, the food is very overrated by my fellow Yelpers. Like others have written, Marrakesh is a Moroccan restaurant. I can't vouch for the authenticity, as I have never been to Morocco or eaten at any other Moroccan restaurant, for that matter. Supposedly it's now trendy to force your customers to knock at the front door-I just think it's cute. Not necessary, but I won't hate on you for making me do it. As for the dining experience: no utensils, no napkins, very dark, very cozy and on soft padded surfaces. Food is a set 7-course meal. Reading these other Yelp reviews, it sounds like the same 7-course meal is offered every time (with some options for some of the courses). Marrakesh serves a very different ethnic taste. Reminiscing back to the meal, it wasn't spectacular, but the atmosphere coupled with the novelty makes it a worthwhile experience. Yes, the whole chicken dish is tender to the point of meat-falling-off-bones. But it tastes like any other cooked-for-a-long-time-in-sauce chicken. Yes, the shish-kabob is stacked with chunks of meat. But it tastes like something I could have slapped together on my own home grill (and theirs isn't as tasty, to be honest). In summary-come to Marrakesh for the fun, but don't come back for the food. My logic is that if you're using the same 7-course set meal every day for who-knows-how-long, that's not a master chef back there in the kitchen, just a seasoned one.

text: Alright, alright. I've already reviewed one Stephen Starr place today, so we'll skip the rant about business tactics and degradation of food costs. Let's begin... *Makes fart noise with mouth* A disappointment is what this place was to me. For all its showiness and stylish creepiness (2 way bathroom mirrors looking into the bathrooms??), it just could measure up to other places nearby. Let's look at the positives, first. 1.) The Look Physically, it's a damn beautiful space. It's like a 50's diner that took all of its best qualities with it into a time machine bound for the 2000's. The colors all pop and exude fun. The shag carpeting on the ceiling at the bar is interesting and eye-catching. Most of all, the seating stands out. If you're lucky enough to grab one of the tables with swinging chairs, do so without hesitation. It'll help take your mind off the food later. 2.) The Service Fast and attentive without being over-bearing, the service staff really excels here. I did have problems with some plate crowding, but its my own damn fault for ordering so much food after I requested a 2-top just for a swingy chair. 3.) The Drinks Continental Midtown boasts a very creative drink list. An entire section of the menu is devoted to specialty martinis. I know it's been harkened to a lot on this site, but the Buzz Aldrin is an amazing concept for a drink. Wow, that was glaringly positive. I guess it's time for an appropriate counterbalance. Here comes my lone negative... 1.) The Food Now, it is entirely possible that I picked each of the worst items on the menu, but even so, they should still be decent to even be on the menu. To start, I had the humus with pita. With such a simple dish, I've become accustomed to chefs trying to play with the humus a little. Truffles, garlic, and red pepper come to mind. But Continental Midtown offers a plain garbanzo bean humus, something I could purchase in a supermarket for a lot less than this restaurant's pricing. Next, I went with the crispy calamari salad, having had great experiences with fried calamari in my time. What I got was unpleasant. The menu didn't lie, it was served over arugula with sesame oil among other embellishments. However, the smell of the sesame and the taste of the peanut oil the calamari was fried in overpowered everything else. I'm sorry, but your fryer oil should never overpower the taste of what it is frying. In the end, my dish smelled like a skunk and tasted liked peanuts. Finally, I decided to end with the menu's sole sushi plate, which I think was a spicy tuna roll (it's been a while). This was actually very good. But that in itself leads to more questions, like: Why does a non-Japanese restaurant fail in every piece of its menu except for its only sushi roll? Sheesh. Sorry about the rant, but this is my first overtly negative review, and I had a lot to complain about. Overall, Continental Midtown fails in my eyes. It is aesthetically pleasing, but the fact of the matter is that I decided to go out to eat; to have someone else prepare a meal for me knowing full well it would cost me. Tragically, the preparer of this meal did not hit the mark. At the end of the day, what is a restaurant if it can't feed people into satisfaction?

text: I seriously don't get the popularity of this place. I keep thinking I'm missing something so I go back, and no,....I can't find a thing I'm missing. This bar opened a couple years ago (?) intending to be a dive bar with interesting and better than dive bar food. And when you go in, they clearly succeeded with the dive bar feel. They failed with the food. It's not that the food is bad -- it's just exceedingly mediocre. Originally the signature dishes were the curly dog on a bun and the meatloaf. The curly dog was fine, but then it's just a big hot-dog on a bun. The meatloaf was dry and blah. They have since dropped the meatloaf as an entree but you can still get it served as sliders. The hamburgers are fine but typical bar hamburgers. The hummus is interesting and very good. the juke box is great but the times I've been there the music was so loud I couldn't talk to the people at my table. That's great for a club, but when I'm eating with people, I like to talk to them. One final point: They refuse to serve Anheuser Busch products. I wouldn't care if their point was to only serve premium micro brews -- but they have no problem with mass produced beers including PBR and Miller products both of which are fine. The exclusion of AB is offensive for one simple reason -- growing up in the St Louis area there was always 3 or 4 kids in my class whose dad worked at the brewery. The brewery has supported thousands of local families with high wages for generations and spent untold millions in our community. This is the worst kind of snobbery because it has nothing to do with quality and has everything to do with putting a finger in the eye of the community. I prefer Pepsi to Coke, but if I open a restaurant in Atlanta I'm serving Coke. There are lots of much better places to go including businesses who respect their community. And to be clear -- neither I nor anyone in my family has ever worked for AB or any business directly supported by AB.

text: Five stars isn't enough for this gem. Rumba gets infinity stars. I've been in stuck in Tennessee for a while now and have been subjected to some of the worst food in my entire life. On our second round, we did the coconut shrimp which came with this yummy relish.. and one of the flatbreads. This is where it got interesting. The flat bread was made with blue cheese, bacon and grapes. My tastebuds threw a party in my mouth and my urge to tongue wrestle with my date was getting stronger! Oh, and that's also because Sunday nights is their wine night. All wines are half off. So we had a bottle of cabernet too. We finished our meal off with the tres leches dessert. text: I went here with about 5 or 6 friends to celebrate. I was the only woman in our group and we still can't tell if they had a better time, or if I did. There was a $20 cover, but it was worth it. I'll tell you from personal experience that not every strip club in this area does that. I was pleasantly impressed with the set up. It's pretty spacious with comfortable chairs from the stage area on back. Although smoking is allowed indoors, the layout is such that it's not overwhelming, unless you walk into it, or are next to the person smoking. The dance area isn't bad, either. They're velvet-y booths that are tall enough, to offer you enough privacy that the person next to you can't peep at the dance you're getting. Their website has current dance prices, but keep in mind there's a $5 entry fee to the private area each time you go back there. There was a pretty good selection of girls, although I wouldn't have minded seeing some bigger butts. I'm not complaining about what they had, though. Kennedy and Princess were my group's favorites. They were quite live and I liked the way Princess moved. I spent entirely too much money there, but definitely plan on going back a few more times. I'd recommend it to anyone planning a birthday celebration or bachelor/bachelorette party, or someone just looking to unwind.

text: Wow, there are over 400 reviews on this place. My conclusion: I never ever will come back here again. I've been here twice and each time, it was a 1-star experience so I'm going to take my 20s elsewhere. If you are a true beer enthusiast, this place is a great place to try new beers (if you can stand all the rowdy students--I don't know why this place attracts loud drunks; is that why they card no matter what? or what looks like the strangest mix of people I've ever seen in a popular downtown restaurant). Last night, I tried the Hercule stout which was decent ($8) and my bf had the Oaked Arrogant Bastard, which we both loved. The service was good considering our waitress promptly returned the watery and mushy mussels we got and came back with a piping hot, much more flavorful batch that was correctly cooked. The moules frites are the absolutely worst I've ever had (ok, not fair to compare them to ones I've had in Belgium, but even in the US, this is as bad as it gets). Could the mussels be any tinier? Could the sauce be any greasier (there was a cm-thick layer of oil on top of our broth, and even when we tried to mix it up with spoons, most of the ominous layer would not dissipate)? There is no flavor to the red light broth except a spicy kick, which isn't hard to do, you throw in some hot peppers. I cannot believe they would serve their mussels in such a flavorless broth. My bf has made moules frites at home and his sauce is a thousand times more flavorful. It also seems that they don't cook the mussels specifically for your dish. The pomme frites are good but they are doused in salt, cut up in tiny little pieces and they give you all of 10 fries. The bourbon mayonnaise is delicious but like I said to my bf, how do you mess up mayonnaise? I looked over at the other tables and there were plenty of burgers and sandwiches being served. I hope they are friggen out of this world because I don't know how people would waste their $20 on this place. There aren't fries at Audrey Claire, but try their mussels (or even moules frites at Nodding Head). Their broth is excellent--I've tried it 4 times and I've never gotten any undercooked, disgusting watery and mushy mussels, not once. I've been to a million and one moules frites places in Manhattan and other US cities and I'm not saying they are all excellent, but Monk's has been by far the worst moules frites I've ever had.

text: I love Holt Renfrew...in theory. Everything in here is so expensive yet beautiful, that every time I come in, I am on the verge of tears. That's why I don't come here often. The first level of Holt Renfrew is reserved for make-up, skin care, shoes, jewelry, bags and other accessories. Some of the skin care and make-up brands represented are Bobbi Brown, La Mer, YSL, Prescriptives and Laura Mercier. Every brand is assigned its own counter and customer service representative. In general, women who work at cosmetics counters are friendly and helpful, and only once or twice have I experienced an unpleasant attitude on their behalf. As you move along, you will see shoes section. Louboutin, Blahnik, Prada, Choo, Weitzman is all I will say :) Except that occasionally the shoes go on sale. The bags, wallets and purses section is what makes me weak in the knees. I see designer purses as an art which at this moment in my life I cannot afford. The inventory changes quite often and there always seem to be purses on sale. The second level of the store is for clothes. Beautiful and expensive clothes. Some of the brands are Max Mara, LAMB, Diane von Furstenberg, Burberry and Cinzia Rocca. There are also more affordable brands such as Theory and Vince. Jeans by Free People and Paige often go on sale, so if you can't afford to buy a beautiful jacket for $500, you can at least cheer yourself up with the fantastic pair of jeans. Overall, after visiting Holt Renfrew in Calgary I realize that for some reason many brands don't make it to Edmonton. Calgary's store has the selection that is more ample. The underwear selection is limited to two brands: Hanky Panky and Elle McPherson. There are fantastic cashmere robes the only downside of which is that they cost around $400. In close proximity to underwear you will find Wolford tights. I splurged on one pair, and I can't praise Wolford enough. Holt Renfrew has a men's clothes section. text: Don't stay at the Best Western South Coast Inn! We are posting this here to warn you and we are filing a complaint with the Better Business Bureau as no one should be subjected to what we endured. This is a hotel where the owner and the manager have demonstrated they don't care about their customers. During our second stay at this hotel we were in a room where the toilet wouldn't flush. It wouldn't flush even if the toilet was empty. We had to call the front desk twice to get it fixed, and each time they sent a new maintenance person, and each time we were told the problem was fixed. When it wasn't fixed for the third time, I called the front desk in frustration. After being put on hold for a long time, the front desk person offered us the use of the bathroom in a room about 10 doors down from ours. We couldn't just move into that room because it had only one double bed. We were four people in a suite with a king and a sofabed and no working toilet. No other rooms were available for that night. I couldn't imagine getting up in the middle of the night and walking outside in my pajamas to use the bathroom. We weren't camping here. We were paying lots of money for a hotel room for four nights. So, I explained how I didn't see how the two rooms could work being so far apart and I said in frustration, "How about just comping us a couple of nights and bringing us a plunger." I added that I had to think about what we were going to do here since we had been told that most hotels in the area were sold out. After a few minutes, I called the front desk back and accepted the offer of the second room for the toilet. We were also offered a new suite room to move to the next day, which we gratefully accepted. We thought everything was all resolved. We would have a new room with a working toilet and everything would be fine. .....but it was not to be. We were meeting friends for dinner so we had to leave. When we returned, the same front desk person knocked on our door and told us maintenance had snaked the toilet so it was working now. I wish maintenance had done that after our first call. We thanked him and gave him back the keys to the second room. I was told to talk the front desk the next morning about the situation. The next morning I talked to a new desk clerk about the nonworking toilet and he said he knew about it and the owner had heard and we were told we were required to vacate the premises immediately that morning and we were never going to be allowed to stay there again. I was in shock. We have been staying at hotels on a regular basis, including many Best Western's, with no problems. And during our prior stay at this hotel the front desk person said our file said "really nice people" and how we must have made a great impression. Now, because we were frustrated that we were in a room without a working toilet, we were told we were required to leave. It didn't make sense. We still had two nights on our reservation. This new clerk told us that last night's front desk person relayed to the owner that I had demanded to be compensated for two nights when all I did was ask as a suggestion in frustration. The desk clerk was apologetic and made excuses for the owner telling us he was under stress because of the renovations and also how the main computer system had gone down that night. We asked to talk to both the hotel manager and the hotel owner but we were told neither could be reached and the situation wouldn't change even if they could be reached. There was apparently no way to get this miscommunication undone. He was sympathetic and he did comp us $30 which we appreciated, but there was no way we could connect to the two decision makers, the hotel manager and the hotel owner to get the situation fixed. This is not the way you treat a customer. No one talked to us except the front desk person who was accusing us of demanding something we only asked for in frustration and as a suggestion. Plus, shouldn't a hotel do something more when your toilet doesn't work? The broken toilet wasn't the only problem. The cold water at the faucet only turned off at a precise point that took a while to find. The shower had very low water pressure. And, the next morning, the toilet wouldn't flush again. Plus, we heard another customer complain about how a hotel staff person walked in on them in their room really early in the morning. In the end, the owner did us a favor. We found Pacifica Suites. It is closer to our Goleta destination. The toilets work and work and work!! The rooms are much cleaner. The breakfast is better. The people are nicer. And we are very happy to give them our business - we have many trips we will be making each year to Goleta. Do yourself a favor and don't stay at the Best Western South Coast Inn.

text: I think I may have scared our server at Zinburger. Not that a table of six highly boisterous people walking in toward the tail end of the night on July 4th wouldn't be intimidating... I think it was more so my pointed questions about how food was prepared, whom the executive chef was, whether the restaurant was in a restaurant group, and if they had a beer sommelier that really threw him off. Zinburger has this very contemporary look, with lots of exposed metal moldings, simple clean lines, a very open dining room, and a number of wall-mounted flat panel TVs. As the name would indicate, it's a mash-up between a wine bar and an upscale burger joint, with most burgers rolling around the $10 range. Not much for a DCer to bat an eyelash at (hello, Central, I'm talking about you) but definitely not cheap by Tucsonian standards. Between the lot of us, we ended up trying many different burgers, and the boy got the seared ahi salad (beautiful and tasty - I'm glad they brought the dressing on the side... it would have been a bit much poured on it). My Samburger was done up just medium - great and juicy beef patty with a slice of cheese melted on top. Although the menu mentions that it's served with Thousand Island, I didn't really notice. What got my attention was the savory smoky bacon on top. Mmm! The only garnish with the burger were three slices of pickles (which I nibbled on in between bites of meaty joy). Even before I bit into my burger, I was already a little tipsy from my draft Sierra Nevada - they have a number of great microbrews on tap! Who does wine with burger? Not that I disapprove - I just find it much more satisfying with a cold one. And apparently so did everyone else in my party. Plus, our fries came out as quasi-appetizers. Sweet potato chips were meh. The yogurt sauce was good, but they need to be a little thicker so you can actually taste any sweet potato. Double truffle fries were typical truffles frites with truffle aioli. Surprising for Tucson, but not as good as Poste's in DC. Zucchini fries were the winner for me - cover in parmesan, these little nibbles were a mite crispy, but very tender when you bit into them. The Ranch dressing became dangerous the more I imbibed. Don't forget to check out the interestingly decorated restrooms before ditching out of Zinburger. Ladies - ever wanted to know what it feels like to be hounded by the paparazzi? Wonder no longer, just go and take a whiz!

text: Came here with my Vietnamese girl (Ha) after finding out the local Italian restaurant (California Pasta) was shut-down. Boy did I wish it wasn't. The first thing I noticed was the broth, it wasn't clear and smelled like Miso. The broth is the single-most important component in Pho, and this one was an epic failure. For $9, which is insane for Pho, I expected much better. I guess I was paying for the nice plates the Pho was served in? Ha wasn't thrilled with her Rice Vermicelli with grilled beef either. Noodles were dry even with the addition of Fish Sauce. All in all the total came out to $40 + tip. I think Santa Barbarans need to head down to Westminster, CA (with cash since most places down there are cash only) and be amazed at the Authenticity of Vietnamese cuisine there. text: There are a few rules one should always follow: -Never get involved in a land war in Asia -Never eat Mexican food in Middle America. -Never eat Korean food in Nashville. I went in here with high expectations; my friend had come here before for sushi, so I expected that the Korean food would be even better as the place is *run by Koreans*. Alas, my hopes were dashed to the ground and stomped all over. The bulgogi was sweet. I know that it's supposed to be sweet - but it's not supposed to taste like sugar. The meat quality was poor; poorer than the quality that I got at rest stops in South Korea, and that's saying a lot. The kimchi.... Oh, what to say about the kimchi. It was pickled sweet, and it had LOTS of reddish sauce dumped all over it. The bean sprouts were good, but bland. The cucumbers were spicy, sweet, and bland. The broccoli was decent, but also bland. *sigh* My one foray into Japanese was the edamame and that was both overcooked on the outside (WAY too hot!) and undercooked on the inside. I was wondering if it had been freezer burnt, and then tried to be salvaged, it is was so bad. The service was pleasant enough, though our waiter was new and couldn't tell us much about some of the options. I'll never want to come back to this place, but if you do and want to try the Korean: on the way out, I saw the ethnic Koreans eating bibimbap & seafood soup. Presumably those are their specialties. I have no desire to ever come back and find out for sure.

text: Went here on Saturday October 9 after a round of golf. Was looking for a late lunch with 3 hungry lugs and a cold beverage. As we entered we were directed to a table near the window facing the street which already had 2 large baskets of tortilla chips on it. I remarked off hand "Hey, how long have those been sitting there getting stale" to which the waiter remarked "No Senor...I saw you coming so I put them out for you"...only problem is that 10 minutes passed and we still didn't have any salsa, despite trying to flag down several staff. So, we get the cashier gal to bring us salsa and shag down our waiter, who took drink orders and then disappeared for another 10 minutes once he returned with an ice tea. Finally, after delivering 2 beers and a margarita the slippery little guy left us again and never came back. One of my more vocal diners in our group by this point was fuming. He shagged the cashier over and demanded that the waiter get over for our order. He shows up, all indignant that he was pulled away from his one other table (the place really was not that busy at 2 p.m.) and at this point my buddy is berating him about taking up his time and if he's too busy to wait on us we can pay for our drinks and leave, etc. They waiter is embarrassed, but deserving of the tongue-lashing. The only problem now is we're all worried about what might happen to our food behind closed doors. It turns out, we were right to worry. The food was horrible. I mean, inedible. Having just played a round of 18 in the late summer heat, we were parched and starved. None of us enjoyed our meal. The steak chimichanga was a brick-sized load of chewy, flavorless flesh and beans. I love a good steak chimi. This was bland and yuck. The refried beans and rice on the side were afterthoughts that remained on the plate after a small taste of each. The tamales were equally gross and the soft tacos were soggy because of the shredded chicken and beef seemed to come out of the can. Overall, I am in the doghouse with my friends because I mistakenly took them to Mariachi's thinking it was Margarita's, which is a few blocks away. My bad. I can not ever imagine another circumstance where I would willingly or unwillingly visit Mariachi's again. If the people of Belleville like it, good for them. For me, never again!

text: As much as I hate to say it, I have to admit that this Portland Brew is a step up from the one on the East Side. I used to frequent the 12th Ave. Portland Brew back in my Lipscomb days (yes...believe it or not I am an alumnus), and it was always a great spot to stop in for a sandwich and a brief moment of peace. I didn't get many of those over at Lipscomb...sandwiches OR moments of peace. The booths are nice and very isolated, and the staff was always extremely warm and fun to flirt with. I admittedly don't visit the old West Side Brew as much as I once did, but from what I can tell, not much has changed. I've always thought Portland Brew has some of the better coffee in the city, and this location actually has staff and food that are equally impressive. As I was conjuring up the next bit of my enlightening diatribe about Portland Brew, a memory came back to me. I actually ate dinner at this location immediately after my college graduation. My friends and family had all left and planned on meeting up with me later, and I decided to grab a sandwich at Portland Brew and reflect a bit. I ordered a large mocha and a turkey sandwich and had an introspective moment in one of their secluded booths. It was one of the loveliest and most placid moments I've ever had. text: My memory is a little fuzzy - as to exactly what we had at commanders, however, it's not fuzzy to the point where I don't remember that the meal (whatever we had) was absolutely fantastic from start to finish. Not a single meal could be deemed bad, we were three girls on a mission to stuff our faces despite bikini season, and we did it proud. Commaner's Palace was slightly out of the way, but were we glad we made it for dinner. The establishment itself is classy, and elegant, sort of like the place you would imagine your soon to be fiancee to be meeting your republican senator father for the first time - or something along the lines.
