text: I travel to New Orleans frequently on business, so I have stayed at almost all the hotels around Canal Street, and this one was my least favorite, for several reasons, the most notable one being that I felt cheated and swindled. I must have caught this hotel on a series of very 'off' days, because I found it to be less than satisfactory in almost every way, yet I see many positive reviews from other guests. Perhaps they got more for their money than I did. My room was not properly air conditioned, and no matter what I seemed to do, I could not get comfortable. The hotel sets a limit on the temperature so that the unit cannot be set below 65 degrees, and when it's over 90 with humidity at night in New Orleans, that simply will not do. If I pay for a room I expect to be at least reasonably comfortable, and I did not sleep well even one night there. Little things began to add up to big irritations. I would put money in the vending machines to buy bottled water and they would spit out Mountain Dew- then after wasting several dollars trying again I would try to order from room service, only to be further disappointed. And questionable fees seemed to follow every single interaction with staff, or any attempt to utilize the facilities I had already paid for. The last straw was when I went to check out and they tried to charge me for using the gym- I had walked in to check it out, and promptly left after being informed they make additional charges EVERY time a guest uses the gym. They tried to charge me for walking in and LOOKING at the facilities. Then they tried to charge me for a series of mini bar items I never consumed that were missing from the fridge since before I checked in. When they put me in the cab to the airport the driver quoted me a flat rate, and then waited until we got to the airport to inform me he had no change. Even a fool could see that the entire operation was less than professional, and lacking a significant amount of integrity. These types of petty scams for nominal hidden or misleading fees are unacceptable. I would not stay at this hotel again, nor would I rec commend it. "Fool me once, shame on you"....it won't happen twice with this hotel.

text: This is solely about the AYCE Dim Sum special. We came here Saturday night since I've been wanting to try out the 13.95 AYCE Dim Sum special. First off, the place was SLAMMED. We were in line for about 10 minutes waiting for a table, as the tables were completely full. After being seated, it took almost ten minutes to get our drinks, which were ordered as we were being seated. My first round of Dim Sum came out pretty quickly, about ten minutes or so, but was missing an order of spring rolls. Not a huge deal--I figured I'd order it again on the next round. Our server was busy to the point where I had to get up and got my own sauces, which, for the record, I was fine with. If you'd rather sit there waiting for the obviously swamped server to come back around to your table than to get up and get it yourself... well then I think you deserve to be sauceless, my friend. 100 percent without sauce. After I'd polished off the first round, I had to walk around the restaurant to try to track down the server in order to get another order sheet. Filled it out quickly and thrust it at him as he rushed by to another table. I suspect that had I not done that, it would have taken five or ten more minutes for him to get back and pick it up. The second (and as it turned out, final) round of dim sum came out quicker than the first round. Turns out it came out faster because it was undercooked a bit, as well as saturated with grease. It was as if the oil temperature was too low, so the oil just soaked the food rather than cooking it crisply. Within five minutes, the oil had leeched out of the pot-stickers and crab rangoon, pooling in the bottom of the tray the dim sum was sitting on. It was pretty rough going from there, and I only got through about half of the remaining food before I couldn't do anymore. Luckily this place isn't anything like Sushi Pier 2, where they watch over your shoulder and ring you up full price for each individual roll you don't finish entirely, so it wasn't an issue that I didn't finish everything on the tray. Out of everything I tried on the dim sum menu, only two items struck me as being noteworthy. First, the shrimp and pork siu mai was loaded with shrimp, which was cooked to perfection. And while I'm sure that all shrimp is magically cooked to perfection in the bay area (just like everything else is... I think the bay area fairies must fly around sprinkling 'perfect food' dust on everything there--at least according to a ton of fuck-tard bay area yelpers anyway)... finding shrimp cooked so well in Reno tends to be a rarity, so it's worth mentioning. Second, the crab rangoon had actual crab in it, and not "krab flavored juice" or whatever these other places in town try to get away with. I can say I probably won't be doing the dim sum again, but I'll be definitely back in here soon for some regular menu items.

text: $9 for a great, filling AND healthy meal? SIGN ME UP! Oh and did I mention its BYOB? It's great in the winter because it really warms you up. You can order soft tofu stew/soup with beef, seafood, mushrooms, kimchi and pork, or you can mix all of them into one! They come in a variety of spicyness ranging from plain to so-spicy-that-the-stew-is-purple (careful of this one because it'll come out the way it looked when it went in). They come out in these clay pots and are still bubbling when it's brought to your table (this is the perfect time to drop in that raw egg they give you!). You also get a stone pot full of white rice to accompany the soup/stew. The korean side dishes are tasty too! The spicy cucumber really settles the hot temperature of the tofu soup. For the non tofu eaters, this place will make you into a tofu eater! If not, there's a few other dishes like Glass noodles, Korean short ribs and seafood pancakes, which are all tasty but not their specialty. Service is quick and if it's not attentive enough, there's a little call button (sounds like a door bell) on each table. There's a parking lot which, when packed is a pain. I usually (safely) make my own spot in the lot (yeap, I'm THAT gal) or I park in the street, which there is always plenty of. The waiters/tress' speak English, Korean and one of them even speaks Chinese! Awesome!

text: Once, I got a massage at an "express-spa" at the Philadelphia Airport. Yeah, the idea was good in theory - but I pretty much got fleeced for getting patted on the back for 20 minutes. I checked in on the first floor by the not-so friendly receptionist, then sent to the 2nd floor where I was supposed to be "taken care of" by the "host" - that didn't happen, so when the esthetician finally found me, she took me to disrobe in the tiny treatment room for my facial. Like the massages and manicure I've had before here, I wasn't terribly impressed with it. They used Dermatologica products which was nice, but the experience wasn't calming. The room was the size of a prison cell and the horrible elevator music was turned up to 11. At the end of my treatment, I was given tap water and sent on my way. My go-to rolls are the summer roll and firecracker roll- the former's mango sweetness and latter's jalapeno spiciness each blend perfectly with yellowtail (my favorite fish) to delight my palate every time. Wash everything down with a pitcher of sake sangria and you'll leave a happy camper. Unfortunately, the service leaves a little to be desired. I come here relatively frequently, and most of the time things go pretty smoothly. On the off days, though... I had a lunch where it took nearly an hour to get my bill settled after we had finished our meal, and a dinner where over half an hour elapsed between the appetizer and entrée service. text: I am in full agreement with the previous poster's assessment on Coquette. The food was absolutely on target but the service, specifically the timing was a bit off. I went with the fiance and we had planned on having a low-key, slow, drunken dinner to give the place a try. I have to say that I love the decor of the building, especially the set-up. We were ushered over to a table and immediately presented with a pretty thoughtful drink menu and wine list. I, of course, went with a Sazerac just get the mood going and try to catch the vibe of the place. It was delicious, maybe even one of the better ones I've had in a long time (certainly good enough for two of them!). She got the special drink of the night, a champagne ponchatoula strawberry cocktail. Let me tell you, that thing sang in your mouth, delicious! The first course came out quickly; she got the soft-shelled crab and I got the pork belly rillettes. Hers was juicy, crispy, fresh; mine was savory, fatty, delicious, especially when paired with the sour cherry compote or the dijon that was provided on the plate. Got another Saz at that point, then about 5 minutes after they took our plates from the apps, the entrees came out. I got the cobia with bacon, onions, and peas. It was perfectly grilled, hot and well-seasoned. I especially loved the way the sweet onions, salty bacon, and fresh peas played off of each other. She got the redfish with some sort of pea puree on a bed of crawfish risotto. It was just as good as mine, as buttery and delicious and redfish should be, and the risotto was freakin' divine. I would like to point out at this time that the kitchen obviously really enjoys the fact that peas are a very fresh and very delicious ingredient right now, because they used fresh peas in 3 out of the 4 dishes that we ordered. This was definitely a good thing at this place. Also, I ordered a white burgundy to go with the fish and it came out stingingly cold and perfectly complimented everything. This place made me happy but they definitely could use some work on the time. I mean, I definitely would've had at least a few more drinks had they slowed things down and let us take our time. That being said, I definitely will be adding this to my list of place to eat at again!

text: How can you not love a resort that celebrates Elvis' birthday every year? The irreverence factor alone makes it well worth a visit. Located at the top of Mt. Rose Highway, this resort sits halfway between Reno and Lake Tahoe. This means spectacular views of both the lake and the desert, depending where you are. Terrainwise, this place is more intermediate when the Chutes are not open. When they are, however, it means access to some of the steepest lift served terrain around. Mt. Rose has no lodging on site, no spas, and no real amenities - quite refreshing in this age of villages. It also doesn't take itself too seriously, and doesn't have aspirations of resort development. text: MangoMoon is a roomy venue sporting multiple floors. A stocked bar takes up much of the second floor, and draws a healthy crowd. A small upstairs lounge provides a perfect setting for intimate events, with small pillows and a view of the entire restaurant. (Good date spot.) Try Thai-influenced tapas that will catch your eye, from the adventurous grilled pork neck and chicken livers to more familiar favorites like satay skewers, dumplings, and beef jerky with sticky rice. Everything comes in small plates, perfect for nibbling. Personal service is one of MangoMoon's hallmarks. Thanks to bartender Heather, we knocked back shots of Patron XO Cafe - espresso-infused tequila with a kick. Our server shined, meeting our needs, and chef Moon even stopped by to chat! Don't miss their amazingly soothing sea cucumber soup ($6), with an approachable, slight peppery broth. We shared raw oysters ($9), fresh blue-points with a tangy chili-lime dipping sauce, diced garlic, and mint leaves; peppers added color and crispness. To close, we had the Sai Auh (northern Thai-style sausage; $6), full of minced pork with galangal, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, scallions, shrimp paste, and red curry. It had a bit of a bite and wasn't bad. For a side, we had brown rice, but that didn't add to the meal; try the noodles instead. While the concept of Thai tapas doesn't exactly resonate with me - when I want Thai, I want more than a tease - I won't deny that MangoMoon delivers quality service and cooking into an attractive package.

text: Yes, we did do more than eat and drink while we were in town. We went into a few shops and this was my fave. In the window was a chair that had a seat made out of different ties woven together: pretty cool. - Super nice girls working there: very helpful, were there when you needed them to grab you a room or another size, but weren't pressureful, and gave you their opinion when you wanted it. On this alone I'd give the store a high rating, as it's rare to find these days. I go into a lot of great looking stores where I love all of their stuff, but the thrill stops after I look at the price tags and everything--even a tank top--seems to be over $200. Lowlights (my flip side to highlights): - Not everything looked as cute on me as it looked on the hangers. :-O - Sizes and cuts weren't consistent: some mediums fit me and some didn't, but that happens in most places. text: I had to go to the ER this morning, only the third time ever in my life, thank you very much. What can I say, I'm a klutz! The hard and icy snow piled up so high along the streets and parking is pretty crappy, so when you do park along the side and bring your utility vehicle up onto the hard packed snow, do not underestimate your first step out of the truck like I did. Little did I know that under several feet or so of snow was a drain, if I had parked a little further back or forward I would have been fine. Expecting to step onto the hard packed snow, I stepped right out and my left foot and leg went slamming down to the drain grid. At that I then lost my balance and went sideways. I see you laughing, but ouch! It was painful yesterday and last night I could barely sleep it hurt so bad, when I awoke this am. the pain was twice as bad as I tried to apply pressure to the foot. Being the stubborn fool that I am I waited for hubby to leave for work, called my own work and then drove myself to the ER using one foot. Am I your hero? The ER waiting area was empty and I thought joy, joy. Checking in was as quick as a wink and I only waited about ten minutes before being taken back. Yikes why did I come here today? I saw how busy they were and it wasn't even 7:00am, so I said no to a bed that was offered to me and said I was fine in a chair after hearing all beds were full in both the hospital and the ER. During my time there I watched ambulance's bring in patients who were registered right there in the hallways from the stretchers they were brought in on. Some of these patients stayed right there, because there were no rooms left. Maybe they would have moved me along a little faster so they could have had my room, if I had agreed to one. Two hours I waited for a simple foot Xray, it did not even require the ER's time, it was a matter of calling an Xray tech to come and get me. After seeing someone brought in who fell on the ice and get attention right away, I started to get angry, but I started to cry too. I finally said to a Doctor passing by that it has been two hours and no one has seen me and I would like to leave and go elsewhere, since they were so busy. Dr. Jack did not catch his last name, grabbed my wheelchair with fury, swung me around and down corridors in a very rude and malicious way! He was so ignorant in the way he talked to me and handled my wheelchair. Two techs were standing there talking, doing nothing else, had no patients and I was seen right away. They were very nice. Turned out I have torn ligaments and tendons, no broken bones and I'm in a show boot and on crutches for the first time in my life and hopefully the last. They prescribed me heavy duty narcotics, but I'll pass on those. This is the closest hospital to my home, I tend to drive three times as far to go to another hospital, for the couple of times I have had to go. I have heard nothing but horror stories of St. Mary's, but hubby has been admitted here several times and I thought it was okay, not as good as others, but okay. I wonder how they will open up beds in the hospital for the heart attack patients just arriving. Do they go by who could have been released two days a go and their insurance is just being milked? Do they weigh the insurance of the new patients arriving or do they really care about who needs the most care? The way they handled the patients coming in and out was unbelievable. Most were pacing like hello, what is going on here with my care. Instead of standing around for a good half hour talking in huge groups when the shift changes, keep on moving to take the few minutes of care you need to for the many fall victims who came in and the burn victim. Get us in and out to free up your space and time for the seriously ill. I lost two dear friends in this hospital, one was a diabetic who had fallen and was in for injuries and treatment, he ended up with pneumonia and died, another was in after a stroke, he was to be released and go into therapy in two days, he got pneumonia and never did leave. I am not a fan of this hospital. I give kudos to Michelle who fitted me with this awesome blue boot (not) and crutches and taught me how to use the damn things. She was awesome.

text: Gotta love a Portuguese byob in the no libs. I have been eating Portuguese food for years. One of my best friends is Portuguese so I cut my teeth at a few places in Newark. With that being said, I enjoyed my dinner at Koo Zee Doo. Four of us walked into the small, quaint space on N. 2nd. First things I noticed were the open kitchen (plus) and the exposed brick (double plus). We were seated immediately and began to look over the menu. We decided on the shrimp in piri piri, chicken gizzards and the Salada de Cores. I was very happy with all of the appetizers. The shrimp in hot sauce was very flavorful and they prepared the dish with large shrimp, head on (that's where all the flavor is). The sauce was so tasty that I cleaned it up with some bread. The chicken gizzards were served in a small casserole in a delicate sauce. They were soft and very flavorful. The salad was also surprisingly good. It was bursting with flavor from the dressing and the veggies were cut nicely so it wasn't awkward to eat. Nice presentation. For the entrees we chose the rabbit special and the Feijoada de Marisco. The rabbit was awesome. Very rich tasting but not heavy. I definitely ate more of it than I should have. Rabbit tends to be bony by nature so this was just par for the course as far as I was concerned. Once again, some bread was used for sopping up sauce. The seafood and bean stew was prepared well but lacked the "pop" of the other dishes. Don't get me wrong, it was very tasty. It just sort of paled in comparison to the rabbit. Our meal concluded with four of us splitting one dessert. Tarte de Amendôa which was light a flavorful. Just the right amount of sweet after our very savory meal. I will go back to this place. Next time, it's Bife à Portuguesa.

text: 5 stars?...Well I rate by the "It Is what it is" rule...and if you go to Gene's because it is what it is, you'll be getting genuine 5 star fulfillment. One of the more minor post Katrina tragedies was the closing of Verti Martes overnight shift. When I worked there a million years ago, they didn't even have a lock on the door (the day of the French Quarter bloackout, they left a semi-crazy cook in with a hatchet to deter the non-existent looters...but I digress). the lack of late night Verti Marte could crush a drunk Po' boy lovers soul...but there still is Genes. Genes is big and pink and filled with New Orleans, its another place not for the faint of heart...at 3 AM you'll be waiting with gangsters, musicians, surly cops and professional drunks of all shapes...but, yeah, they do all know something. If you rate a Po boy by how greasy it is...how easily the roast beef tries to slither out of the bread with every bite, Genes is the place. Crunchy french bread meets an incredible goopy mayo cheese lube that has the meat sliding all over the place...and at 3 AM, if you can keep it together or not, there is no better taste in town. Roast beef Philly is my choice, but they also have a great hot sausage, and video poker to boot...obviously you are feeling lucky; you stopped here, didn't you? If thats not enough, the next building over is Gene's daiquiri stand. Worth the short walk from the Quarter any hot afternoon. There's more booze in a large Genes daiquiri then in 5 on bourbon street; and that is before you pay the extra buck for an additional shot of some 190 proof firewater in there. With all the sugar It's like slurpy and crack cocktail, but without having to sell your mommas TV. Visitors to New Orleans, get out of the Quarter and into Gene's and your a step closer to understanding the town.

text: Nobody enjoys a good steak like I do... unfortunately, this was not one. Let's face it, it's gonna taste good, even if I did feel the need to scan the room for my doctor before digging in. Just as unhealthy (and salty) was the Creamed Spinach - think Boston Market's version - with maybe a pinch of Tarragon? Not bad, but clearly nothing special. As for the main event, one of our party ordered the Porterhouse ($42 I believe) and we opted to share the Porterhouse for Two, at $73. We received exactly the same steak, the only difference being that ours had been pre-cut into many little pieces... perhaps to make it appear larger?! Retro theme is one thing, but I haven't needed my mommy to cut my meat for many years now, thanks. While tasty (grilled meat crusted in salt, of course it's tasty), I have never been served a Porterhouse that was as surrounded by grisle... and frankly for $73 I would have expected better. As for those tasty - if not very clever - side dishes, their prices were very much not retro, mostly in the $9 - $12 range, nothing unusual these days but in serving sizes for one, possibly two patrons at the most, absolutely not for the 'whole table' [of four] that our waiter had suggested. While not a bad meal, this is very much not a special meal. Perhaps we are old-fashioned, but I still expect a special meal when spending more than $100 a head. The restaurant will be a huge success for many years, as it has 'Starr' status, but if you are a true old-school carnivore, you might want to give up a bit of the ambience here and opt instead for Fogo de Chao instead, at half the price.

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Fauxdoo 2 in the French Quarter More liquor and random wanderings led us to Marie Laveau's, and, throwing caution to the wind, I hoped that maybe I'd find something, anything, better. Selection: A lot like Rev. Zombie's shop, meaning a lot of mistaken tourists will grab it all up as authentic. Yet again, there are some pieces here and there that do impress, especially their tribal statues, but what I found here was invaluable. It wasn't a trinket or a talisman, no potions or voodoo dolls. No, I found a goth gay. Now, normally, this would not be a sight to behold, his black makeup standard and bleached hair nonextreme, even his choice in feminine punk rock and gothic clothing were pretty normal, but he had information. My little gay goth drew me a map and all but jumped for joy when I asked if he knew a good apothecary we could go to. "Thank god," he said, "you're the first person in months to ask." So, there you go, a store worker even admitted that the House of Voodoo was fauxdoo. But still, that said, the selection at Marie Laveau's is more specific than Rev Zombie's. They, on average seem to have about a 22-78 ratio or real to fake, but they also have different things than RZ. If you're looking for souvenirs, then go to RZ or ML, they're about the same. If you're on the hunt for some real supplies, then try Island of Salvation, because that's what I found to be worth it. Venue: It's on Bourbon and that's all you need to know. You'll find it, keep wandering, look for a big bright voodoo sign. And then look real hard inside, you might find something worth buying.

The turkey burger itself is ground turkey mixed with celery, spanish onions, shallots, garlic, scallions and peppers. It makes for an extremely tasty burger, even without cheese. (And I love cheese!) And all the extras inside probably are what kept the burger from tasting dried out as so many turkey burgers have the tendency to do. My only regret is that I wasn't more hungry so I could have finished my entire burger and side of sweet potato fries. Some people may think the portions are a bit on the small side, but I actually appreciated the small side of sweet potato fries. It's more in line with what a REAL serving size should be anyway. text: My absolute favorite croissants! AND the croissant turkey sandwich is fantastic too. I'm ordering a doberge cake for my party-- it is a 7 layer cake that will blow your mind it is so moist and not too sweet but perfect in every way! HISTORY: Doberge cake is a layered dessert originating in New Orleans, Louisiana. Still popular in the area, the cake is made of multiple thin layers of cake alternating with dessert pudding. Very often the cakes are made with half chocolate pudding and half lemon pudding. They are covered in a thin layer of butter cream and then a layer of fondant. They are normally made with six or more layers, but many amateurs make versions with fewer. Beulah Ledner opened a bakery in New Orleans in 1933. She became very successful after creating a Doberge cake adapted from the famous Hungarian/Austrian Dobos Cake. The doberge cake is based on a recipe originating in Alsace-Lorraine. Beulah Ledner's recipe is available in the cookbook, Let's bake with Beulah Ledner: A legendary New Orleans Lady by Maxine Wolchansky. In 1946 Joe Gambino bought the name, recipe and retail shop, including her recipe for doberge cake. After a couple of years of illness, she reopened in a new location on Metairie Road under the name "Beulah Ledner, Inc." As her business and popularity grew, her son, Albert, designed and built a new building and a new machine to mass produce sheet cakes using his mother's recipes. She opened her new bakery on May 21, 1970; she ran it until the age of 87 when she sold the shop and doberge recipe to Maurice's Bakery, which is still in the business of baking and selling Doberge cakes in Metairie, Louisiana.

text: I attended a wedding reception at the Franklin Room recently. It boasts that it's vintage and unique and will provide for a lasting experience. Granted, its close proximity to 3 or so churches in the area make it a very convenient place to hold a reception. Convenience for parties that leads to assured business for the venue should not lead to complacency, however, and that is just what this experience felt like with regard to what the Franklin Room has to offer. First and most disgustingly, may I point out the level of cleanliness in the women's bathroom. Upon closing the top lid on the toilet seat, I noticed that I must be the only person who has that habit of closing the lid b/c the back of the bowl was completely filthy. It was unbelievable that in cleaning that place, someone hadn't thought to close the lid and clean the top of the toilet. It's not like it was just a little filth either - it looked like it hadn't been properly cleaned in over a month. If that wasn't enough to make me lose my appetite, the food sealed the deal. Stale rolls, canned potatoes (trust me, if you've even eaten those little canned whole potatoes, you know them when you see them), a soggy salad, and mediocre entree meat (it appeared that they were taking thick cut deli meat and throwing it in gravy to heat it up). I haven't seen salt passed across members in a table so much in a long time. I really hate to give such a poor review b/c the wedding itself was simply gorgeous. The wedding itself was simply gorgeous, and it seemed very obvious that the bride and additional organizers really worked hard to make sure everything was perfect. As a result, the gaffes with the reception seem very one-sided (and that would not be by fault of the bride's planning). I understand that some people don't necessarily care about the food at the reception given that the celebration helps create memories of the bride and groom's first moments together as husband and wife. There is a huge problem, however, if instead of thinking of their time together, I've called other friends who thought the food at their reception was bad to tell them not to fear b/c the food I had just eaten made their wedding reception seem like a gourmet affair. AND the bathroom - that's just inexcusable.

text: We decided to try Wang Gang because of a group coupon special. When we entered the mildly crowded establishment, we weren't exactly sure what to expect. The cash registers and large flat panel TV made us think this was more of a fast food type of establishment, and we were right. After a slightly longer than average acknowledgement from waiting in the "Please wait to be seated" zone, we were sat down and introduced to our friendly waitress. She took our drink orders as well as our appetizer orders; Tom Kha Kai soup and Spring Rolls. After the waitress came back a few minutes later to take our main course order, she had remembered that she'd forgotten our drinks, no big deal, but she did mention that she was a novice and just began working as a waitress. Hmmm...Friday night, busy with lots of people...waitress on her 2nd expedition into the restaurant world. :/ We received the appetizers after 10 minutes. The spring rolls were very large although awkwardly prepared and unusually shaped. The taste was bland because the roll was mostly lettuce and had little sprout and carrot. The dipping sauce was overly tart and had a sharp after taste to it. The soup was served acceptingly hot, but not steaming. It had a rich mushroom creaminess but lacked some other ingredients one would expect from a spicy thai soup. My partner wasn't too hungry and simply ordered a fried rice for an entree, but since the expediter didn't bring it out even though we mentioned it was missing, she never got it. The waitress was very busy with other tables (full of other relatively not too happy customers) so by the time she came around, it was too late to re-order it. One thing I'd like to encourage the mgmt. there is to teach the staff to never say "the Mexicans in the back don't speak any English and that's why your fried rice did not make it to the table". :/ The other entree that did make it (called #88, $10) was described as a "classic black pepper dish with vegetables and a 3 pepper soy sauce." Since I am a huge fan of the Thai style pepper dishes, I was looking forward to a zesty chicken dish, but was served something that reminded me of take-out Chinese bucket food. The meat was sub-par and had the rubbery consistency of a take out dinner meat. To top things off and what ultimately went down from a two star review to a one star was the music. I do not want to hear country music, and pop rock music while trying to enjoy Asian fusion.

text: Mountain Mike's Pizza surprised me! I was expecting it to be like your average cheapo pizza buffet - but it was really impressive. The Wednesday night buffet (all you can eat) runs from 5pm-8pm I believe. They also have carry out and delivery. You go in, pay for your meal - two buffets, and two drinks was $18.00. That includes the salad bar - which was REALLY good, and fresh. The pizza was WONDERFUL.... the best pizza I've had in Reno thus far. The serve yourself fountain drinks were cool. I only have two simple complaints about this place. One is they give you a salad plate, and a dinner plate when you purchase your meal..... but they do not have extra plates on the buffet for refills - which to me is ghetto because I like to use a clean plate when I get refills! I also like OTHER people using a clean plate in case the serving spatula touches their plate- I rather it NOT be touching a plate they've already eaten from. I'm sure that they would have given me a clean plate if I would had ASKED ......... but I thought it should have just been there for me. MOST buffets ask (have signs) that you use a clean plate for refills..... My other complaint was..... they only have plastic forks and knives - and I dont like plastic. They are giving out washable plates and drinking glasses so I think they could easily use silverware instead of plastic - would be better, more cost efficient for them and better for the environment. The staff I encountered was friendly and nice,the place seemed very clean, there were TV's but they were not blaring which is a plus, there was no waiting, the place wasn't busy, but even if it would have been the dining area is large, and they had about 6 or 7 pizza's on the serving line the whole time we were there. I love LOVE LOVE the pizza - its really good quality, and the crust is really great - crispy on the outside, soft on the inside like I like it, and the dough actually had a nice flavor. We got bread sticks from the buffet and ask for a side or marinara sauce - it was REALLY amazing sauce. This might be our new Wednesday night eating spot. They offer a daily lunch buffet 11am-2pm if your on the north side of town this would be a great place to get a quick lunch. They also serve beer and wine

text: YES. This is my favorite coffee shop, bar none. It seems like there's something going on at Milkboy almost every night, with free Open Jazz Night and free Open Mic on Monday and Tuesday and shows that cost about $10 from Thursday through Saturday. The quality of the music is always really high, especially at the free events. And the space is very comfortable for working by yourself or meeting someone for a drink. Milkboy has a bunch of very comfortable couches with built-in cup holders, and has seats built in to the nearly floor-to-ceiling windows, a very cool place to sit. They have found the happy medium for music and noise so that it's quiet enough to read or write (I'm looking at you, Starbucks), but not so quiet that you feel like a jerk for having a quiet conversation. The food is very fresh and the portions are huge. I had the cheese crisp for my first dinner, with chicken, onions, mild green chiles, and lots of cheese. These traditional Tucson flour tortilla crisps can be greasy, but not here. It was very mild (gringo food), with obviously very fresh ingredients, and served super hot and melty. I ordered the small and it was the size of a small pizza. The second meal I had the Three Color Burro with shredded beef, which was also very mild. I highly recommend this place, but if you're looking for something spicy, ask your server, because what I ordered was not spicy at all!

Occasionally we'll supplement with some of the other maki/rolls--my favorite is the rainbow roll--but usually the combo platter is plenty of food for two. If you're not a sushi eater, Samurai offers plenty of other options--such as teriyakis, hibachis, tempuras, and hot pots (my husband loves the beef one). The choices extend well beyond chicken, beef, shrimp and tofu...think salmon, lobster, filet mignon...yum!! The seating is "cozy" but not overcrowded and the staff is genuinely friendly. The guys slinging the sushi are always willing to chat and answer questions. There's even a nice outdoor area during the warmer months...a rarity in this part of the Main Line. text: Time - an awesome destination. When you walk in there are two options - to the left to enjoy some live jazz, or to the right to enjoy more of a swanky restaurant/bar that had some flat panels and some sort of music in the background. Both sections had nice crowds for a Wednesday night, but my friends and I (we were 5 total) opted right and grabbed open seats at the bar. Great vibe, cool decor - we were immediately greeted by one of the most extroverted bartenders I've ever been served by. The dude was super friendly and was great with offering drink and food recommendations. At some point he was fully involved in the conversation we were having and it was as though he were out with us; some may not like this, but this guy was cool enough where you'd be fine with it. Great beer selection - had some stuff on tap you won't find at many other places. Big whiskey selection too, though I hate whiskey. Had what seemed to be all of your standard bar fare, but all the menu items offered their own Time flare. Between the five of us, we ordered the stuffed clams, burger, vegetables, mussels, and wings. I had the vegetables, and boy, do you get your share of vegetables. Served tempura style, they provide a generous serving of cauliflower, carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, and some other tasty treats that I can't recall / identify. Ketchup, mayo-ish, and some Indian-esque sauce were served on the side. Very tasty, but it ended up being too much fried food for me. Everyone else loved their meals, and the mussels comes with a FULL PLATE of fries, and I do mean its own dedicated plate of fries piled high. Two beers and the veggies ran me 35 bucks - maybe a bit pricey but the experience was worth it. The live jazz section was really happening by the time we left, and I really wanted to check it out, but the night was over for me. I'll definitely go back, and this is a must for anyone who enjoys good live music (jazz is good music, I don't care what you think).

text: my wife and i sat ourselves because no one was at the front. we had to wait a good 10-15 min before anyone came to take our drink order, during which time my wife wanted to leave. i wanted to give them a chance, but i should have listened to her. the orders came out very slow, and the rolls were underwhelming. it is an embarrassment to sushi restaurants, pure and simple. entrepreneurial koreans trying to jump on the japanese sushi bandwagon, and there's nothing wrong with that, but the sushi just doesn't taste good. and the service is horrible. it has no chance when there is only one server running around by himself. and the sushi chef appeared to be high school siblings! you can not tell me they have had proper training, which is to actually pay your dues for years learning the craft from a proper sushi chef. rice is doughy and too sticky, and they give you way too much with the rolls, which is a sneaky trick used by many korean owned sushi places. i don't enjoy the experience of almost choking every time i grab a piece of sushi roll. this is the worst sushi in tucson next to sushi saga, much worse than sushi garden. at least sushi garden has more than one server. when the only positive review touts "cheap " sushi i would seriously wonder about the place. if there was anything in life you should pay a premium for it would seem to be raw fish handled by bare hands, don't you think?

text: It kills me to do this because I love the Dmitri's near me, but apparently they just aren't created equally. My family and I chose this location because we all had off on Monday (the one in GHo is closed on Mondays) and my dad had been wanting to eat here for like 10 or 15 years or something. We got there around 8pm and my first impression of the place was how small it was. There were only like 8 seats at the "bar", which had a smaller, open kitchen behind it. That was kind of neat because you could see exactly what was going into your food, but other than that there were 3 tiny high-top tables and enough tables for MAYBE 20 people in the back section. So, being that we got there at peak dinner time, there was a wait. The hostess was really cool about it and said we could wait at the bar across the street (where we were tempted by their lobster macaroni and cheese special) in the mean time. After she came and got us, she placed the 4 of us at one of the tiny high-tops in the front area. It was super cramped and we really didn't have much room. Strike One. Strike Two was the service. I know that it was almost a full house, and I understand that completely, but it took almost 10 minutes to get greeted by our server. To compound that, she wasn't even that busy. We watched her stand at the food bar almost the entire time talking to her co-workers. She had no personality and just seemed really indifferent to us. Strike Three was the food. Like I said, I love the Dmitiri's near me and I really don't understand how the same restaurant could be so different. The menu is INFINITELY smaller and a lot less appetizing. The grilled octopus was really tough, chewy, and tasted like it had been pre-cooked. The baba and hummus that we got was really bland, which really annoyed me because it's really hard to screw up hummus. The mussels, which were pre-shelled, were served without a sauce or broth of any kind. They were alright, but again, lacking in flavor. The salmon entree that my sister ordered was WAY overcooked, and served with bland rice and watery cabbage. The calamari was really good though, and remains to be some of the best in the city, in my opinion. It's lightly fried and not chewy at all. It was just a really huge let down. I felt horrible for my dad because he had looked forward to eating there for so long and basically everything was terrible. We left full of food, but almost nauseated by how bad it was. We learned two important lessons, though. The first is to never return to that location, and the second is to never turn down lobster macaroni and cheese.
label: NEG

text: Ugh I was so disappointed with this place. Of all the places in Reno that the Food Network could have featured in their show Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives they showed this place. Why not Peg's?? text: Looking for a date spot that won't break the bank? Bobby's Burger Palace definitely hits the spot. Saturday night the boyfriend and I were looking for somewhere new to try without having to get all dolled up. For under $30 we both enjoyed a burger, a side, and a beer. The food was delicious--I had the Classic Burger cooked well done (and it was--without being burnt which is hard to find) and he had the Miami Burger medium which arrived perfectly pink through and through. We also had a side of onion rings and the sweet potato french fries. Both were awesome. The dipping and side sauces were a great addition as were the homemade (?) pickles (which we requested extra of they were so good!) The decor is very Farrah Fawcett meets Philippe Starck. Other yelpers have described it as a "retro bowling alley cafe" which although I do agree is aesthetically somewhat accurate, I should add that it definitely has a clean, contemporary, and bright atmosphere that feels comfortable and modern simultaneously. Our service was top notch and definitely worth raving about. Our "server" was friendly and polite and definitely worth leaving $5 on the counter for. We watched as several other patrons left their dirty plates without so much as a dollar. In my opinion, regardless of the fact that you pay on your way in does not mean that you shouldn't consider the service you receive while you're there (which was great!)
label: POS

text: They say everyone plays Douglas Corner. I think they are right even though you might not think it looking at this modest little bar from the outside. It's on 8th Ave. right across from Zanie's. I guess it's been there for a while. It seems like an insidery-type bar, but it brings out all kinds of people. One night my friend and I were counting how many girls had on their Ugg boots (well, it was mostly me). We saw an amazing set of singer-songwriters including the guys from Halfway to Hazard and Jon Nicholson of the Muzik Mafia. Douglas Corner is a fairly small, straight-ahead bar so every show there is intimate. We sat at the bar and watched the bartender make tons of strong drinks. My only beef with that is they are served in plastic cups. You can see incredible performances here from all kinds of musicians. The cover charge is usually very reasonable for the entertainment you get. In a lot of other respects, Douglas Corner is like a lot of other smoky bars in town, but you should really check out at least one show here.

text: I am really disappointed that is the only rib place Graduate Hospital has to offer. I don't really even know why they bother with the sides as they are tasteless and might as well have been prepared by my 6th grade lunch lady. The cornbread is barely edible...dry, flavorless, dry, gritty, dry, hard, dry. The most disappointing thing about this place, however, is their ribs. I ordered a rack of the beef ribs and they were straight-up disgusting. At first I was really looking forward to them because they were HUGE and smelled pretty good, but I was so so so disappointed when I actually took a bite. Turns out they were huge because they were SERIOUSLY more then 50% fat: I'm talking chunky, white, thick fat all over the ribs and just a little bit of meat on top of the fat. We ended up throwing away the majority of the ribs because they were not edible, save a couple scraps off each rib that was actually meat. Save your time and money and go somewhere where they actually have quality pieces of meat. It's not like the ribs are extremely cheap here, so I totally didn't expect the low quality.

text: This hotel is WAY too perfumy -- from the air in the lobby to the pillows and sheets to the soap in your bathroom. I have been sneezing non-stop all night because of it! I suppose it's better than cigarette smoke... Another thing that really bugs me about this hotel is the poor keycard readers in the elevators. While it's nice that they use this as a security measure, it's completely ridiculous that so many people get stuck in the elevators because they can't get their keycard read so as to push a button to go to their floor. I can't tell you how many times I've run into people in the elevator who had been in there for several minutes trying to get the keycard reader to work. And I'm not sure if this was just my room, but you really have to push/pull your door shut -- it gets stuck at the end, and if you're not careful, you could be leaving your room unlocked. The keycard reader for my room also isn't that great. I also find this hotel frustrating because it is like a maze -- to get from the street to my room, I have to take two different elevators in two different parts of the building. And there are so many different entrances/exits, which makes it even harder to find where you're going. On the plus side, the staff is very friendly and helpful, the grounds are beautiful (including an outdoor terrace/garden with a romantic gazebo and lots of [perfumy] flowers), they have complimentary jasmine green tea (and English breakfast and earl grey) tea in the room, and it's pretty conveniently located just on the border of the French Quarter but not in it so you can avoid all the noise.

text: The drinks are good (although I once asked for a bellini at the indoor bar and received champagne mixed with peach schnapps-- I don't think so!), the food is consistent and tasty, but the rooftop deck has several issues that this cupcake does not love. First, the glassware. Or shall I say, plasticware. When I order a ten dollar martini, I do not want to drink it out of room temperature plastic in a martini glass shape. I'm sure the reason behind this decision is so knucklehead drunks don't go throwing things over the ledge... but at the very least, they could serve real glasses to the patrons seated at the bar or at tables having dinner, or save the plastic for after 10 p.m. Second, although there were no pools in sight, the entire deck area curiously smelled like one. Musty, chlorine-filled air combining with the scent of prepared foods was not at all appetizing. A rooftop bar in the middle of Philadelphia should not smell like low tide under the boardwalk. Please, Mr. Starr, give this place a good scrub down and replace the flooring with something that doesn't absorb spills. I'm sure this wasn't my last visit to the deck at Continental Midtown... but with more bars and restaurants opening outdoor patios and setting up street-side tables, this place won't be topping my list for drinks al fresco.

text: Overall: A cool place to sit on the patio and have a couple drinks and very basic pizza, but nothing great. The pizza wasn't bad and there are TONS of toppings, but there was something pretty unimpressive about it. Don't waste your calories/money on the pasta... it's pretty mushy and the sauces are pretty bland. I've also had the caprese salad which wasn't bad, but then again, how do you mess that up? (Tip: don't get the "roasted chicken" on top, it's very dry and seems like it was out of a bag). My rule of thumb for "good Italian food" is something I couldn't make in my own kitchen and I can safely say I could make 95% of the items on that menu just as good or better. Sorry, Mafioza fans. It really is a cool place for drinks and maybe an app or 2 though. Location/Service: The neighborhood is always fun, no complaints there. It's possible our service wasn't great because I was with a decent sized group, but the waitress we did have was pretty spacy.

text: I n every town I've ever lived, I always wanted to work a local job. I mean a job native to that town, or area of the country. Like, working on a cheese farm in Wisconsin or a winery in Southern California. In New Orleans I worked a tug boat on the Mississippi and on a derrick barge in the Gulf of Mexico, but I always wanted to shuck oysters at Cooter Brown's. This Place is great. Imagine yourself going for a bike ride on the levee or a jog around Audubon Park, then meeting up with some friends for a couple dozen oysters and a few(or many) beers at Cooters. Speaking of beer, they have about 400 different kinds, 350 being imports and 46 on tap. Where else can you get a Golden Pheasant from Slovakia? Yep! Ol' Cooter Brown's... right there where St. Charles Ave. meets Carrolton. Park out in front or by the railroad tracks. Watch a game on one of many big screens(nice ones), play a game of pool or philosophize with the likes of Alfred Hitchcock, Jerry Garcia and over thirty other famous dead people, all very much alive in spirit and drinkin a cold one at Cooter Brown's.

text: Great googly-moogly! Don't be scared away by the $75/pound price. It works out to approx. $2.25 per truffle and it's worth every penny! If you really enjoy chocolate, I recommend the Nama truffle. To put this review into perspective, I'm a chocolate enthusiast who has lived in Paris, and who seeks out sublime eats and treats in every city I visit. The best spots I've found so far include François chocolate bar in NYC (it's hidden, like a secret garden!), Fran's Chocolates in Seattle, Thomas Haas in Vancouver (I love Thomas Haas, the man AND the brand!), Pierre Marcolini here and abroad, Venezuelan handmade miracles at Sazon in Philly, and an Ecuadorian melt-in-your-hand bar my friend brought me from Ecuador. I'm attending the Salon du Chocolat in NYC next month, and going on an adventure of chocolate discovery in Switzerland in December. Bottom line? I declare these the finest traditional truffle chocolates I have ever tasted!

text: BF has become the occasional go-to casual weeknight dinner place for 3 of us who are friends since it's equidistant from all our homes. And consistently fine service: attentive, helpful and often funny (and we're not regulars, so it isn't a matter of knowing us) - never had anyone serving us who was indifferent. I've also been there for Sunday brunch once and it was nice, not overrun with tourists. If you're seeking a solid dependable meal with friends in a good setting that's professionally and smoothly run, this is it.

text: Great with dogs... not so much with people. It's all about the money. If I could break it down, it would be 5 stars for the dogs, 0 star for customer service. This is the only facility of its kind in Reno, and the owners take that as an opportunity to deliver customer service that would be absolutely intolerable in any other business. We have lived in a number of places, and used different "doggie day care" services, and without exception, the first time I have brought my pet in, I was invited to tour the facilities, so that I would be comfortable leaving my 'fur kid' with them. Not at Pet Play House. As a matter of fact, there are curtains preventing owners from looking into the outdoor areas from the lobby, and requests for information are handled rudely and defensively. Before you can board or leave for daycare, you must bring your dog in for evaluation - an absolutely standard practice in the industry. But I have NEVER been asked to PAY for a full day daycare for that. And that was in facilities of equal or better quality, and in cities with MUCH higher overhead. I have also never done business with someone who has less concern for their clients' needs - you want to board? You MUST bring in your dog before noon. Why? It's what is convenient for Pet Play House. Can you make an exception? No. As long as you're booking a family vacation that won't change, you won't have many issues - but heaven help you if you're traveling on business and need ANY flexibility with dates or times. If you're late, you can't pick up your dog, or will be charged extra. If you cancel less than 10 days in advance, you'll still be charged for the booking. If you come home early, you'll still be charged - even if you call in advance (even a few DAYS in advance). If you make changes less than 10 days in advance, you'll be charged - and if you call to ask - the money is the FIRST thing out of the owner's mouth. When I called to cancel an extra day I had booked the day before, I was told "You can leave him if you want - since it's less than 10 days before (the booking) you'll have to pay for the day anyway". My jaw hit the floor when the owner said that. Our dog was healthy and exhausted when he came home. Will we go back? I sincerely doubt it. I am probably going to cancel our future booking (and eat the 50% booking deposit), just because I don't believe in supporting a business that provides bad customer service - I own my own business, and would NEVER treat customers the way they do.

text: I am so glad for this place! I have used Klaich animal hospital for years.... nothing bad against them, but when my mouse got horribly sick I had to take her to a vet that treated small animals (not klaich). My mouse had a horrible skin problem that wasn't healing, for months and months she was afflicted with this problem that I can only assume was painful. I would have put her down if the vets had told me that it was the right thing to do, but they were always hopeful about finding a solution. They gave me topical meds for her skin to ease the pain. Finally one vet approached me with a new procedure they were trying out on animals called "Bicom." It was very expensive, but I had already paid quite a bit of money on my mouse and wasn't going to give up until I had tried everything. So I had the procedure done on her and a week later she was totally normal again. It was amazing.... I thought she was going to die and then suddenly she is healed. The vet told me of other extreeme situations animals have been in, in which the Bicom prodedure has saved them. The vets and the office staff care for the animals so much, you can tell. It's not about the money, even though they are expensive. And if it is about the money - well, they sure can hide it. It seems like they are so interested in helping animals. So after my mouse was better, I decided to take my new cat there to be neutered. He got his vaccinations too. Boy, it was pretty expensive, but I really liked the service. The vet met with me and discussed my cat's health and asked me numerous times if I had any questions. I felt really good about leaving my cat there, because of how the vets and staff members were willing to talk with me and make sure I was ok with everything. After everything they also sent me home with pain medication.... I thought this was interesting because when I had my other cat neutered elsewhere years ago, they didn't sell me any pain medication. When I had my female cat spayed they did - but I just thought for male cats it wasnt something they did. I was glad they sold me the pain medication. It made me feel a lot better, because I knew he wouldn't be in as much pain. I will take all my animals here from now on. I know most vets give amazing care to animals, but at Community Animal Hospital they seem to also care about how the owners feel.

text: I was a patient of 2+ years and I finally have had enough! I originally signed up as a patient in their office because I lived nearby and my employer did not offer any dental coverage. Once I learned about the office having the ability to provide you with their insurance, I was sold. Well... you get what you pay for. For less than $200 a year, you can expect x-rays, two cleanings and 20 % off other services which is pretty decent. However do expect to wait at least an hour in their waiting room (even though you show up on time), schedule your own cleanings 3 months in advance with no reminder card and wait on hold for a minimum of 10 minutes when calling. Mind you I am a patient person, mindful of dates so none of the above bothered me very much. I am bothered that when I did take advantage of the 20% off other services, for four (4) impacted wisdom teeth extractions it cost around a grand (and yes this is with their insurance). Plus you do not have the option of being put under only nitrous oxide is offered. I was awake and in a lot of pain for my procedure. I had injections and nitrous but I still cried through the procedure. I could not only feel everything but I could also see the entire procedure through the surgeons plastic face shield. After the procedure was completed the shots finally worked so I was numb for hours later. I was only given pain killers for 4 days. My prescription ran out on a Sunday at noon so I called the 24 hr emergency hotline. After waiting 5 painful hours Dr. Kasahara finally returned my call and said he would call my prescription into the pharmacist. Well... he not only waited 10 minutes before the pharmacy closed but he also only ordered me Ibuprofen. Last time I checked that was over the counter- thanks for nothing Doc! Thankfully I have found a new Dentist that listens to my needs and treats me like a patient that is in pain, not a junkie looking for a fix

text: This is not my favorite mall. In fact, except for the Roosevelt Mall, Franklin Mills is my least favorite mall in the Philly area. I live about 5 minutes away, and I only go into the actual mall about once a year, usually when a friend drags me there. It's a dark, maze-like building, and I find the layout unappealing. I do, however, like that it's 1 mile long, so at least you can get a workout while you're there, since nothing else is worth the trip. Most of the stores are weird stores that you've never heard of, which have cheap-looking clothing that I personally wouldn't waste my money on. The only worthwhile stores are the Banana Republic, Gap, Old Navy, and Ann Taylor outlets (and Ann Taylor is still expensive) and Steve & Barry's (but only for Sarah Jessica Parker's Bitten line). Otherwise, this mall sucks. I also don't like the theater. I used to go to the movies at Franklin Mills all the time back when they were in a separate building, not attached to the mall proper. But, once they attached the theaters to the mall, I noticed that the moviegoing crowd was a different demographic. Suddenly, my fellow moviegoers were the kind of people who answer their very loudly ringing cell phones in the middle of the film and then proceed to have very loud conversations for 10 minutes, or they bring infants, or they're annoying teenage boys who do obnoxious things during the movie. All of these things have caused me to stop going there (I prefer Woodhaven, which is clean, quiet, closer to my house, and which still has student discounts, and Neshaminy). As for the mall area itself, I sometimes go to Sam's Club, and I avoid Wal-mart at all costs (evil, evil conglomerate). But the beer distributor in the Wal-mart shopping center is awesome - they have a great selection. And the wine & spirits superstore has the best wine selection in Pennsylvania (at least that I've found). They're way bigger than the usual state store, and they have a lot of wines to choose from (not as many as stores in NY state or NJ or Total Wines in Delaware, but I'll take it). In all, I'd say save your money and go to a mall that has real stores. Even the good stores at Franklin Mills are only outlets, so they have last year's styles or items that were not made correctly, so basically, the stores here are reject stores. No fun.

text: I hate to sound like a vengeful bitch, but I just realized that this restaurant has way more stars than it deserves. It was Valentine's Day, a few years back. Husband and I had reservations for ten o'clock...probably not the best time for great service, so we were willing to be forgiving. We arrived at 9:40 and were asked to wait in the bar. The people who arrived before and after us had no reservations, and were also asked to wait at the bar. They were both seated before us, and in better tables. The table that our reservation got us shouldn't even have existed, it was so bad--a tiny two-seater directly next to the kitchen. I was about to get up myself and grab them when Husband flagged down a busboy to bring us our order. Of course, the dinners were, by that point, inedible, and that is when I went to find the manager. Normally in a situation like this, the manager is apologetic and ready to do whatever it takes to make things right. Not here, though. The manager was rude and treated me as though I make a habit out of trying to get free meals, despite the fact that neither myself or Husband had touched our food. He grudgingly comped our bill and sent us on our way without so much as an apology. I know a lot of people really like this restaurant, but I am unwilling to gamble my time and money on a place that was willing to treat even one customer so incredibly poorly.

text: I can understand the dichotomy of reviews for this place. It is a spectacular experience to spend a day in this outlandishly tacky biodome. But if you have to be there for more than a day, you realize they have trapped you there by design, and then they leach from your wallet relentlessly, and by the time you leave you are glad. Right from the beginning, a shuttle form the airport is $35 per person round trip. Highway robbery, sine the cabs are only $25 one way for up to 4 people and run whenever you want. If you get a rental car, they will charge you $16/day to self park or $24 for them to valet. You might as well take a cab there, because you won't drive a rental car anyway. This place was designed to keep you there. It is so big and the exits are so far away and inconvenient and they have everything you could ever need there anyway . . . for a price. The boat ride is $9 per person I think, a beer at Findleys, a decent pub, is $6 a pint. That's San Francisco prices in Nashville. After the second day, you feel trapped. You are in the Truman show. You try walking to the nearby mall to escape and get some fresh air, and it is a decent thing to do, but it is tacky too, so you don't feel completely free. But eventually you return to the oppression of the terrarium. You are living in Disneyland under a bowl and without the rides. The biggest shame about staying here for a full vacation is you will not get out to see all the great things that Nashville has to offer. You think you will, but it is just such a headache to get anywhere else, and so expensive, that you won't bother (Yeah it is expensive to stay and expensive to leave). If you want to see this place, you can visit, even stay for one night of your trip maybe and go see the Grand Ole' Opry, but in winter that is downtown at the Ryman, which is cool. If you have a convention here, enjoy, and maybe try to stay at a downtown hotel for your first or last night. If you are vacationing in Nashville, I would find a place downtown to stay.

text: While doing some shopping in Maplewood, I got into the spirit of staying local and felt the urge to dine at Nosh. I was not disappointed! We walked in on a Friday night around 7pm and got a table right away. It filled up shortly thereafter, though I never saw a wait. This place is so cute! It's small but they have really cool small pieces of flair as the decor. The light fixtures, artwork, and bar area are nicely done. Not too much but enough to notice. We sat pretty close to the door and regretted it because it was a little colder than we preferred and also there was a piano playing there, so it was a bit loud. Not a big deal. The restaurant did get loud, but a lot of it was a group of people with "that girl" in it. Aka, the loudest, obnoxious, clap and scream at her own jokes type. Certainly not Nosh's fault. I've found one of my top 3 favorite cocktails here! Their list is very long and full of fruity stuff (and more). I ordered the hard blueberry lemonade. It was like candy! So fresh and refreshing, even in this weather. It had real, FRESH blueberries in it. I wanted more but I limited myself to one. It didn't taste like alcohol at all and I didn't care one bit! What other diners said is true, the food comes out REALLY slowly here. There is a blurb on their menu about making everything to order and taking time. Don't come here if you want it fast and ordering an appetizer is recommended if you are really hungry to start. The service was by no means inattentive. Our waiter (also the bartender) came by frequently. The manager came around to check on us too, and was very visible. I ordered the Orchard Melt and Butternut Squash Soup and my hubby ordered the Fried Egg BSRP with chips. Vegetarians, check out the menu because there are several vegetarian things, and gluten free or vegan meals are clearly marked. My sandwich was piled high with apples, maybe a little too many, but it was really nice flavors. The butternut squash soup was AMAZING. Nice and nutty and savory. Not really sweet like some soups with butternut squash tend to be. I felt satisfied after my meal but not like I had stuffed myself. My hubby liked his sandwich but wished he had gotten a salad or soup instead of chips because he has a hollow leg and needs a lot to eat! We will definitely be back!

To which I received a "I wasn't here so I don't know what happened, if you want you can have a seat and we'll call you when there's an open space." I was furious by this time, but had about 40 minutes to contemplate and strategically plan out my argument for the assistant manager. 1pm came and went... 1:30pm came and went... 2pm came and I inquired about the assistant manager. As a good anthropologist, I know that if things can be solved at the local level you need to lobby to the next highest level to effect change. I decided it was time to call corporate... I explained the whole situation, including the fact that a manager had not been present since the store opened. The woman on the phone said my reservation was valid and she would look into getting me a free oil change. I agreed to wait for to call back before making any decisions. I went back to the waiting room... Fast forward 60 minutes, and the mechanics still had not returned; 75 minutes no return and no phone call; 80 minutes and no return, no phone call, and no manager; 90 minutes... I had all I could take and demanded my keys back. The woman had the nerve to give me a comment card and ask if I'd like to take a survey on my experience at Pep Boys! ARE YOU FREAKIN KIDDING ME?! I got my keys and the survey (a nasty-gram would soon be sent)! I got in my car and called Jiffy Lube who told me to come on in... My oil change was done in 30 minutes. At 6pm that night the customer service woman from Pep Boys corporate called me back. She had informed the manager of everything that had happened and my free oil change was waiting for me. I told her that I had gotten great service at Jiffy Lube and that she could shove her free oil change up Ghengis the Skanks ass! Don't ever go to PEP BOYS! THEY ROYALLY SUCK!

text: I am a fan- the previous chef from East Sushi in Scotch Plaza has opened his own restaurant in Marrazzo's shopping center, and I think this has been a wonderful addition to the Ewing restaurant line-up (which, trust me...could use a few additional players!) I love the rolls here, always fresh, and the seaweed salad is prepared perfectly, with swirls of daikon throughout for an addiitonal crunchy surprise. I have tried many of the noodle soups and curry dishes, and they are always fabulous. I appreciate the variety in the menu...from Japanese, to Vietnamese to some Thai options. This is a great way to introduce foods to a neighborhood with previously limited pan-Asian fare to choose from. There are plenty of non-raw items to enjoy, if you are not feeling ready for the sushi plunge. The only set-back, if you are looking for a certain j'ai no se quoi in your restaurant ambience...is that being this is a family owned establishment, the owner's children are usually there, and if it's slow...they can be found running around, maybe spoiling that romantic kid-free evening out you were hoping for. In all- I believe diners must approach this establishment with a reality-check, and a bit of openmindedness....NO, this is not your city-sushi joint, hi volume, unusual options tempting young 20-somethings to feel cool when tossing back raw fish....NO, this is not your west coast sushi which is always #1 in freshness and authenticity....this IS what it IS, a family-owned, small buisness Ewing, NJ attempt to bring new, high quality pan Asian fare to a neighborhood which could surely use a restaurnant make-over. I hope that diners continue to try Yummy Sushi, so that they may grow and invest in their menu and establishment. For goodness sakes, Ewing has enough Pizza places, let's try to be welcoming to new venues and give them a chance to thrive!

text: Alternative medicine, to my understanding, includes looking at someone with a holistic approach. Unfortunately my experience with Dr. Garcia was anything but holistic. Twenty minutes after my scheduled 10am appointment, Dr. Garcia escorted me back to his office. He sat at his office chair looking at the laptop on his lap and asked brusquely, "What are you here for?" This is the approach I would fully expect from a conventional doctor, but not from someone who practices alternative medicine. Since I am hypothyroid and need my prescription renewed, I need current blood work done. He suggested that this be done in his office right now. I'm not a medical expert, but I have had blood drawn several times a year for the past several years and EVERY time I'm told to not only fast, but also don't take my thyroid medication because it will throw off results. I was concerned and confused that Dr. Garcia was going to make a determination on my prescription with blood drawn right there on the spot. When I mentioned that my cortisol was very high a few years ago, Dr. Garcia made a sweeping statement that my adrenal system is shot. Again, an assumption I would expect from a conventional doctor. My expectation of someone who practices alternative medicine is that they would inquire about what external factors were going on in my life at that time, and what are your cortisol levels now? Had Dr. Garcia done that, he would have learned that I was going through a divorce at that time, and labs since then have shown that everything in that area is fine. At the end of our consultation he wrote a list on the back of a piece of scratch paper (I'm not making this up!), which included "diet and supplements" as my course of action, along with a number of treatments he offers. When I inquired about which supplements I should take, he said he sells a package. Again, I inquired about which supplements I should use, because I'm already taking a few things. Instead of giving me a clear answer he wanted me to list what I am taking and he'll let me know if I should take it or not. "Or you can just buy my package." I'm guessing he has considerable markup on his package and other office treatments. After about 45 minutes, I knew a lot about Dr. Garcia's view of mammography and thermography (how did that even come up?), about his supplements, about his other body cleanse services, about his cancer patients (the bulk of his business, it appears), and he knew very little about me or my life situation. How can a doctor take a holistic approach if they don't even have half of my story? I felt like I was just another dollar sign passing through his office, much like his terminal cancer patients. Unfortunately, I did make a considerable contribution to Utopia on this initial consultation, but I won't repeat that mistake. I thought I had done my research. Dr. Garcia's website said all of the right things. I wish I had had someone else's experience to draw on before making my appointment. Jim & Colette http://www.roamingtogether.com http://www.facebook.com/followrt

text: All tourists ask the same question, "I've seen all the tourist stuff, but really, where do the locals go." My answer almost always includes the Carousel Bar in the Hotel Monteleone. Yes, it's a bar. And, yes, it's in a hotel; but this is more than your average Hotel Bar. Here, you are just as likely to find coworkers having a drink after work as you are to find tourists looking to relax after a long day of exploring the French Quarter. On one visit to the Carousel Bar, while having drinks alone, two older gentlemen from Texas asked me to join them. Pleasant conversation ensued. They explained how they were staying at another hotel, but they loved coming to the Carousel Bar. The older man told me the story of how he had gotten married at the Monteleone about 50 years before. Nothing much had changed. He said, "We spent our honeymoon right there." While pointing to the bar. Then, with tears in his eyes, he went on to tell me how they would come back nearly every year until she died a few years ago. Being gentlemen, they paid my tab (which included a few French 75s), excused themselves and went to catch their dinner reservation. This story, epitomizes all of why I love the Carousel Bar. There's history there. Memories are made. Strangers become friends. And they make pretty good French 75s.

We had a great bottle of wine...it was called Natalie and I wanted it because that's my name :) Anyhow, we got the seared scallops and that was actually very good. I ordered the braised beef as recommended by our waitress. It was incredibly salty and dry. The only good thing was that it came with yummy creamy french style mashed potatoes. My husband got the duck which he really like...however, I thought it too was very salty. I was trying to look on the bright side and I decided to order dessert to make up for the bad meal. I ordered a lemon tart or torte or something and it came with a scoop of ice cream. Both were terrible! I love lemon and it was gross! In addition, the ice cream tasted as if it had been in the freezer for years! It was a very unfortunate experience and I would not recommend this restaurant...there are way too many great places to eat in Santa Barbara, don't waste your time here!

text: I went there Saturday for pizza with my daughter. Its a pizza joint so no need to check yelp right. Wrong. Management was extremely rude. He was sitting at the bar having himself a cold one at 3pm which is his business but when you are rude to customers its a problem. He didn't greet us. Just stared. I had to ask him could we get a table for slices. He flags us over to the other side. The waitress just however had sent us to this side. Um......the menu is pizza. A few other Italian dishes but its primarily pizza. Special seating? Come on now. Apparently they don't realize they are a pizza joint/bar and not an upscale restaurant where you would expect a pretentious attitude. I guess this is why the wait staff was also very rude. The pizza crust was good if you like thin crust. The onions and peppers were soggy, the chicken was flavorless, there was no rosemary. You are going to have to season it yourself. The wait staffs loud conversation was.........gross. Save your money. Go to Mix on 22nd or Dock St on 50th and Baltimore.

text: All hail Iron Chef Jose Garces! I made a same day reservation - dinner for 2 at 9:30 on a Saturday night. Top notch atmosphere, seemingly effortless service and bold food. If you read nothing else, know that they are selling autographed copies of Garces' book Latin Evolution for $35 (what a steal!!). We sat in the front dining room - cool yet dark in its color scheme, with shutter-lined walls for added perceptual depth and large high metal ceiling fans spinning slowly overhead. I love the contrast between this room and the warm reddish-orange glow of the back dining room (mostly for larger parties). Francesco was one of the best waiters we've had in a long time! At once his friendly disposition and knowledge of the menu made us feel at ease in his capable hands. He informed me of special vegetarian options (tofu buns & red curry without crab) and made excellent drink recommendations (white sangria with heavy orange flavors for my date). Of the many dishes we ordered, the Red Curry Del General and Arroz Con Pato were our favorites. Both portions were fairly large. Only the Chupe was disappointing. It had a slow poached egg inside which gave the dish a runny consistency - something that my boyfriend didn't enjoy. The Yuca fries would make a great bar food, just be sure to stir up the dipping sauce in the bottom of the cup. In general the dishes were mildly spicy, surprisingly sweet, less salty than Tinto and larger portions than Amada.
label: POS

text: Maybe I'm spoiled from all of the great tapas places I've been to when living in Chicago, but I just don't get the tapas scene in Saint Louis. Most of the places are very expensive for what you get, including the new Sanctuaria. Almost every selection was over 8 bucks and the food was neither your traditional tapas, or a fun new take on traditional tapas. Chicken strips, a pulled pork sandwich and shredded beef on mashed potatoes were all on the menu. Of course, they weren't described that way, but really you can put lipstick on a pig..but does that turn it into an interesting tapas dish?...no. I also ordered the featured drink of the day because I read a review that the bartenders there know how to make a good cocktail. The drink was the Gentleman's Touch..and while it was very tasty, and seemingly made with unique ingredients, I felt like I purchased an $8 tiny glass of kool-aid. My portion didn't even fit in a small martini glass. In summary, Sanctuaria feels like just another Saint Louis gimmick that is preying upon a population that digs the advancement of the grove area and is gambling that their patrons will like anything with an ethnic flair and nice decoration, and who will pony up their credit cards blindly for it.
