text: This is the YMCA that I grew up with and I still live pretty close by. I love the facilities here. Over the years, it's gotten a lot busier, but they still manage to keep everything in working order and clean. I really appreciate the clean. As much as I love it here, I think the prices are a bit high. As a student, I can't afford to go here as much as I'd like. The gym is great for shooting hoops - especially in the winter when my basketball hoops sees snowballs instead of basketballs. And the workout facilities are nice. They have great equipment and it's a really nice place to work out. I love the pool too. This is one of my favorite pools to go to. I wish I could spend more time there. This is a great YMCA. Check it out if you can!
label: POS

text: My dining at Modo Mio last night was so pitifully disappointing, I felt it necessary to join yelp to write about it. First, as a party of 4 with resos for 9pm, the hostess was glib and flippant in seating us 20 mins late. My chair was covered with an unfortunate slime, that got all over my hand when I went to sit down. When I went to the bathroom to wash it off, I was saddened to see how filthy it was. Toilet paper all over the floor, fecal matter splashed over the toilet. Gross. After reading "Kitchen Confidential" this bathroom experience had me worried. But I figured the food could salvage my experience. Everyone I know insists that Modo Mio is good, and I was excited to be there. I was starving and really looking forward to deliciousness. IT IS NOT DELICIOUS. We all ordered the turista menu, which includes an appetizer, pasta, entree and dessert for $33. Bargain, you say? Not if you leave hungry. After being told it was late on a Saturday, the waiter informed us of all the things the kitchen was out of - essentially everything we were going to order. For starters I had the fried artichoke heart with a fried egg. I LOVE artichokes. What happened to this artichoke was a crime. It was fried to the point of flavorless grease. The egg on top was undercooked, with clear whites running off it. A huge disappointment. The pastas were underwhelming, oversalted and tiny portions (i had 3 of those candy pasta things - which if you are sharing with 4 people at the table, left none for me). For my entree I ordered the veal cheek, which I have had several times at other establishments. It was tough and grisly. It came with undercooked poached pears and a hunk of blue cheese sitting on top. It didn't have the appearance of a cohesive dish and it definitely didn't have the flavor or texture of a yummy dish. Really the nail in the dining experience coffin was the water refill situation. It is one of those restaurants where they are refilling your water glass every 3 minutes. I took one sip and I had an arm in my face filling it back up. I don't love that. Overall, I do not understand how this place is so well-loved. It was very loud, dirty, with tasteless uninspired food. I will not return.
label: NEG

text: I really felt like trying a new (for me) Thai restaurant tonight, and man was this place the wrong choice! It started fine with very tasty cha gio, although we got the appetizer 15 minutes before our drinks arrived. The rest of the meal was a disaster. There was one waitress for the entire restaurant, and she was running as fast as she could. There was no way she could keep up. I asked for the yellow curry chicken to be extra spicy - asian hot, not Boise hot. In spite of the large number of red flakes floating in the curry, there was almost no discernable heat. The chicken in the dish was dry and crumbly, the rice on the side was dry and hard, and the curry flavor was mediocre at best. The curry dish was mostly composed of potatoes, with a little carrot and chicken. My wife had the stir fried flat noodles with shrimp and vegetables, and the minimal flavor the noodles had was not pleasant. Even the water we had to wait 20 minutes to get, didn't taste good. We won't be going back.
label: NEG

text: Went for dinner around 5pm on Tuesday... note to self: only go for breakfast!. Service was bad. waitress took her time getting our orders. The cheeseburger was good/fresh but the fries were like little grease balls! yuck! but the apple pie a la mode is still up to par....

text: Bomb Bomb is a friendly, cozy place with great food and usually very good service. The food has never disappointed, but the menu is a bit of a wonderful mish mash. The Italian entrees are good. The staff is mature and totally not worried about being cool, a refreshing change. The staff all appear to be neighborhood types which is also refreshing compared to the Latinization of other Philly kitchens. The only drawback is the service lag that happens at small restaurants when half their tables are taken up with one large loud party. text: So sad, the most famous critter at the Zoo has died. That's Gemina, the crooked neck giraffe, she was 21 years old. The zoo itself is a nice place, I've been going there all my life and remember the days when small monkeys used to climb about in the trees above some picnic areas and try to nick your food. But, as you can see by the fact that all the photos uploaded here are the giraffes - including one from me - Gemina was quite the attraction. Anyway, sorry to be the bearer of bad news. RIP, Gemina.

text: Sometimes a diner cut from the cookie-cutter mold can still stand out in your mind. Maybe you yearn for its freakishly tall slices of delicious German chocolate cake. Perhaps you're craving its thick-cut French toast covered with bananas and whipped cream and drizzlings of pure maple syrup. Or maybe you just need a serving of that feisty waitress who knows just what to say and just when to fill your coffee up, without asking. Not this one. It's aptly named, for it delivers no more flavor - edible or charismatic - than a country club might. Drab. Here, it is what it is: a place to grab a bite when you don't feel like making it yourself. Nothing special. It'll do.
label: NEG

text: I'm a pretty positive person so prefer to just write glowing reviews for the great places i experience and leave the others on their own. But I just had to write because this place was terrible and I would feel bad if you spent your hard-earned money there. We ate there back in October. I gave it one star because the Spanish wine was amazing and the waiter was super-nice and very attentive. But the food was horrible. It was like something out of the frozen food section. The paella was a sauce on top of dry rice, which is not the traditional way to prepare it. The cheese plate included cheeses that were cheese-products, not real cheese. The edible saving grace was the dessert, which based on how quickly it came out, definitely was not prepared on spot (but it really was delicious) At the end of the meal, I kind of felt as if a hidden camera was going to be revealed and they were going to tell us that all the food was from the Wal-Mart frozen section or something crazy. If you are going to go out to dinner, you deserve something fantastic and I'm sorry to say, Fuego is not it.

text: I do not feel bad at all for giving this the worst rating I will ever give here. Ok, I have a great deal of Philly Pride! I am also a techie. That's great for anyone on a budget with a laptop. I had this service for one whole year. I sold all of my friends on it. I watched them all cancel their services for one reason or another. One by one, not me. I was being Mr. Philadelphia and totally championing this services saying, "Give it a chance". After a year, I called them and asked to be cancelled finally. May times, nonprofit leaders get comfortable with their salaries and meetings that they forget that the programs they are providing need to be consistently observed, revised and supported overall. Tech Support told me, "Oh, I'm a customer too and I never have connection issues." I told them to say it for someone who doesn't support networks for a living. I hate when tech support asks you to do all of the things you did before calling them all over again! She said, "Is there anything else I can do for you?" I said, "I want to hang up the phone and no longer have service with Earthlink!" Earthlink was beat out in Philadelphia for dsl, what made the city think they would provide a reliable municipal wifi service? Sorry, this one is near to my heart as myveins are actually cat5 cables...hehe. Here's a tip, fire the guy who spearheaded this agreement and hire someone new to clean this place up!

text: Tavern on Broad is not in my regular rotation, though the location is convenient for the lunchtime and after-work crowds. Some folks might find the forty-odd televisions blaring sports and news entertaining, but for our small party just looking to drink and catch up, it was overwhelming; like crawling inside one of the giant screens from Blade Runner and trying to make small talk. We were the guests of a friend who had won a "free happy hour", but this translated roughly into the same happy hour specials that everyone else in the bar was already enjoying. They're not bad- half off most drinks and appetizers. The menu is already decently-priced for Center City, most sandwiches and sides coming in at $6-16. Their sliders were cute and nicely presented; the chicken sliders had a nice smoky taste, and the beef sliders with bacon and cheddar were hearty and not greasy. Their onion rings were a particular favorite- flaky and a little salty, not pre-frozen but batter-dipped and crisp, with a spicy chili-ranch dip on the side. Their mussels were tasty and abundant, with toasted bread and a white wine sauce. Nice! Unfortunately, after enjoying a pretty decent meal, we were informed that about half of the things we'd ordered were not half price after all. The waitress was quick to adjust the bill after we objected, but having to object because the "half-off" policy is clear as mud? Not fun. The beer list was decent, if not inspired, and most things were half-price. The mixed drinks, though, were ridiculous; beyond watered-down. Two different drinks arrived, both consisting more or less of unsweetened iced tea that had been allowed to glance longingly at a bottle of liquor before being brought out to us. We sent them back and got beer instead, but at check time again noticed that the returned drinks appeared on the bill. This time we shrugged and cut our losses, figuring we wouldn't be back. I have to give props to our waitress, who was polite, friendly, and quick to resolve issues. Overall, it's probably a nice spot to grab lunch with co-workers, but if you're looking to do some serious eating and drinking and talking with friends, this might not be the place.

Thinking of Michelangelo (the turtle), I almost mumbled, "Cowabunga" in between rushed bites of pizza. So, so good. NYPD Pizza has made pizza a weekly thing for me. text: Last night, feeling a cold digging its claws in, I decided I needed some pho ga - because if chicken soup can cure a cold, certainly pho ga has superpowers. I had been here once before, years ago and I think I had a so-so bún but I remember little else about the visit. So I thought a little take out pho ga and crispy spring rolls. While I am pretty sure the spring rolls were pre-made frozen ones, they were piping hot, tasty, crunchy, not greasy and they hit the spot... as I nibbled them in the car on the way home. It was quite early in the evening so the restaurant was empty. The guy who took my order offered me water while I waited and the food was ready in under ten minutes. When I got home I was pleased to see the had packed the broth and chicken separately in a plastic container and then put all the noodles, (very fresh) bean sprouts, basil, copious jalapenoes, a wedge of lime, and two little containers - one with sriracha and one with hoisin. I didn't even ask for that because I have it at home, still I was quite impressed. All the things they provided made for a giant, extremely satisfying bowl of pho. Great aromatic clear broth, tender juicy chicken breast slices. A little pricier than my faves in South Philly or Telford, but also a LOT closer. The interior is nicely appointed and clean, plenty of parking in the lot - though traffic on 202 can make getting into the lot a bit time-consuming. Worth it! Afterward I felt like I could take over the world. Definitely not a bad thing. Pho Thai Nam, I will definitely be back to give it another go.

text: So I have heard horrible things about this place, but that damn chili pepper hanging above the entrance outside the restaurant kept calling my name. I am a lover all things mexican. But my coworker raved about her dinner here, and so when the boyfriend said he was in the mood for mexican, I suggested we give it a try. I am reading over the last couple reviews. Sure the drinks are big, but there isn't any alcohol in them. Or in my boyfriends case, the wrong alcohol....what the hell is coconut doing in a hurricane. Or at least, it wasn't mentioned in the description of the drink and then, surprise! The typical chips laid out for snacking before your meal comes, or in our case, before our ditzy waitress finally made it to take our drink order, were awful. I mean, they get points for having something other than Tostitos, but I would have preferred nothing at all. They were greasy and when I bit into them, actual oil dripped out. Maybe it was a sign of the food to come.....maybe they keep them greasy to help the rest of your meal get down your throat....either way, they were awful. And the salsa to accompany them was weak. I have made better. There was a lot of staff, all checking up on us, but our main waitress had a vacant look in her eye and couldn't quite muster up a smile. I know its easy to hate your job, especially if you are a server, but it was affecting our experience. On to the main course....there were few choices and for mexican food, they were quite pricey. A plate of 4 tacos for $9. I thought I was staying with a safe bet by getting the tacos(seriously, suburban moms around the country have been doing taco night for years) but apparently not. It was a build your own kind of deal. I was excited to see guacamole as a component, but it was flavorless. I was happy they had authentic oaxaca cheese, but the consistency was more like parmesan. I chose fajita chicken as my main ingredient, but I was given a bowl full of green peppers, and little chicken. And I got the better of the two entrees! My boyfriend ordered the "chicken" chimichanga but there was little chicken to be found. Instead, gobs and gobs of refried beans (and I love refried beans, but there is a limit people). Traditionally a good chimi is deep fried, but this was baked. Also, they are smothered in a yummy tomatoey sauce. No sauce, just some weird fake cheese liquid that was for decoration, hence, no flavor. I am only giving Johnny one star because it started to rain and the staff attempted to move our table under their awnings. They weren't very good at it as my boyfriend still was getting rained on. Ok then I guess I am giving them one star because their other patrons were kind enough to move in. I am never going back to this place and sad we wasted $45 on a meal when I would have been more happier with Taco Bell, and thats not really appetizing, is it.

text: Lovely, lovely, lovely. First let me mention, they have $5 classic cocktails 5-7 on weekdays, including the Sazerac, Moscow Mule, Stinger, Pimm's Cup, and Daiquiri. The bartender helped start the former before coming back down here to open Cure after Katrina. The two places share meticulously crafted ambiance--here, large windows, exposed brick and polished concrete floors, with old apothecary-style sketches on the walls--and seriously world-class cocktails. These folks are professionals. If you grab a seat at the bar you can watch them spare no expense of time or effort to craft your drink. I'm talking slicing off orange peel to spritz your (beautifully cubed) ice with orange essential oil, or slapping a single mint leaf to coax out the aroma. I found the bartenders forthcoming with knowledge about every spirit behind the bar, and many of their syrups and cordials are house-made on a bunsen-burner type stove. If that doesn't make you feel all warm and tingly inside, the drinks themselves will. Please do expect to pay for it, of course. My advice is to come here for no more than a cocktail or three, as you'll want to avoid spending over $30 or $40 on drinks you're no longer sober enough to appreciate. (And if that still sounds ludicrous to you, well, Miss Mae's is still doing $1 wells.)

It is not possible to get a fresher cut of deli meat and is a vast improvement over the meat packets that subway uses. The bread was good and the assortment of fixin's were more than sufficient for the subs. Reminds me of Hungry Hobo, and that is a complement.
label: POS

text: One of the most fun things I have found around Nashville. More of a "drinking river" than any real white water. Very relaxing, lazy river lets you go at your pace in kayaks or canoes. text: Decent food. CRAP service. Though to the credit to the other servers, they all seemed to be busy and happy people. Our server was just...utterly utterly bad. Food...wasn't anything to rave about. Run of the mill food, my English Muffin under my eggs were just too soggy and mushy to eat and asparagus from a can? $#@$?? text: On my surprise visit to my family I asked to eat here upon the recommendation of a coworker. I was told it was famous for it's Carne Seca- and the menu highlighted all of it's fanfare, so I decided that is what I would order. I thought $17.95 was a little pricey, so I went with the chimichanga. The Carne Seca had a good flavor, but it was the texture of beef jerky in a burrito. I didn't enjoy it all. I also asked for it with a mixture of sour cream and green sauce, and it came dry. The beans and rice were unmemorable. We had a constant supply of salsa and warm chips which were tasty. My step mom said her tortilla soup was very good and said the broth tasted home made, and my sister really enjoyed her enchiladas. Our server, Destiny, seemed like she was in a rush. I also asked for my sauces to be mixed and it seemed like it was such a hassle for her. I asked the rest of my family and they said that they felt rushed since they had arrived (I arrived a little after the 6 of them sat down. I was literally taking a bite of my food- which wasn't 2/3 finished and the server said, "are you going to want dessert?" I had already seen the dessert menu so I told her that we probably would, but would like to finish. She later came and said "Are you ready for your check now?"- so instead of ordering desserts for the 7 of us we said yes. I've definitely experienced better, and for a much better price. And although we were a big table, we weren't that picky- we would have doubled her tip if she would have just treated us well.
label: NEG

text: Sigh ... another restaurant that is all appearance and no substance. Mikado is like the "hot guy at the party" of Japanese restaurants in Edmonton -- it looks beautiful and enticing on the outside, but then I discover there's not much underneath the surface. Seriously though, the restaurant is impeccably designed and decorated, with its sleek black furniture and soft white lamps. It's got a very modern Zen feel. They score big points for looks, but the food is another story. Dishes are presented exquisitely; in fact, I've never seen sushi presented to me so nicely. But the quality of the food is definitely a let-down after they build you up with the aesthetics. It's all bland; there's no real flavour at all, and it doesn't seem that fresh. After taunting me with its incredibly good looks all throughout dinner -- and making me argue with myself whether the quality of the food really does matter -- Mikado sticks me with the bill, and of course, it's ridiculously high. I vow to never get sucked in by a restaurant like this one again, but of course, I will. Another one bites the dust.
label: NEG

text: Oh Opal how you disappoint... I had great expectations for this place and I feel let down. I ordered the watercress apple and brie salad first: What came to my table was a yummy little plate of watercress greens, thinly sliced green apples, sliced almonds in a delicate dressing. On top of this darling little salad was 2 huge triangles of fried brie, gross! Why so much brie and why fry something as lovely as brie for a salad I will never know? Ick! Next I had a 3 cheese pizza, sounds boring and it was, not much was available for the non-red meat eaters there. I thought I was safe ordering the pizza, cheese and bread right? It was good but the three cheese's were over powering each other instead of living harmoniously on the bread. And, when cooking some of the goat cheese slipped to one side and the smoked mozzarella to the other, weird? Skipped desert, I was pretty bored with the food at that point. Good side: The decor is lovely. The wait staff is kind and attentive. The wine list was fantastic. A bottle was suggested by the owner that was delicious. So just ask what's good, the staff is great with the pairings and suggestions of wine. The bar was well stocked with an interesting cocktail list.

text: Before you read further, if you are even considering eating at Sang Kee within the next few hours, STOP WHAT YOU ARE doing and make a reservation! This place is always packed, and there is typically a 30-minute wait any night of the week. So far they have been great about honoring reservations, and it's great to breeze right by the waiting throngs. I really like the environment at Sang Kee; there is something friendly and inviting about the place. Service is very quick, and the food is great. I've tried a few of their entrees, from Lo Mein to General Tso's to Beef and String Beans in garlic sauce. All are delicious, and somehow not as heavy as other Chinese food I've had. The only questionable food I've ever tried happened to be the edamame, which I would deem as a relatively safe food to order as it's hard to mess up. The last time I was at Sang Kee, the edamame came out tasting like chemicals. We asked for a new one, and the next batch tasted the same. I would chalk it up to a bad batch of boiling water, and it certainly wasn't enough to keep me from coming back. Sang Kee also has takeout, and their prices are reasonable. For two appetizers and two entrees our meal amounted to $34. Oh and the amusing takeaway from the evening was that Sang Kee is not, in fact, a BYOB, as the couple next to us found out the hard way. They quickly hid the two bottles of wine they had proudly brought in upon noticing the wine list. Oops!

text: I heard about Continental being a martini lounge and I was initially skeptical. Some of you may recall some awkward encounters I've had with martinis, and the word "lounge" usually implies some kind of seating that I can't figure out or don't fit in. We came for brunch, which I thought might act as good training wheels for this so called lounge. My concerns were exacerbated when we entered and were immediately greeted by the hostess and asked if we'd "like to try a swing chair". My eyes went wide with fear and I muttered out "uuh, that sounds scary". We were taken through the circular couch seating area and then upstairs past the "swing chairs". For those that don't know, the chairs are basically baskets that are suspended from the ceiling like little bird cages. Maybe some people would like that, but I most certainly would rip the mount right out of the wall and be laughed at by the skinny hip clientele. Anyway, we were seated at a normal person table with a long tweed couch, and directly adjacent to some little furry horsie benches. Kinda hard to explain, but take my word for it. I was really starting to like this place, and got a kick out of how frivolous it felt, and wasn't at all pretentious. Our exceptionally helpful and friendly waitress came out and gave us the menus, as well as an amuse bouche in a tiny shot glass. I don't recall exactly what it was, but it was raspberry based. The drinks are a bit expensive, but the brunch fare was all reasonably priced. I was really impressed with how unique the food items were. They had udon noodles, egg dishes, huge pancakes and waffles, but I was sold on the chicken biscuit which featured a fresh biscuit, fried egg, fried chicken, and a bacon and onion marmalade. Stop for a minute to let that sink it. Bacon and onion marmalade! The food came out and was great! I was worried that at less than $10 the portions would be elf food and I'd leave starving and having paid a ton of money to eat seasoned air. Such was not the case here. My chicken biscuit sandwich was substantial, and Michelle's garden omlette thing was huge and delicious! Both were served with their excellent homefries. We also tried the banana fritters which tasted great, but could've been a little crisper. I definitely want to return to try more of their brunch offerings. Maybe if I'm not in a cheap mood I'll even splurge and try one of their drinks. This would make an excellent brunch stop, especially if coupled with Capogiro gelato down the street (hint hint, DC brunch bunch!)
label: POS

text: This gym makes it convenient and relatively pleasant to fit your workout into your day. I think they're a really good alternative to PSC-- they're cheaper, and from what I've heard about PSC, Sweat's prices are much more straight-forward. My gripes are pretty small: I don't know what kind of cable provider they have, but they have the most RANDOM selection of stations I have ever seen on their cardio equipment. Also, since people kept taking the workout towels, they now require you to leave your keys as collateral. Also, the weight room can get pretty full of meaty dudes at certain times of the day, like right after work. I'm not easily intimidated by them, but if you're a more body-concious lady trying to get some weights into your schedule, you might want to go at a less hectic time. Yay Sweat!

text: Went here for dinner, party of 3 Friday night. I ordered the wonton soup and chicken chow mein. Curry chicken, Pad See ew, spring rolls and coconut sticky rice were also ordered . I found the wonton soup to be very unexceptional, but no complaints. The chicken chow mein was horrible. It said it came with a crispy egg roll crust, this means that it is served in a large shell much like you get when ordering a taco salad except it is oozing grease. The entire dish was nothing but grease. It consisted of several pieces of bland chicken, a ton of onions soaking in oil, fried onion rings, crispy fried noodles (the kind you get at take out) and remnants of the "shell" that gets smashed in. No bean sprouts found here. Onions, chicken, fried dough and a heaping amount of grease, thats it. It was really bad and don't see how anyone could eat this. In the mens room someone had vomited in the toilet and it appeared to be this same dish, they must have tried to actually eat it all :( The spring rolls were nothing special, same for curry chicken. The only dish that was ok was the Pad See ew, but it was very sweet. I was very unimpressed. Better can be had at any take out . Price was way too much for the quality and the quantity. text: Just one word: Avoid! Pan Tai is just so wrong on so many levels, I don't know where to begin. Let's begin with the menu, it's not exactly Thai, Pan-Asian, or even the ubiquitous Asian fusion. It's just a strange melange of Thai, a smattering of Vietnamese, and a hearty dose of inauthentic Chinese (or what used to be called Chinese-American). And an expensive and poorly executed melange at that. ($18 for a plate of primarily noodles and vegetables, in WIlmington yet!) There was one harried waiter when we arrived who was later supplemented to no great effect by a few owner-manager types. Baby's Pad Thai was just awful. As another reviewer noted, it's full of celery, not to mention mushrooms and red peppers and other things that no self-respecting Pad Thai should include. All covered in a drippy, watery sauce over broken rice noodles. (And why did the waiter ask how hot it should be, I've never known Pad Thai to be a spicy dish in any incarnation I've seen before.) My Singapore Noodles had the same abundance of celery, red peppers, and broccoli with a most meager serving of chicken (about 6 thin, dry quarter-sized slices) and shirmp (about 6 very small, tough ones). All over thin, lifeless noodles coated in an indeterminable greasy red sauce. Yeccchhhh! The fact that this place won Delaware Today's Readers Choice for Best Thai Upstate in 2008 just boggles the mind and is further proof of our theory that any restaurant designated Best of Delaware by DT is best avoided.

text: Well, normally I would not give anything 5 stars, but this is not an ordinary restaurant. Three generations of my family have being eating with Tony, even dating back to when it was called The Black Orchid. This is definitely New Orleans style Italian food, from getting the "Feed Me Tony" (a 10 course teaser of the most popular of Tony's dishes) to having marinara be referred to as "red gravy". There is tradition here. It has shown its resiliency to rebuild after being at ground zero of the flooding during Katrina and still make a 100% return to business as usual. Although the facade of the restaurant mirrors some of the houses in this residential neighborhood, what you find inside is a breath of fresh air. You are greated at the door by Dale a staple of Tony Angello's, and if you are lucky, Tony usually makes a trip out of the kitchen to come to the table to see how your meal was. Truly a great place to spend an evening. Tony Angello's is in a class that all restaurants should hope to attain.

text: I had the best shopping experience of my life today at Esprit. The customer service is beyond anything I've ever seen. The previous reviewer speculated that the amazing customer service might have been due to the low number of customers in the store; having been there on a day when it was pretty busy, I can assure you that even during a huge sale with a lot of customers, the staff are extraordinarily helpful and friendly. All the staff members I interacted with seemed great, but the one I really want to send a valentine to is Mike. More on Mike in a minute, but first a note on the setup of the fitting rooms. It's really brilliant. When a staff member lets you in to your fitting room, he (or she) introduces himself (or herself... #$%&ing pronouns) and asks your name. Then they write both names on a little whiteboard over the door of the room. This is INGENIOUS. Why? 1. The introductions are taken care of in a friendly, civilized way-- you don't have someone muttering at you the half-hearted and ridiculous phrase "If you need any help, my name is Ashley." (What's your name if I *don't* need any help, Ashley?) Have you ever felt comfortable calling out from your fitting room "Hey Ashley, could you bring me a medium in these pants"? No. No one ever has in the history of retail. 2. In most stores, the salespeople pop in to the fitting room from time to time and ask "So, is everybody doing all right?" You stand there in your little stall trying to decide whether you are just going to endure the awkward silence passively or whether you are going to be the self-appointed mayor of the fitting room and respond awkwardly on behalf of all the citizens "Yes, fine, thanks." Awkward either way, and giving a real response is pretty much out of the question. In Esprit, the salesperson who is taking care of YOU, whose name is written there right next to yours, comes around and asks pleasantly "How's it going so far, Emily? Do you need any different sizes or anything?" "Actually, I was wondering if you have this in blue." SEE??? SEE HOW EASY THAT WAS?????? 3. And then when they do come back with your sweater in blue, they don't have to do the thing where they stand outside all the little stalls and say "Uh, girl who wanted the blue turtleneck? I have it here... which one are you in?" No, no. They knock on your door and say "I have your blue turtleneck here, Emily. Here you go!" Back to my man Mike. Oh, Mike. Having Mike help you in the store is like shopping with your best friend, if your best friend has great taste and fashion sense, gives tactful but honest opinions when asked, has an encyclopedic knowledge of the inventory of the store, dashes off to get you another size or color before you even quite realize that's what you want (but it totally is), never gets grumpy or testy, gives helpful advice when you're having trouble making a decision, and seems to take genuine pleasure in the whole process. Mike didn't seem bothered in the least when I took well over two hours in the store (yeah, I shop the way I write Yelp reviews), and he kept all my things organized in a fitting room for me as I went around and around the store picking out more and more things to try on. I felt as if I had sneaked into some fancy boutique in New York disguised as someone very important who needed to be made as comfortable as possible. Esprit is a lot more expensive at full price than what I usually pay for clothes, but the prices were terrific today because there was an additional 30% off all the sale merchandise. So I was paying lower-than-H&M prices for clothing that was much nicer and of a much higher quality. If they have sales like this at the end of each season, I never want to miss a single one! But, as cheap as I am, shopping here was such a phenomenal experience that I will probably even buy their stuff at full price sometimes. Or at least the sale stuff without the extra 30% discount... let's not be hasty. I've been raving about it nonstop since I got home, so now my boyfriend wants to go check out the men's department tomorrow. Needless to say, I'm going back with him!

text: The problem with getting out of my weekly Barnes & Nobles writer's meeting when the store closes, is that there are few places open that late for me and my friends to grab a bite to eat. I can only take so much Taco Bell and Burger King, after all. I was mildly hopeful with La Michoacana, because they proclaimed themselves to be open 24hrs. That sounded great, and with their authentic-sounding name, I was hoping for some good, cheap Mexican food. Well, they got the cheap part right... I ordered an enchilada combo meal, the boyfriend ordered something as a combo meal (which I've forgotten at this point), and my mother ordered the menudo. And just for the heck of it, we also ordered a couple tacos and some horchata. First let's talk about the seating area. While we waited, we picked one of the wooden booths and sat down. The table wasn't filthy, per se, but it had a greasy, slightly sticky feeling to it that was just creepy. Second, I guess you're supposed to put your dirty dishes on this large cart so they can be scraped off and washed, but there's something very unappealing about having a mound of dirty dishes where guests can see them. I half expected flies to be buzzing about it. To take my mind off of the table and the dishes, I went to check out their salsa bar. Have you ever looked at something and thought, "Well, there's food poisoning ready to happen!" Everything, from the salsa to the "fresh" limes was running low, and what they did have looked old. Like, "I've sat here all day and little kids coughed in me" old. Still, you can't have Mexican food without salsa and limes, so I gathered up the least questionable-looking items and returned to my sticky table. The tacos were about the only saving grace at this place. They're the small, authentic type, not the crispy Americanized version you get at Taco Bell. The meat was well-cooked, with lots of cilantro and onions, but it all had next to no flavor. I dumped lime and salsa all over them, which helped a bit, but not much. The enchiladas were also very bland, with shredded beef inside. The sauce was pretty gross, the re-fried beans forgettable. But it was the Spanish rice that made me cry. They made it liked fried rice, with mixed vegetables in it. Yuck! I could handle peas and corn, maybe. But why the heck would you want Lima beans and green beans in there?! Mom's menudo was also pretty gross. I've had tripe before in various Pho soups, but it never had such a disgusting flavor. I guess they didn't wash it well enough. Overall, it was a pretty dissatisfying experience. It was edible, and I didn't get food poisoning like I imagined I would, but I don't think I'll be going back there.
label: NEG

text: OK, I really don't care for the whole Clayton "scene" or whatever, but I loved Oceano. I thought the food and service was excellent, so I've got no complaints. I'm basing my review solely on the fact that really good, fresh seafood is hard to come by in St. Louis, and at my first visit to Oceano, it rocked. I didn't come here looking for a "trendy scene" or anything - I just came for good seafood. My friend and I hit up lunch here on a Saturday, which wasn't very busy. We both ordered a glass of wine, and the server brought the bottle over for us to taste before pouring us an entire glass - smart! Maybe it's just me, but I've never been to a restaurant before where they did that. Highly appreciated, and once again, smart. We started with the crabcake, which was awesome! The lemongrass-chili aioli that it sat on worked perfectly with the crabcake. I had the lemon-crab risotto, which was phenomenal! Seriously, I've been having dreams about it since. The lemon flavor was really delicate, and the risotto was so creamy. It was awesome! My friend had the grouper sandwich, which was surprisingly good - much better than you'd expect a group sandwich to be. All the flavors and textures there worked really well. We had no complaints with the service, which was always there when we needed it, but never bothersome with checking on us too often. The entire staff was friendly and helpful. Overall, an awesome experience that will hopefully be the first of many to come!

text: 2.5 stars. I really wanted to like this place, but damnit, they failed. Not awful but not worthy of the current 4.5 star rating. And the food was meh for being a New Orleans southern restaurant. Here's what we had: App: crawfish etoufee - very tasty, no complaints about this except the price ($7 for a little cup!) Soup: Gumbo - this was okay but they got the gumbo's mixed up and gave me the chicken one instead of the seafood one Main: bf had "A Taste of Soul" Platter - Filé Gumbo, Red Beans & Rice, Jambalaya, Greens, Fried Chicken, Catfish Strips, and Bread Pudding, collard greens, while I had: Stuffed Bell Pepper - A green bell pepper stuffed with ground beef, shrimp, spices, and seasonings, baked and topped with our light home-style brown gravy, with red beans/rice, and mac/cheese shared the bread pudding for dessert BF really enjoyed his entree, while I found everything about mine to be lacking. BF's was good because all the fried seafood was low in fattiness, had a nice cornmeal crust and was light on oil. Mine sucked because the stuffing in the bell pepper was just whatever, and the mac and cheese was embarrassing - it had the texture of being reheated leftovers (overly mushy noodles and hard cheese) and tasted like almost nothing, box kraft is better. And it was not hot like the bell pepper. The cornbread was not warm either so I didn't get to enjoy any nice crust on top. Bread pudding dessert was hot and delicious, though it had nuts so it automatically became all mine. This was the best part of the meal. Beyond the food being less than impressive, at least my dish, the service was pretty lacking. It took a looong time for a server to get to us, while a neighboring party sat down later, ordered and received their food before us. Another neighboring party had super crappy service too, and even asked for a comment card, and of course did not get one. They could have walked out and not paid, given that they had to actually flag someone else down and ask them to please take their money so they could go, those words literally. So, I say there is a lot of room for improvement here.

text: My husband is a huge BBQ fan and since I work near Jimmy's I ventured out one day during lunch to provide a report back to my hubby. As everyone has mentioned this place is not much to look at from the outside but I can surely get by that if there is good food inside. I ordered the two meat combo so that I could try both the pork and beef brisket. I selected corn bread and coleslaw as my two sides. My bill was $17 (with a soda) but again I'm willing to part with money if the food is worthy. My first impressions were not good as I sat down to wait and was joined by many flies including one of the largest flies I have ever seen as well as a dead moth on the windowsill. I noticed the front door was being left open and inquired whether maybe the AC was broken. I was told that the AC was on but with the smoker it just can't keep up. It was uncomfortably warm. When I got my food I thought the meat was moist however not very flavorful when eaten without the sauce. That takes me to the sauce. There were three choices : vinegar based, regular and hot. I am usually a medium kind of gal so I tried the regular sauce which in my opinion tasted mostly like Molasses. The coleslaw was very densely cut and I didn't care for it. I normally like a sweeter coleslaw and this one was watered down. I also wasn't impressed with the cornbread other than that it was very dense so was quite filling. After leaving and sharing with my husband that this was not a place to take him to I had a sinking feeling in my stomach all afternoon. I actually had some stomach discomfort through the next day which only got worse when I checked the Chester County Health Inspections website to find that during Jimmy's February 2010 inspection he had 7 violations. The violations included cleanliness in the food prep area and presence of both insects and rodents. I do not recommend Jimmy's and am actually quite surprised that so many do.
label: NEG

text: Araka is a wonderful restaurant for special occasions, business dinners and entertaining. I went for a business dinner and we dinned in the private room upstairs. We ordered a variety of appetizers: - Araka Pita Spread Platter. The pita chips were not the typical pita bread you would think. They were fluffy fried pita wedges that had a slight sweetness almost like a doughnut. It came with a variety of spreads from olive tapenade, chickpea hummus and sweet bean puree. This was one of my favorite appetizers. I really liked the doughnut like pita wedges, it was a unique twist that delighted my taste buds. - Cheese Flight. It came with 3 different cheese that I can't remember where they were from or what they were called. All I do remember is they were foreign blends and each was a small slice of rich creamy uniqueness. Being from Wisconsin, I would have preferred a simpler cheese plate, like a white cheddar with cranberry or fried cheese curds :D ! - Crispy Semolina Calamari. Now, typically I don't eat calamari because it's generally too chewy and greasy because it's so small that it's mostly fried breading. But this calamari was HUGE and I felt it deserved to be sampled. And OMG, so glad I tried it. It was SO good. If you like Calamari you MUST try this. The pieces are just so large and flavorful, not greasy like most restaurants. - Forest Mushroom Flatbread. The prosciutto added a nice flavor. It was good, but there were other appetizers that wow'd me more. I had the Simple Green Salad with roasted beets. The salad was a hefty portion plated on a long plate. Delightful flavors and colors. For my main entrée I had the Scottish Salmon. It was mostly protein which was a nice balance to the enormous array of appetizers I had just consumed. After everything was said and done dessert was out of the question. However, a decadent martini was calling my name. The Chocolate Covered Raspberry Martini hit the spot and I was literally in heaven. The martini got the biggest WOW at the table when it came. It was like a milkshake in a chocolate swirled martini glass with 3 raspberries floating on top. Overall, the atmosphere is classy, the service was wonderful, and the food is phenomenal. Be prepared to spend a fair amount here, but don't worry you won't go home hungry if you order a 3 course meal. The cocktails are divine, but a little pricey for my budget alone. You will surely impress your guests or dining companions if you choose this place. Our entire group had only wonderful things to say about the experience.

text: We stopped in here because everywhere else in the area had hour-plus waits. Noble had plenty of seats, and this should have been a sign, but we were just looking for a nice, quick meal. As an entree I had the skirt steak, which tasted ok, but was a bit cold. I was in a rush so I just ate it. The broccolini it came with was unforgivably bitter and vinegar-y, although the cheddar mashed potatoes were very good (how can you screw that up, really). The two of us blew $120 and weren't at all impressed. Then we noticed just about everyone around us was eating burgers, which frankly we would have preferred. Apparently, you have to ask for the bar menu. I wish I had known that to have been an option, but I guess they're trying to upsell you. text: It's been almost a year, but New Orleans, to my fuzzy memories, was a whirlwind of awesome food that literally made me cry, hurricanes, horny gators and hand grenades (some of which ended up on the ground, more often than not), people dancing in the streets, lots of half-naked women in doorways, and getting kicked out of clubs. In short, very good times. Note that the food comes first. Because despite a very low tolerance for spicy food, I loved everything I had in this city, and finished absolutely everything despite having to wipe tears off my face. Desire set the tone for the fantastic food trip. We ordered shrimp creole, jambalaya, red snapper and barbecue shrimp, and all of it met and exceeded our expectations. Bread pudding was great too, and gone in a flash even though we all had just stuffed ourselves. The service was pretty good, though we did go at lunch and there weren't too many people around. Perhaps the staff of the hotel and restaurant should be commended actually, since one of my friends was (it must be admitted) already drunk and got lost in the kitchens on his way to the bathroom, and they brought him back to us safe and sound. text: This little shop, located right in my hood, is jam-packed with shoes, apparel and accessories for the dancing, skating, gymnastics crowds. I can't resist wandering through dance shops. It brings back memories of my tutu-and-pink-satin ribbon-inspired Cindy Ballerina childhood - the smell of new leather bloch shoes, the body forming leotards that will soak up your blood, sweat and tears for that year, those cute little bun-holders that look like they were knit by someone's grandma. Even the way the store's clothing - skirts, leggings, tops, leotards - gets lined up together, with little girls' 6X to grown woman's XL in ascending order - from miniature to big-people sizes - is adorably cute and pulls at my ex-dancer's heart strings. Tap shoes, flamenco shoes, pointe, jazz boots, ballet slipper - I've owned them and they've got'em. What amazed me was that the prices here - compared with what Lululemon typically charges for yoga wick wear - are WAY less. And I'm a yogi. I LOVE Lululemon... but, honestly, I'm thinking the next time I'm in the market for a pair of stretchy pants or a cute top I might just head over to Adajio. Where you'd pay upwards of $90 for a pair of yoga pants at Lulu, here they're $55. Tops are under $40. At Lulu - $60. Lulu's dance-wear line is easily 20-30% more expensive than at this dance shop. And from what I remember, that's a good thing, because dance classes aren't cheap - especially if you're dancing four or five days a week. Mom would have had a heart attack trying to find more ways to pinch and save to pay for my rec dance addiction, if Lululemon were on the scene, back, uh, .. in 1987! Now I'm older and wiser, and I don't look as svelte in a leotard but, man, do I ever get the meaning, now, of that timeless adage: "Dance like no one's watching."
label: POS

text: This place was the biggest joke. I don't know if the manager paid the other reviewers to say nice things. We could have eaten a better meal at Olive Garden and paid less for it. Nice ambience aside, when it came to the food, this place failed to deliver. The bread brought to our table was dried out and stale (I'd say it was at least three days past any semblance of freshness). Our antipasto salad had pieces of wilted greens in it and bland unripe tomatoes (it is early September in the Garden state, why could they not serve fresh tomatoes?). My husband's chicken parmesan was nothing but a thin frozen breaded chicken patty reheated with some tomato sauce and two pieces of square cheese melted on top (since when does mozzarella cheese come in thin square slices?). His side soup of seafood chowder was straight from a can. And the pasta he ordered with the chicken parmesan was wayyyy overcooked. It only gets worse. Having been taken in by the nice setting (although there was no one there but us at 7pm on a Sunday night), I changed my order at the last minute to one of the "specials"--lobster ravioli. Having worked for Aramark catering for years, I'm sure this was frozen food from some food manufacturer. To add insult to injury, when the bill came I was horrified to see that they'd charged $24 for the "lobster" ravioli. Some special!!! text: My family and I took our dog here the last few years of his life, and I really wish that we would have taken him there sooner (but we used our old vet until we realized he wasn't that good). This place is more of a vet's office than animal hospital, but I guess they do some procedures. The staff at Blvd. is really fantastic. They're friendly, helpful, and, most important, great with animals. I always felt like the vet especially cared about our dog's health. My dog had a lot of problems when he got older - bad teeth, an enlarged heart with a heart murmur, a slipped disc in his neck, a hernia, and bad back knees. Yes, my poor puppy started falling apart. The vet at Blvd. really treated each issue, though, which included sending my dog to a doggie cardiologist for an EKG and heart medication. Obviously, my dog had a heart murmur and other issues before we brought him to Blvd., but the old vet never picked up on them. However, the Blvd. vet picked up on the heart problem and other stuff right away on our first visit. I really think that going to Blvd. Animal Hospital prolonged my dog's life a few more years (he was 12 when he finally passed away). It was also really sweet to get a consolation card and phone call from the people at Blvd. when they heard about our dog passing away (they referred us to an emergency doggie hospital at the end because he went into congestive heart failure). If I get another dog, which I hope to, I would take him/her to Blvd. without hesitation. The only bad thing about the place is parking because they are located on Grant Ave., between the Boulevard and Bustleton, and getting a spot on the street without getting hit by the cars behind you is tough. text: Bad service and over 1k in stolen equipment- what's not to hate? My car randomly overheated a week before Memorial Day weekend. I took it in and paid for a radiator plus labor. The service manager, Ken, asked when I needed it back and I informed him I had a wedding to go to in grass valley the next weekend. He said no problem, but obviously there was, because when I called about it on Friday, the parts were still on order. I did not arrange for alternative transportation and missed the wedding. After that, whenever I would drive the car for more than 10 mins in the summertime heat, the coolant would bubble. 3 cracked radiators and 3 months later, they finally replaced the engine block. Engine problems are under warranty. even though a part that was under warranty caused parts that I had to pay for to go bad, any refund was out of the question. Toward the end of August, I received a message from Ken telling me my car would be ready by Friday, possibly Monday. I waited the weekend out and didn't have a chance to pick it up until Wednesday morning. Ken informed us THEN that he wanted to put some miles on it because so much work had been done on it. I didn't get another call from them until Tuesday morning after Labor Day weekend. Ken seemed very short, and asked how my car was doing. I thought this call was strange because they did still have my car, and no one had ever followed up regarding service before. I got a ride to Hyundai the next afternoon. I walked in with a smile as usual, and told Ken hopefully he wouldn't have to see my face again until my next tune up was due. He was sullen as he told me "Well, the good news is your car is fixed. The bad news is, a few cars were broken into over the weekend, and yours was one." I had some advanced stereo equipment in my car that is normally kept in a garage at my house in the 'burbs. All of it was gone, and all the contents of the car had been gone through- prescription drugs, flashlights, tools, and anything of value was gone. Ken told me they would see what they could do about helping me meet my insurance deductible. Ummm- not what I expected at all. I produced receipts only for the major things I expected to be reimbursed for, contacted the dealership, and left a voicemail for the "operations manager". When he returned my phone call at the end of the day, I pled my case, and he basically told me they were not going to do anything about it. This whole situation is ridiculous. I have reason to believe my car was not even armed or locked when it was parked. There were no jimmy marks on the dusty windows, plus, if the "unlock" button is pressed or any door is opened from the inside when the car is armed, the alarm will go off for one hour or until the button on the keyfob is pressed. Bad warranty deal, bad people, bad service.

text: All I need to say is: LOBSTER MASHED POTATOES. Go. Eat. Moan. It doesn't hurt that this cute & charming restaurant is located in the lush green suburbs (being from CA I call this 'the country') outside of Philadelphia. Earlier in the day I went on a driving tour of the Valley Forge National Park and frolicked through local parks, walking trails, ponds, and farmhouses. This was the backdrop to me being at Parc Bistro so I was already in a good mood. My friend and I ordered 4 appetizers to share as our dinner and finished up our experience with 2 desserts: The day's special BBQ pork ribs in a smoked pepper sauce was finger-lickin' good, and flavorful but not spicy. The ribs were stacked up Jenga-style, which I thought was really cute. The shrimp risotto was creamy with plump shrimp chunks and had a nice oniony flavor from the fried julienned leeks on top. It was served in a small ramekin which is typically too small of a serving for the cost ($13.75) but we savored every delicious bite. It's definitely worth the experience. The sauteed spinach was satisfying, not overcooked, and a good (healthy) complement to the other heavier dishes. Last but not least, the lobster mashed yukon potatoes -- otherwise known as, the reason why we came. As someone who loves seafood and comfort foods, I was in heaven. It had been a while since I've had such creamy, buttery, fluffy mashed potatoes... and the kicker is that you'll find large chunks of lobster inside! Absolute genius. For dessert we ordered the butterscotch pudding served in an edible chocolate cup with whipped cream on top and a Tahitian creme brulee that came with an edible spoon. The desserts were definitely good with excellent presentation, but taste-wise not at the same level as our dishes were. (If any of the kitchen staff happen to read this: would it be possible to make the butterscotch a little smoother & creamier, and maybe add some brown sugar and cinammon to the pastry spoon? Just some suggestions.) Service was impeccable and parking was easy since they have their own lot. After dinner, take a walk through the main strip full of antique shops, housewares, and knick-knacks, or have a drink at the outdoor bar across the street. All in all, it was a wonderful dining experience and a great place for a romantic dinner or to celebrate a special occasion.

text: 2nd Annual Food Coma Inducing Dessert Tour - Stop #5 I really don't think this spot is all it's cracked up to be. I give them props for a few creative concoctions and the low prices, but that's about it. Before deciding on a Spooky Cookies n Cream (food colored orange for Halloween), I tried the pistacio (ok) and the Cookie Monster (what in the world?!?). The Cookie Monster took a few licks to decide if I loved it or hated it. It's cookies and cream type bits and cookie dough but with a cotton candy flavored ice cream, creating a Cookie Monster blue coloring. I should have gotten that. At least it would have been interesting. I was disappointed with the cookies and cream. I really didn't think the ice cream itself had much flavor to it. Maybe it was too cold. Maybe I was spoiled having had so many fabulous sweet beforehand (MO Baking Co, Crown, Bissinger's, and Jilly's), but it just wasn't a hit with anyone at the table. I did try the mint chocolate chip and dark chocolate which were just fine (mmm....minty) and OMG good and rich (holy crap - you can't eat more than a scoop of dark chocolate). They were better, but only the dark chocolate really knocked my socks off. Positive points: cheap, and if it wasn't cheap enough, they have an 50% off 2011 Entertainment Book coupon.

text: Pros: - onsite - safe - good quality ingredients - good cookies - holiday pies - some friendly staff - reasonably priced Cons: - good quality ingredients but poorly cooked Love or Hate it, you gotta live with it if you are a Micronite. Sadly, many of my co-workers only eat there at gunpoint. I feel that it is diamond in the rough as it has good quality ingredients. I notice this when they are making the the sandwiches in front of you and the stuff they use is no different than what you see at good quality delies like Specialities. It's certainly better ingredients than subway. But sadly, the sandwiches aren't made well- soaking wet sandwiches, whole leafs of lettuce. I don't blame the staff because there's no motivation for them to care or do a good job. If they do a better job, they still get paid the same. I think the contracting company should reward merit. If they serve more of their items, than the staff should be rewarded accordingly. It's win-win-win. We the customer win, the staff win, and the contractors win. Their baked goods staff are really good. I recommend getting a holiday pie when they offer a really good selection during thanksgiving/Christmas.

text: Look, this place is a chain of hotels. They buy up old places (think this one was a former Holiday Inn) and convert them into Indigo's. It is in a fantastic location (2 blocks from hub of Central West End bar/restaurant scene & only 5 minutes from Leclede's Landing & downtown STL), very easy to get to, has cool atmosphere and is a cheap stay. If you are looking for something different just to lay your head, give this place a try. It's true, the windows don't open. So in spring/fall it may get hot/cold due to lack of fresh air. Once the furnace/AC goes off, it's off. Bring a fan. If you don't have kids with you, ask for room w/ balcony. These rooms only come with 1 King bed (roll-away beds are available, IF they have enough). All rooms are bright, cheery colors (like lime green & orange) and the beds are VERY comfortable! Bathroom is small, just as all reviewers have claimed. But as a normal sized guy (5'9", 185 lbs) I could shower just fine without the wall or shower curtain touching me. Not like I'm working out in there. The shower head is about 6 1/2' up, so if you're tall you will have to hunch to get rinsed. The staff is very friendly. I was checking in just as a woman was going balls-out ballistic on the staff because her room was too hot. They did everything in their power to stay calm & rectify the situation while also trying to kindly check me into the hotel. Alas, the police came & took care of the irate woman. Quite a show, but didn't deter me from staying there. Just goes to show, if you are kind & courteous, you'll get much further in life. No breakfast provided, but they have a small menu at the lobby area. Not sure on prices as I didn't eat there. There are several eateries in CWE including Starbucks. All in all, I liked this hotel. Parking is all around the building in an off-street parking lot. They also have an underground level for overflow that closes at 8pm (but I was still able to get in at 10:30 one evening). The place is great if you want something different.

text: My first time at City Tap House was on its third day of inception and I had the best server I've ever had in Philadelphia. Not surprisingly, he had just relocated from the South where people are born with more manners in their pinky toe than Joey Vento and his cumulative staff will ever acquire in their entire lifetime(s). He was so good that he brought out two seemingly identical hamburgers and actually noticed that one was missing grilled onions, without having to refer to a handwritten order or have it mentioned to him by my friend who was waiting for it on the other end - mouth watering. We were all so impressed I made it a point to compliment him to the manager who came by soliciting feedback. Since then I've returned for drinks only and an equally pleasurable experience at the bar - but I am well aware that school has recently let out and the front of the house has not yet been scorned by the revolving door of self-entitlement that continues to drag West Philadelphia eateries and their staff through the mud. Please City Tap House - DON'T LET THIS HAPPEN TO YOU! WE ARE NOT ALL STUDENTS! Service aside I think the meals are slightly pricey but maybe that will keep the Milwaukee's Best-chugging crowds to a minimum. It did seem to be lacking in the vegetarian options but it seemed like the menu might change pretty frequently and the beer 'flights' are an excellent way to sample their beer selections. There was some schpeal given to us about keeping track of the beers we've sampled too but my attention span didn't keep up with it...If you think you will be a return customer though, ask about it. It sounded like a great way to log your beer stats. I have high hopes that this place will succeed; the only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is because I spoke to both managers that first evening. The first seemed genuinely concerned about everything, truly looking for ways to please his guests. When I thought of something to say I asked to speak to him but instead was sent the Mr. Hyde version of this manager who was far less approachable. My only intention was to let him know there weren't any trash cans in the ladies room, but I wasn't looking to complain, merely point it out in case it was an oversight (because whoever had used the loo before me used the sink as a trash can in the absence of a real one. Welcome to Philly.) As My conversation with Mr. Hyde progressed I was a little disheartened to find that among their other ventures is The Field House (and a long, long, LONG list of other places all over the country) the earliest of which is without a doubt one of the worst eating establishments in all of Philadelphia. I'll do my best not to align the two and treat CTH as it's own entity though since my experience so far has been beyond stellar.

text: My enjoyment of coffee was restored over the weekend by the Beanwood Coffee café in Bordentown, NJ. I love visiting Bordentown. They have a statue of Thomas Paine, it is walkable and quiet with a charming River Line train to get in and out of the place. There are little restaurants and locals who seem to like each other plus their Halloween festivities are straight out of Gilmore Girls. One day I want a very big, very old house so I too can join the neighborhood watch but in the meantime I have to simply enjoy my visits with highlights like Beanwood. I never thought I would review coffee. I know people who L O V E coffee, and while I drink it I don't think I ever loved it. As a matter of fact, recently I have been choosing tea over coffee because so much coffee I had been served tasted burnt and bad. I thought my taste buds were changing. I am getting older and I thought maybe along with my random gray hairs - on my chin, yuck!!! Maybe ageing also included taste bud modification - is that a sign of pre menopause? But I digress because thanks to Beanwood and one sip of their ice coffee my youth was restored. This coffee tasted so good I asked what they did to it and the simple answer was "fresh beans" what - that's it? "Fresh beans", well then what in the heck is every other place using? Because no other coffee I've ever had gave me such pause. No, there has to be more to this secret then fresh beans and I applaud them for not exposing the secret. What I can reveal is that I can't wait to go back to Bordentown (hello Cranberry Festival in the fall) and while I am there I will get a coffee from Beanwood and stroll the streets and greet the locals. And while this image is a bit too Redbook for comfort I will be there with a smile on my face, a hair on my chin and a coffee in my hand.

text: I have been eating at the Taj Cafe on downtown State for several years. Over time food at the Taj has changed in quality much like at any restaurant. When I first started eating at the lunch buffet here in 2004 I was impressed with the solid variety and sauce and meat quality but saw some downturn after a couple years. More recently, however, since early 2008 I have been most impressed with the quality of almost every item in the buffet. The highlight has been the vegetable korma which uses large chunks of vegetables and potato. The sauce of the korma is really well spiced and balanced with level of cream. In combination with some of their excellent garlic naan and basmati rice it is crave-worthy and has been the focus of many lazy Saturday brunches. Their curries have similarly improved using large tender chunks of white chicken meat which I look forward to each time. The buffet has an excellent variety with a thorough salad bar and many excellent desert options. The rice pudding is subtly spiced and goes perfectly with their irresistable carat desert (Gajar ka Halwa). Other options include sliced melon and those brown colored dumplings of dried milk and flour soaked in sugar syrup (Gulaab Jamun). Forget ordering items from the menu as the buffet has plenty variety at a reasonable price. Bring a big appetite and friends you want to impress.

text: The Ambassador is a pretty hotel made up of three old warehouses. ("Old" will be a common theme in my comments here. The rooms are old, but nice, with dark hardwood floors; there's definitely some buckling under the floors which squeek loudly as you walk over . . . and since the doors aren't exactly thick (maybe the walls and floors/ceilings too), you can clearly hear at least your immediate few neighbors wandering their rooms also. The same atmosphere is found in the lobby (the old-style feel). And the staff is excellent -- warm and friendly at all levels. I had two major issues. First, the Ambassador's vision of a "continental breakfast" is laughably skimpy -- bread (croissants, plain danishes), coffee, and water -- and is only open for 90 minutes, from 7:30-9:00am. And second, the surprise MANDATORY $15/person "resort fee" (covering use of the tiny gym and business center, eating the previously mentioned skimpy breakfast, and free local and long-distance calling [despite the fact that most people use cell phones these days]) is extremely irritating. The Ambassador's alright, but, barring some amazing deal, I'll look elsewhere the next time I visit New Orleans.

text: 2.5 stars. I WANT MY 1/2 STARS. Damn Yelp. So I decided to drop in for dinner after my Tunes runs this afternoon/evening. The parking lot was pretty full, which almost led me to leave, but I decided to go in anyways. The interior is a little dark, but not overly annoying. I sat down in front of a wall full of Frida Kahlo paintings. Eatingi in front of a woman with huge eyebrows and a monkey staring at you is a little bizarre. They were playing some Latin music that wasn't half bad. The cooks/bus boys were even singing in the back as I made a trip to the restroom. I was seated, offered a drink and chips and salsa within 2 minutes. All very good. They gave me a big bowl o' chips that were of decent size and weren't greasy. I had two different kinds of salsa, one that was more of a red salsa and I believe a pico de gallo type. The red salsa was not good. It was way too sweet, watery, and the flavors were muddled. On to the pico de gallo type salsa. That was better, though I was craving a little more spiciness than was in there. Still all the vegetables were fresh and tangy. Allright main course time. I ordered a combo platter with tacos and an enchilada suiza. The dish came with a guacamole salad, rice and beans. I had the guac salad come out first. The vegetables in the guac salad were very fresh and presented well. The guac was decent, but could have used a bit more spice, maybe some garlic and/or onion. The only thing that really bothered me about this salad was the garnishing with tortilla strips. They got in the way more than anything else. Small annoyance though. The tacos and enchilada came out next. The tacos were pretty decent, though the chorizo wasn't quite as spicy as I"m used to. The chicken enchilada suiza was served with a green sauce on it The chicken was fairly moist and tasted allright. The tomatillo wasn't bad at all but there wasn't much zip to it. Likewise the refried beans were a little bland, so I added a little habanero sauce to it(you only need 3-4 small drops. Otherwise you're going to be spending a lot of time on the throne). The rice was cooked just right, nice and fluffy and moist, unlike a lot of places. My waitress was pretty attentive in spite of the crush of people eating there. All of the staff was polite and made sure that I was taken care of. So their service was pretty good. However, I wasn't real thrilled with the price of my meal for what I got. I was told by someone knowledgeable in all things NJ that prices are higher at places with liquor licenses, since they are so expensive. So I get the fiscal reason. But I've definitely had better Mexican or Tex Mex for less. If the cooks had executed better I would have enjoyed my meal more.

text: I recently moved back to Santa Barbara and felt the need to revisit all my favorite places to grub at during college. Thai food was introduced to me here, and I've been in love ever since. Panang curry was what did it for me, and that's what I ordered here... It was just okay. Not bad, but not great. I like my curries with a lot of flavor and a sauce-like texture. The Roasted Duck Curry was not good at all. It was so oily that there was a thin layer that separated itself on top of the curry and so watery that I had to eat it out of a bowl like soup. There was very little flavor and the duck was rubbery... blah! And it was expensive at $12.95 (compared to 9.95 for all the other curries). Same thing with the Pad Thai (10.95) - too expensive for the quality, it lacked flavor and the chicken and shrimp were dry and rubbery. I liked the combination of Mixed Vegetables (9.95) though, which had a good garlic and sweet basil flavor. Again, it was very watery and I thought it was too expensive for it being a non-meat dish. Definitely not representative of all the "Best of" awards they've been winning, but from what I've been reading, it's because the choices here are limited. Overall, this place compares in taste and quality to bargain casual food (lunch specials are reasonable at 7.99-8.99), but maybe I'm spoiled from living in the Bay Area? I think I've come a long way since being a regular at Appethai (which I hear is out of business now since the food was so bad, haha!). If you're ever in SF, I recommend Little Thai for really good food at comparable prices. As for me, my hunt for a better Thai "Choice" continues...

text: I used to drink the kool-aid too. Ikea used to be God's gift to man. The other day I found myself unplugged from the Matrix. I went there with my roommate to pick up a few items. A shelf she wanted was "located" in a bin that didn't exist. After waiting in a long line, they finally provided her with a slip that would allow for her to pay for it up front and then pick it up at the place near the exit. Well, we had to wait in a line where there was a real register operator because of her purchase order. There was only one line. The person in front of us also had a purchase order, but the machine that processes it was broken. We waited about 15 minutes just to get up to being checked out. Then, as you could imagine, my roommate encountered a similar problem -- add another 10 minutes onto my time in line. (While all of this was going on, a second line was finally opened. But, they took everyone from the BACK of our line and they could only pay with credit cards -- no cash. Good job Ikea.) Now it came my turn. I had a very large shelf for myself in my cart and when I went to present it to the cashier, it was discovered that there was no bar code. I worked in retail for over five years, and whenever that happened at one of my jobs, it was my responsibility to get on the phone and have another employee come and get a new one for the customer or just look it up. Instead, the cashier informed me that I should go get another one myself! It gets worse.... Then, she reminded me that I had to GET BACK IN LINE. That's right, the same line that I just wasted over 25 minutes of my life in. I asked to speak to a manager at this point. Instead of calling one over, she pointed to a desk where I could find one myself. Guess what? That desk had another huge line at it. So, I nixed the manager and decided to just get the heck out of this hell hole. I retrieved a shelf with a bar code and dutifully waited in line again. FINALLY, I was able to check out and I joined my roommate in the waiting area. She was STILL waiting for her number to be called even though there was only ONE other customer that was being waited on. At this point, I went up to a desk and got very firm with them, insisting upon speaking to a manager. Can you imagine, they actually LAUGHED AT ME when I explained the problem?!?!?! I finally managed to get a manager and he very slowly corrected the problem and got my roommate her shelf. I understand that Ikea is low priced and low priced for a reason. But, come on people. This is a little too much. I'd rather pay 10 more dollars at target in order to avoid another headache like this. It took us over 45 minutes to exit Ikea after we began our stay in line. That is NEVER acceptable for a retail outlet. Stop drinking the kool-aid people!

text: Sorrento's is one of those traditional italian places, of which there seem to be a bunch in the area(Scoogi's, Roberto's, etc.). This one has been here for decades, and it sits by itself right off of Ridge Avenue. The place itself looks very unassuming. The outside and inside look worn, a symbol of what should have been a tried and true restaurant. The decor is minimalist, which is not necessarily a bad thing, but could use an update. I don't really mind bad decor, as atmosphere is a distant third to food and service. The service was good. Friendly, quick, but not trying to rush you. It can be pleasant to not have servers hovering over your table every couple minutes, and it is great that the restaurant is a BYO, so the final total is kept down. These two reasons are why I did not give this place one star. The food, on the other hand, was awful. Not awful in a 'i want to vomit' awful, just bad in that NOTHING is really homemade. Let's go course by course: Bread & Garlic Bread: The bread is your typical quick-bake store bought bread. It comes out warm, but the texture is very bland, and not that good compared to true italian bread. The garlic bread is made from the same bread, but it tastes like they use margarine instead of butter, and the seasonings are all dried - no fresh garlic at all. Salad: There is nothing bad to say about the flavor of this salad, because you can't criticize something that doesn't exist. The salad was iceberg lettuce, three pale grape tomatoes, some sliced white onion, and a single olive. With a salad, you need some flavor. Since most don't come through with that, it needs vibrant color to entice the eyes. With iceberg lettuce and extremely light tomatoes, it did not look appetizing at all, and the flavorless taste to it made it one of the least memorable salads I have ever eaten Main: After finding that the shells and manicotti are frozen and pastas are dry from a box, I opted for the veal milanese. It came out a touch overcooked, which is expected every now and then, so I won't complain. What I will complain about is that it didn't look to be made in-house, but rather came in frozen pre-breaded. The sauce was terrible. It was loaded with cheap parmesan cheese, which is a cheap way to add flavor when your sauce comes from a can or cheap/few herbs are added to your own. All in all a very meh dish. Dessert: We were told ahead of time that they didn't make their Tiramisu, but that it was 'extremely delicious'. What came out was a travesty. Before our server got it to our table, I could see the shortening in the supposedly-whipped-mascarpone topping. One bite confirmed it - the topping tasted like eating sweet crisco, and the cakes tasted like your average PathMark sheetcake, with almost no coffee flavor whatsoever. If I wasn't eating with friends who would get embarassed, I would have sent it back. Summary: None of the pastas or sauces are made from scratch in-house, which really disappoints me. I go to Italian restaurants for the home-cooking that I can't get at home without lots of labor. Anyone can boil a box of pasta and open a jar of Prego, so why do restaurants do that, and worse yet, why do we let them get away with it?
