text: We have always loved Great Basin over in Sparks and have visited for years, but I have to say, I love this new location much better. It's got a great vibe, busy and bustling and fun. The beer is, of course, fantastic, and the menu, which seems nicely expanded from the Sparks location, is just wonderful. I would love to give this place five stars, but I have been to this location several times and I have to say I agree with some of the complaints about customer service. It's not always on. So minus one single star for that. When the service is good, it's very very good, but when it's bad, well, it's meh. We always sit at the bar if we can, or in the bar area, because the bartenders are ALWAYS awesome and attentive; the same cannot be said of the waitresses. We don't ever get a table because it's a very busy place and generally, once one is seated, one tends to be forgotten. So that's why we sit in / near the bar. Who cares about a waitress forgetting you when the bar is right there? It's easy to just lean over and order another one. And you will want to order another one. That's why you're there, anyway, isn't it? To drink pint after pint of GBBCs life-changing beer. Since I'm years behind in reviewing GBBC let me just give you a quick rundown of the things I enjoy. First, the beer. Any of the beer. All of the beer. It's all great. Our most favorite of what is a truly awe inspiring selection has to be The Chili Beso, The Lemon Wheat, The Jackpot Porter, The Old Fitz Stout, the Wheeler Peak Wheat, the Ichthyosaur Pale Ale, the Wild Horse Ale and, oh, heck, whatever else they are pouring that day. But our two absolute most drop dead favorites are the Rosemary Rye Patch and the Harvest Ale. It was because of the Harvest Ale we were last at GB, as you can see from the photos I uploaded. We were there to help shell pinenuts for the Harvest Ale - for every glass you filled with shelled nuts, you got a free beer. Now, if you've ever shelled a pine nut, you know how difficult it is. But let me tell you, it was worth every bit of that hour's worth of work to get a free beer. And we have been back to taste the resultant batch, and ahhh! Heaven! It tickles me a lovely amber hue to know we "helped make" that great beer, even if it was only in a teeny tiny fashion. On to the food. Just try anything. It's all great. text: This architectural landmark in Tucson has quite a twisted history...the fourth replacement for the original church of St. Augustín de Tucson (founded in 1776), construction began on the new cathedral in 1897 under the supervision of two French-born bishops (Salpointe and Bourgade), who envisioned a Gothic structure with two pointed spires (which were never completed due to lack of funds). For thirty years, the church stood unfinished, with bare-brick walls, until American-born Bishop Gercke decided to finish it in the Mexican baroque style. Inspired by the Mexican Catherdal of Querétaro, the sandstone façade and mission-style towers were completed in 1928. Structural deterioration prompted a restoration in 1966 under Bishop Green, who demolished everything except for the facade and the twin towers. The new building (completed in 1968) sadly is a product of its age...industrial acoustical tile, kitchy folk tapestries adorn the clerestory, a giant floating Jesus looms over the altar, red kitchen tile lines the floors and ceiling mounted florescent lamps cast a dull pallor over the interior. text: Edmonton's downtown pyramid on Churchill Square is City Hall. It houses our local government offices, on the second floor they hold council meetings at least once weekly - check the website for specifics. It's a beautiful building inside and out. The decor changes often as new events or festivals take place in the city. The main foyer is often used for award ceremonies, local events and festival activities. There are lots of historical photos - of previous mayors and old local government buildings. There's more to this place than the counter where you go to pay your city parking tickets! In the front, facing the square, is a large fountain in the summer which is converted into a skating rink in the winter. You can hear the bells of the clock chime in a sort of creepily beautiful way bouncing off the tall buildings of the city's core. The underground parking at City Hall is meters, so bring your change. I'll give you some inside advice that I picked up working downtown in the past - after 6pm, the cost is only $0.50/hr, from 6am-6pm during the week, the rate is $1.50/hr. Weekends are also $0.50/hr. They may have changed things but the meters used to be free on Sundays and Holidays. Still, it's connected via the LRT pedway to the Winspear Centre, Edmonton City Centre shopping, The Stanley Milner Library, The Citadel, The Westin, and many other locations. Check out the pedway maps. It's great in the winter to park in one spot and not have to go outside! It's also a LOT cheaper than any other underground parking in the area.

text: Probably the best coffee in Tampa, and in my mind, one of the best coffees I've had anywhere. Of course I happen to love tradition, and their coffee satisfies my desire for great tasting Cuban coffee. Naviera coffee is located in the historical Ybor City district, which is the old Latin quarter of Tampa, where Spanish, Cuban, and Italian immigrants worked in the cigar factories, and congregated in restaurants and social clubs. To give you some perspective, Ybor city itself architecturally resembles somewhat the French quarter in New Orleans. While a little sleepy during midweek, it's a neat place to spend a couple of hours in the afternoon for lunch and coffee, followed by a stroll down 7th Ave. Naviera Coffee doesn't look like much from the outside, but their coffee packs a punch. They roast coffee in the back, and serve traditional delights in the front. My favorite is the Ybor special: Cuban Espresso, with a touch of condensed milk. Soooooo good !!! While the seating area and sit down atmosphere is lacking, the coffee is so worth the visit to Ybor. Even our former President Teddy Roosevelt paid Ybor a visit before embarking on his journey with U.S. troops to fight and free Cuba during the Spanish American War (early 1900s). His troops even invented the "Cuba Libre" drink during that time, when they combined coca cola and rum for the first time in Ybor. http://www.elmolinocoffee.com/

text: After all of the glowing reviews here on Yelp, I thought Lacroix would be the perfect place to enjoy some Philadelphia French gastronomy. And while my dining experience had a few hits, unfortunately, the misses will stand out most prominently. First, the hits. The service is great. The waitstaff perfectly balance the high-brow service you expect in a place like this with a smiling, down-to-earth helpfulness that makes you feel welcome. The service is graceful and efficient and encourages you to savor each bite. I began with a dinner salad with a "chocolate" dressing. Which, although it sounded gimmicky, was very good. The only trace of chocolate taste was kind of a darker flavor that complemented the bitterness of the frisee salad beautifully. For an entree, I had the Muscovy Duck Breast which was spectacular. The skin was beautifully browned and crisp, the inside was juicy and flavorful, and the parsnip coconut sauce was creative combination of old and new world flavors that was smooth and rich. Unfortunately, though, there were misses. And they were big ones. My companion had the butter lettuce salad to start, which offered an Asian twist on the traditional butter lettuce salad. And the flavors just didn't work. The chef put sesame oil in the dressing to Asian-it-up a bit, and the pungent flavor of the sesame oil melded with the stinky flavor of the gorgonzola cheese and resulted in completely palate-offending combination. My companion also ordered a side dish of enoki mushrooms with chili sauce which was not only palate-offending, but pretty much inedible. The enokis were soggy and wet (after all they're enoki mushrooms--that's why the Japanese use them in soup) and no amount of thai chili flavor could redeem their sorry state of affairs. And finally our dessert, 5 phases of pumpkin, was disappointing. In the chef's quest for uniqueness and creativity, he forgot that pumpkin is comfort food. And unforch, there was nothing comforting about the 5 measly pieces of odd-flavored pumpkin-oriented minutiae that dotted the dessert plate. Ultimately, the food here tells me that the chef here is very impressed with himself. I also think that if he read this review, he would disdainfully proclaim that "she knows no-ting about zee French cuisine". However, I am too classy to name drop my French gastronomy street cred here. So suffice it to say "zat was zee last time zat I will dine at Lacroix."
label: NEG

text: Cheekwood Botanical Garden is located in the suburbs of Nashville. It's a bit hard to locate without a GPS. We visited during the fall of 09 and were treated to a monster exhibit. Local organizations, including schools, scouts and more created monsters of all sorts, and donated them to the garden. Garden staff placed the creatures along walkways and open spaces, and even a few tucked away in the groves. Quite fun to walk around and enjoy not only a well kept garden but these creations. The garden staff, though sparse, were friendly and helpful. Staff point out where to start your walk through the park. Signs augment there directions and help in navigating the sprawl. Grounds here are well kept. Greenery abounds with paths leading to small groves and installations. Sculpture, statues, stone paths can be found all over. There are even openings hidden behind trees with a cabin, an iron gate, and a zen garden. All said, the place is a bit on the pricey side. They do however generally accept memberships from other gardens. Definitely should be on your Nashville to see list.

text: If you ask people what restaurants are "can't miss" in NOLA, there are definitely a few places you will hear time and time again. Commander's Palace is one of NOLA's dining institutions and it's an experience you won't soon forget. If you happen to be in NOLA on a Sunday, make your reservations for brunch. The price of your entree includes an appetizer and dessert and if you choose Chef Tory's Jazz Brunch, a bloody mary is included. The Commander's bloody mary is a bit on the spicy side (which you can make spicier with the rim of cajun spice) and is finished tableside by your waiter with his extra pour of vodka that is frozen into an ice block to keep it chilled. I did order the Jazz Brunch but I substituted the Shrimp and Tasso Henican. The appetizer is just the right portion - 4 shrimp stuffed with tasso with a spicy sauce that is cooled down by the pepper jelly that surrounds your plate. The "jelly" is more like a thick sauce and it compliments the spiciness from the shrimp sauce. The okra that is on the plate is cooked perfectly - it is not gummy (which only happens if you overcook it.) For my main course, I had the Eggs Couchon De Lait. The description from the menu: "Smoky braised pork debris over black pepper and rosemary biscuits with soft poached eggs, winter mushrooms & bourbon-bacon fat hollandaise." A lot going on here but it was a wonder to eat. If you think it sounds like an upscale eggs benedict, you would be right. But the differences in the ingredients made the dish really special. The pork was tender and had a smoky flavor - there was a bit of the braising liquid in the dish that soaked into the rosemary biscuit, which was sweet and buttery and had an amazing texture even after soaking in the braising liquid. Add the perfectly poached eggs into the mix along with the hollandaise and you have a very rich, multi-layered entree. The sauces mixed together into what I called a "sauce of love" which I used french bread to savor more of it. Dessert was equally impressive - the Creole Bread Pudding Souffle is a great twist on bread pudding - the top of it is a souffle which is pierced by your server when it arrives in order to spoon in the whiskey cream sauce. The souffle mixed into the pudding lightens up the dessert. I won't speak for my friend who was with me, but she ordered the Duck Confit and Strawberry Salad, some sort of crab dish and the Bourbon Pecan Pie. She was very happy with her meal and I did try the pie, which was amazing - you can tell that real cane syrup is used for the pie, it really gives such an amazing depth of flavor. Of course, service was impeccable and we even had the host come over and speak with us during our meal. They really made me feel at home and I felt that they appreciated my business. Also, they had a three piece band playing music - another great touch to a stellar experience.

The olives are good too, but the pickles! -If you're the kind of person who never has enough tahini in your life, you can get an extra cup of it at the salad bar. -Add some fries if you're eating in; if you're picking up or getting delivery, skip 'em. If you happen to like your fries cold and extra soggy, strike that and reverse it. -Bring cash. Your ATM card will also suffice. -Don't even think about eating here on the Sabbath (even Friday afternoon is a roll of the dice) or on Jewish holidays. -If you want someone to bring your falafel to you, you'll want to call during an off-peak time. They don't have time for that stuff during the lunch rush. This last one is important. -Order hot sauce to liven things up, but unless you love the sensation of five-alarm fire in your mouth, ask them to take it easy. Otherwise, you're liable to end up with a few hot sauce-soaked bites at the end of your pita, and they will burn your face right off. I've warned you, now.

text: Le Pavillon has its charm, but then again, charm can only take you so far. The reviews on Trip Advisor that talk about the place being old and dingy are not entirely off the mark. Conversely, if you aren't looking for the clinically minimalist design of the W, but rather some old school charm, you probably won't be disappointed. Upon arrival, we were greeted with a million facets of light radiating off the crystal chandeliers, juxtaposed with the smell of grandmas. Talk about a statement. The place oozes old-school Southern opulence, but also has tinges of just plain old. Not going to lie, the paintings on the walls and the creaky sounds all make this a great place for ghost hunters - it all feels like the inspiration for the Disney Haunted Mansion. Not to mention that our running toilet seems to flush sporadically in the night - I think a ghost is haunting our bathroom, if you ask me. Our room was oddly upgraded to a 2 queen room (what did my husband and I need an extra bed for?) which apparently had extra space. Fine. Come to find out that the hotel pool is being painted (which no one told us) so we think that the upgrade was meant to cover that up. They offered us the pool at the Homewood Suites next door, but that was a severe downgrade given that it was A) indoors and B) across the street. PB and J bar is kitschy - I actually hate PBJ, so not my thing, but a cute touch. The hot chocolate was all over the table and table cloth when I got down to the bar, and the mess (coupled with the heat) turned me off. Room service was actually tasty, despite the price, but then again, when is room service not expensive. Gumbo was flavorful, and the oysters in my po-boy were crispy and delicious. If you are stuck in the hotel, you could do a lot worse for a comforting meal. If you are a stickler for cleanliness, you may want to skip this place. There was still small trash on the floor of our room, and hair on the bathroom tiles. The entire room looks like a holdover from the early 90s pretending to be the early 1820's. Maybe that was the last time the place was properly cleaned. All in all, I can't say that we are having a horrible time here, but we certainly won't come back. I was at the Intercontinental last time, and despite the much higher price tag for the room, it was a huge value over this place.

text: I have a booked called Hamburger America in my bathroom. It's a nice read, and it was also my inspiration for a spontaneous trip down to Delaware this weekend. We seated ourselves, and our server came over quickly. Everything she said was a statement, like "You want more time" and "You want mayo" instead of asking. The atmosphere here is pretty traditional 50s diner, and although we were eating a little early (around 5pm) it was oddly almost exclusively populated by senior citizens. For food, this place is supposed to have excellent ice cream as well as burgers. We were all too full from dinner to try dessert. The prices here are great. We each had a 8 oz cheeseburger, fries, and a drink and it was under $10 each. The french fries were pathetically soggy. Our orders were all mixed up. When finally sorted out, I had a medium rare burger topped with lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, and onions. The fixings were good, but the bread was soggy and thin. My burger was cooked well, but I can't say the same for everyone at the table. Its great to bit into a burger and have to dripping juice. The meat wasn't anything special. Bottom Line: George Mots, you mislead me on this one. The poor service coupled with an average burger produces less than desired results. I wouldn't go to this place if it was in Philadelphia, and I'm certainly not making a trip out of the state to go here again.

text: "Talk about a bad day..." Wow. I can honestly say, that my experience at Big River was the stuff in movies and sitcoms. Never in my life have I seen so much go so wrong so quickly. Arrived at the restaurant and went to the bar with my mother to get some Sweet Tea, and wait for the 3 others in our group. Every one of our party arrives and we put in for a table. It was Sunday Night about 8:45PM and Labor Day Weekend. Mom and I had ordered Crab cakes and those arrived around the same time as the rest of the party. Excellent. Good flavor, good texture, not oily. I'd give them a solid 4+ There was absolutely NO INDICATION of what was to come. The Buzzer telling us our table was ready went off and we were seated in the back of the restaurant. 20 minutes later, still no waitress. We waved down someone busing a table near us and asked, "Do we have a waitress? We've been here for 20 minutes and no one has come by." The buser let us know, "Of course you have a waitress. She'll be right out." Um, okay. Five more minutes go by. The Hostess who sat us come back and take our drinks order and appetizer order on a coaster... lets us know our waitress should be out in a few minutes. *Also let's us know by the way, in the strangest comment ever...that she doesn't like people.* Five more minutes go by, and we've been sitting here for a half an hour. Our waitress - the girl busing the table we spoke with earlier brings out some of the drinks we ordered and lets us know that they are out of the egg rolls we ordered... as a matter of fact, they shut the doors to the restaurant at 9 PM because they are out of most things. Really? You are out of 50% of the menu at 9 PM on Sunday of Labor Day weekend. No Sweat. We are there for the company anyway. We will shake it off, and take a deep breath, and start over. We order another appetizer they aren't out of and settle in. Everyone takes a sip of their drinks. Oh no. No lime in the Gin and Tonic, the Stoli Martini, isn't Stoli. And, is there any gin in the G&T at all? It actually doesn't taste like there is. Waitress comes back a few minutes later. We ask for lime, and aks what the Martini is - because it isn't Stoli. 5 Minutes later she brings us some lime. Tells us the martini is Grey Goose. Hmmm. Grey goose is a LOT more expensive than Stoli, and it really doesn't taste right. She goes away. On her next round back we finally tell her its bad. We send it back and get a beer. Waitress comes back to take our order and this time brings a list of all the things they have run out of. We finally order a Cobb Salad, Shrimp and Grits, and a Burger. For 5 people. We also order more drinks, and this time we order name brand Gin, because those first G&T's taste an awful lot like just tonic. And we try one more time for that Stoli Martini. Drinks come and they are fine. But we are told when the G&T's are delivered they the bar is out of Limes - and incidentally they've run out of almost all the wine as well. Manager comes out and tells us that they are sorry (not for our service problems or difficulties earlier) but because - they didn't realize that we hadn't gotten food yet and the grits are gone. Do I want something else from the limited selections? Not, really. But I get carrot cake, because the manager says its made in house and big enough for us all to share. Food comes. Cobb Salad, Burger, and Shrimp on Rice...wait. But the manager came out 10 minutes ago and we canceled that dish and ordered the carrot cake. There is no Avocado on the Cobb, the bun for the burger is hard... and I don't mean a little hard, I mean HARD. "Maybe it's the last bun" we giggle, after all, they are out of everything. Why oh why is there shrimp? We taste the food. Yikes. That is bad. Really, bad. 7 minutes later the manager walks out the the carrot cake. We look at him like what happened? We are just beaten by this time. And It's funny, in a way, but only when your telling someone about it, not when its actually happening to you - and especially when the $116.00 bill comes at the end of this nightmare. Maybe it was just the worst night ever for the restaurant and we were unsuspecting diners... but my goodness, what a horrible night. I will Not be back and you may not waste your night there in case it wasn't a fluke after all.

text: BJ's kind of blows... Or sucks depending on your perspective/preference. I haven't been to a BJ's in years, and I probably should have kept it that way. When the first one opened up on Oracle, I recall a conversation with a friend about why anyone would name a restaurant BJ's. For those of you with virginal minds, BJ is in fact acronym for a sexual act of an oral variety. Hence my aforementioned preposition that BJ's sucks. Why would I apply such an unseemly metaphor in my assertion? Because it does. I went this past Saturday to celebrate a friend's birthday. It happened to coincide with the Wildcat's big football game against Iowa, so the cavernous and sparkling brand-new building was packed. Indeed, everything in the place was gleaming, (including my food). I think the place is a little bit over a month old. Oh, they have a freaking revolving door. Who in the hell puts a revolving door in front of a restaurant? I should have revolved my ass right on out the second I walked into that door. Alas, I could never leave my friend hanging on her birthday. *sigh* Our server was nice and friendly enough, but the service overall was somewhat tepid in the efficiency department. Granted, however, our party numbered ten and the place was pretty crazy with the game and all. But the check-in periods from our server at our table seemed entirely too long. Here's an idea of how it went: five or more minutes from ordering my beer to it arriving at my table, 10-15 minutes from having our appetizer brought out to having our server take our entree order, 15+ minutes from two in my party to have to order another drink. Now onto my food. I ordered the Miso Salmon. Yeah I know, why order fish from a chain restaurant? And in the middle of the desert of all places? For some reason, the description of it in the menu struck my fancy. Anyway, how do express in words how I thought of this dish? Well, let's begin with its appearance. In my 30+ reviews on Yelp, I cannot recall if I've ever written in any length about how a dish looked like. I feel absolutely compelled to so at this time. It's hard to describe, but the best I can do is just to say that the Miso Salmon looked oddly fake. The color and sheen of it threw me off the second the plate hit the table. It kind of resembled those plastic display-model dishes of food you see at Japanese restaurants, like at Yoshimatsu. All of the dishes at BJ's, judging by my friends' orders, were arranged in almost perfect beauty. My dish looked pretty as well, with the vegetables strewn around the salmon in perfect harmony, which itself was on top of a bed of rice. While visually appealing in artistic terms, it just didn't look real. Put another way, it looked quite artificial. Perhaps the cook's training at BJ's is focused on the visual arts rather than the culinary arts. Perhaps the beauty is an illusion cast upon diners to mask its substance. Speaking of which, the Miso Salmon was certainly edible, but enjoyable it was not. I might have liked the dish if it weren't for the fact that the fish might have been a day past its optimal freshness. Indeed, I think some my pickup lines were fresher than my fish at BJ's. And if you're a single woman residing in the Tucson-area, you know that's not a good thing. The miso sauce that the salmon was prepared in was not too bad, which is a shame that fish forced me to assign one rather than perhaps two stars. The beer wasn't bad, but it wasn't orgasmically memorable either. Remember that Brewhouse is part of this place's name. To end this review, allow me to elaborate on the price: it's as high or higher than Paris Hilton on cocaine. If one were to order what I did that night, three pints of brew, one piece of appetizer, and entree of Miso Salmon, one would be set back in excess of $40. Throw in tip for the two-hour long service, and one can expect to drop a cool Ulysses S. Grant. If it weren't for the fact that I was celebrating a friend's birthday that night, methinks that it would have been better spent if I someone at BJ's repeatedly punched me in the stomach till I puked and then took my wallet, as empty as it normally is. Okay, so I never vomited from eating there, and I was able to keep my wallet (minus the cash), so that's probably hitting below the belt of BJ's. Did I ever mention what BJ stands for?

text: Salt-Lick! I think I satisfied my sodium intake for the year after dining here recently. The rest of the menu isn't any better, or terribly exciting nor different than what the other local Mexican jaunts offer. What does make Jose Pistolas stand out from the crowd is that the place doesn't pride itself on margaritas or cocktails of the genre - but focuses on a good beer selection. That's always a smart move in this city of beer snobs and enthusiasts. But a decent beer list alone does not a great restaurant or bar make. In different iterations of restaurants past, I always found this little piece of real estate a challenge. The restaurant and bar area is always split in two. Very little bar space on the first floor, tiny bathrooms are far away located in the back past the emergency exit doors, a couple floors up. Also, though I hate places that try too hard to establish an atmosphere, I find Jose to completely lack one. Perhaps that is their intention, especially when you're located across that heinous Italian food chain (the name escapes) and just down the street from Applebees. Food isn't bad, but it definitely isn't good either. Offerings aren't any better than what you could make yourself or find at your local grocer. Big blah. What brings this restaurant's wattage down is their excessive use of salt, each time I've eaten here, I leave feeling like I've swam through the Dead Sea with my mouth gaping open. Also, the place is kind of expensive. After splitting chips+guac+salsa, getting a order of shrimp tacos + 3 happy hour beers (don't judge) with tip = $40? A little rich for my blood. When all is said and done, Jose is good for a quick stop for a beverage before a show on Broad Street when Good Dog is too packed. It's sort of a decent back-up option to watch a game when all the other places nearby are filled to capacity.

text: On August 12, 2010 my husband and I had one of the most phenomenal dining experiences of our lives at Capital Grill Indianapolis. We were immediately greeted by Jason who had a happy smile on his face and a genuine expression in his voice. (Even though it was 8 pm and he had been working many long hours already.) Jason did a fabulous job of explaining the menu to us and answering all of our questions. He did not pressure us to order every course, nor did he suggest the most expensive item on the menu as "his favorite." I have to admit, I was almost embarrassed it was our first time and that we were there for a celebration. (We were not your "typical" Capital Grille guests ordering bottles of wine and lots of lobster and fillet.) Despite this factor, Jason still treated us as his most important guests of the evening. He was very honest about portion sizes and quantities, often mentioning that things were big enough for sharing. Jason was extremely attentive to our dining needs and worked perfectly with his companion Alberto. Our water glasses were always filled and you better believe they never let a crumb sit on the table for less than 3 minutes. While Jason and Alberto were extremely attentive, they still allowed us to enjoy each-other''s company &we definitely enjoyed a private dining experience. They never interrupted us and waited until after each conversation to ask us about our food or potential needs. Jason did not blink two eye lashes when I ordered inexpensive glasses of wine and he only treated my husband and I with the up-most respect. (Even though we are a younger couple.) The chocolate hazelnut cake per Jason's & Alberto's suggestion was amazing and it was even more special with the Happy Birthday message. The Capital Grille experience is still fresh in our minds, even 5 days later. This is all because of Jason, his phenomenal service and the delicious food of course! I was more than impressed and I look forward to going to The Capital Grille in the near future. I will also be entertaining guests there, now that I know about the amazing food and service. Two words: Thank you.

text: A love letter for you is an urban romantic poem in every sense of the word. It's a series of 50 spray-painted murals, (they are more like signs, really), located on the upper walls of buildings, businesses and homes from 45th to 63rd streets along the Market Street corridor and the EL in West Philly. The artist, Stephen Powers, a native Philadelphian graffiti artist decided to create this temporary masterpiece which is not only a love letter from a guy to a girl but a love letter to his native city. His words are poignant, clever and fitting. They stay with you. "Co-sign on Our Lifetime" - "We Share Receipts. We Share Sheets. We Share Defeats" amongst many others already written about here. Unlike the other murals through the Mural Arts Program, these works were not painted to remain on these walls permanently and they will not be repainted or maintained. So go now, take the Market-Frankford Line westward and see them for yourself, or take a Mural Arts tour to get more in depth discussion and story about each piece.

I usually get a double order of this one as a standard, and play around with whatever else may be featured on that visit. All in all, a great place to go with a group of friends, or a date, if you're ok with picking off of each other's plates. Everyone I've brought here has enjoyed it. text: A bar is a bar, and a cheap bar is better. For me, McGillin's is no exception to the rule when it comes to settling for a divey joint for a cheap beer. They often have a lot of really great specials on good stuff, like Walt Wit or Ithaca, two of my favorites, not on junk like $2 Bud Lights - stuff I wouldn't drink if they paid me the $2. They even have a microbrew sampler for $8.50 or something in which you get to try 6 decent sized glasses of stuff you may not have had before. But I digress. The true reason I'm writing this review and have only given it 2 stars is because of service service service. As I mentioned at first, McGillin's is more of a laid back, divey sort of place, so I'm not naive enough to assume that it would the pinnacle of white glove service, but even in the grimiest of bars, I've never gotten service bad enough to keep me from returning. Submitted for your approval are two scenarios that occured on two separate days. 1) I was to meet up with a group of friends at McGillin's one night. As is typical, the place was pretty slammed, which is good for them. I stood at the bar and waited for my turn to order a drink and in the meantime, I texted one of my friends to see where they were. As I had my phone out, a red haired girl bartender approached me and said something to the effect of 'you shouldn't be standing at the bar with your phone out' (I'm paraphrasing because this happened last year) and I said 'excuse me?' and she replied 'you should be ready to order when a bartender comes over to you'. Now, I'm a grown-ass man. I don't appreciate anyone talking to me that way, but I also don't expect it either, so I really didn't know what to say. I put my phone on the bar and ordered my drink (I was ready to order) and she picked my phone up and put a napkin under it, saying 'the bar is all wet'. Don't touch my phone, ma'am, I wanted to say. But I didn't. She came back with my beer and I said 'how much?' and she said 'you don't even have your money out? Can't you see how busy it is in here?'. Again. Don't talk to me like I'm 12. I'm all for playing around with customers and feigning attitude, but this girl was dead serious. She took my twenty, I handed her a $2 tip and said 'a little less attitude next time'. Taking into consideration the sheer volume of the crowd, I knew that if I stiffed her a tip, it wouldn't put a dent in her income and I would just be looked at as 'that douche bag with the phone who didn't tip', so I gave her a good tip just to sort of show I was the bigger man. Needless to say, I avoided her for the rest of the night. 2) Ever since that first night, I vowed to never return to McGillin's. However, a lot of my friends really like that place. If it were a normal night, I'd gratefully decline an invite to go there, but if a friend wants to go there for their birthday, etc., who am I to say where they should go? This past July, a friend of mine wanted to go there, so I went knowing which bartender to avoid. We sat upstairs on a less busy weeknight and I asked a guy bartender for a pint of Ithaca. His reply was 'we're all out' and then he walked away. If a bar runs out of something, I'm not looking for a freebie or even an apology. I am, however, looking to order a different drink, so I was stunned that he didn't ask me if there was something else I might want instead. I stood there for a minute or so and then decided to go to the downstairs bar to order something. This is the only bar I've ever gone to that I have to navigate to different areas of the establishment to avoid bartenders or to just get what I want. This was also open-mic night and our table was situated near the stage. The Emcee spoke to us more than a handful of times about where we were sitting and that we were in the way. This would have been a 'my bad' kind of situation if we had moved the table there ourselves, but it was how the place was laid out. If he thought that table was too close, he should have had it moved at the beginning of the night, not leaving him to bother us as we're trying to have a good time. So, in conclusion: Yes, this place does have cheep beer and ample seating. Karaoke night is also actually pretty fun if you're into that kind of thing. But unacceptable service and attitude from employees will keep me from coming here on my own accord.
label: NEG

text: I have mixed feelings about Sangkee. Their service and food is top notch. I love their small platters, most particularly their fish with candied walnuts, their appetizers, including their spring rolls and fried won tons, and their main courses. Their won ton soup is amazing and I keep going back to the sesame chicken, which is my favorite version anywhere. Everything is expertly and quickly prepared using fresh, quality ingredients and servers are always most accommodating. That said, the decor and surroundings are noisy and not terribly conducive to a nice experience. Dining at Sangkee, unless you go quite early to beat the crowd, can be outright unpleasant. Unless you get one of their rare booths, chances are you may be sitting smack next to strangers. And, while I don't believe in placing a review for a business based upon the quality of their clientele, Sangkee somehow has more than their fair share of utter douche-bags in their customer-base of any restaurant on the Main Line. Loud, rude, and obnoxious fellow diners can and do put a damper on the dining experience. Unless I arrive shortly after 3 for an early dinner, I much prefer ordering Sangkee from Main Line Delivery.

text: Billed as a "boutique hotel" Hotel 43 left a lot to be desired during my recent stay. The pros? Free WiFi (slow but it's free), free pass to the Boise Art Museum, and the bed (very comfortable with lots of pillows and nice linens). It's also got a great location in the heart of downtown Boise and the staff is very nice given they were constantly apologizing for everything. The cons? i seriously kept looking to see if I was on a Candid Camera episode as everything was a joke. How about a call telling me in the morning that the hot water was going to be turned off for repairs, and the hotel hoping I had already taken my shower? Not funny, but true. But wait. There's more. Room service came with the wrong order including some foods that I am allergic to even after I explained it a couple of times. No coffee in the room (really? what hotel doesn't have coffee these days?) Tired bathrooms that looked like something out of 1980 with a separate area for the sink, no 24 hour room service, keys that don't work (I had them re done 3 times) and the worst thing? They "forgot" to clean my room and leave clean towels. How can all of this happen in a span of 24 hours? I get that I was only paying $89 a night which is a steal. But when the hassles outweigh the benefits, you can bet I am staying somewhere else the next time I am in town. Cold shower, anyone?

text: Great great great tacos! I biked out here one day because I really wanted some authentic Mexican food and I actually read all the other Yelp reviews to find it. I prefer the red kind but I mix it with the green sometimes. We ordered the chicken, beef and chorizo tacos and they were all really delicious and cheap. The meat is a little on the fatty side but I say it's worth it if you're going once in a while. They also put freshly cut raw onions on there with cilantro and they give you plenty of lime slices. It's also BYO which is awesome. I haven't tried their other menu items but there are definitely lots of other options. I saw a big mix of people there--Latinos, typical grad students, families, etc. The place wasn't packed but there was a constant flow of people for dinner. I went back for lunch and there's outdoor seating in the back with not much of a view (it's not in the best part of Philly) but it was nice to eat outdoors in the spring. I definitely can't wait to go try some more tacos again!

text: I am so conflicted about this place, I had to create a Yelp account to talk about it. Let me start by saying that the food and drinks at Bumstead's are absolutely amazing. I had a Bloody Mary (with pepper vodka) and, rather by accident, a meatless portabello mushroom "burger". The ambiance was comfortable and it's open late. All wonderful points that should make this place indispensable. So why are there 2 stars? This restaurant is like someone who looks great from behind but makes you run away when they turn around. Their back-end is fantastic (e.g., chef, bartender, etc.) but their front end (service, menu) is keeping me from wanting to go back! Like I mentioned, this is very conflicting. What do I mean? I went there for the first time about a week ago and their menu has a section listed 'Burgers'. Next to the name of each burger is a list of ingredients. Pretty simple. I made my order, the waitress asked me what I wanted and that was it. Right? No. My "burger" had no meat on it. The waitress - who had asked me how I wanted it cooked - claimed that we should have known that if a burger has meat in it, the meat is listed in the ingredients. ("WHAT?" I say to myself, "It's a LIST of BURGERS! By default, it should be *assumed* that the BURGERS contain, well - a BURGER!" o_0) There is no mention of a vegetarian bias anywhere on the menu, on the walls, in the decor, nor the people who eat there. So in my utter confusion and assuming that it must be a mistake, I very nicely inquired as to why there was no meat in our "burger" - and we got the kind of thinly veiled acerbic response that one would expect from a pretty young blonde (nothing against blondes, just want to identify her) who, because of her looks, is terribly resentful of having had to try hard at anything because she's been hot all her life, and as a result, is now a waitress and isn't doing that very well because, well, she's kind of dim and her attitude sucks. (And like I said, when we ordered it, she *did* ask us how we wanted it cooked - to which we replied 'medium rare'.) So until the service gets better and they BURN all copies of the Most Misleading Burger Menu in America - perhaps making one that assumes the presence of meat or puts those 'meatless burgers' into another category (it's *really* simple concept, guys) - I'm not going back and this review will stand.

text: Growing up, this was my favorite place to go on Tuesday mornings! Sometimes my mom would take me during the school year and I'd get a note to go to school late, "doctor's appointment" and all that. I believe now it's also open on Saturdays, but Tuesday is still the OG in my book. You can find just about everything here. At least ten years ago I bought these plaid reusable shopping bags that I still use, and everywhere I go people ask me about them. I've bought incense, patchouli, baskets, sunglasses, baseball hats, flip flops, clothes, and nail polish here. And lets not forget the soft pretzels and baked goods straight from Amish Country. I can't wait to go home again so I can visit Rice's!
label: POS

text: Got a new tattoo by Amanda. She is so awesome. I loved her very colorful tattoos and asked her if she would mind doing a small one for me while I was there waiting for my sister to get hers done. She was so nice and fit me right in. I would recommend her 100%.
label: POS

text: We've used Mt Airy for over a decade but have recently decided to switch vets. It's really slipped the past year or two. We have had one problem after another in terms of records not updated, wrong medication administered and a general deterioration in terms of organization. We have also boarded our dogs and they have come back dirty and sick. Having said that Dr. Lauderdale is wonderful - I wish she were somewhere else. I'm sad to leave but my sense is that there is a real push to see more patients and not as much time is being devoted to service. Oh and the prices - there are more every time we go - even if it's only been a month.
label: NEG

text: I started noticing this little place on my weekly way to Wegmans a little less than two years ago. Thai and French? Count me in! I had always wanted to stop by but never actually made it there until last night. Perhaps it is one of those stones better left unturned... This ranks among one of the worst meals I have had on the East coast. My Fiancee and I decided to split a salad and an entree because the menu turned out to be far most costly than anticipated. The salad was a small pile of spring mix, lightly dressed, with a julienned jicama spear, a single cherry tomato and one candied walnut. (When I went for the tomato it popped out from under my fork and made a break for it rolling along the floor, so no tomato for me. Boo) Then our entree, Crispy Duckling with Pineapple Cranberry Glaze, arrived. The dish looked alright... until I cut into it and was immediately reminded of Chevy Chase's Christmas Turkey. I was under the impression just the skin would be "crispy" but this duck was so dry we had some difficulty chewing it. I was glad they were so prompt in refilling our water glasses. Final word: The food came out quickly and the wait staff was attentive but the meal was so poorly executed that I would not recommend it.
label: NEG

text: Great diner experience. The french fry omelette was.... interesting. This place isn't the best greasy spoon you will visit, but it's definitely one of the coolest ones. There's a historic feel to it, and the service is unbelievable. Just be smart and avoid peak times, even though the line moves somewhat quickly enough. Expect to rub elbows with people, as you're all seated at the counter. Burgers are good, chili is decent, waffles are good, omelettes are okay. I can't speak for much else here, but all in all you should give it a go at least once. If you're a tourist staying in the French Quarter, this place is accessible by streetcar, just take the St. Charles line all the way down, it's a gorgeous ride. When you hit a 90-degree corner, after passing Audubon Park and Loyola, you've hit Carrolton, and you'll need to get off there. You'll see Cameliia Grill from the corner, and don't be put off by the line, it moves fairly quick.
label: POS

text: This is my favorite park, because it is only three blocks away from where I live on Whitland Avenue. I used to play baseball there quite a bit, but baseball has sort of become out of favor in this area. I wish there was a viable adult baseball league in Nashville. We used to play baseball at Elmington, but there just aren't enough people who want to play real hardball, and there are too many other people in the park to make it safe. There are a couple dozen former major/minor leagues in Nashville who would still like to get together, but we are spread out and never seem to be able to get together. Still, I like walking up to the park and using it for my turnaround spot when I walk the neighborhood. I have seen the Australian Football games there, and it looks like fun. I kicked a couple of those balls one time, and they asked me to join the team. I was quite a bit older than the guys playing, so I passed. As for the kids who dress in black and hang out there, hey it keeps them off the streets, and that has to be good for something. There was this one pretty auburn-haired girl who was about 25 years old, close to 6 feet tall, dressed in black with purple lipstick that I must say looked darn attractive. She looked like she could have been a model and her costume was intriguing and becoming.
label: POS

text: I should have known better when the parking lot was nearly empty on a Saturday night.. Shame on me. First the food.. While not horrible but it's basically what Chi-chi's would serve, well minus the Hepatitis A. Even though I don't like it I know a lot people who do, personally I think Taco Bell is a step up. However the worst part was the service. Not only bad but rude to boot. As others said we waited almost 15 mins for service and the place was empty.Then to make it even worse we were not even done our meal the waitress comes over and slaps the check on the table and just walks off. I wish I had a larger pair of testicles or I would have left 50 cents as a tip, but I'm a wimp. I could not wait to get out of this place.
label: NEG

text: My car was hit while it was parked and caused severe damage to the front bumper and one of the lights. Basil's was suggested to me by my mechanic and I am extremely pleased with the work that was done. The price was reasonable and did not exceed the estimate. It was also very quick. It took only one day to order the parts and one day to repair the car. The owner was professional, knowledgeable, helpful and not pushy. I am very pleased with the end results.
label: POS

text: From Boston but now winter in Tampa. I spent many an hour looking for an Asian restaurant that could stack up with the selections in Boston. Finally I tried Big Bok Choy Bistro and was very pleasantly surpirsed. It was the best Asian food I have found in Tampa. Give it a try.
label: POS

text: This is a consistently great neighborhood restaurant. Giorgio is usually there every night and just awesome. My boyfriend and I are devoted regulars. Ambiance: Warm and jolly to put it best. When it is busy it can get loud but it's all very familial. Service: They know the menu and are more than accommodating. They are friendly and efficient even when it is busy. First thing that comes to mind is that they are all pretty experienced. Plus, Giorgio really tries to look after his diners - checks in and meets people throughout the night. Makes you feel doubly welcome. Food: I normally do not like cream sauces as much but I love their linguine w/prosciutto & peas in tomato cream sauce. It is my definite go-to. Their mushroom bruschetta is fantastic - very earthy but not too subtle. The arugula salad is refreshing and citrusy but the grilled caesar salad is my favorite. (Again I really do not like caesar salad..) It is grilled baby romaine that is nicely dressed. Everything that I have had is a just a great dish. Nothing immensely creative but is just simply good italian food in a simple italian restaurant. Drinks: BYOB! Wine is our usual but I've brought along some nice beers that have complimented nicely with the meal. Dogfish's Red&White did nicely last time. I'll always be back for more!
label: POS

text: After seeing an episode of "Throw Down" with Bobby Flay I decided to take the trip and check this place out. The Mac & Cheese is nothing short of legendary. Made with 7 different exotic cheeses. It even made it on Oprah's list, lol.
label: POS

text: Went there for lunch for the first time today and enjoyed a fabulous 1/2 sandwich + salad (I had the Detox veggie sandwich). Everything was really fresh, very flavorful and inexpensive compared to other restaurants in this area. I will be back. Hm, and I thought their pastries looked very fresh and tasty, too. But I resisted. :) I also love that all their carry-out packaging is made of compostable materials.
label: POS

text: A friend and I went for lunch on a weekday; i.e., NOT busy and were seated immediately. That was about as good as it got. I ordered the shepard's pie and my friend got chicken quesadilla. Both were stone-cold when delivered and had to be sent back. My shepard's pie was boiling hot when returned - too hot to eat. And my friend's quesadilla was still barely lukewarm. No effort was made to satisfy her or offer her a dessert or a comped glass of wine. Will probably never give this place a second chance and I live right in town; was looking forward to a new,casual restaurant. No such luck.
label: NEG

text: Update 12-09: Since we have been here once before, I decided to try it again with 2 other couples. It was just a casual get together dinner date and I wanted to go to an Italian place with good pricing and consistent tasting food. Remember my past experience, I decided to make a reservation here. Unforfunately, this time, I can only give it 2 stars but really if I could 2.5 stars. The food was fine. Not spectacular but fine. Everyone ate their food: Gnochi, Veal Parm, Fish pasta (special of the day)... cheese cake, tiramisu, bruschetta. It was the service that took some points off this time and I was REALLY embarrassed. Maybe I shouldn't be but I could not help it since I was the one that picked the place. It was very crowded and the tables are very close to each other. You should work out before you arrive. The waiter was very aggressive at stopping your conversation to speak (but his accent was so thick my friend couldnt understand and we had to translate). They took our plates very aggressively as well. God forbid you wait a few minutes to tackle last few bites! You practically have to slap the hands out of the way! The last straw was the bill - ****** One, Uno, 1 Credit card PER table!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! ONLY!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! OMG!!!!!!!! If you dont believe them, they bring out the menu and stick it in your face because it is printed there and so if you ignored it or didnt read it then you are screwed but there is an ATM in the restuarant so you can still pay them! And if the party is 5 or larger, they automatically charge you 20% tip. I guess you can only eat with 1 other couple there. This is really what took the star off from last time. We should've gone to Brazino.
label: NEG

text: Very, very overrated with extremely unfriendly service. Would give it 1 star, but the baked potato was decent.
label: NEG

text: Best pizza in South Jersey, period. Crisp thin homemade crust, perfectly seasoned, creates the palate for the rest of the pie. The signature pie is my first choice, followed by the marinara pie. Both are fantastic, it just depends what you're in the mood for. The Signature is more of a traditional pizza with a layer of cheese, topped with spinach and crushed seasoned tomatoes. If you're in the mood for something with a little heat, try the marinara pie. Just crust, spicy marinara sauce, topped with grated asiago. Simple and truly satisfying. Service is great, but expect them to be busy on the weekends! The line is usually out the door. Be advised, they have strange hours and are cash only.
label: POS

text: New ownership and the food has gotten even better! Order anything from cheesesteaks to cold sandwiches and you will be content. Small parking lot in the back makes this more of a pickup or delivery place than an eat in place.
label: POS

text: I tried the 50% off menu and it was really just that..small portions of fish, not outstanding.....I love Sakura across the street...nicer menu and better taste overall
label: NEG

text: I like the concept of the store. There is no doubt that Fond is a great restaurant. I have always stressed ingredients as key to great food. I like that they are able to sell the makings of what makes Fond food excellent. However, I wasn't entirely impressed with the inventory. Much of this food can be obtained elsewhere. I was under the impression that it would be Edwardsville or neighboring town grown food. Even if this were so, it would have a hard time operating on days of the Farmer's Market which I think is a opportune time to support our local businesses in Edwardsville. Anyhow, at the Grocer, the selection volume was not as big as I anticipated. The ambiance is great. It really feels like a general store. The service was excellent. They were willing to help me out at moments notice. Perhaps I went on a bad day. I'll come back to reassess sometime.
label: NEG

text: Tick-tock STL! I'm commited to an Aug 20 departure back home to San Francisco. In the interim, I'm soaking up St. Louis' must-eats and must-dos. My most recent stop was Harvest. Per usual, saddled up to the bar and well-attended to by the bartender. The nightly appetizer special an Asian-inspired tuna tower was good, but had too many things going on-seared ahi tuna, heirloom tomatoes, chinese longbeans, and some potato crips. All fantastic alone, but didn't quite work together. If the tomatoes were nixed, it actually would have been a better dish. The steak and frites was fantastic; not sure of the cut, but seemed like sliced filet or another lean cut and cooked perfectly to medium-rare. Fries in duck fat - come on, you can't go wrong there either. Fries accompied by some tasty dipping sauces too-one like ranch another like catsup. Regrettably skipped dessert, but the Rye (that's right, rye) Manhattan filled in nicely.
label: POS

text: Sweet mother of all that is good and holy...Number One is not the name that should have been given to this MSG palace. No, just the memories of my husband and his two roommates ordering food from this place and having only one bathroom in the apartment is enough to trigger PTSD. Enough said. Husband likes to justify it because it was so cheap...he might as well have eaten deep fried cardboard soaked in Ex-Lax, because it would have accomplished the same effect at the same price.

text: I visited the Platinum Grille on Mother's Day. The reason why I visited this restaurant was because a local radio station WDAS had given it such a nice big shout out. From what the radio station said, I thought I would give it a try. Well, when I first arrived and didn't see a waiting line on Mother's Day that should have told me something. Let me say that I found the place to be decorated very very nicely. I thought the colors and decor was very nice. The ladies room was very nice and clean. The staff was very friendly, but our waitress seemed a little bit out of the know. She couldn't answer our questions about prices and had to keep going back and forth to find out answers. It took the staff forever to supply some spoons for desserts. In fact, they gave us a soup spoon for dessert! The dessert table did not have any presentation at all. Given the space at the Platinum Grille I thought it was a little over crowed for a buffet style menu. I didn't like the variety of the food. Not much to choose from. It was enough to get full, but I left unsatisfied with the menu. I know usually a place can have an off night, but I can say for sure I won't be back to try it again.
label: NEG

text: Ahhh, Weber's! I didn't think these kinds of places existed anymore until my friend's mom brought us here. I have since returned multiple times. You drive up, order while parked and everything is brought ought onto a clip-on tray that probably chips your window up, but who cares! Everything was hot, tasty, and their rootbeer was unique and refreshing. The fries are skinny, as far as I can remember, which isn't something you see in big-fat America. Consistently good and a place in my memory would cateogirze Weber's.
label: POS

text: This use to be my go to theatre when I wanted to see some new block buster release. It has an odd smell of popcorn butter, mildew, and moth balls... The seats are older and depending on the film can be pretty uncomfortable. The gummi bears are not fresh. The soda tastes flat. The floors are sticky. The ushers can be rude if they're not too busy text messaging. And it's the only theatre I've been to where it's okay to talk throughout the whole movie, get into a screaming match on your cell phone, or let your kids run up and down the isles unchecked...
label: NEG

text: I can't think of another place to fix my brown rice craving. For just 50 cents extra, you can get brown rice with any of their lunch options. I usually stick with the spicy string bean with chicken and brown rice, but have on occasion gotten their house salad. The salad has a nice bed of crisp greens with sliced apples and some other yummy things. What other chinese restaurant serves fresh crispy salads? As for service, they're always very fast with your order, whether you're sitting in or taking out. I've come in during the lunch rush, ordered at the register, and taken it out to go all within the space of 7 minutes. I tend to get my Chinese fix here, rather than the food trucks, mainly because of the brown rice. The food is a little pricier, but I can usually squeeze two healthy lunches out of the deal. And I don't have white rice bloat later on.
label: POS

text: I hope this place burns to the ground. Literally. My first summer in law school I figured I'd take a waitressing job here, after waitressing in SF and making a small fortune doing so. not only is the minimum wage with waitressing in nola $2 (vs. $9 something/hr in SF plus tips obviously, but i digress), but this place is run by incompetents. I'd always heard the food here sucked ass, but never tried it myself, and it was nearby, so in my random application process, i ended up here. The co-owner (wife) seemed nice, and when the barely literate 'manager' called me to come in to 'go over the menu' a couple nights later i was excited to begin working...I came in and they were shocked that i hadnt come in that am (apparently the imbecile who told me to come in that afternoon to 'look over the menu' meant to tell me to come in in the MORNING to TRAIN. as in not look over the freaking menu, but to actually begin working. either way, wouldnt typical protocol be to call me that morning when i didnt show?? having put this event in my phone, and being a responsible law school student, it seems fairly obvious to me that the 'management' is inept.). a couple days later, i was terminated for my failure to come in that am, to which i responded with a lengthly letter to the owner, that it was their managers fault, as she told me to come in that 'afternoon to look over the menu.' As i'm responsible, i brought waitress style clothing just to be safe, although i dont believe that would be implied when told to 'come in to look over the menu'. As i'm rambling now with rage 1.5 yrs later at the absolute idiocy that this place embodies, i'll discuss other details of the restaurant. As my friends had previously said, the food here is awful. bland bland bland. my boyfriend liked the margaritas as theyre fairly cheap, and we all repeatedly would get heartburn from the shitty jose. to top it all off, i have heard (and experienced nothing else myself), that the service is BEYOND poor. the staff is comprised of artsy assholes, who dont give a flying rats ass if you have any food/water/have ordered/have died at the table from food poisoning. literally, you will bus your own table and if you ever see a refill of water or anything else you are beyond lucky. everyone i know in nola has had nothing but negative experiences here, and after the first termination of my LIFE, due to someone elses incompetence, i have refused (as have all my friends) to ever set foot in this shit establishment again. if you like wasting money on bland food and god awful service then feel free, as the 'owner' informed me in response to my letter addressing my inappropriate termination, they were 'overhauling' the management. Strangely years later, i have still yet to hear anything good about nacho mamas.

text: We went there a couple months ago for my birthday, and we were VERY happy with the entire evening! The service was (for the most part) prompt and very friendly. The only issue was our server did not tell us any specials and when we heard another server telling a table nearby, we had to ask our server about them. Otherwise, everything from the Sangria to all of the different tapas we tried were outstanding. Highly recommended!

text: Ended up going her 3 times over a long weekend I was staying in the El Dorado. They have the same food out night after night, it doesn't taste all that great and if you've had it the night before there is no "newness" factor to it. If you are in Reno, go and check out the buffet at Harah's or at the Atlantis.

This one is my favorite of the 4 that I've been to and the one I frequent the most. Never had a bad burrito, a dirty table or a surly employee. The other stores haven't earned that distinction. If you don't know chipotle, get over there. Always fresh (really) and always yummy.

text: I have been here twice and each time I've been impressed with the vegetarian options on the menu (besides pizza). Waitstaff were not incredibly friendly but were knowledgeable. Their garlic bread is so yummy. There are a few different desserts you can choose from. And, overall, I think i'd treck over to the French Quarter another time for a taste.

There is the usual Azian fare to include sushi, hot wings and some traditional southern dishes. Lunch time didn't appear too busy and dishes were promptly refilled when they ran out. Like I said, I don't like mass produced buffet style food but if you do they have a nice selection of food, salads and sushi to include several desserts and ice cream.

text: Ugh, thinking about the place makes me a little sick to my stomach - that might be due to the fact that a few hours after I left I became violently ill and I still haven't recovered. Coincidence? Probably. But still... Anyway I was happily surprised when I was greeted by a nice hostess and had a nice server and I thought the previous reviews must have been wrong. I've never been chastised so badly in a bar for standing instead of sitting down. God forbid you stand up to talk to someone at another table - your server will most likely go into a catatonic state until order is regained. Greatest Funeral Ever was the band and I would go there to see them again. I guess.

text: This funky little bar is across the alley from the rear courtyard of St. Louis Cathedral. Friends and I stopped in on a recent Saturday afternoon to sample their absinthe. The absinthe preparation is a show: absinthe plus burning sugar! Cool. Not being a fan of licorice or Sambuca, however, I am not a fan of the taste. No worries - one of my friends finished off mine and hers. Whew. The clientele here is truly eclectic: locals, tourists, and wedding parties slamming down a few drinks before walking down the aisle at the cathedral. The owners are the bar tenders and are pleasant and accommodating. Fun bar that I will visit again.

text: I've been to the Stone Creek locations in Plainfield and Noblesville, and sadly, the Greenwood location doesn't hold a candle to either of those. The atmosphere wasn't cozy and upscale like the other locations, and the menu and service didn't seem as good either. Maybe my impression of those was too influenced by the decor, but I wasn't impressed. I would go back to the other locations again, but not this one.

text: Visiting Philly for a day, and this was walking distance from the hotel, and recommended by the concierge. Oh man he was so wrong. Tuesday and I walked in with the dashing Daniel and the hostess asked us about 20 questions before sitting us in their dark, dungeon-esc EMPTY dining room around 8pm. The menu was boring, and very much wanting to be Italian. Is it italian? I have no idea. Tuesday and Daniel both got the Salmon, and I got a 10oz filet. Rare, please. We order, and wait, and wait, and wait. I was drunk off 1 glass of wine before the bread came for my dining companions. The guy who brought the bread assured us it was fresh and just had come out of the oven. Cold and tough. What a liar. Our meals finally arrived and my risotto appeared to be swimming- it was like risotto soup under my steak. Whatever. I hadnt eaten in 8 days. Not a real meal anyway. I wolfed down my veggies, and risotto before getting to the steak. I was so excited for a cold center, bloody, nutritious, perfection- EFF MY LIFE. I cut into it. There's no pink. Not til I hit the middle where it was a hot pink center. SO not rare. I specified as bloody as legally possible. Hell, bring it out raw, and I'll eat it. Fine by me. Well, after the long wait, and both my friends dissatisfied with their meals, I wasn't about to try again. Also- I was ridiculously hungry. The manager came by when we were about 80% done with our meals and asked us how everything was. Daniel and Tuesday both averted their eyes knowing that my mouth was about to fly open. I explained the steak situation and he offered to remove it from our bill ($41). I declined as I had eaten almost all of it, and it just didnt feel right. Instead he comp'd the drinks, and even then I felt that was generous. I don't want anything for free ever- I just want it done right. Creepy gothic atmosphere, like a vampire would live there( i suppose thats 'in' right now). Mundane food, over cooked steak, and according to the friends, lame, cold salmon. Go to Capital Grille. Even though its a chain, at least you know it will be consistent.
label: NEG

text: I don't give 5 stars to greek restaurants easily, but this place deserves it. I wish it were more of a sit down restaurant, but enjoy it as it is: an order-it-at-the-counter-the sit-and-wait-for-it kind of place. I grew up eating Middle Eastern foods, and fancy myself a full blown greek/lebanese foodie. The prices are amazing if you stick to the specials. I regularly indulge in the greek salad topped with grilled chicken. The chicken shwarma is also delicious. The best part is the pickled beet, onion, cucumber garnish. YUM!
label: POS

text: This place is great. The wine list is extensive and varied. The food comes in small portions and is reasonably priced given its quality. We are local and have eaten there many times, and tried many of their entrees. Of particular note are the Smoked Trout and Salmon Crepe and the Fondue Crepe. The steak sandwich is also excellent.
label: POS

text: My wife and I stopped there for an early dinner on 7/8/2010 after dropping my son off for his first quarter at AIPH. Not being a beer person like I am, she was a bit hesitant at going there. She ended up having a few glasses of wine from their short winelist, while I had a few of the Belgian specialty brews a Cantillion kriek and an oak aged sour Petrus both were quite good. The brew list is impressive, heavy on the Belgian styles (the main reason I wanted to try the place), but there are quite a few selections from other parts of the world (around 200 varieties overall). Overall the brew selection is slanted towards the higher alcohol styles. The food - We had the Charcouterie Platter as a starter. The rabbit terrine was wonderful as well as the grilled sausages and the mix of Belgian and English cheeses. The coarse mustard included on the platter was one of the best that we have ever had. She had a small pot of the Ghent style mussels (leeks, bleu cheese and bacon in a DuPont Saison) while I had the grilled duck salad. She said that the mussels were great (I can't eat them, as I sometimes become violently ill while eating mussels - something to do with whatever they were feeding on rather than the mussles themselves, so I avoid eating them altogether). I had a vew of the pomme frites that were served with the mussels, and was not impressed with them. The cut of the potatoes was all wrong, limp skinny shoestrings rather than thick cut & chunky, the included burbon mayo was quite good however. The duck salad included a perfectly cooked half breast, and a nice slice of fresh goat cheese but the mesclun green salad was rather average. The included spiced walnuts were good, but nothing to shout about. When I get back there again, I will probably just have a burger. Overall, I would give it a 6/5 (yes I know the scale only goes to 5 but the list was well above average) for the beer and a 3/5 for the food - call it a 4 overall.
label: POS

text: Awesome place for lunch, with 5 or so sandwich places within a stones throw of Pickles, I am and will remain loyal to the ruben or the philly at pickles deli for now and forever. I have had about 4-5 different sammy's there but continually go back to the corned beef ruben while my partners in sandwich eating stick with the philly cheese steak. In addition have these awesome potato chips that I haven't seen anywhere else that are crab flavored (sounds weird but try it.) I recall on one of the first times in after they opened, the owner overheard us querying the crab chips and then he gave us a bag to try free of charge. Just like a crack dealer...the first one's free. (Or so I've heard) Friendly staff that will bring your sandwich after they grill it up, as well as clear the table and bring your refills of your fountain Diet Dr. Pepper, a must stop for lunch if you are south of Lindell in the CWE.
label: POS

text: I would NEVER eat here. We stopped in at Mona's after dinner to have a hookah. The place was so dirty I could not believe it. Good Hookah Though!

They do however have actual silverware and not plastic forks. Our waitress just placed our check on the table and didn't say anything, didn't offer us the little club deal thing or thank us. Seriously. 2) Shady activities on the lawn. Listen, I am not the least bit prude. And PDA usually doesn't even bother me. But I've seen people getting it on here more times than I cared to see (for the record: twice). Hearing Dave Matthews crooning about Superman really makes you lose all inhibitions? Really? Rampant fights and drug use are common too, but hey, I didn't come here to go to church so those things don't really bother me much. I can see how others might be turned off. I'm not sure I've ever seen security doing anything here besides making sure you can't get into the seating area without a seating ticket. 3) Bathrooms. You have a good chance of missing half the set if you have to go during a show. The lines are long because there are a pathetic amount of johnny on the spots and most people use them for non-bathroom related activities (see #2) 4) The experience sucks. You mean I only have to pay 50 bucks a ticket so that I can see a band I like from half a mile away, while being trampled by retarded kids and hoosiers? Sign me the fuck up! I feel bad for those suckers who pay half as much to see much better music in a much smaller venue, where you actually feel like you're in the same time zone as the band you're seeing! 5) Food and drink prices are ridiculous but not really unexpected. Look, I have definitely had fun here and have seem some good shows. But this place is very poorly run and managed with ZERO consideration to the customer experience. The thinking is that they have the only large outdoor concert venue in St. Louis. No competition = no desire to improve. Every year people gripe about lousy parking, no bathrooms, expensive prices, and every year the same people come back anyway. Where else is Aerosmtih and Dave Matthews going to come in June? Well...not me. It would take a very impressive lineup or one or two of my all time favorite bands to get me to come here again. I've passed over a few shows I wanted to see because I didn't want to come here. It's just not worth it. AVOID!

Although rumored wait times of 45 minutes during lunch rush hour are not to be doubted, my 3 PM order for 3 burritos (I roped in my friends) took about 20 minutes. It was possibly the best burrito I have ever eaten. Don Memo's burritos are bursting with flavor and freshness. Always prepared in front of you, the deliciously marinated steak, the freshly-cut slices of ripe avocado, the beans, tomatoes, and rice all combined together and wrapped in a toasted, warm flour tortilla is almost too much to ask for. I savored every bite for a good twenty minutes as I chomped through the humongous burrito. Washed down with a sweet bottle of pina soda (pineapple, like pina colada), I was quite content with my mid-afternoon meal. Probably don't need to eat dinner later tonight was what I thought as I crumpled my napkin to throw it away. You could easily split one of these honking burritos with a friend and both end up satisfyingly full. $6 for a burrito - choice of chicken, beef, pork. Other items on the menu also look delicious. Highly, highly recommended and added to my food trucks list.
