text: The Arts Condo building is located in the old Sylvania hotel building at 1324 Locust Street. Billed as "luxury condominium", one is easily fooled upon walking in the front door. The lobby is gorgeous - marble and hard wood, amazing modern chandeliers and leather furniture, velvet chairs, a security staffed front desk, gleaming new elevators. This is where the luxury ends. A little over a year ago my spouse and I had to move out of our apartment unexpectedly because our landlady decided to sell without telling us. (Yes, we sued. Yes, we won.) Not wanting to relocate out of our own neighborhood we rented a studio apartment at The Arts Condos. The studios run for between $800-1100 depending on how well refurbed they have been inside, but make no mistakes - these are studios at the truest sense of the word. They are extremely small, the size of a large master bedroom. They have tiny kitchenettes with one cabinet and a mini fridge. There is no oven, no counter space. The bathroom is equally small, room for one and one only. The building tries to explain away the high cost of these tiny apartments by including all utilities including digital cable access, but it just isn't worth it. Granted I haven't seen the one or two bedroom units that are available, but the majority of the condos are studios. One of the worst parts of the building is the central air and central heat which you cannot control in your unit. Sure, you're SUPPOSED to be able to do so, but you can't. I managed to live in not one, not two, but THREE different units over a year and two months in the building. I left the first unit after two months, demanding that the landlord let me out of my lease. I did this because the knob that was supposed to allow me to control my central air did not work, and it was the dead of summer. I stayed in the second unit for 10 months, but it was an ongoing struggle to get anything done. Right after moving in the central air stopped working for my entire floor, and it stayed non-working for 3 1/2 weeks. We got a notice from the management company saying that they were not responsible for helping us with the problem. Fortunately our landlord allowed us to buy a window unit and deduct it from the rent. However the problems continued - plumbing being a major issue in the entire building. Another big issue is that the property management office - which by the way is ONE employee ONLY - is only open from 8-5 on Monday-Friday, so if you have an after-hours or weekend problem, there is no one to go to for immediate assistance. This means that if you put your laundry and detergent into a washing machine in the laundry room and then it won't work, you're screwed. And yes...that happened. In the winter the heat wasn't working properly, and when I reported it to the property manager I was told that she thought the problem had been fixed...LAST YEAR. It was always something, and it was clear that the property management company didn't give a crap about residents. Only about property OWNERS. Another thing they try to use to "sell you" on living or buying in the building is an "office center" in the lobby which ostensibly provides you access to the things one might need for office purposes. What this amounts to is two PC computers in little cubby areas and one printer. The computers are internet enabled but useless for anything practical as practically every feature has been disabled. And the printer is good for copying ONLY, because it is not attached to the computers for actual printing! Eventually our landlord stopped responding to our complaints, which admittedly isn't the management company's fault, but I think he was just fed up of the constant complaints and mad that the management company wouldn't help. We ended up suing him to get out of our lease. Unfortunately we wound up stuck in a THIRD apartment on a month-to-month lease for 2 months because the arrangements we'd made to live elsewhere fell through. Those two months were our best in the building thanks in part to a hugely attentive landlord but also because we stopped taking the crap of the staff and began standing up for ourselves. One of the other things the building doesn't do anything about is disturbance by neighbors. The building is FILLED with college students; every day it seemed there was some 19 year old taking a tour with his/her parents. Consequently there is a ton of drinking and pot smoking, and partying. In the first and third apartments we had problems with neighbors being too noisy, and in the third it was a big problem. I filed complaint after complaint about the late night noise and the smell of weed coming through the walls, and nothing was done. We finally left after 14 months, one lawsuit and a lot of nonsense. Just as we were finally leaving they managed to put together a condo association. I'm glad we won't be there to see that. The Arts Condos is a MUST AVOID property in Philadelphia.

Overall, the food, service and value were terrific. The kitchen staff is young, but it does not show in their food vision and execution and they have the added bonus of being eager and looking to please the clientele under the experienced front of the house guidance of Tory Keomanivong, a vetran of Lacroix and Founders (Bellevue). text: Tortilla Press NEVER disappoints me! The staff is friendly and very helpful (we hosted a party there and they went above and beyond). The food is fresh, tasty and unique. Brunch - I've been 3x for their Early Bird brunch and it is a serious value for what you get. $6.00 before noon on Saturday or Sunday and you get a smaller menu that packs a flavorful punch. I've had the Cheese Chilequiles as well as the Quiche of the Day and they are amazing. You can add on things like fresh squeeze orange juice, chorizo coins, chorizo hash if your meal doesn't come with it for an additional cost, but it is really not necessary as the portion sizes are generous and when you sit down they bring you a basket of cinnamon/sugar tortillas with their signature sweet yogurt honey dip. DELICIOUS!!! Dinner - I've been there twice for dinner. My own meals ordered were the coconut habanero shrimp - great flavor, not TOO spicy, but just enough to compliment the creamy coconut sauce. The mashed potatoes and sauteed veggies that came with it were good too. I've also had the Pork Enmoladas and WOW was this flavorful. The portion is huge, and everything complimented each other very well. I'd never had a mole sauce before and it was a very nice first experience. I've also tasted the smothered shrimp and scallops burrito (HUGE and very good) and the carne ranchero and rainbow shrimp (tender steak, and the shrimp had a great flavor). Tortilla Press is located in the dry town of Collingswood, so it is BYO. We ordered delicious virgin mango margaritas and added tequila at the table. I would recommend dining here any time.

They keep the fresh bread coming (just ask for a refill), which helps keep the hunger pains away when the busy kitchen is a tad slower than usual. We don't mind waiting because the cocktails are tasty and we're such huge fans of the food, the ambiance (It's relaxed and beautiful at the same time), the experience as a whole. text: This is one of the better Starbucks around. It's busy and the area is nice also. It's conveniently located across the road from Grant MacEwan University which might make it a lot noisier and tough to find a seat once school is in session. It's a pleasant, spacious location with a good array of indoor and outdoor seating. I've never noticed the parking sign, but you can bet after getting a parking ticket at North Town Mall last week I am looking at the signs more closely. Unfortunately the lot here is managed by Diamond Parking as well. I have only begun to deal with that. Watch for my review of Diamond Parking and North Town Mall. It should be obvious that you should keep an eye on your car for the parking Nazis. If you're going to be longer than two hours, you might want to find a better parking spot. I think I saw some free street parking. Busyness - This is a pretty busy location. It's fairly close to downtown and just across from Grant MacEwan University. I would imagine that it gets even busier once school's back in. Noisiness - There's a nice high ceiling that seems to absorb the noise reasonably well. The music isn't too loud either. Ambience - I've been coming to this Starbucks for a couple of years and I've always liked it. Power - It is available, but the window seats and tables in the centre have an issue. I'd bring an extension cord if you want to use some of the tables in the centre. Free wifi - Available and works well. Being one of those people who keeps a number of tabs open, you might want to login with a browser which you don't use often, otherwise each page becomes a login page, oddly enough. (In Firefox Windows 7 at least.) Staff - Always friendly and helpful. I've rarely had a complaint about a Starbucks employee. Seating - There are 28 seats in this Starbucks, with four armchairs and two good sized tables for laying out a bit of work. I like the square tables they have here. They're at a nice height and are quite roomy, compared to the dinky round cafe tables I normally see at Starbucks. There are four or five tables outside on the spacious patio. It's also bordered by some hedges to give it a bit of privacy. I don't know if they ever use the patio heaters. Security - When I first started coming to this location, there was a homeless camp in the empty lot nearby. It's gone now, but the Starbucks is close to downtown. Not too bad of an area but 107 Ave is close by. Take the usual precautions.
label: POS

text: I'm going to come right out and say it. I love the Brass Tap. If it weren't for my wonderful back porch, it would be my favorite place to hang out and have a beer. Well, on second thought, my back porch doesn't have hundreds of different beers to choose from. So yeah, the Brass Tap IS my favorite place to have a beer. My first experience at the Tap occurred almost a year ago. The wife and I were at Wiregrass mall doing some shopping and were really hungry. We saw this new place and thought we'd try it. As I looked through what I thought was a food menu, I realized that there was only beer and wine available. We left in search of food. Flash forward to March of this year. Wife takes me to the mall during March Madness. She can tell that I don't want to go stand around in Express while she tries on half the store, so she tells me to wait at the Brass Tap and watch some basketball. About an hour (and four beers) later, she finds her slightly drunk husband perched outside on the patio about to order another one. Since that wonderful visit, the wife and I have spent many a day and night sitting out on the patio, people watching and drinking great beer from all around the world. Best of all, we've made friends along the way. See, The Brass Tap to me is kind of like my back porch away from home. I feel comfortable. I feel happy. And what makes a better drinking environment than that? The Tap has plenty of entertainment to keep you occupied too. You can play darts in the back, watch one of about 20 televisions, or experience some great live music. Every Thursday, Friday, and Saturday night, The Brass Tap features great local bands and singers. I really enjoy live music, especially good live music, and I've never been disappointed there. Perhaps my favorite night though is Tuesday. Starting around 9:30, The Tap offers karaoke until the wee hours of the morning. Let's face it, drunk people singing is usually great, even when it's terrible. I've been known to get up and sing a few tunes myself. I fall into the terrible category, but at least I realize it. Oh yes...The beer! With over 40 beers on tap, a list that changes quite frequently, and hundreds of other beers in bottles, you can go there and never have to drink the same beer twice. Sometimes I find it fun to go on a tour of a particular county while there. Although I usually end up just living in Belgium. For non-beer drinkers they also have a nice selection of wines, and if you are the type to bring your kids to a bar, they'll even rustle up some sodas. You can even purchase cigars there as well to accompany your drinks. I mentioned before that on my first trip there, I was disappointed to not find any food on the menu. Fortunately, the two restaurants that bookend The Brass Tap offer to go service, usually going as far as having waiters come over to take orders and deliver. This comes in handy for someone like myself, who seems to really like the 8% alcohol and above beers. What really sets The Brass Tap apart is the staff. We have been fortunate enough to get to know many of the girls that serve there and every one of them is always knowledgeable, friendly, and pretty easy on the eyes too. Even when the waitresses we love move on to new things, the management seems pretty capable of finding the right kind of people to work there. So, in case you couldn't already tell, The Brass Tap is my favorite bar. If I could, I'd go every day. This blog would get pretty boring though if I never went anywhere else. Still, this is always a must at least once or twice a week. Sometimes more. In fact, just writing about it has perked up my taste buds for a nice, cold Chimay. Before I hop in the car, I'll leave you with this. Remember the show Cheers? Sometimes you wanna go where everybody knows your name. And if you're like me, then that's usually a bar. The Brass Tap is my "Cheers" bar. Come in sometime. I'll be sure to scream "Norm!" at you.
label: POS

Anyway, I thought that it would be cool to try out... I've never tanned a day in my life, but liked the idea of the Mystic Tanning. I thought that I would try it for a month to see if I liked it. My friend said she was paying $50 per month for unlimited use of all of their stuff and that the people she recommends get the same price. So I went in. I filled out what I thought was a ridiculous amount of paperwork. I explained that I just wanted to try the place out and that I only wanted to pay what my friend was paying. They ended up quoting me a price of over double what my friend was paying. So I bid them farewell. As soon as my friend caught wind of the price they gave me she spoke with several people at the salon and explained that I was suppose to get this "special rate", etc... The employee working there said it had been a misunderstanding and that I would indeed get the same price that she was paying. I even called ahead of time and explain what had happened, how much I expected to spend and that I just wanted to try it out for a month to see if I like it. They gave me the OK on everything and told me to come in. So I go in again. I listen to the loud music again. I fill out the same ridiculous paperwork again. Within 15 minutes of leaving Planet Beach, the owner was calling me on my cell explaining that there had AGAIN been a misunderstanding and that I should come back. I explained to him that any ounce of tanning-desire that had once been inside of me had died in his salon 15 minutes earlier when his employee told me I had to sign a two year contract. That's when the owner decided to set me straight by delivering this little gem: "Planet Beach is not a tanning salon. Planet Beach is a 'contemporary spa'." As if people's white asses AREN'T lying naked all over his beds trying to get tanned. At the End of the Day - I wasn't willing to commit to a "contemporary spa" for longer then most people commit to a boyfriend.

text: Chloe is a hidden treasure buried within Old City! Chloe began seven years ago when Dan Grimes and Mary Ann Ferrie decided to form their own restaurant - after years of working together at The Latest Dish. The found a wonderful spot - tiny in size - but perfect in atmosphere. The place is candlelit to a warm glow and it is the interaction between the dining customers and the servers and even the owners, that give this place it's overall charm. Now, before I get into the food - the fact is the place can be a bit noisy at times (when all tables are buzzing etc) - but its not a distraction, just one of the ingredients that give this venue its casual feel. Now the food! The menu changes with the season and features some wonderful dishes. Start off with the Chloe Salad; baked panko crusted goat cheese, mixed greens, red onion, topped with an orange chipotle dressing. Summer on a plate! If that doesn't interest you, they have a decent selection of starters; salads and such - including the a grilled free form pizza with fig jam, gorgonzola, applewood smoked bacon and extra virgin olive oil. Then for the large plates, they offer a spectrum of dishes including a great roasted pumpkin and ricotta ravioli with dried cranberries, pumpkin seeds and brown sage butter. If you're looking for something a bit 'meatier' - try the lamb ... grilled Moroccan spiced lamb skewers, minted couscous, cooling cucumber raita and spicy tomatoes. Or perhaps the sushi grade tuna seared rare with banana ginger soy broth, jasmine rice, seaweed salad & crispy wonton chips. But save some room for the desserts - which vary daily and are sinfully fresh! Chloe is unique in that it is a BYOB that takes no reservations and also no credit cards. Additionally, this treasure box is only open Wednesday through Saturdays from 5 - 9:30. With that said - it's worth the trip - especially on a Wednesday or Thursday night, when the wait isn't long (if at all). **I originally submitted this review to http://phillygrub.ning.com in spring 2008**

Pulled pork BBQ, Texas beef BBQ, half and full chickens, brisket, half and full rack of baby back ribs and one strange menu item homemade BBQ hot dogs. I chose a medium takeout of the pulled pork as well as a fullchicken, Sweet mother of God, they piled on enough pulled pork to feed 10 people. She enjoyed them both but said she would pass on the Cajun if offered again. The BBQ chicken...oh that unbelievable BBQ chicken literally fell off the bones as soon as I took it out of the foil container. The chicken was beautifully smoked, the moist smoky meat literally melting in my mouth. The price was also incredible. The pulled pork was only $27.00 (considering there was at least 3 lbs of meat in the container it was beyond a bargain) and the whole chicken was $5.50. I could have fed a family of 10 with all the food I brought home. The service was fantastic and friendly. Everyone behind the tables had a smile and a friendly hello to every customer. Again, if you ever have a lazy saturday when you're bored or looking for something new, try driving out to Blooming Glenn and have the best BBQ in the area. text: Located right off the Monon Trail on Westfield Blvd, Monon has a 'Cheers-like' feel to it with the regular crowd of locals who fight the power and choose local business over corporate espresso. Many of the baristas have been working there for several years and give it a very welcoming feel. Monon has that personality that coffee shop addicts crave in addition to their beverage of choice. Monon serves up all the standards, as well as some of their own signature drinks like the Mocha-Loco Freeze, which is basically an iced mocha blended to perfection. My personal favorite (ask for a 'Helicon' from one of the vets and they'll know what you mean) is a double shot, iced, white chocolate mocha. When things really get tough, I reach for the stars and get a triple shot. I was put to bed once in one of my first visits to Monon back in the day when my friend explained his disbelief that I ordered two shots of espresso in my drink. The female barista, who no longer works there, responded, "I put 5 in mine." One of the best places in Ripple for a daytime business coffee meeting, they also have wi-fi and usually plenty of seating, although it can get busy at times, especially during events like the Broad Ripple Art Fair, when everything like that is busy. In addition to great coffee drinks, Monon has a nice selection of teas, desserts and great smoothies, as well.
label: POS

text: This was the first time that I used a Groupon (a coupon purchased at Groupon.com). Unfortunately, this was the first and will be the last time I will ever visit La Dolce Via though. I booked a reservation for nine people a week in advance. Although it was not particularly busy, they sat us at a table made up of two small tables of different heights pushed together in the back of the restaurant just outside the toilet. The waiter came with a marker board with a short list of "small plates" and "large plates," all priced on the level of fine dining with ambiance and not what I would have expected from a provincial cafe and bakery. My wife and I ordered the goat cheese small plate and the scalops large plate. The silver dollar size dollop of feta and the six small slices of bread were hardly worth the $12 price tag. The four scallops were quite good, but they were paired with instant mashed potatos, which made the $24 price seem outrageous. To top it off, the woman behind the counter who occasionally came to our table wearing a stained tank top and no bra was particularly rude and seemed rather unhappy about the fact that we used the groupon to cover part of the check when we paid for all nine people at our table. There was a resounding "I will never come here again" echoed around our table as we left. So although I love Groupon and will continue buying them, I highly recommend passing on La Dolce Via because there are just far too many unique restaurants in St. Louis to give this place another try.

text: This place has been on my radar for a while because: (1) It's in my hood; (2) it's Asian (Japanese street food from Osaka!); and (3) when you order, you get to say "balls" (I'm 5 years old). When I first heard about the takoyaki balls, I assumed they would be deep fried a la falafel. So when we scheduled a work lunch here, I went in with the mindset that I could indulge now, and eat a salad for dinner. I was surprised to learn that the balls are not fried, but rather hand-cooked in a waffle-iron like contraption with divets the size of golf balls. And while the skins were slightly crisp, the inside was warm and doughy. For lunch, I ordered the health salad, and the classic takoyaki with shrimp. If you are the kind of person that likes quinoa-like grains, you will LOVE the health salad. It's a blackish grain with some veggies cut up on top (carrots, cukes) served with two vinaigrettes. The green pesto-like dressing was delicious, and the salad kept me full for the rest of the afternoon. Takoyaki balls were ooey-gooey and totally scrumptious - unlike anything I've ever eaten before (note: if you don't like Nori, skip the classic takoyaki flavor). A few weeks later, around dinner time, I had a hankering for these balls (hehe), so dining companion and I ventured over. I got the health salad, AGAIN, and the BBQ takoyaki with shrimp. DC got some yakisoba noodles and the sweet 'n sour miso takoyaki with chicken. I definitely prefer the seafood fillings (shrimp, octopus) to the meat fillings. I also loved the BBQ sauce, but was more or less "meh" on the sweet 'n sour miso. Yakisoba was a little too sweet for my liking...but DAMN those balls are good. This is not an everyday place for me, but I know I will get sharp cravings for these tasty little snacks on a fairly regular basis, which is why Maru Global gets 4 stars.

text: The Mercy Lounge is the favorit-est of my favorite venues in Nashville. Almost all of the bands I like, local and touring, play here at least once when they come through town. It's a smaller, intimate type venue where you can get right up in a performer's face if you want or you can chill out off to the side at a table. It's what I'd picture my own club to be if I was lucky and financially secure enough to have one. Their main bar is long and decorated with vintage pin-up girl characters which helps lend to its rock-n-roll attitude. One of the best things about the Mercy Lounge is it's variety of shows that come there. I think it's one of the few, if not the only, venues in town which are not type-casted to a specific genre or music. Their calendar hosts bands from all ranges of the music spectrum and some weeks I can find myself there almost every night. They have a full bar with a decent selection of beer on draft, you can get local brew Yazoo here which is alright by me. Their drink pricing is pretty standard for a venue but they offer drink specials sometimes on nights they do events with local bands. Every Monday night they have 8 off 8th which is a hosting of various local musicians and bands that rotates from week to week. It's always free and it's a good place to be to cure the Mondays. They have a couple of pool tables and some booths in the back room which is a fun place to hang out in-between sets or during an opening band you're not interested in. They have a limited menu, which I have yet to try, but it looks like you're run of the mill 'i've drank a little too much and need to munch on something to clear my head' kind of bar food. Not overtly disgusting but nothing really to excite me into trying the fare. Their door man is touted as the best in Nashville and the bartenders are nice, but usually busy. The parking lot is limited so come early if you don't want to pay, otherwise the independent lot next door can range anywhere from $5 to $15 depending on the expected turn out and how evil the people that own it feel like being. Another thing to note is that the Mercy Lounge tends to sell out easily, especially for bigger name bands. It's best not to wait on buying tickets to shows here or you might find yourself standing in the parking lot hoping someone has a mercy ticket they'll throw your way. Also its located in the middle of an industrial district next to the railroad tracks, so there isn't really anything within walking distance. So if you feel like continuing your evening somewhere else after a show at the Mercy Lounge I suggest you keep your alcohol intake down to a beer or two.

text: I'll preface this whole review by saying that I have a weakness for cheap, hole-in-the-wall diners filled with bunches of interesting "regulars". I love picking up the check for a table of five and finding that the bill is $21 even. I love walking in and feeling like the only people who know of its existence are sitting in its booths. I love seeing the same faces, eating the same breakfast platters, in the same reserved seats, while reading the same sections of the same newspapers each Sunday morning. I love trying to imagine what these people do when they are NOT eating eggs and drinking coffee. It's as though I (along with a coven of fastidious senior citizens) have discovered The Fountain of Deflation and it serves pancakes. Pancakes! The Ranch House is the Crme-de-la-crme of such diners in the Town 'n Country area. It's located at the east end of an old strip mall and easy to miss. It's a small place with a coffee bar, eight or nine tables and four and a half booths. Yes, there is one half of a booth. Stop by. Seat yourself. Order some greasy bacon. Enjoy the scenery. At the End of the Day - Once in the Ranch Houses' parking lot, look for the flashy pick-up parked in the handicapped slot with the personalized "PIMP" license plate and try to match it with its owner sitting inside. You'll never guess right in a million years.

The menu is extensive at first glance, but I quickly realized that at least half the rolls are available at dinner only. You will have access to the sushi basics however, including some really dynamite options like the rainbow roll. Since the prices are low, it's tougher than it sounds to get your $14 worth (the price of the all-you-can eat lunch). This is especially true because the rolls are ENORMOUS (8-10 pieces each!!!). I stuck to the nigiri for the better part of the meal, eating only the fish, and leaving the rice. The fish slices were not too thick and not too thin, and tasted fresh and tender. text: The Fountain on Locust is truly one of my three favorite restaurants in St. Louis. Maybe it's the retro vibe. Maybe it's the excellent customer service. Maybe it's the pricing. Maybe it's the decor. Maybe it's the fantastic portion sizes. Or maybe it's all of the above. The food at Fountain is truly unique. For example, the Blackhawk - the Fountain's spin on the traditional roast beef - now comes with delicious roasted peppers, creamy goat cheese and the most perfect bun that you'll ever have. If soup is your thing, you'll be doing your tastebuds a real disservice if you neglect to try one of Fountain's soups. From peanut to dill pickle to my favorite - cajun corn chowder - their soups are unique, healthy, and really never disappoint. Keep in mind that everything at Fountain is handmade or home made - they avoid high fructose corn syrup and other "crud" that so often fills restaurant food and end up delivering a really mouthwatering plate. Make sure to try the ice cream martinis - there's nothing wrong at all with drinking your dessert! Oh, and one final tip - if you can arrange to sit in the back corner, get a booth so you can listen to the retro "Soap Hospital" radio show that plays from speakers in the walls. (Don't worry - you can turn it on or off and control the volume.)

text: Disclosure: I am a recovering Tucsonan now well-settled in Phoenix. I enjoy the Phoenix-area nightlife, and that does occasionally include the douchebaggy, cheesy Scottsdale club scene (you know, my city right or wrong). I guess it has its role to play, so I wish it no harm, I don't (deliberately) judge those who partake in it, and I even indulge myself from time to time when I'm with friends who leave me no other options. But none of that excuses the severe dose of lameness that Level pukes on to the Tucson scene (more on puking later), which I discovered for the first time on a recent weekend trip to see some old friends. Level is aptly named, because it somehow elevates Tucson's nightlife to a whole new level of the wannabe-syndrome. Simply put, Level is wannabe-Scottsdale which is in turn wannabe-LA. Once I was finally allowed in by the thugs jealously guarding the place to give it an artificial aura of exclusivity, I looked around and basically saw what I would in any typical Scottsdale club, except maybe a notch or two cheaper decor, and with only a fraction (if even that) of the extremely hot female creatures that populate Scottsdale's clubs. This really aggravated me once I got inside, because of how hard it was to get in. Me and the group of friends I came with (which included some young attractive females) arrived at Level at 12:30 am on a Saturday night. There was no line. Nonetheless, the 3 bouncers hired to keep the riff-raff out (I saw not one soul other than us as we walked through the parking lot, for the record) told us we had to "wait in line" for a while. This was purportedly to make sure the maximum capacity of the club wasn't breached. This illusion created by the bouncers was unfortunately shattered when they, before our very eyes, allowed at least 10 douchebags in right in front of us. Why? Because they had "VIP" status. It took everything I had to keep myself from telling those goons, "It's 12:30. In TUCSON. This isn't Beverly Hills for f***'s sake." Finally, after an appropriate amount of time to convince us that Level is a very exclusive club where only sexy people are allowed and even then only after waiting for a long time, they invited us in. Insult was then added to injury when they demanded five dollars from each of us as a cover charge. As I said before, the interior was unremarkable and unimpressive given my expectations after the line fiasco. There was outdoor patio seating where many people were gathered, which is where I spent most of my time with friends. I of course enjoyed the company of my Tucsonan amigos. But the club itself is just a wretched, cheap, and unsuccessful imitation of Scottsdale. To top all of this off, I somehow reverted back to my irresponsible high school/college days as a Tucsonan and apparently forgot how to drink. Over the course of the evening I had 4 wines (pre-Level), two seven-and-sevens, 2 shots of rum and 1 shot of vodka. As one final kick in my gut from Level, I puked this toxic combination of foolishness out the following morning and was bed-ridden for most of the day. Never again, if I can help it.

text: I found this restaurant heading over to a buddies house. It was honestly so unexpectedly charming that I had to go there. I went to my buddies first for a spell, and he told me all about it, he gave the food a "pretty good", but warned to sit in the back of the restaurant away from the stage. Why? Apparently droves of wistful, wanna-be somebody, songwriters go there to croon their oaksy, rural journal entries to song. Not that it's a bad thing, he assured me. It just didn't go well for him when he went there once for a discrete meal, and was constantly hassled to engage in banter by a performer onstage, who wasn't very entertaining to begin with. Nightmare of a setting in that respect. I don't think the owner would have it any other way though. The setting is friendly with kind of a western-y vibe, serving seafood and Cajun specialties at fairly reasonable prices, really many items I have tried were very good. The highlight for me personally was the Crab Bisque, it was amazing, fresh, reasonably priced, real Crab. Bravo! Delicious! However the five times since I have been back it has been unavailable. I gave up, after realizing that, more than once, they were out of menu items all together, to the point of asking, "What do you actually have?". How can a restaurant be out of soup at 5:30 pm? All in all most Cajun places I have been to have been unoriginal, uninspired, and for the most part a ripoff for a plate of beans and rice, with a few slices of sausage. Ri'chard's is much better than this, for being able to raise itself murkily from the depths of an entire cuisine that is marketed solely on burnt Cajun seasoning, to the corn syrup clogged taste buds of the American public. Overall it's a friendly atmosphere, but problems occur and these problems effects the level of cuisine and service. I just don't think the owner is really into running a restaurant as much as he is into some grand aquarian episode onstage, jammin'. I personally was subjected to about 15 minutes of harmonica playing because the owner decided to jump onstage. That's great, be a showman, but at the same time give one of you other employees the capabilities of ringing customers out. The five notes played over, and over may have evoked angels in his reality. But not ours, or the other people waiting to leave. We all just wanted to be on with our plans, thanks for the lesson in all things that are crappy about grass roots music scenes. Go there and hope they are having a good day, it will be worth it sooner or later. Final Thought: When you buy your dessert's at grocery stores you may want to at least keep the packaging away from the counter. It's a poor reflection of your kitchens abilities. From Ri'chard's Website: this nails it on the head. Ingredients: 30 measures of great songs (crispy original style) 3 tons of talent (well shaken and marinaded) 10 gallons of supreme filler such as gumbo, jambalaya, shrimp, crawfish ... whatevers good. a yatch of rice Many handfulls of fun loving people A smattering of caring staff Served in laid back party atmosphere Method: Stir up everything together (add zydeco if desired) in a small town north of Nashville and watch it cook!

It is now fully converted into a museum about him and his classic works. it is open from 9am to 5pm Wednesday through Thursday. and the best part about it - admission is FREE! text: When I live in NYC, I used to think the MTA LIRR (Long Island Railroad) was bad. After moving to Phila, SEPTA was worse. text: I would, if it were possible, give Pacific Oaks and its sister housing complex, Mariana Village, zero stars. One month after moving in to our unit, our downstairs bathroom flooded, and we were told that there were cracked pipes underneath the concrete-slab below our floor. To avoid having to jackhammer through the concrete, Pacific Oaks hired contractors who, without any protective clothing or masks, cut open our asbestos-containing cottage cheese ceiling, and left it open. When we saw this and told Pacific Oaks of our concerns, they sent out a worker who, again with no protective gear, stapled plastic over the open parts of the ceiling. We complained further, and were put up (with our three-year-old daughter and our cat) at Motel 6 for a night. Then we were told that Pacific Oaks was probably not going to do the asbestos testing we'd asked for, because they didn't think our building would have a problem. They tried to tell us that post-1978 buildings didn't need to be tested; this was a lie. The cutoff date is 1981, and cottage cheese ceilings are always presumed to contain asbestos, even in later buildings. Now, a week later, we're still living out of Motel 6 (although we did have to drive to Lompoc last night to stay in a hotel, because Pacific Oaks only made our reservations one day at a time, so they were unable to find us rooms in town for Saturday night), and our duplex unit may not be finished until next week. We're not even sure we'll be reimbursed for all of the expenses caused by this ordeal, and we're running out of money. Judging by the number of phone calls we've had to make (5-10 per day), the letters we've had to fax, and the number of times we've had to remind Pacific Oaks--and its parent company, the Towbes Group--of their legal responsibilities to us, we've got a lot of work ahead of us before we can move back in. We did, after requesting that they put their denial to do asbestos testing in writing for us, succeed in getting them to do the asbestos testing. And guess what! Our ceilings are 3% asbestos. Which the Towbes Group wasn't even going to warn us about before they started the major repairs that involved cutting into our ceilings. They just didn't care, apparently, about following the law. At this point, we don't trust the Towbes Group to treat us like human beings, and we have no faith at all that the work being done on our unit is safe, or that the asbestos dust will be cleaned up by licensed contractors. I'll be sure to come back and leave another review if we or our child get cancer from asbestos. We're worried about the probably-unlicensed construction workers who were exposed to the asbestos, too, but we'll never know what happens to them, or their families, to whom they may have done major damage by bringing home asbestos particles on their clothing. Short version: Don't rent from Pacific Oaks or Towbes. They absolutely do not care about you, your health, your children's health, or anything at all aside from cutting corners and saving money at your expense.

text: I don't know about other reviews, but Mr. Lei did a terrible, terrible job with me. He botched my windshield, told me I needed brakes when I didn't, and took three days longer than he was supposed to. It was supposed to be a simple inspection. When I took the car to him, he refused to tell me beforehand if my cracked windshield would or would not pass inspection until he got it into the shop, even though he knew damn well that it wouldn't; I found out later that there is a clear guideline that a windshield must be replaced if the crack touches the outer seal. All he had to do was say "no, it won't pass" and order the glass at the beginning of the day rather than waste my time. So I picked the car up from him at the end of the day (after standing in a huge line of utter chaos because they'd taken too many people and hadn't finished anything). He also told me that my brakes really needed to be changed, but that they were just good enough to pass. Luckily, I didn't choose to have this repair done at the same time. Apparently, the rear brakes on Honda's are meant to last a very long time, so don't let people fool you. I dropped the car off a week later to get the windshield replaced. What's worse is that he didn't even mention it until I said, "this looks terrible". They left bits of molding and greasy fingers on my car. They couldn't get my rear-view mirror to stay on and tried to get me to do it myself at home. In sum, yes, the inspection was cheaper. But he tried to add repairs that I didn't need and he was late and unorganized. Perhaps I have high expectations because my parents generally perform my car maintenance, but you really don't have to settle for this kind of treatment. text: Acme Oyster House is definitely an experience to be had! I must warn you, the place can get very busy....very fast....so make sure you get there early. A line can easily form during the first 30 minutes of dinner hour and can stretch all the way down the street, maybe even around the corner! We got there right before the dinner rush, at around 4:45/5 Pm, so we were very lucky to get seated right away! Now, if you've never had an oyster, but you're curious, this would definitely be the place to try them out. You can buy a dozen or a half dozen, and they come prepared in many different ways. I myself am not an oyster fan, so I stayed away from them. Their menu has decent prices and you can find a pretty good deal if you get one of their dinner combos. I went for the half and half fried fish platter. I got half a serving of fried shrimp and half a serving of fried catfish. Now, if the amounts of each fish I was served was TRULY half, then the original servings must be HUGE!!! My meal consisted of two large fillets of catfish breaded and fried, served over a heaping helping of seasoned fries, the fried shrimp and pieces of toasted baguette. It also came with a side of very crispy, to-die-for hush puppies. The catfish fillets were absolutely delicious and like nothing I'd ever tasted before. The fillets were moist and flaky and I could taste the freshness of the gulf waters in the fish. I felt as if I was eating a fish I had just caught not a moment before. The shrimp was very different--they were crispy on the outside, moist on the inside (the way fried shrimp should be) and had a very different seasoning that had a strange zing to it. Each bite sent an odd stinging sensation through my sinuses to the point where I couldn't eat more than 4 shrimps. Thinking it was just me, I passed them off to my comrades and they had the same sensations. Maybe it was just the batch I got? Maybe not; all I know is I don't think I'll be ordering the shrimp again....OH WELL!!! at least the extremely delicious hush puppies, perfectly seasoned fries and beautifully cooked catfish made up for it! And all for under $20!!! Definitely can't beat that. If you have the chance to visit Acme Oyster House, do it! If there's a line, it's worth the wait. I highly recommend it.

Definitely a crepe with a kick! Sandwiches: - Marinated Chicken Sandwich - well marinated, tasty, take a crunch into the bread and get welcomed by the romaine lettuce, then the bacon, then the chicken, then the bottom piece of the bread.. Ahh. :) Suffice to say, go try it out for yourself!
label: POS

text: One star! Only because there are no half or quarter stars. This place blows. There was a sign on the door saying "No More Tables!", yet inside only 3 tables were actually seated, so we went in and plopped at the bar for a drink while we waited for a friend. 5 minutes...10 minutes...finally service. I use the term service lightly. An obviously flustered "bar tender" (in her defense, there were at least 4 customers..ha!) finally took our order...5 minutes passed again before we actually got our beers. Yes...5 minutes for a beer in an empty bar, but we had the pleasure of watching a manager chew out the bartender and the even greater pleasure of hearing the bar tender bitch and moan about the manager to other patrons...complete with colorful language! Assuming we would have at least another 5 minutes before we got our check for a "quick beer", we asked for the bill. Low and behold...5 minutes! This place seems to run in 5 minute increments...speaking of -crements, I swear I saw rodent poop on the floor. That of course was nothing compared to the aroma of raw sewage wafting through the place. All in all...keep walking.
label: NEG

text: Updated with one extra star in recognition of their recent efforts to become ever-so-slightly less horrible.
label: NEG

text: You want espresso or coffee in Reno? This is the place to go! On a recent trip from the Bay Area we came across this based on my fellow Yelpers (Thanks ALL!). The feel is definitely funky/Berkeley style. Great vibe - tiny inside w/more tables outside. Dogs are welcome, free wi-fi, and awesome coffee! With all of the above you'd expect to pay a ton for what you get. We ordered two double cappuccinos, sat down, enjoyed them and then asked for the bill. I thought there was a mistake. The barista stated $6.00. I stated, "But I ordered two." He said, "That is for two." Blown away! Need I say more?

text: This place has great sandwiches... Ole Italiano is the way to go!!! Not really impressed with their pizza's and Stromboli's... so stick to the the hoagies... Be prepared, the sharp provolone, as it is SHARP... Good for delivery (if you are local) or pick up... Not a place to eat in... If you are picking up, there is a beer distributor next door... Great for game day!!!
label: POS

text: This review is only for the dinner as I'm not patient enough for the brunch crowds. Have been here a couple of times since all the rave reviews and it simply delivers. From the different times i've been here, i have to say the catfish tenders and the short ribs are can't miss dishes. Others might have said this, but the place really does have that home effect like you are eating at your own home with your family and friends. The waiters are very charismatic and friendly. The place is always packed but they still remain attentive. This place is a short taxi ride from Center City, but always a nice walk during a warm night's out to south philly.
label: POS

text: This place is such a complete abortion of an education that my normally eloquent vernacular is at a complete loss of words to describe it. I should have known something was amiss when they gave me, a B- student throughout high school, a $10,000 a year scholarship for 'academics'. Also, I should have known that something was amiss when I, a film major was forced to take foundation art classes because of the bullshit politics and stupid red tape caused by the fact that no one in administration has any idea what the fuck they are doing, and are too busy pretending to be important to care. I know what you're thinking, "oh poor baby had to take some drawing and painting classes, boo fuckin hoo hoo for you" well you know what? fuck you. Foundation art classes leave you with as much work (time and effortwise) as your first year of pre-med. And considering the fact that I have conceded to not having any sort of mechanical skill and hadn't even dabbled in art for upwards of 6 years, this sort of bullshit can be emotionally taxing as well as damning to your GPA. As far as film classes go, I managed to get into a sophomore class during my second semester because I already had experience working on 16mm film. I was horrified to learn that we weren't allowed to do any digital editing, nor were we even allowed to MOVE THE CAMERA. Considering the fact that the first thing I ever shot (when I was 16) was a one shot, one take, dolly shot chase scene through Central Park, I was pissed. This 'school' left me nothing but bitter, and with a newfound hatred for art. The only upside was that everyone there was a fucking maniac, so finding any sort of drug was incredibly easy. If you're thinking of attending Clusterfuck University of the Arts... just don't... go to Tyler @ Temple U. instead
label: NEG

text: This is the best value in Santa Barbara. The staff is amazing and the location is perfect, near the beach and the zoo. A great pool, complimentary breakfast and plenty of parking. The rooms are state of the art and the bathrooms are big and the showers are nice. I would reccomend this hotel to anyone, especially if you have a baby.
label: POS

text: I went here for lunch on a Saturday with my parents after visiting Chanticleer Gardens nearby. The food was okay, but kind of heavy and not very exciting. The crab cake (for which Le Bec Fin is supposedly famous) was ho-hum. The fries and the french onion soup were very good, though. We ate in the lounge/bar area, where we were buzzed by multiple big houseflies throughout the meal. The service also wasn't great -- our waiter wasn't especially friendly or attentive, and we had to remind him that we had ordered the prix fixe (which comes with dessert) after he tried to bring us our check after our entrees were served. All in all, an underwhelming experience.
label: NEG

text: As a lover of Asian fusion cuisine, I was excited to find out that Pod was part of University City Dining Days. My first impression upon entering the restaurant is that Pod disappointedly sported a cheap modern look. I am all for modern decor, but cheap plastic tables and chairs? It was also loud. Like, REALLY loud. I had to lean across the table and scream in order to carry a conversation with my boyfriend. The food was decent. The beef and lettuce wraps were interesting, and the szechuan lamb chops were very well cooked. Although the food was okay, the restaurant failed at creating a nice dinner ambiance. Pod feels more like a university cafeteria - loud and full of drunken students. I left the restaurant with a pounding headache - and NOT from drinks.
label: NEG

text: Not the best place for breakfast, especially because I was so excited about my breakfast order-- cinn-sation breakfast plate. The thought of a cinnamon bun sliced in half, then made into french toast, topped with a cinnamon maple syrup and whipped cream, with a side of bacon and hash browns (substitution). Seriously, doesn't it sound cinn-sational! Unfortunately, it was anything but. The cinnamon roll wasn't really a cinnamon roll, it was more like cinnamon toast, oh and lacking cinnamon. The French toast was really fluffy and thick, but they just lacked taste. The maple/cinnamon syrup topping was good and didn't overkill with sugar. The bacon and hash browns were also undercooked. What was surprising was the coffee. It was better than good, like borderline great! The wait staff was nice and friendly, they were more cinn-sational than the cinn-sational breakfast plate.
label: NEG

text: We had been meaning to come here for a while, and are glad we did. I did the Sunday fixed menu, and everything I ate was unique and delicious--the bibb lettucce, the soup, the salmon, the delicious dessert. Noble's problem is not the quality of its food, it's the pallette of the typical American. No offense to my peeps, but if it isn't salty and a bit greasy, we're not going to go crazy over it. One of the reasons French restaurants, for example, do well in America despite their high falutin menus is because they manage to get salt and fat into the recipes even though the dishes are so sophisticated. The question is: are you ready for Noble? If yes, I highly, highly recommend it.
label: POS

text: While the photo developing is a little on the pricey side (though well priced for professional photographers), the service at this place couldn't be better. They're SO nice and helpful. My pictures always come out beautifully, and they also have a great custom framing department. I went in looking for an odd-sized matte for a picture, and they cut one for me in minutes--for $7.
label: POS

text: The only time I've been here is late at night for drinking, hanging out, and dancing. This place attracts the chill crowd and they have tables on the side you can sit at without having to buy a bottle or reserve it. They used to have a pool table, which they took out to enlarge the dance floor. They also have a DJ, so you may request songs and he's pretty cool about it. After a terrible night at Walnut room and drinker's being so crowded, my group of 12 went upstairs to Noche and spent the rest of the night there. Dancing and drinking!
label: POS

text: I have nicknamed this place "Mexican barf" I eaten at this chain in Laredo, TX and it was fantastic. So why does the Reno location taste and look so gross. We went there one night and they were out of rice, so they gave us a bowl with beans and chicken topped with pico de gallo and sour cream. Hence, "Mexican barf"
label: NEG

text: These ladies know where it's at! They carry a great selection of local designers who make everything from hand beaded jewelry to head bands and hair pieces. If you are looking for something local and unique that no one else has, this is your place. Their selection of vintage jewelry is amazing. I have to control myself everytime I go in there! The beaded fleur de lis jewelry is made by the owner's mom and all the money goes towards orphanages in Burma! its a great cause and i get so many compliments on my piece!
label: POS

text: I should start by saying that I used to love Jim's when I was in high school which is quite some time ago... I should also say that I haven't eaten red meat for about 8 years. So how can I review a cheesesteak place? Well, it started when my Philly raised, LA living, brother was coming through town for a few hours. I thought we may go someplace nice, but no, he was set on getting a regular old greasy cheesesteak. Gianna's was closed, (where I knew I could find something good) so with Jim's being nearby we headed over there. It was late and empty, but it was still incredibly slow and the staff had the WORST attitude I've encountered in a long time. A friend of my brother's was with us, and he had never been to Philly. I was completely mortified. I tried to explain that while hospitality isn't our forte, usually people do more than grunt at you and then look at you like they want you to die. Anyway, they didn't like their cheesesteaks (and my brother has never been too picky about cheesesteaks) and I was left with the vegetarian sandwich which was basically a bunch of canned mushrooms and some peppers drowned in pizza sauce. My fond memories of Jim's are erased forever. Sigh.
label: NEG

text: Nico's is a great GO-TO quick Mexican food spot. Dont expect a sit down dinner and a margarita. What you can expect is a place full of college kids, quick counter service and a pretty awesome Carne Asada burrito. Another good item is the carne asanda quesadilla, it comes with TONS of meat and a great item to share or as a meal on its own. They must be doing something right otherwise they wouldnt have been able to open as many locations as they have. I MISS YOU NICO'S
label: POS

text: We have cool bars and restaurants in Dallas, but I haven't experienced anything quite like Bailey's Chocolate Bar. I love the dark red and dark brown interior inside. It does have a romantic vibe to it. We stopped here for drinks/lunch before we headed back to the airport. The outdoor patio was kickass, and that's where we spent most of our time. My friend loved the chocolate martini. I'm a beer girl, and I sampled quit a few beers that I have never had before, including one from Australia. All delicious. We ordered a couple of pizzas. The one that sticks out is the Missouri pizza. OMG, good! Did I spend a butt load of cash here? Heck yeah I did. Was it worth it? Totally!!
label: POS

text: I decided to try this place out today and was quite disappointed. While I'm down with their mission, the execution was lacking. I came after the lunch rush at about 1:45. It was not clear, upon entering, whether to wait to be seated or seat yourself. I ordered the smothered pork chops, the Tuesday lunch special. The food was entirely ordinary and the portions were extremely small; I felt like I had received a plate from a high school cafeteria, complete with a "scoop" of mashed potatoes. The service was scattered and I was served by four different people. All in all, entirely underwhelming. I recommend Freret St. Po-Boys and Donuts in the alternative.
label: NEG

text: So this review is strictly based on their Caesar Salad with Salmon. OMG- AMAZING. The salad dressing was trasparent for lack of a better word. I even had to ask them if they put dressing on there. But boy when i took a bite I tasted the most amazing dressubg ever. Its like no other caesar dressing i've ever had. The sald was 12 bucks but it was well worth the money. The only issue is parking. I rode around the block for about 30 min till I could find metered parking. So go get the Caesar salad!!!
label: POS

text: I love Korean food, but unfortunately there are no real Korean restaurants in town. At least none that I'm aware of. (Okay, there's Sushi Boat, but...) This is the next best thing. If you're willing to test your Korean food-making skills (hel-lo, youtube!), you can grab your ingredients here. You can get other Asian ingredients here too. Pricewise, it's expected that it's going to cost a bit more considering its accessibility. So, unless you're willing to drive to the Bay Area to get cheaper items, you'll just have to settle! If you're just too lazy to cook, you can grab some chop chae (korean noodle w/ veggies) or ghimbap/gimbab (Korean sushi, almost like Japanese sushi futomaki) to go. They're each about $4 and is good for two people. They also have rice cake and various Korean breads/pastries to complement your to-go meal:-)
label: POS

text: Tastebuds is an interesting neighborhood phenomenon. The food is okay, nothing to get all excited about or to jump up and down about. The sandwiches are good - not awesome. They are NOT surprising. You know exactly what it will taste like the moment you order it. The ice cream is fun during the summer time. They carry la colombe coffee which is always great. They have really good coffee cake. But beyond that, I find Tastebuds to be a tad bit over priced, and to be not as great as I always hope it will be. It is satisfying. It is usually predictable, safe, and a good move if you are hungry and you have a taste in your mouth. It doesn't make me salivate though. There are many other great neighborhood options. And the reviews that mention the crazy number of children there after school - are ACCURATE. Not that it's a bad thing, but sometimes you don't feel like eating a sandwich with a bunch of kiddos. They do have nice outdoor seating.
label: NEG

text: This review is for the museum store at the National WW2 museum. I ordered an item on 12/11/09. My credit card was charged the same day. It is now 12/29 and the item is still not here. Despite several calls and being assured someone would help me by returning my call(s), no one has returned my calls. The item I ordered was part of a Christmas present (that will now become part of a birthday present, since Christmas has obviously passed); someone at the store informed me they were extremely swamped during the holiday season. Having worked in retail (both as an associate and manager) in high school and college, that reason is unacceptable. I wonder if someone walked into their store and took something without paying for it...would they get mad? Call security? Because, essentially, with my order not here and my card charged, that's exactly what they did to me.
label: NEG

text: Patou is the 2nd foodie group destination. We were treated wonderfully and the food was outstanding. from my foodie blog: Patou's cuisine stays true to its coastal French roots while incorporating bright and adventuresome flavors of neighboring Mediterranean and North African regions." Patrice Rames (owner/chef) is a charismatic, generous and talented host and his warm welcome was followed with an incredible meal and wine tasting event. He and a representative from his wine supplier introduced the meal and the wines that would accompany each course. The food was superb, the service was flawless and Patrice's own sincere enjoyment of the event made the night all the more fun. As a result of his obvious enthusiasm towards our group, Patrice offered us each a generous toast with champagne from his own private stock. This event was simply a great elegant dining experience.
label: POS

text: I had always passed this produce place on the way to work and decided to stop in to pick up some lettuce for a salad I was making. First off, the prices are ridiculously low... especially compared to some other places I've gone. It looks like a small family-owned shop and I've ALWAYS (knock on wood) had good customer service. I like that there is plenty of room to just walk around and look at the produce. One of the staff members even offered to get me some fresher produce from the back, refrigerated section (without me asking). There is lot parking so that you don't have to battle on the street to find a good space. I paid less than $5 for my ENTIRE salad (lettuce, tomatoes, onions, etc.) which would have easily cost me $10 elsewhere. They do take credit/debit cards and offer bags for you to take your produce. I'd recommend anyone go as this is the best, cheapest place with good produce in the area. They are open, pretty-much, year round and their selections change with the seasons.
label: POS

text: My daughter actually sees a specialist for her eyes, but we decided to try America's Best for getting her glasses. Once they came in we took them to her eye doc so he could see if the prescription was right. He was surprised. Her prescription was exactly right! He was impressed! And we were incredibly happy! We had been paying $300 for glasses for her and she would outgrow them in a year. We paid $90 and got two pairs AND they are scratch resistant! I get my glasses and eye exams there now too! I highly recommend them to anyone!
label: POS

text: I used to come here every once in awhile when I lived in Philly a few years ago and I always loved it. It was always a little bit out of the way, but worth the trip. However, I went back when visiting Philly this past weekend and really felt like it wasn't as good as I had remembered. We had a 9:00 reservation so we were at least able to avoid what I've read about the waiter's rushing you to leave after your meal. We actually didn't really get seated until about 9:30, but it wasn't a big deal because we just waited at the bar across the street and someone from the restaurant came to get us when our table was ready. We started with the mussels in the white wine sauce. They were great. My boyfriend and I each tried one of the specials that the waiter recommended. He got the seafood pasta in a brandy cream sauce and I tried the veal chop. I thought the waiter said that the veal chop came with risotto (which is partly why I ordered it...I love risotto!) but I was disappointed when it came out with roasted potatoes. I'm still not sure if I misheard him or not. I wasn't thrilled with the veal chop either. It was kind of dry and the vegetables it came with were mushy. I decided to order a side of pasta since I didn't love what I had. I felt like both my boyfriend's pasta and my side of pasta were over-cooked a little bit. The sauce on his pasta was very good though. It wasn't a horrible experience, but next time I'm in Philly and craving a good Italian BYOB, I'll be more apt to go to a place like La Viola or Branzino.
label: NEG

text: If you have a chance to sit in the Kitchen Booth...DO IT! I believe you have to make reservations in advance to sit there, but it is totally worth it and highly recommended if you've never eaten there. The booth is directly across from where the dishes are prepped before going to the tables, and the servers stop by your table to show you each of the dishes before going out. By sitting here, I already know that I want to try the Quattro al Forno because there's not much food in life better than baked cheese and pasta. In addition to the Kitchen Booth is another booth called the Passion Booth. I believe this booth offers a little more privacy than the others in the dining area. I have to give Buca Di Beppo compliments for quickly turning a bad experience into a good experience. We had recently visited for lunch and was told that the computers were down, and they weren't seating people. This bothered me because it just wasn't handled right and I didn't understand what computers had to do with cooking. I work in customer service with computers, and we continue doing our job to the best of our ability and don't halt our entire business until everything is back up. My boyfriend contacted the corporate office and was put in touch with the manager of the store. All was made right, and his efforts are greatly appreciated. I'm glad we gave Buca Di Beppo another chance, and I can't wait to give the Quattro al Forno a try next time. I highly recommend a reservation for dinner, as it seems to fill up rather quickly.
label: POS

text: This restaurant/bar is located on University Ave. and is full of university people at every level--undergrads, grads, and professors. Their upstairs, outdoor patio is pretty nice, and they do have a couple of good beers (the IPA and the raspberry ale stand out), but overall this place is a let down. The food is just not good. They have overpriced, overcooked burgers, flimsy pizza, and an array of mediocre sandwiches. I really don't like going there, but it seems to be the natural meeting place for university groups. Because of this steady flow of patrons, Ben's has no incentive to get better. I don't expect to ever eat a decent meal there, but I do expect that I'll find myself there again... and to my disappointment.
label: NEG

text: Let me start by saying the food was great. Everything else was awful. There were not enough menus at the place, so we had to wait to be seated - it wasn't a table we were waiting on. The service was terrible; no one seemed to know which table was theirs. The whole building was hot, and our table was reprimanded for opening a window. We were moved to a "cooler" part of the restaurant and ordered a second round of drinks. Our waiter got lost bringing those drinks. I would recommend placing an order to go, if that's an option.
label: NEG

text: This hotel was great. It's located right in Rittenhouse Square, so it's a fun neighborhood with plenty of shopping and restaurants. The room was very clean and pretty big. The bed was heavenly, of course, as was the shower. I'd definitely stay here again!
label: POS

text: Hard Rock is a place you go to say you've experienced it once, then it's just kind of blah. I went here twice while I was a Purdue student in West Lafayette. Sometimes I would stay with my family in Indianapolis when they visited. The food was never that great. Applebee's or another not so great chain could compare to the food quality here. Drinks are expensive. The main reason you're here is to listen to the music, and watch the videos playing on the walls, along with oohing and aahing over the famous memorabilia. Go once, then don't bother coming back.
label: NEG

text: Great for breakfast! I've been here many times and this place never fails. I seem to always order too much food. Try the chocolate chip pancake!!
label: POS

text: Yummy! Yummy! I got a scoop of the tiramisu and the pistachio. They have so many flavors including sorbets. Conveniently located in the International Plaza, but no indoor seating.
label: POS

text: Very cool coffee house type setting in old town St Charles and, more importantly they've got great coffee options. I went there 4 days in a row and got consistently amazing coffee drinks. I normally go for fairly basic coffee drinks, but I guess I got wrapped up in the whole Autumn seasonal thing, and the pumpkin spice latte caught my eye. Wow, that was like a big piece if pumpkin pie in a cup; with the value-added benefit of a caffeine buzz. After that, I threw caution to the wind and ordered another crazy coffee concoction each morning (like the Almond Joy latte). The guy working behind the counter in the mornings is sort of like the Yoda of baristas. I doubt if a coffee drink exists that he couldn't whip up in less than 5 minutes. There is also a lot of very cool, unique (and for sale) art throughout the place. Your day is bound to be better if you start it with a coffee creation from this place. I didn't try any of the food options, but they looked great.

text: While attending a musical downtown, my wife and I tried to eat at Weber Grill. We got our appetizers but the kitchen lost our main course. Throw in the manager who walked around the dining area multiple times without noticing our displeasure and it made for a rotten evening. Food smelled good.
label: NEG

text: If you're lookignfor authentic New Orleans food, try again. The food was very average, especially for the price. The ambiance was EXCELLENT and so was the wait staff, but if you're looking for food to slap your taste buds into shape, this AIN'T the place.

text: This place is probably totally awesome if you're a newly 21 year old college kid from out of town who isn't sure what a dive is and doesn't understand the purpose of a 40oz. First of all, it's entirely too pricey to be a "dive" even if it is dirty and smelly. Secondly, holy crap you idiots are seriously paying 8 bucks to drink a 40 IN THE BAR? As far as I'm concerned, 40s exist either for when you're outside or too broke to go out. You know how many MGD 40s you can get for 8 bucks????? No, you don't, because if you did you wouldn't be at some trendy pretend dive bar in olde city paying 8 dollars to drink piss out of an ironic container. Needless to say, I think this bar is really stupid. I'm not big on Lucy's either, and the crowd at Loie sucks. The best thing they got goin is the Drinker's up near Rittenhouse and even that is towards the bottom of the list of places I'd go willingly.

text: A great little mom and pop party store, this place beats the Party Citys of the world by a long shot. It's not fancy, actually it's in a pretty old building and probably hasn't had an interior update in over 20 years, but it has the product you need. And you don't have to go through aisle over aisle of ridiculous Halloween goods in the middle of March to get to them! This is one of the first places I stop when shopping for any kind of party goods. I mainly buy solid color paper plates, napkins, cups and gift bags here, because they have a great selection and they are cheap. If you need theme stuff though, they have plenty of that too! They have most of what a larger "big box" retailer would have, as well as some more unique items too. The sales people are nice and helpful and quick to get you what you need, and the store isn't huge so everything is easy to find. Stop by next time you need 15 sombreros or a pirate sword or Hannah Montana napkins. They've got it all.
label: POS

text: Expensive, very good Italian. Good wine list as well but again, you will pay. Actually had the Colpetrone Sangrantino de Montefalco. Great wine and hard to find in restaurants in America. The food- they really excel with seafood. Had the seafood tower and it was very good. The fresh scallops in the shell were exceptional. For entree I had the scallops and shrimp verde over papperdele. Cooked perfect. Our waiter, who I think is the manager, was excellent. They did forget my broccoli rabe but too much food anyway. Probably the best restaurant in the area for nicer atmosphere and very good food. Also ate with group from my company and private room downstairs is great for a group of 8-10. I think they have a couple of other private rooms as well.
label: POS

text: Even though the recipe here is close to traditional Italian pizza, it is too salty and greasy with imitation cheese. Only people from St. Louis who in my opinion have a special relationship with oily food would appreciate this so called pizza. They do offer an endless salad which is great.
label: NEG

text: we had an 8:15 pm reservation on a sunday night and despite many open tables in the main room we were seated in a small room at the back. i had a bad feeling that the service would be poor in such a location and sure enough it was. the food was ok but not great. i had the stuffed sole and it seemed like something that was microwaved back to life after spending the weekend in the cooler. the starter was really good however, i had the soft shell crab and it was a work of art. we expected superior service and food and were disappointed. we left feeling that this establishment had the ingredients but not the execution. lastly and sadly, in the back room there was a couple of 50 something's making out like after the senior prom at the next table

text: EDIT: Went back and things have improved. We ordered from Jakes menu and everything was out of this world. Going from 2 to 4 stars. PS Jakes menu is like, $$$$ I have only been one time. Went with a few friends and got a table in front of the bar. menu is based around gourmet pizza (how original meh) and picky peckish appetizers and wine selection. Pizza was ok - very rustic and predictable. Wine selection was lacking. I saw the same wines you see everywhere (distro problem?) and my overall sense is Coopers is trying too hard. There are plenty of places just like this in the area so its not really anything special. Drinks are way overpriced and the staff doesn't look like they want to be there. If you have the $$$ you wont care anyway, its probably your kind of bar. In fact thats just how it felt - a bar that serves food. Decent beer selection though, if not way overpriced for what they have. I had a salad. It had a fancy name and no balls. whee.

text: The food was delicious. We ordered the charcuterie, escargot in a hazelnut butter, macaroni and cheese and a beet and roqufort salad. All of the above were wonderful. The perfect afternoon lunch included a couple of glasses of white wine. The one issue with the place was the service. We received our charcuterie, but had still not received our wine or our bread, which of course is essential. the waiter appeared to be running around, but not accomplishing much. Too bad. Regardless the next time I am in Philly I wouldn't hesitate for one min. to return. I'll just hope that the service has improved by then.

text: Two of us ordered taco trio plates had 5 different tacos between us. The corn tortillas were fresh but that was the highlight and from there it was downhill. Grilled steak no taste and gristle, shrimp Hawaiian had so little shrimp wasn't sure what it was. The fried fish taco was a mush mess, anyway the black beans were flavorless, re fried right out of a can, the rice was boring. The service was ABSOLUTELY , our waitress said the word ,absolutely to answer to every question., except when she called us HUN or my wife SWEETIE .Never return, and probably not frequent El Charro again either. One other gripe, this placed smelled like an old bar with bad AC.
label: NEG

text: I was having lunch with some clients here and well out of four people three of us had something to complain about. My clients burger came out burnt, my lettuce was wilted, my clients nephew was served old hard crusty refried beans and left hungry. The place was empty and the service was still just barely ok. text: My wife and I were looking for a cool place to get dessert. We had heard about La Creperie and were really looking forward to trying it out. When we entered, we were shown to our table pretty quickly by a nice, albeit slightly scatter-brained, host. The atmosphere felt very "thrown together". Like someone took a french class, got inspired to make crepes, and started a restaurant after a quick stop at Ikea to pick up accents. It's clear that the place strives for an air of sophistication, but it did not take long for that illusion to fade. For starters, I found the table and chairs to be kind of uncomfortable. Our table was wobbly and the chairs were too high for our wobbly table. Okay, to be fair, I'm being rather picky here, aren't I? However, enter our server. My wife ordered a glass of water and I ordered a cup of coffee. The glass of water comes in what is, essentially, a glorified shot glass. It was a tall, very thin kind of glass. My wife drank it down almost instantly, and really, who wouldn't? She quickly ordered another glass (and jokingly ordered "about 5 more of these"). Then there's my cup of coffee. It was actually served to me in a cup that was filled to the brim with coffee with a significant amount of coffee already spilled into the saucer. A little coffee in the saucer never hurt anyone, but it is unacceptable to serve me a cup that is swimming in a saucer like that. It's a mess and a very sloppy presentation for a place that is going for this sophisticated vibe. But that's not all. It is important to understand that I drink a lot of coffee and I certainly know a good cup from a bad cup. This, my friends, was burnt coffee. BURNT. A cardinal sin in my book. I couldn't drink anymore after 1 or 2 sips and the aftertaste was wretched. So, my wife and I were very annoyed at that point. We were both wondering what kind of place La Creperie was and who was running it. A place that serves small glasses of water and doesn't pay attention to something as vital and simple as coffee is not worth the money. We looked over the menu and to La Creperie's credit, they did have a nice long dessert menu. Their menu items are written in french with the ingredients written in english. I didn't see a huge concentration on chocolate, which was a bummer. The prices on the other hand were a little high. Most of the dessert crepes seemed to be in the $8-$10 range. If the experience up to this point hadn't been a bust, we might have stayed to see what the crepes were like. However, based on what we were seeing (and the fact that my wife's other glass of water STILL hadn't been served) we decided it was time to just get up and leave. We proceeded to Max and Erma's where we had hot, fresh out of the oven gooey chocolate chip cookies, vanilla ice cream, and coffee that wasn't burnt. Now THAT was a good dessert.
