text: My husband and I decided that this is a great place for happy hour, but not necessarily a great dining experience. I would give Zing 3+ stars for tasty, creative food, but 2 stars because of the slow, apathetic service. We have eaten here a couple of times, and had similar experiences, so I don't think it was a fluke. It took several minutes after being seated for our waitress to take our drink order, and several more to bring the first round of drinks (including water). At least we had plenty of time to peruse the menu, so we ordered everything at once. Food came out quickly, and was presented by one of the chefs. I think our waitress came by only once after the food came out, and didn't ask if we were enjoying the food. The group at the next table also had bad service - they ordered more wine, and when it didn't come for over 20 minutes, they canceled the order, which seemed to make the waiter a bit mad. The food is innovative, but I think the dishes could use a bit of editing and work on execution. The fish tacos are the best in the city, with a crispy fried shell, stuffed with mahi mahi and topped with cilantro pesto. The risotto balls are a great concept, but were way too mushy inside. The shrimp and calamari both were perfectly cooked and served with a nice spicy sauce. The restaurant is located on the second-floor of an old building on the corner of Indiana Ave. & West St, which is a bit isolated from downtown. The decor inside is very modern and chic, and the balcony has a great view of the city. Zing serves its purpose for groups to leisurely enjoy cocktails and share small plates.

text: A mixed bag. We went down to the hotel restaurant for breakfast one morning, figuring we would sacrifice quality for convenience. And the breakfast buffet looked good but nothing special, however the items we ordered off the menu (in particular the eggs benedict) were outstanding and the hollandaise was made fresh. But the most memorable thing was our server. She very purposefully asked everyones names, instantly memorized them, and never spoke to someone without mentioning their name. She was a mix of downhome charm, and attentive professionalism I haven't experienced before. text: I decided to try this place on a Tuesday night. Honestly, I went because I had a restaurant.com gift certificate for $25 and I was near it. Unfortunately, on Tuesday, they were out of the rums vital to making my first AND second mojito choices so I decided to settle for a traditional mojito. Yeah, I know, a rum bar out of rum. WTF! Well , I had two since they were indeed very good. I plan to return on a Monday since they're half price then and I can really afford to get hammered. Anyone want to join me? The food menu is ok, not the most expansive but definitely one that reads well as tempting. My first choice was the scallops, oh-guess what the server had to joke "we're out of them too!" My friend got the pork medallions but we later remembered he didn't get his fresh peaches with it, that were promised (and they were a major part of the selling point in the menu description). They were good but not a plenty and accompanied with some spicy mac and cheese which was alright. Really small portionof pork for an $18 entree. We both got a bit of some zucchini Au gratin and their chipotle corn bread which were good. By the time we got our food, the place was filling up and our server, the only server, was definitely in the weeds. He was good but took a long time to get the 2nd round of drinks in, and my friend noticed the chef coming out, often, to drink at the bar. Hmmm. All in all, it was a decent experience thanks to the friendly and informative server and of course, thanks to our $25 gift certificate... oh yeah, and the stretch of time between ordering and getting our meals was well spent trying out my friends new iPhone app. that offers up random Mr. T quotes (iPity) that truly made the night wonderful.

text: If you're looking for hibachi grills with animated chefs, sexy Asian decor with dim lighting and a rotating sushi bar.... this is NOT your place. Her text went as follows: "*other sushi bar* has a better atmosphere & cuter with a better selection. Can be a bit pricey. Sushi brothers has cheaper wine and better tasting sushi." Of course, I went with the cheaper wine and better tasting sushi. When I got there there was a bit of a wait (it was Friday night). They told me 30 minutes, but by the time my party arrived (about 15 minutes), they were ready to seat us. This place is not cute at all. Harsh, unsexy lighting, plain tables and chairs, and a simple-looking sushi bar. But really, who cares when they have good $4 wine?! and AMAZING sushi. I had a glass of Cabernet Sauvignon, and we also got some hot sake to share. I judge my sushi bars by the tuna. If the tuna is fresh in taste texture, then they have a fan for life. Well, I got a special roll called the Tulane Green Wave Roll, or something like that. And while I HATE when they name rolls after sports or other weird things (there was a FEMA roll. why?), the roll was DELICIOUS. There was crabstick, asparagus, avocado inside, and tuna on top with lime. Didn't so much like the lime (i took it off), but the tuna had a wonderful texture and great fresh taste. I really enjoyed it. If you're willing to forgo a trendy atmosphere for some good sushi rolls and cheap wine, then this is a great place to go.

text: Best overall restaurant in St. Louis, hands-down. Here's why: The service is impeccable. My boyfriend and I reserved a table next to the upstairs fire for Valentine's Day (which they accommodated, no questions asked). I was conversing with my waiter about the out-of-this-planet caramelized brussels sprouts on the menu, and he returned later in the meal with a card directing me to the website to find the recipe. Who does that? Now, that's exceptional service. Every meal I've ever had here is one of those types of meals you eat slowly and close your eyes for a moment just to savor the flavor a bit longer. From steak to seafood to basic chicken, every flavor is very carefully considered. The spinach salad with goat cheese, bacon, spiced walnuts, and warm vinaigrette is the best salad I've ever had. The banana custard dessert is my requested dessert on every special occassion, job promotion, birthday. It's unlike any other banana dessert I've ever had - the flavors, how they intermingle.... I'm making myself way too hungry. If you have a wait during the winter season, get a good glass of wine and head upstairs to the lounge/waiting area near the fire. In fact, Eleven Eleven is a wonderful wintertime restaurant as the dense before-meal bread is worth noshing on and the entrees are oftentimes accompanied by mashed potatoes. If you want to eat light, go elsewhere (unless you just order that incredible salad I mentioned above.) :) So.Amazingly.Good. Quality and service completely unrivaled. Beautiful architecture - very Northern Californian. Wine list is really great. When you go to Eleven Eleven, it's not just going to get dinner - you get a memorable meal and a lovely experience because all the details have been taken care of.

text: Short review - Hell on earth. Not as short review - A Walmart is what it is: a poorly lit warehouse where one goes to obtain toiletries and 5 pound bags of rice on the cheap. You don't go to find last year's styles or even something that was fashionable 5 years ago. The stereotypical clientele has been documented on tumblr blogs aplenty, but one doesn't really pay much attention to them as you dash in and out in hasty fashion. The South Philly Walmart takes every terrible impression you have about this chain and multiplies the pain you feel by how many items you have to purchase during your shopping excursion. There's never a cart to be found at the entrance because they're littered about the store. The ones you do find has three rickety wheels and a screeching that would force a sane man to puncture his ear drums to cease the misery. The shoppers are oblivious to anything outside of their headspace, plowing you over to get the last jar of peanut butter you intended to buy. The layout of the store isn't intuitive, as the last item you have to pick up is never in the spot where it would be in any other big box store. And, if you require assistance, the best bet is to just hit up a person on a register because there's no chance you'll find someone on the floor. That's what I learned as a customer butted in while I was checking out in the express lane. Oh, did the cashier ask him to wait? Of course not. She departed her station to help the guy not find the razor blades he sought out. If I want to lose faith in humanity, this Walmart is a wonderful place to start. If a place has me ponder "wait a second, the South Philly Target is a wonderful store!", you know they're doing something very, very wrong.

text: The Epicurean Restaurant and Bar reminds me of a model home: nice, unoffensive, a little comfy. Three of us had just cleaned up an apartment and worked up an appetite, so we stopped in to sample a bevy of appetizers, including some scary, scary plates (thanks Ann for bringing them out). The grilled New Zealand baby lamb lollipop chops ($14.50) were a promising start, glazed in a tangy Dijon-teriyaki sauce. On the other hand, the Jamaican jerk wings ($6.95) were smothered in "Caribbean spices" that were Pam-esque. Ew. (Blue cheese dressing and celery did little to make those better.) Their Caribbean sweet potato fries (mercifully inexpensive; $4.95) also suffered from the Pam taste. The Epicurean nachos ($8.95) were a patriotic mix of red, white, and blue tortilla chips covered in a typical mix of black bean salsa, sour cream, tomatoes, scallions, black olives, fresh jalapenos, Monterey jack, and cheddar cheese. Nothing to write home about. We moved on to their buffalo shrimp ($8.95), slightly crispy, but mellow. Their Louisiana red sauce, fried spinach, and Gorgonzola cream were quite unexciting. When my friend asked, "Do they taste their own food?" that wasn't a good sign. Not a fan of flatbreads and hummus, so the Epicurean sun-dried tomato hummus ($7.95) had no effect on me. I liked their pan-seared, jumbo-sized, sesame-crusted scallops ($11.50), so not all was lost. Epicurean's appetizers are a mixed bag. We didn't leave satisfied, but we didn't leave hungry. Your mileage may vary.

text: My first experience with Cohee's Shoe Repair on Nolensville Road in Nashville will also be my last. I dropped off a pair of high-heeled boots and another pair of heels that both needed the taps replaced. I called Cohee's before visiting the establishment to check hours, etc. The person who answered for the business wasn't very friendly, sounding a bit like I was an interruption. I should have known better at that point than to actually visit the place. However, I brushed my concern aside and went anyway, as this was the closest shoe repair shop to my home and they were open until 6 pm, making it easier to get there after work. When I actually visited the shop, the worker there treated me much the same as the person who'd answered the phone days before. I suspect they were the same man, and I fear he may actually be the owner or at least manager. I explained that I needed taps on the shoes and was brusquely told me the total and that they only take cash and check. First, I've never been to a similar type of service shop where they charged you up front, and I was a bit taken aback by this. Every dry cleaner, alterations shop and shoe repair service I've ever used previously charged upon pick-up. Not only that, but I didn't even get a receipt, only a claim check. I always want a receipt for purchases, but especially having paid up front. The claim check didn't even have the name of the business on it, so I had to write it on myself so I wouldn't forget where the ticket was for. The fact that they don't take my preferred method of payment (Mastercard) or any form of credit or debit cards was enough for me to hesitate to return. I never use checks, preferring to pay via debit card or online bill pay whenever possible, and I don't keep a lot of cash on me. I was lucky that night I actually did have enough with me to pay, but I really felt this is the kind of information that he should have told me when I called to find out about this business. I can't remember the last time I encountered a business that did not take credit and debit cards - something so highly unusual should be made apparent to potential customers so they can adequately prepare before they visit the store - ESPECIALLY when you require payment up front. The worst and final straw came when I picked up the shoes. I will say that the taps I had replaced look fine and seem sturdy. My issue started when first he couldn't find either pair of my shoes. Then when he finally found my boots (slender, knee-high, high-heeled leather boots that pull on - no zipper or fastener) and then told me my heels were INSIDE my boots! I checked and yes, he really had stuffed my heels down into the toe of each boot. I would NEVER have done this to my shoes, as I would not want to take a chance on stretching the leather at all and have it become baggy around my ankle area. I mentioned that I was not happy to see the heels stuffed inside the boots and would never have done this to my shoes. He said it was necessary to keep the shoes together. I think the bag I brought them in would have served that purpose much better and told him so. I also stated that customers expect their property to be treated better when they bring it for repair and I would not be back. That's the point where he started yelling at me to "Leave now!" Then he repeatedly yelled "Get out!" and "Go!". As I left I told him his customers did not deserve to be treated like this, that I would be detailing his behavior at online review sites to warn others and that he would not keep business if he continues acting this way. I have to say, judging by his attitude from the phone call to each visit, I have to think this man is deeply sad and possibly disturbed. It is just not normal to treat people this way - especially when you are in the service business. A little common courtesy goes a long way. I feel sorry that his life is so bad that he takes it out on his customers - just not sorry enough to return. Hopefully I can save a few others the same terrible treatment by sharing my own experience with this man and this store. Only a masochist would give Cohee's Shoe Repair repeat business. There are plenty of other shoe repair stores in Nashville that will treat customers with decency and politeness and not disrespect their property.

text: We had Mother's Day brunch here, $85 per person. (On Mother's day, brunch is served all day, we had a reservation for dinnertime.) Three stars for the food , minus 1 star for the service. The good part: they had a lot of high-end dishes using a lot of expensive ingredients (lobster, caviar, etc.) So why such a low rating? After having the brunch buffet here, I became convinced that high-end food can't be served buffet style. There were dishes that I could tell would have been good had they been cooked to order and not sitting out. It's really disappointing to have overcooked pasta or a cold escargot tart. And remember, for $85 / person, you can have a tasting menu at many restaurants where food is cooked to order for you. Another thing we discovered was that there was too much to try and too much going on. We got lots of little tastings of everything , but never had time to savor it. Before our mouth could savor an item, we had switched to another. Having a prix-fixe meal of 5-6 courses is much better -- sure you don't get to try as much variety, but then you really get to savor the different flavors and textures that the chef is aiming for in a dish. You let a dish grow on you and understand the nuance of a dish. Instead this buffet brunch is like taking the top 40 pop songs and taking a sentence from each stanza and just playing them right after the other. It's a mad slapdash of really good things - but you don't really have time to savor and enjoy. Service: OK, this can't be too hard considering it's a buffet service. Yet our service was not good. We ordered sparkling water and had to wait a good 10 minutes (after we had already gotten our food). We ordered wine, and it also didn't come promptly. They took away my silverware but didn't replace it. A lot of things we seemed to have to ask for twice -- really, service should be a lot better than that. It wasn't rude or anything, just not top notch. And it seemed like they were really trying to rush us out of there. They kept pushing us to go to the next course. My boyfried and I like to use our expensive dinner dates as a time to talk and catch up on life , but instead it was like "go! speedracer go!'" to the next buffet table with these waiters. So we didn't get a nice elegant romantic dinner, we got a mad dash to try all these buffet tables.

text: We stopped in after a long morning of trade show set up. Rusty's is just a TGI Fridays in a sports bar decor and minus the "flare". Put the waitstaff in ref jerseys, bolt several TVs on the wall and throw in a boxing ring to "dine" in and you got yourself a sports bar. The food was your typical sports bar grub. Wings, burgers, nachos, clubs sandwiches, grilled chicken and a couple of salads. For lunch I had the the Buffalo wings and fires. The wings were your basic wings tossed in Franks Red Hot, which isn't that bad, and the wings were very meaty. Others at my table had burgers and they were very please with their Black and Blue cheese burgers. Service was just okay. On a second visit a large group of us wanted to watch the game and just have a few drinks. The bar was full so we asked if we could have a table and we were told that if we wanted a table we could not just order drinks but we had to order food. Huh?! text: The bubbles were the only good part of this place- my friend and I both got a glass (I had Chandon blanc de noir, she had a George Something-or-other blanc de blanc), they were both nice and bubbly still, so at least we weren't let down by flat sparkling wine. That's what the 1 star is for. What we WERE let down by, however, was the sushi. This was, no question, the worst sushi I have ever eaten. Perhaps it was our mistake to limit our food choices to the sushi side of the menu-- but the rest of the menu is so disorganized and confusing I didn't feel like bothering with it. Maybe previous reviewers who liked the sushi here have never actually eaten good sushi? That's the only explanation I could come up with for anyone describing the sushi from Swanky Bubbles as good. Before the sushi arrived, a server came over and poured out large dishes of soy sauce. I thought this was really weird. First of all, leave the soy sauce on our table, please! Second of all, not everyone likes a giant lake of soy sauce-- I for one like to mix in an ample pinch of wasabi to make almost a paste... and having a full dish of soy sauce made this impossible. So that was odd. We ordered 4 rolls: Vegetable Timebomb, Unagi Roll, 247 Roll, and the My Thai. Only one of these, the unagi roll, was anything near tasty. The rest of them were miserable: the rice was completely wrong. So wrong that we could tell as soon as the plate of sushi was brought out-- flat and dense and squished and flattened around the nori and fish. That was the first mistake. We started trying the various rolls, hoping that maybe they just looked funny but tasted fine... but sadly that was not at all the case. The fish was not good. It was not fresh, it was not flavorful, it did not taste like it was supposed to- the tuna was overwhelmingly fishy and stringy. The salmon was meh- also not very fresh and bland. The My Thai roll- which was supposed to contain spicy sauce, cucumber, poached asparagus, tuna and fresh thai basil, was the most disappointing to me- there was no basil flavor, there was no spicy sauce as far as I could tell, and if it contained asparagus it tasted like wood. Or nothing at all, in fact. The vegetable timebomb seemed to have lots of vegetables, as promised... but lots of wasabi? No. Also a boring, flavorless roll and also surrounded by way too much gross rice. The 247 roll was a waste, too- same problems of overly dense rice and unfresh fish. Nasty. The only good thing, I guess, is that I didn't get ill from eating here (it's noon the day after) so I guess I'm better off than some. We asked our server about the sushi- her explanation was that they have a "different style" of making sushi. Ummm... like making it totally nasty and gross? I don't think I like that style, and I don't think that excuses the plate of stuff we were served: It. Was. Not. Good. From now on, I'm sticking to Koi (N. 2nd Street between Green and Fairmount) for my sushi fix. We considered ordering something else after we took the first couple bites of sushi... but then decided we didn't want to give them any more money. Glad that we ordered the bubbly- it was the only redeeming feature. Also glad that Franklin Fountain is right around the corner... Another point: not sure who thinks this place is wheelchair accessible. There are several steps to get in, plus the back part of the dining room is up one more step. That, and the restrooms are located down 10 or so rather steep stairs. So, it's accessible only if you eat outside (there are a few tables on the sidewalk), and don't need to use the restroom. I strongly urge against eating here if you at all enjoy sushi.
label: NEG

text: Sketch was the second stop in my on-again off-again national tour of burger joints. The first one was Louis Lunch, one of the restaurants who claim to have started it all. Amusingly, Sketch's dining room is about the same diminutive size as Louis', barely room for a few small tables and booths. But while Sketch doesn't have the lore of Louis, the buzz has drawn me to Fishtown to experience, in my mind, the ultimate burger: the Cyclops, a hefty burger toped with a fried egg and bacon - the new platonic ideal. My take out took about 50 minutes to complete from the time of order. One of the servers explained that the cook was new and it was his first Saturday night. Both servers pitched in the kitchen to help out. It would be easy to get upset over the wait, but the server was nice, really apologetic and offered to comp a cookie for the wait. I appreciated that. What I really found amazing, even though the orders were backed up, there were no Gordon Ramseyesque tirades in the open kitchen. The staff was supportive of each other and encouraging instead of letting the stress get to them. Gotta love that. The food, unfortunately, was disappointing. My medium rare sirloin burger was medium-well and dry. The over easy fried egg was pretty salty and overcooked. I was craving a runny egg, but the yolk was pretty much dry. The saltiness of the egg combined with the cured bacon (which, by itself was fresh and tasty) made the sandwich overbearingly salty. The Belgium fries may have been good right out of the fryer, but I sampled some as I was leaving the store and it was lukewarm. I reheated them at home in the oven and they tasted much better. The best part, though was the pistachio shake. Overloaded with whole nuts, thick and redolent with nutty flavor, it was pure bliss. So kudos to the professional service. I may want to return when the cook gets some time under his belt, or maybe I'll just get the shake.
label: NEG

text: It is not a trip to New Orleans without a trip to Bayona. This restaurant is what I consider to be the essence of perfection in dining in this country. There are occassional lapses, but who does not have disagreements even among friends. It is because of the love that these are so unimportant. The important is that Bayona is truly the restaurant I wish were in my neighborhood. First, the staff is incredibly friendly, service and hospitality oriented and generally have been at Bayona's for such a length of time that they are intimately familiar with both the food and wine and can serve you as the guide to a lovely meal. However, this familiarity with the restaurant can sometimes leave the staff talking on the floor about things that should best not be said in front of customers; this is most evident if you are the last evening seating. Never rude, just a bit jarring. However, they are so good that I can overlook this. Now about all of the positives. The restaurant is beautiful without being stuffy or overdone. Posh and well heeled, but with a patina of age and grace, you can go in your dinner jacket or in a tee shirt and khakis and be treated as well. If you have the opportunity, there is an outside carriage yard for dining that affords you a chance for a lovely meal al fresco. Highly recommended. The food of Chef Susan Spicer can be, without exaggeration, the best in the City of New Orleans and among the best in this country. Her touch with a beautiful pantry of Creole and Cajun flavors is both familiar and new as she reinvents combinations and eschews the trite. This is not the place to come for blackened pork chops; but you can have the best seared rack of lamb with red wine sauce and goat cheese ever. That's EVER. The touch in even the small things is amazing....a brightly flavored lemony, smoky eggplant tapenade appetizer served with kalamata olive tapenade and feta cheese makes a brilliant start. The mushroom crostini with goat cheese makes me wake up from dreams wishing for one more bite. Do try the Garlic Soup. Unlike imitations, her garlic soup is deeply roasted and thinned with chicken stock and thickened with bread; no cream, no fat, no oil. Delicious and simple. In fact, after a big meal there recently, both my friend and I commented that the meal left us both satisfied and surprisingly without the food hangover of other fattier or richer restaurants. Bayona is my all time favourite New Orleans Restaurant, from food, hospitality and ambience. Everything is summed up in the one piece of art that hangs in the bar now for years, "Be Nice or Leave" it says. Life in the Big Easy is simply to be enjoyed. Bayona makes it an art.

Yea. Wow. Duhhh. Hey, Omar- you don't need to have Superman X-ray powers to find slices of white bread in a huge CLEAR plastic bag! How hard is it to NOT select a piece of wheat bread, or dutch crust or some funky garlic smelling bread and pick up the piece of white bread next to it? How did you even get a job, if you're that damn inept?! Why can I pick my own bread for my sandwich and not my soup? Why am I forced to eat whatever scraps of bread you deem worthy? Why do I have to pay for bread I don't like and won't eat because you're lazy?! So my boyfriend, being the nice guy that he is- just takes the bag of bread he's given. Actually, I think his acquiesence is probably due to the fact that he has a bad temper and it's easier to just shut up sometimes than argue with an idiot. So yea. He goes to pay for the soup and discovers Omar (duh duh duh) only marked that he had one soup. (As I'm sure the owner of the Deli would have wanted him too) I can't take it personal though, according to the ladies at the register Omar had managed to muck up a bunch of orders before ours. Surprise, surpise there is zero white bread in the bag. Instead we have a large pile of the funky smelling garlic bread. Oh my, isn't that nice? I guess my palate isn't delicate enough to appreciate garlic bread with Broccoli Cheddar soup. Ooops, I meant Broccoli Water. My soup was not soup. It was cream colored runny liquid and had huge chunks of broccoli floating in it. Although I am happy to report that after much digging I did manage to find one small chunk of cheese. I got a vague sense of deja vu as it reminded me of combing through a box of Cracker Jacks, looking for the 'prize'. Both of these ended the same way, with me standing there looking dejected and thinking "this is it?". I was so disapointed. But I resisted the urge to hurl my broccoli water across the room, but only because I knew I'd be the one cleaning it up. Thanks a lot Omar, you destroyed my faith in Deli Towne and it's ability to consistently provide the level of service and yummy-ness required. It's too much of a risk going all the way there after being let down by your laziness and 'can't do' attitude. "Make a fool of you once, shame on them. Make a fool of you twice, shame on me". They are comedians, but I am guessing they are someone who did well at an open mic night and are cheap to hire. The middle act is someone who is experienced and usually funny. Sometimes they are better than the featured comedian. After seeing the first two acts, then the featured comedian comes on and usually does a 30 to 60 minute show. My wife and I just went a month or so ago to see Kevin Pollak. He was very good but maybe a little overpriced. I guess it was fair seeing that he was a Hollywood star and we enjoyed all his stories about Hollywood people he knew. Emo Phillips was the best I have seen by far. His humor is so unique that you laughed during his entire show. I guess the secret to a fantastic experience is searching out their website and finding big name comedians who are coming in. As for the two purchase requirement, its OK. The drinks come with about 85% ice so you have to tell them no ice. The food is alright, but you sure don't go there for it. You have to feel for the wait staff. Trying to deliver your food and drink in the dark must be a real challenge but they do a great job. So go. Go once and see if you like it and if you do, you probably will go back. Once good way to tell if you comedian will be any good is to listen to Bob and Tom on the radio the week they are appearing. One down side to that is they usually use about 50% of their material in their act that they use on the radio, but the visual aspect of seeing the comedian do it is a better experience.

text: I'm surprised there aren't any reviews on this place, yet... whatever. I'll do the honors. Whereas you'll be listening to pop-rap or cover bands up *there*, at the Crack Fox you'll most likely be listening to some obscure industrial or electronica. On Washington, it's button-up shirts and tiny, black dresses, but at the Crack Fox, it's often see through mesh shirts and leather dresses. You starting to get the picture? It's an alternative club, in the truest sense. The decor is all dark-red and black, making for a good match with its clientele. Carrie, the owner, is a real fine lass, and she holds great events through her own production company (Conspiracy STL) and others (Subversion, Rapture, etc.). The cost is always reasonable, and the drinks are as stiff as they need to be. Some of St Louis' top alternative talent plays here, but that also bring me to the reason I can't give the Crack Fox a 5-star rating: the sound. It's not *horrible*, per se, but it's just mediocre enough that you'll probably make a comment about it. With some bands, it's not a problem, but if there's a drum kit up on stage, there might be problems. Overall, though, you SHOULD go to the Crack Fox. It's one of St Louis' best bars, and unless you're a complete douche, you'll enjoy it! UPDATE (9/8/2011): After coming here a bunch more times, I'm changing my rating to 5-star. Although the gripe about the sound is still there, it's less of an issue after they upgraded their stage setup. New sound equipment, new lights, etc. Sounds and looks better than before.

The fries are awesome. Freshly cut that morning and still had the skins on em. They were cut "homemade" style and not through a presto cutter like In-N-Out's, which I thought were groovy. Our waiter was really attentive and nice. He even showed my son to the bathroom! All in all the experience was good. I would like to give it another chance and come back for breakfast. For dessert, we went two stores up to a gelato place called Spoon. OMG! Highly recommended. One of the best gelato places I've ever been to and the service was top notch. They kept feeding you samples and the prices were reasonable. State St. is just a great place to hang out, eat and look at shops on a lazy weekend.

Food and Drink must be ordered at the bar, where there is no formal line system. I started my trip with a stronger Monkey named beer and orders of onion rings and zucchini. text: I absolutely loved Salon Thalia for many reasons including location, attentiveness of the staff, look of the place, but most of all because of my new favorite stylist, Leanna! I got there on Friday morning, at 10 am, and was greeted by the reception people who took me through the first part of the beautifully decorated salon to a little room to put on a robe. I went back to the reception and was offered water, OJ, or coffee. A few minutes later Leanna came and took me with her through the entire salon to the back. The place is HUGE and gorgeous. First, she gave me a consultation, asked a lot of questions about my hair, what i liked and disliked. She also played a lot with my hair and gave me a few suggestions. Then she took me to get shampooed, and after that she offered something to drink again. The haircut was awesome. Although she only took a few inches off my hair, Leanna did an amazing job at fixing my disastrous layers. She made conversation and was always friendly even though I'm kind of shy. While she was blow-drying my hair, she made sure to teach me how to do it and explain to me what products she was using and why. I was so impressed that I ended up buying the one product she recommended for my hair. After we were done, she asked if I had some extra time to make some "sexy" waves in my hair. Of course I did! I absolutely loved how she went out of her way to make me feel pretty. I came out of the salon shining, smiling, as happy as I have ever been (I know how exaggerated this sounds but a great hair cut can do that to a girl). I now adore Salon Thalia and Leanna. She is young, beautiful, and understands hair and how to cut and style it. I will keep seeing her as long as I stay in Philly. And the place is so fancy and elegant, and located in such a beautiful neighborhood that anyone that goes there will feel like a million bucks. Final thing... I was a little hesitant about the price but it was totally worth it. If you call to make an appointment, they will ask if you want to be paired up with a junior or senior stylist (senior stylists charge about $25 more than the juniors, Leanna is a junior stylist and she did amazing!). They will also ask questions about your hair type, what you want, etc so that they pair you up with the best suited person for your needs. I found that to be great and very helpful.

text: I picked the Louisiana Bistro because of the Feed Me Option - the chef comes out to meet you, asks you a couple of questions, and then goes back into the kitchen to prepare your meal. We chose the 4 Course meal ($49 pp.) since we went hungry. Since we were so hungry, however, we went through a basket of the wonderful soft and warm bread in 5 minutes. text: Simply one of my favorite quick-stop sandwich shops, bar none. Located on the (not really) scenic Delaware River waterfront in South Philly, Shank's offers a variety of huge, Italian-inspired sandwiches. Let's start with the most popular sandwich, the Roast Pork Italian. Delicious. Another reviewer said that it lacked flavor; with all due respect, I couldn't disagree more. The provolone is sharp and bitter. The pork is slightly spicy without being greasy, a rare feat for this sandwich. The greens are moist. The roll is crusty and soft, yet holds up to the monstrous quantity of its contents. My fiance, a vegetarian, also loves this place. She gets the Eggplant Parmigiana sandwich. According to her, the eggplant is thin and crispy. The cheese and sauce are in perfect quantity. As a veteran of these eggplant sandwiches, she claims this to be rare, as often the eggplant is drowned out by the other ingredients. The mozzarella sticks are tasty. Again, not a touch greasy. Another thing- their breakfast sandwiches are out of this world.

I can't say 100% because there times when the tikka masala was too watery, or I asked for chana saag and I got paneer saag instead. Usually their delivery is ontime, and pick up is easy. But I do have to say one time it took them about an hour and a half to deliver our food. When my husband called to see where they were, they got upset at him. Then when our food finally came, it was cold. Not sure what happened, but we were so hungry, we just ate it without any questions. But usually, it's a perfect place for takeout on a cold night when you don't feel like cooking. Plus, leftovers are great for lunch or dinner the next day.

text: So Shere-E-Punjab may be a staple for Swarthmore students venturing out for more exciting fare than Renato's and Cheng Hing's, and the food is pretty decent, but as previous reviews have intimated, they have some serious service issues. When they started offering delivery, my friends and I rejoiced - finally, decent food that didn't require a car for pickup! We ordered $40+ worth of different dishes, including several orders of naan (their naan is admittedly v. good, if overpriced). That was only the beginning of our adventure. Well over an hour later, we called, desperate, plaintive, begging for our food. They assured us that no, they had not forgotten, and yes, it would be coming. When? we asked. Soon, they replied. We could extract no further details. It was a full thirty minutes more before the delivery guy finally limped onto campus (understand that the restaurant is a ten minute drive away, fifteen max). After bestowing a generous tip on the good man who finally alleviated our starvation, we headed inside for a feast. We soon discovered that we had only received one order of naan, but been charged for everything we ordered. I don't know about the rest of you, but I pretty much hate eating Indian food if I can't scoop my food with bread. We called the restaurant, and they said they were sorry, all of their people had left and they could not come bring us the naan we were missing, but they would write down our names and info, and the next time we ordered they would give us the bread we paid for for free and a discount on the meal to repay us for the trouble. Well, maybe I'm an idiot for not getting something in writing, but I think you can guess what happened the next time I called and asked for my already-paid-for naan and discount. Not only did they not make good on the deal, they were nothing short of rude in responding to the suggestion that anyone at their establishment might ever have made such a promise. Now, their eggplant is amazing, their mango lassies are good and their chickpeas are extremely tasty in all forms. But they are unquestionably overpriced and poorly organized. I, for one, am not going back for a repeat performance.
label: NEG

text: The only thing that was "melting" was my patience. It took us nearly THREE HOURS from being seated to the moment we walked out. Given how small the entree was (about a dozen small 1 inch pieces of various meats and seafood for $25), I actually would have walked out about as hungry as I walked in. What saved the meal from disaster was the dessert. Dark chocolate fondue with strawberries, bananas, and a variety of sweets like brownies, rice crispies, cheesecake and marshmallows really saved the night. The staff seemed truly apologetic and took care of us, and that plus the dessert earned them the one star from me. If you are with someone with whom you can chat for hours and don't mind food arriving occasionally to remind you that you are actually at a restaurant, then this is probably the place for you. If you like to "oooh" and "aaah" with each dipped piece of bread into mediocre fondue and pretend that you are actually enjoying your meal to impress your date, this is also a good place. I just prefer the novelty of a great and satisfying dining experience and be able to come home before the sun comes up.

text: This place definitely has potential. For take-out, I'd probably rate it a star higher. The service was friendly and fast, but we were the first customers of the day. I went with family and most of us got a pizza, which turned out to be huge. At around $12 for a medium pie and $2 per topping, it's not the cheapest stuff and the quality certainly reflected that. My cheeseless (too much cheese makes me feel sick) pizza with mushrooms and olives was great-- since it's essentially dough, sauce and toppings, all of these needed to be quality ingredients, and they were. I highly recommend the brick oven-style, and my sister really enjoyed her "bar" personal-sized margharita pizza. My boyfriend got a huge Sicilian (they were out of the smaller size, and upgraded him at no charge). I had a bite, but didn't really care for it...something was off about the dough, but he liked it. Another member of our party had the plain white pizza, which was pretty tasty as well. Anyway, you get the point: the pizza is decent and accommodations were easily made. The atmosphere, however, is where this place loses stars. I didn't enjoy sitting next to a humming refrigeration unit, and the floors and bathrooms looked a little cheap and dirty. The tables and benches were also off-putting and I couldn't think of a good way to explain it, until my boyfriend said "this reminds me of a pizza place at the shore." The cheap long table and "wooden" plastic benches have their time and place, and that time and place is (and can only ever be) the Jersey shore. The plates fit right in with the dirty shore corner pizza parlor feel. The artwork was somewhat amusing, a combination of Pink Floyd-inspired canvas paintings mounted on the wall, some plastic plaques featuring names of Italian cities, and a creepy fat Italian guy statue looming in the corner amidst some fake plants. I feel bad bashing the setting, but the pizza is actually good. And I might actually go back if it was a nice sit-down place. But even for takeout, Buckingham Pizza still wins in my book. We went here because my dad had a restaurant.com coupon, so if you have one of those, it's no big loss. Overall: meh, but tasty leftovers!

text: I've been going to Yoga Vida 1 - 2 times/week for a couple of months now. The classes are great and I really like the instructors. They make an effort to be supportive and learn names. The second thing is the changing room - it is very cramped and awkward. There is only one shower. But the weirdest part is that there is not a door, but a hanging fabric partition to separate the areas. It is hard to see when someone is coming or going through the door, and results in near-collisions almost every time I am there. The class schedule does not announce the instructor, and they rotate. I never know who the instructor will be until I arrive. I have gotten used to this but it bugged me at first. I do really like the people and the yoga at Yoga Vida, I just don't care for the space.

text: Authenticity is what it's all about at Smiling Elephant. 'You're never going to find beef and broccoli on this menu," said the owners' son, who along with his sister was helping mom and dad get the restaurant up and running. The limited menu is a sign that they're smartly looking to get it right by starting small. The service was wonderful and homey - I very much appreciated the complimentary lemongrass tea delivered to me with a message that it's "good for my health." And the Pad Thai? Delicious and unique, thanks to the wide noodles, crisp, fresh bean sprouts, a tangy vinegar flavor (rather than the more common odd sweetness found in lesser attempts) and use of a light olive oil. And unlike other Thai restaurants in Nashville, they promise no MSG, ever. I'm excited to return and try other menu items and wish the Smiling Elephant all the best. It promises to be a great addition to a great neighborhood!

text: I am not an art person but I do love coming here and pretending I see the deeper meaning and significance of certain works. But most of all, I really just like how peaceful I feel when I'm in the museum. There is something about how massive it is. I also took my 5th graders here on a field trip a few years ago and the staff was so accommodating and great with the students.

text: Had an amazing first time. It will now become my new Thursday ritual. The fried tilapia taco is soooo good. The best $3 taco ever! Next time I'd just ask to go light on the sauce.
label: POS

text: My visit to Marathon Grill reminded me why I so often dine in Chinatown. Chinatown never lets me down. Marathon Grill let me down. I wish I could give it no stars because that is what it truly deserves after my experience dining there on Thursday. My friend was in town and I liked that Marathon Grill was participating in Center City Sips, and that the exterior of it was inviting. So we stopped in there. They have got to figure out a better layout for their seating because it was empty at 6 pm and all the little tables are so crammed together that you cannot help but kick your dining companions in the shins. Furthermore our waitress was unfortunately the worst server I am have ever had. It all started when she came over a minute after giving us the menu with an incredibly abrasive "So what'll you have?" to which our response was "Can we have another minute?" which was answered with a roll of her eyes and her stomping away. Might I add that we were here only responsibility at the time? When I asked her some questions about what constituted appetizer and what didn't (the layout of the menu is very unclear, and options are extremely limited especially for this type of restaurant), she was annoyed and highly unaccommodating. Not only was she terrible, but so was the look of my friend's sandwich. They brought out his fish sandwich with the top bun off, unfortunately for them exposing a disgustingly wilted, nearly inedible looking piece of lettuce. Come on, if you are going to only put one piece of lettuce on and display it like it's important- at least don't screw it up??? My vegetarian chili was boring and near tasteless. My arugula salad was uninspired but fine for its price ($6.50). While we were still eating, my friend with 3/4 of his sandwich uneaten, our highly unpleasant waitress slammed down our check in front of him and stormed off, proceeding to just hang out and chat at the front with other Marathon Grill Staff members. She then ignored our pleas for a to-go box, and we managed to get one from another waitress. Needless to say unless enticed by some amazing coupons or something, I will never return to Marathon Grill - and especially not this particular location. Boo. Hiss.
label: NEG

text: Dierbergs is a nice store with high quality products. I usually go there for the salad bar or for something different and for the most part, it's amazing. I love it! however, I will save the five star review for the one in Brentwood. They have a food bar and an extensive salad bar. Take home message is this: you can't get any better than Dierbergs fresh produce and salad "bar"(s)-- but don't be oh-so patriotic. If you can find Ritz crackers (or knockoffs or whatever) for half the price, just go to that store (e.g., Walmart, Shop N Save, Save A Lot, etc). In this economy, go to Dierbergs if you want to treat yourself, not for everyday shopping unless you're rich-- and as a college student, that clearly doesn't apply to me.
label: POS

text: Best Sliders ever tasted. Do yourself a favor and head to this place for happy hour or dinner. Great atmosphere, great drinks and definitely amazingly good at casual prices.
label: POS

text: Clean, pleasant, friendly, and if you get a coupon from a magazine at the tourist center, it's also cheap. ($50) My only gripe is that the breakfast is crap. You get a choice of sugar packed cereal, plastic meat patties, or dry danishes. To be fair, there was a basket of powdery apples and that gelatinous yoplait stuff. They use way too many disposable plates and cutlery items for breakfast. Styrofoam in this day and age is not cool. It's not environmentally responsible and yeah, I'm one of the few that can get my goat up about details like this.
label: POS

text: I've never understood why there's always a big crowd around Julio Barrio. I wish some of them would get into Yanni's, instead of waiting to be seated! It's quite a rubbish joint. Ordinary food, ordinary service, semi-O.K. margaritas at best, but definitely a substandard overall experience. The only reason I give it a 2* is because I've eaten worse Mexican food! :-D (check out my review of Sophie's Mexican Kitchen in Grand Canyon NP). I give them credit, in that they explicitly call themselves a bar, since their main clientele would probably be bar hopping folks wanting to get some margaritas and chips before moving on. Can't imagine anyone going to this place for the food, although for some reason, almost every time I walk by this place, I see some sad, disgruntled couple on a date out there! If I were to give this place a makeover, I'd go with the bar idea with some unusual margaritas on the menu and some small plates (tapas) to keep company.
label: NEG

text: Recently went for brunch with friends who knew the chef. Between this and having a large group (which was fine - some other review said not great for groups, but we made reservations in advance and everything was okay) I had the benefit of sampling much of the menu. Server was pleasant, although was slow on refilling wine/drinks. Brunch drinks were spot on (Bloody Mary, White wine sangria, STRONG iced coffee & iced capp). Our friend ordered the wine for the table so I did not look at the list myself. My favorites were the lamb ribs and specialty crab salad. Muffins with marmalade to start were heavenly. By the time we were sent a round of desserts I felt like I was going to burst, but everything I tasted was simply delightful. Next time I am in New Orleans I will be sure to check out this place for lunch or dinner. As an aside, if you watched Treme this is where they filmed the shots for the restaurant.
label: POS

text: Worst experience I've had in Nashville. We went to dinner at 6:15pm there were very few people in the restaurant and they took our drink order quickly but then it took us 15min to order our food. Our appetizer (chips 'n dip) was brought out without salsa, we thought no big. Then we had to wait 1 HOUR & 45 MINUTES to get 1 sandwich we had ordered to split. We had three rounds of drinks and didn't see our server for 30min at a time. Even our third round of drinks came with almost all the ice cubes melted. A table of 6 sat down an hour after we did and got their appetizers & all their food before our ONE sandwich arrived. When the sandwich did finally arrive it was wrong (came with tomatoes), the cheese had the 'at one time I was melted but now I have a weird film' look, and the french fries & sandwich were cold. I had to get up and ask the bartender, the 3rd person I had to ask since our server was no where to be found, for a manager. When the manager did come she offered no apology, had a horrible attitude, was the opposite of friendly, and was definitely not a good manager. She took off the appetizer and the sandwich, never brought us a warm one, and I had to get up and find her to run our credit cards as she never came back to take payment. I will NEVER go back there and will discourage anyone from doing so. BAD BAD BAD!
label: NEG

text: This is the place to go if you'd like to feel like a tourist. The food wasn't bad, but the service was pretty lacking. This coming from a really low maintenance person. I can understand being busy, but I think a server can at least make an attempt to act like they care that they abandoned their table. The music would have ordinarily bothered me I think. The older gentleman playing, however, was awesome. There is something to be said for the accompaniment of a casiotone with traditional Greek music and vocals. My only regret was not having a better view of this great spectacle. As far as food. I had their Crete burger with provolone. Which was very tasty. The bread is really what helped make the burger rise above. Their hummus was just o.k., but their pita was pretty good. This place lost points with me mainly for ambiance and service. I will not be back.
label: NEG

text: I wasn't impressed. While the prices are incredibly low, I didn't find the food to be that great. Just OK and nothing better than Panda.
label: NEG

text: Passed by numerous times and kept saying "cool, we should really go in there and check it out!" Took us about a year...but some friends us were out and about and we all decided to check it out. Very nice cool, low lighted place. We had fun, we were a bit loud for the atmosphere, but we enjoyed our service, our yummy desserts and wine. We will definitely have to go back again.
label: POS

text: Was here at dinnertime on a glorious Thursday night and enjoyed the outdoor seating. It was quite crowded, but the Phillies were on so it was a nice atmosphere. I liked the colorful outdoor mural that spiced up this gray part of town. Kite & Key is a great place to go for drink and socializing but I wouldn't go for the food alone. The beer selection is adequate. The staff is friendly and attentive - the food arrived quickly. My shoestring fries were over-done and almost inedible. The mixed green salad was just that, covered in vinegar and could have been a side portion. Half-plum tomatoes were merely a garnish, but for the price, disappointing. I have been here before and the nachos are good. The cheese plate is great, but a bit pricey for the portion. Didn't have the wings, but they looked and smelled delicious. Overall, I would say this place is over-rated, but great for some after-work fare and happy hour. Great place to watch sports with lots of seating to yak it up with friends. As far as food goes, if they can't step it up to to the nearby Sabrina's or Rose Tattoo, they should stick to pub grub and cater to the sports addicts. Sabrina's & Rose Tattoo, walkable from there are two competitively nice places I would opt for if in the neighborhood for the food. K&K's great beer selection versus the wannabe frou frou menu seem incongruent to the overall atmosphere.
label: NEG

text: It was his jolly and bearded mug that dominated grocery isle before Newman decided to make dressings and sauces. Chef Paul Prudhomme has been and remains one of the original crusaders of New Orleans Cajun cuisine. It was on my very first trip to New Orleans, that I decided that my first taste of Cajun (yes, I've managed to avoid it for a lifetime thus far for some strange reason) would be with Chef Paul and his vaunted Louisiana Kitchen. Thankfully the meal was spectacular. The month-in-advance reservation saved my date and I a lovely table with a few of the New Orleans foot traffic below. There was something extremely casual about this restaurant. It had the shiny silverware, the while linen, and the first class service, but at the same time the table was covered with butcher paper with drawings of cartoon rabbits and turtles who happily ignore their fate of turning into pot pie and soup, respectively. I found this devilishly hilarious. But that was my last moment of humor, because it was Chef Paul who got the last laugh. The food was ridiculous. Crazy. Out of control. Off the fa-jazzy. It was my first time having fried green tomatoes. It was the most enjoyable "losing-virginity" experience ever. I highly recommend it. But it was the shrimp chipotle remoulade that really put it over the edge. Other tastes of the evening included the turtle soup, bronzed swordfish, panned chicken breast, and Chartres Street jumbalava. Had death followed me on the tails of this meal, I would have embraced my place in the afterlife, happy, full, and content.
label: POS

text: Its a John Besh restaurant so my expectations were elevated. We started with the Oysters and they were good a fresh. Got the shrimp and grits and it was average at best. To be honest it tasted kinda burnt. My son got sliders which were great. But for this class of restaurant and expense it pretty sad to say order the sliders. I would skip it and try one of Emeril's places on my next trip.

In addition to ordering brocolli and being told 45 mins later they were out of brocolli so I had to order a replacement veggie. I am very dissapointed in this establishment :( I will not be able to order from here again.

text: Nectar is exactly the sort of spot I would choose if I were unmarried and didn't feel like going into the city on a Friday night. But if that is not your situation, then I can't recommend it. It is painfully loud and the food and service are pretty weak. The McSushi is just what you would expect from a scene restaurant and the other dishes are pallid and bland. But it is very pretty and could be just the right choice for certain types of outings.

text: I have never been to a Five Guys before but after my last visit I would definably would go back. The burger I had was sort of orgasmic. The combination of of flavors was enduring and freshness of the burger was something to remember. I would give it 5 stars but I felt the atmosphere of the place as not visually pleasing. The whole place felt like some generic dinner somewhere.

text: I LOVE THIS PLACE! People go here for their sonoran hot dogs, but you HAVE to try their carne asada tacos on flour tortillas and their carne asada caramelos. Those are my two favorite foods at El Guero. The best part about El Guero is their condiment bar - I'm a condiment girl, and this was heaven! From several different types of salsa, to a guacamole type salsa, to pickled onions, radishes, cucumbers, mushrooms and not to forget, their grilled jalapenos, yellow peppers and green onions. Their condiment bar is what makes this place AMAZING - and the food makes it even better! I would visit their newer location on Oracle, it's bigger, cleaner and indoors so you can enjoy the airconditioning
label: POS

text: Had lunch here on Christmas Day. Best meal we had during our entire stay. Loved the white bean spread served with the bread. The beet salad with goat cheese was simple, clean, and wonderful. I had a grilled fish with cauliflower puree. I have no idea how they could make a vegetable taste that good, but they did. They only offered 2 desserts, so my husband and I each chose one. I got the red velvet cake and he had the rice pudding. I'm not a huge fan of anything that doesn't involve chocolate, so I ordered the cake only because it was included with the meal. It was jaw dropping good. And it was an absolutely beautiful plating.

text: Dale did my cut & dry, and it was meticulously well done. I'm from out of town and was a walk-in (due to fido's cafe being too full for me to sit and do some work). Dale was thoughtful in his approach to the cut and his attention to detail throughout the cut & style process was perfect. He was committed to doing a great job from start to finish; really engaged in his work, while still being personable. This, too, was from a stylist who was otherwise going to be done for the day before I walked in before his end in shift. Side note, there were 8 or so chairs in this salon - everyone I saw getting their hair done looked *great* on their way out. I don't think you can go wrong here. Also, I saw a lot of the product they use is organic - nice bonus! Might have to time my next business trip to Nashville 4-6 weeks from now ;)

text: Things you can buy for about $3 off the top of my head: a 10 pk of hangers from Target, gallon of gas, almost a pound of oxtails at soulard's market. Or a grilled pork sandwich from Phuc Loi, if you feel like splurging, drop an extra 50 cents for their special sandwich (Danh Mi Dac Biet, don't know how to say that), which comes with grilled pork, ham, head cheese and egg. I came in to scout it out, the place was clean and bright, I had the grilled pork, tried some of my friend's shredded pork skin sandwich, then ordered 60 more for my lunch meeting the next day. The mom (completely family run), even threw in a couple of the special sandwiches for us. Sweet! The grilled pork is probably the easiest for beginners, I liked the shredded pork skin, but the special with the fried egg in it was my favorite. They were all Vietnamese patrons when we came in, but wouldn't be surprised if this place blows up, definitely a gem!
label: POS

text: Finally made it to Mamacita the other night. Now I know what I have been missing...nothing! Okay, nice atmosphere, great beer selection (all the typical mexican beers: XX, Modelo, Sol, Pacifico and on and on), the margharitas looked good and the salsa's were tasty. Very good gaucamole. So why only two stars? Where is the love Mamacita?? first off, they charge for chips and salsa (huh?). The tacos are put together probably on a assembly line in the kitchen as well as the enchiladas. They are served (the tacos) on a metal pie plate that doesn't hold any heat. The enchiladas were room temp on the inside and just didn't have the flavors you would expect. While this place is okay and along the lines of Baja Fresh and San Antonio Taco, do yourself a favor and go get some real mexican at Hacienda on Nolensville, or any taco trailer in Madison on Gallatin or even better, El Rodeo out in Hermitage...that's the real deal. Not this phony, vibey, location driven tortilla, meat and cheese joint. Good in a pinch but I know better...c'mon Mamacita, show us some love in the food department, you ain't foolin' anyone.
label: NEG

text: We arrived very late for dinner (9:30pm) so they were out of a lot of specials like their dover sole/branzino, bone marrow, sweetbread (really wanted to try sweetbread!). The restaurant is very intimate: seats around 30 people. BYOB makes the place very affordable. The price is extremely reasonable. For 3 course meals with sparkling water, coffee...it was about $55 per person including tax and tip. If this place were in NYC, it would easily cost double. 5 stars for value for sure. The seared foie and scallops were excellent. The pig foot dish was a bit too mushy for me (I am used to the Korean steamed version which is a bit chewier) but still nicely flavored. Also I found the escargo to be too soft although the flavor was good. Overall ALL the dishes were nicely flavored...especially the sauces were seasoned just right: not too salty, not too bland, just right. And the portions were just perfect amount for a 3-course-meal. At the end of the meal, the chef came out and talked to us for a bit: a bit of extra caring touch to the meal. (I love when they do that!). I would definitely come back.
label: POS

text: Whenever we are in town we make a point at stopping on Frenchy's. We especially like this location because it is beachside. The grouper sandwiches are still wonderful but they did shrink a bit since I remember from years ago. Frenchy's now offers a bigger version which is probably the size of the old sandwich. Still, grouper is expensive and hard to come by so I guess this is inevitable. And you absolutely MUST try the she-crab soup. Even if it is the middle of summer and you've been sweating on the beach all day- you don't want to miss it! Plus- all food tastes better when you're on the beach. Parking (metered- bring your coins) can be a pain, get there early and enjoy the beautiful beach first!

The food and drinks are expensive, the decor and ambiance is lacking, and the space is cramped. I know this place is somewhat of a local icon, and that's why I went, but iconic status alone is a poor reason to spend your time, money, and stomach space.

text: My cousin from Florida grew up right by this place, and told me it's the "best burger you'll ever eat." Yeah, right. We went to this place, a group of about 10 of us, and I was pretty disappointed. They have very limited selections...ie. only one dressing, limited appetizers, no bacon for their burgers...come on. Oh yeah, no free refills for sodas, either. The service was TERRIBLE...after my cousins (10, 12, and 13 years old) ran out of their first sodas, we flagged the lady down, and asked for refills. She said "alright, hang on," and about 10 minutes later, brought back a bunch of waters. We asked her about refills for sodas, and she said, "Oh, we don't do that here," in a real snotty voice. So, after waiting for our food for about an hour, it came out and nearly every burger that was cooked medium well was practically still moving. My paper plate, yes...PAPER plate, was soaked in cow blood, and the lady complained again when we asked for it to be cooked more. The burger itself was okay, but definitely not the "best burger ever." I don't know what kind of standards the rest of you have, but mine are certainly higher than what O'Connell's gave me. I will say that the food was pretty cheap, and the atmosphere was alright. The bar was pretty crowded too, and it seemed like they had every kind of whiskey known to man. I certainly won't be going back.

YOU SUCK DEVILS ALLEY!!!!!

text: So many people seem to like this place. Yes, it is all vegan and yes, it is kosher. Which means for people with some religious, dietary, or moral restrictions on diet, they can just about order anything on the menu for once. Don't get me wrong, it's rare that I can do that, too. The prices are reasonable and the dish sizes are generous. Yet I also have to say that just because it's vegan doesn't by any means make it automatically healthy. Most of the dishes I've tried here have been quite oily and very strongly seasoned. Most of the appetizers are deep fried. The one dish that I really do like here is the ginseng soup, which I believe was a special. Be sure to check your take out before you leave. Last time I got take out here, it was a TOTALLY wrong order, nothing in it was anything I had ordered AT ALL. The bottom line is that the food here is really just okay. It's not spectacular and I've definitely had better. That being said, I'm not sure many people have really had gourmet Chinese cooking, the pleasure of which I've been able to experience in my travels around the world. So if you come here expecting the regular Chinese food, but vegetarian, that's what you're going to get here. As for an epicurean adventure, this is definitely not the place to go.
label: NEG

text: Luke is a causal John Besh restaurant located in the CBD. It was one of the few good restaurants open for lunch on Saturday. We had the corn and crab bisque to start and it was very good. For entrees we ordered the burger and stuffed shrimp. The burger costs $16 which seems expensive for a burger (its the most expensive buyer i have ever had), but it was really good. The burger is huge and is topped by a wonderful cheese and smoked bacon. I am not a bacon fan, but apparently John Besh knows how to procure incredible bacon. The burger comes with some really good fries that are placed in a mint julep cup wrapped with paper. The stuffed shrimp was really good and came with vegetables. The wait staff was very attentive and friendly. I will definitely go here again. One word of caution. We at at Luke for lunch and La Provence for dinner. I would suggest only one Besh restaurant per day. There is no way to eat that much food in a day.
label: POS

text: How do you welcome the 200+ people that you helped teach the ways of Yelp to over a weekend? By writing a review for the event that you did it at of course! For better and worse I've followed WXPN for years (shout out to my friend Robert Drake!). But for whatever strange reason I haven't been to a an XPoNential Festival until this year. But I've always made note of how the diversity of the lineup always managed to successfully reflect upon the diversity of the station. And off the bat I'll also add that although I jumped upon the opportunity to be the point man at the Yelp Table with an enthusiastic HELL YES the moment that Monica asked me; They Might Be Giants, Peter Bjorn & John, East Hundred, Illinois and many others would have had me seeing it anyway. I do have to give it up to the dedication XPN puts into setting up the festival, Since I've walked through Wiggins Park as a bare bones park when leaving the Tweeter (whatever it's called) Center before (and will be reviewing now that I know what it's called), I can honestly attest to the fact that NO part of the stages, or any of the booths are there when the festival isn't in session. So that gives you the start of understanding how much they put into it. But when you factor in things like the entire fest being broad-casted on air, how they accommodate it's volunteers and sponsors during the fest, and then some it becomes abundantly clear. and the effort that WXPN puts into shows throughout. In the end I was beyond thrilled with getting to see TMBG and Peter Bjorn & John for the first time ever, and I also enjoyed getting reacquainted with local favorites like East Hundred and Gillian Grassie (swoon). But I also had the chance to discover new favorites like Perkasie and The Hold Steady. I'm not going to lie and pretend that things like the burnt burger with cheese whiz, the random bouts of rain, The Bacon Brothers, and the crowd who came to see Toby Keith play the Center of Evil Ticket Bastard didn't make me want to grab a shovel and bury myself. But over all the festival made for an absolutely AMAZING weekend. And I got to spend it all alongside some pretty awesome yelpers, which made for a priceless occasion.
label: POS

text: I've been here 3 times and I'm not sure why. The first time, about 1 month after opening, the food was pretty good and the burger tasted fresh so I was somewhat encouraged by my 3-star experience. But the following two times my burger was luke warm, the cheese wasn't melted, and the fries were room temperature. I also noticed their bacon was paper thin and had been cooked hours before being served. A fast food burger from Carl's Jr puts this place to shame, and for a cheaper price! There is just no reason to operate a burger shop if your burgers suck, and these ones suck. I wish it wasn't so but they need better help, a better concept and better quality control procedures. The dining area is well appointed and the tv's are nice but other than that this place is a total disappointment.
label: NEG

text: As a self appointed pizza expert, I can honestly state that this is the best pizza I have ever eaten! The dough is thin, the pies are well baked, the sauce excellent, and the cheese tasty. The usual pizza toppings are available. The service is quick and the place smells terrific! They take their pizza very seriously at Delorenzo's and it's the only thing on the menu! Pies start around $14, which is higher than the average pizza place, but I can assure you, the price is worth it! Two caveats: call ahead for reservations and, empty your bladder before you go, as there are no bathrooms here.

Yes, some (ok, most) things are better fried, but a crabcake is NOT one of them. They still make a decent shrimp po-boy though.

text: As other posters have noted, what kind of sports bar in this day and age doesn't have flat-screen HD TV's?? How is this possible? This place is in need of a serious overhaul. Sadly, there aren't many other sports options around (I've recently started to go to Cavanaugh's on Sansom -- much nicer place to watch a game). The food is also mediocre at best. It's like a terrible version of Applebee's, and Applebee's is pretty bad. The only thing saving this place from getting a one-star review is their large selection of draft beers, which can all be purchased for $2 on Tuesdays. When you serve 6 Rogue Dead Guy drafts for $12, you earn a star.

text: The epitomy of what a cheesesteak should not be. Grissle, excess grease, a sponge for a roll...they get it 100% wrong. Note the high reviews are mostly from out of towners who most likely have been lured by a tall tale. Trust the locals people, skip directly past this greasy, unclean, unsantitary hole and go ANYWHERE but Pat's. Any local street vendor or pizza joint will make you a better steak.

text: It was the day after Christmas, and for the past three hours my nephew and I had been doing our holiday spending in the impressive International Plaza and we were hollow. The Earl Of Sandwich caught my eye because I loved the name, for one, and a co-worker of mine had mentioned it a few days earlier for another. It's a very simple, run-and gun process to get your food here. There's a gigantic board that lists 20 hot sandwiches and another that lists salads. You stand in line (which was considerable on that day) and watch a line of workers assemble your order from scratch on their own "fresh-baked, artisan bread". The food comes wrapped in tinfoil and stuffed in a plastic bag. That's about it. There was nothing remarkable about the food itself-I had a paper thin sliced turkey something-or-other with a scant amount of bacon and bland tomato- or the service which ranged from testy to downright bored. text: What spicy (or not spicy if you prefer) heaven tastes like! First of all, I used to frequent Foxy's Red Hots for their super-cheap gyros years ago when they were here. A couple of months later, I return to find no hairy-chested man in a mesh shirt to take my order (REALLY!), which was simultaneously both my relief and disappointment. :-) A Thai joint in a no-man's land of a retail strip mall you say?! A signal in my brain says "approach cautiously". But, an adventure is an adventure whether it ends up good or bad right?! And so adventure it is! Having lived in Thailand for several months, the bar was already set high. I had tried the good, the bad, and the "what the hell is that" while in Thailand. And whether it be served in a sit down restaurant, a night market, or in a banana-leaf bowl from a walking vendor on the third-class train, the majority of it was delicious. So I go for broke and order the Chiang-Mai noodle. Yellow curry plus noodles should equal contentment after all. Yep! Just like the Thai mama that I never had would have made it. A good start. I came back a few days later, dying to try the tom-yum noodle soup. And again, if I had not known that I was in some south country strip mall, I would have thought that I was being served food that was prepared in a much more distant location. Another thing about this place is the incredibly personable atmosphere. Sure, the first time or two they might not recognize you, but after a few times, you are always greeted with a hearty smile and a wave from whom I can only assume would be the owner. So, in closing, if you want to have a meal in a restaurant that is decked out in Thai decor and pay a premium for it, head to the Loop. If you want affordable Thai that is as authentic as it gets, then Zen is your place.

text: This is the tour we should have taken on our first day in New Orleans. Jeff is a credit not only to the tour guide profession but to the city of New Orleans as well. It's a three-hour easy bike ride through parts of the French Quarter you won't see if you're just walking from Bourbon Street, and adjoining neighborhoods. You'll see the architecture, people and changing face of the city, and with Jeff's deep knowledge, you'll get an instant history lesson. Everything from New Orleans' founding to Creole culture to the mechanics of a funeral parade. Great trivia, like the origin of the name of the game of chance we now call craps; how the Po Boy sandwich originated; why a road median is called neutral ground in the city. He'll also dispense great advice on where to the get the best food, drink and music in New Orleans. Jeff's full of energy and knows his stuff, and he can weave tales while seamlessly leading you through the streets without getting run down by traffic.

text: This restaurant has some of the best food I've ever ate. And I have had some good food but let me just say that Chartres House Cafe is truly a must! Okay, so my girlfriend and I are visiting New Orleans for the weekend and of course, we've had a few drinks to say the least. After walking for 2 hours on a Vampire Tour, we stirred up quite the appetite only to find ourselves lost in New Orleans! To our luck or perhaps it was fate, Chartres House Cafe was open and lively filled with people. The restaurant itself was dark. Dark wood, minimal lighting, kind of like a lodge or better said, a cabin-type ambiance. This didn't bother us much as it was already late, about 11PM. The service was great. Our waiter was very attentive and helpful when it came down to choosing what to eat. We decided to go for the Spinach Dip, I got the Fried Catfish with Fries and my friend ordered Jambalaya. What's going to New Orleans without trying some Jambalaya? Of course, I can't go on without mentioning our encounter with an oompa-loompa. Yes, the ever happy-go-lucky companions of our friend Willy Wonka. We were sitting at the booth eating our hearts away when a midget dressed up as an oompa-loompa struck up a conversation with us. In short (no pun intended), we got invited to attend a modern-day Shakespearean Ball in Biloxi, Mississippi. Wow, random. Very random. Anywho, onto the food! Holy cow. When I say the food was insanely amazing, it is truly an understatement. Thinking of the spinach dip makes my mouth water. The cajun pepper seasoned fries that came with my meal were used to dip into the spinach dip. Probably the best combination EVER. Of course we had chips to eat our Spinach Dip with but I'm naturally a bit curious and so I like to mix different flavors when it comes to food. The crispy, seasoned fries dipped in the warm, creamy spinach dip... a definite must-do combo! The Fried Catfish was great. Not oily or greasy, and definitely not fatty. It was very lean and didn't have that fishy taste I loathe. I actually dipped the fried catfish in the spinach dip too... That was pretty good. Now to the jackpot, the Jambalaya. I've never had it anywhere else but after trying it at Chartres House, I would probably never have anything better. It was perfect. Completely and entirely perfect. Fresh cilantro, just the right amount of seasoning, no need for any additional salt or pepper. Truly exceptional. If you order anything at all, it should be the Jambalaya. I will always and forever remember this restaurant not only for the weird series of events that transpired throughout the night but for the amazing food we engulfed in about 5 seconds.
label: POS
