text: Pizza-A-Go-Go has the best pizza in St. Louis - hands down. Although it is small in stature and considered a "hidden" gem, it is big in taste and well known in South City. For a lack of better words I will just say it is "Simply delicious!" Owned and operated by Frank LaFata since 1964, Pizza-A-Go-Go is the essence of simple, yet exceptional pizza. I have been going there for as long as I can remember and the consistancy, which is rare for a pizza place, never ceases to amaze me. My Dad used to take the whole family there back when it was on Grand Blvd. We would drive from South County to experience the perfect pizza. To this day my Dad and I agree ther is none better. New location, same great taste and service. If you too are seeking the perfect pie, look no further. Franks pies are timeless classics. These are no St. Louis-style pizzas. They are traditional, hand-tossed pies with mozzarella cheese that assures you provel cheese is an inferior alternative. The crust is perfect and the sauce is sweet with the right amount of spice. Pizza-A-Go-Go will remind you why you love pizza. No exotic topings. Just fresh pepperoni, sausage, and all the other traditional fixings. The menu consists of strictly pizza. If you want appetizers or pasta, try a chain restaurant. If you want the best pizza in town, you have found it. I love the nostalgia and all that goes with it. Frank could be playing the organ when you walk in the door, while dough is flinging in the air. Oh, and you can bring in your own beer. Yeah, that's right! I challenge you to find me any other pizza place that not only allows beer to be brought in, but encourages it. Save money and enjoy your favorite beverage. Currently, I am on a quest for the "Best Pizza in St. Louis," and I am almost positive Pizza-A-Go-Go will reign supreme. I will keep an open mind and give every place a fair shake, but I think I'll be hard-pressed to find more delicious pie. The price is unbeatable and the service is unparalleled. I challange you to find a better place to get a pie in St. Louis. If you do, be sure to let me know. And rember to stay tuned for further reviews, as I am on the quest for the "Best Pizza in St. Louis."

text: Watching on television isn't as awesome as in person. You have to prepare yourself. Know that: there is tons of walking. Bathrooms are horrendous. You want seclusion? try a port-o-pody. Lots of food options. Generally everything is pretty good. Up and down the streets surrounding the raceway are tons of vendors. Must check out all the food vendors on the outside. The smells will get your mouth watering and stomach rrroarring. Know that you cannot bring alcohol unless its in plastic bottles. Also know that Indiana is a dry state on Sundays. No alcohol sales at convenience stores, grocery, etc on Sunday only. Restaurants and the Speedway are excluded from that. They also have restrictions on the size of coolers brought into the park. Its a must to check out their website. Know that if you don't want to park at designated parking(mostly grass lots), you can opt to park on local peoples' front yards! Yes. The speedway is surrounded by neighborhood. In any direction (of the park) people will offer you all kinds of freebies to have you park on their lawn. I saw a guy showering with the garden hose, at that house they also gave free rides to the main gate of the speedway. Some people offer free breakfast or tents. Know that sometimes while people are waiting in their cars to move nearer to the Speedway, some fall asleep at the wheel. Know that you are going to see ALL kinds of people. *There were alot of people with JACKED up teeth. I thought maybe its the soft water screwing up peoples teeth? Maybe they don't talk about good dental care out here?? (If you know the signs, it could also be Meth use) The speedway is enormous. When you purchase a ticket there is a designated seat for you, but, its on a bench. Chances are someone is sitting there. Which is OK cause you can sit anywhere in the general area. Really, while there are ticket checkers, they could care less where you eventually nest. See a place available in a better area. Just walk over there like you own the place. On the more serious race days, however, they are more strict with seating. Don't stick to just the bench areas. Walk around. You can take an underground path to the middle of the raceway. Try walking underneath when there is a race going on. LOUD. When you walk under you have more options of areas to watch the races. You can sit, stand or lay on the grass. I don't think I saw any bugs. Lay out in comfort. There are two areas where a mound is high enough to overlook 1/4 of a turn on the track. As the day moves its usually later on that people make their way to this area. Its one area where you can stand within feet of the fence surrounding the actual track. There is also an overhead bridge that takes you over a part of the track. Great place to use your camera for an action shot or maybe record a little movie recording. This part of the raceway is actually a 9-hole golfing grounds. Further out this way in a secluded parking lot is where you'll find show cars. Bring plenty of sun tan lotion. Make sure you buy ear plugs or the big padded headphones for children. It gets loud. Like ring in your ear all weekend loud. Like a jet flew past your head loud. I was here for the recent Formula One race this past June 2007. Great time. Great race.

text: There are no Bob Evans in or around NYC and California doesn't have any, either. It was with some trepidation that I accepted my coworkers invitation to grab lunch there while at a conference. From the brief description he offered, it sounded like a faceless corporate version of a standard greasy spoon diner. It was! So we roll in, grab a seat (five dudes cramming into a booth is an unfortunate and inelegant dance), start the never-ending flow of cheap, hot coffee, and peruse. All diner standards were there: eggs, home-fries, grilled cheese sandwiches. The OJ's decent and the coffee's inoffensive. The corporate backing is good for one thing: it allows some experimentation with menu items in traditionally close-minded environments. My tuna melt came with dried cranberries in it, a welcome tart addition to the usual flavor. One of the dudes got pancakes stuffed with vanilla cream cheese and topped with caramel and pecans. Decadent, beautiful, creamy, delicious heart attack. A pulled pork sandwich was a bit too dry. The burger was a mess; hence, satisfactory. In the joint's favor, the price was low, low, low (50 bucks for food to fill five fellows). Also, it's a damned fast food joint, so it's not like one could be disappointed by the health standards of the fare. They do have a scanty selection of healthier items (limited to the salad and 'swap veg for meat in entrees' categories). Would I go there on my own? Nope. If I'm feeling passive though, and know that I'll have an opportunity to exercise compulsively in the next 48 hours, Maybe.

text: OK. I wanted to give this place 5 stars the first time I went, but it went downhill in the middle of that visit, and has not got much better. I have been two times now, and I have had awful service both times. The first time it was pretty slow, and getting a beer seemed to take a really long time. The second time I went, it was during the last game of the World Series, and it still wasn't super busy...but it did take super long to get any service at all. From my experience, the wait staff is pretty sub-par on every level. They are not super friendly, very slow and they tend to completely forget you exist, even if you are with three other people...kind of hard to miss. The burger I had the first time was really good, and the atmosphere is actually pretty nice. It's a sports bar, but it's not ridiculously loud like Bully's on Robb Drive can get, so that was cool. I can't lie, the happy hour from 4pm - 8pm is pretty fantastic with half-off all bar drinks. Basically that means a large beer that would be $5.50+ at Bully's is $2.25, and as an alcoholic, I love that. Oh. The last time I went there our waitress "suggested" the chicken Philly sandwich about 3 times. I ordered the pork sandwich, and guess what...they were out of pork. The Philly was recommended again, so I chose the Reuben. The Reuben didn't have any kraut, which basically means I got a hot pastrami with sauce on it. The pastrami was like leather, and ultimately it was nasty. The wife and children got a pizza, and the dough looked like biscuit dough. It did not look good. Overall, I want to like the place, but the service so far is awful, and the food is so-so at best. When somebody recommends the chicken a bunch of times, I know that means they are trying to move the chicken, and not give me a recommendation based on taste. I hate that kind of stuff. If Bully's is too crowded, or you are tired of getting ripped off by their climbing prices for mediocre food, Sparky's is OK, but that's all I can say for it. If you just want to get straight hammered, then go and sit at the bar for better service (I hope?) and go between 4pm - 8pm for happy hour, then come back at midnight - 4am for a nightcap. Yea...it's not great, but it's not the worst I guess.

text: Everything about my visit was perfect, from the waiter greeting me with a cold glass of water while I waited to be seated, to the dessert I was far too stuffed to even order, let alone finish! I saw the @StarrRestaurants tweet about a new $15 Prix Fixe lunch special, and quickly arranged a hot date. Be warned, two desserts and two bottles of Pellegrino bought our tab up to $67, but it was so worth it! So, from the beginning... To my surprise, even at 12:something in the afternoon on a weekday, with no reservation there was no wait for a table. The place was far from empty, but there were a few open tables. There was, however, a wait for my dining companion, so after a few minutes de-sweating myself (it's a 1.6 mile walk from my house, and it was like 90 degrees) in the restroom, I had a seat in the waiting area. Within like 30 seconds, a waiter came over and asked if I would like something to drink. And even refused my $1 tip when he brought it to me. I didn't know how to take that at first, but, since he offered, rather than me having to flag him down, I couldn't take offense. lol. Lunch date arrived before I finished my glass of club soda, and we were immediately taken to our table. While I was busy ogling the decor - I'm captivated by the carvings on the very high ceilings - waiter appeared and the excellent service continued. I went with the caesar salad, he chose the tomato and mozzarella salad. Both were fine. I chose the salmon and truffled pureed potatoes, he had the Butcher Burger and fries. The salmon... it was all I dreamed it would be. Slightly crispy edges and all. Literally exactly how I imagined it. The potatoes, however, were more than my little mind could fathom. It looked like a bowl of some kind of aioli or something; that's how well they are pureed. When I tried them, I had one of those orgasmic moments... I can't even describe the smooth, rich, creamy, buttery, garlicky goodness. I told my date, "if I were to go right now, you could tell them I honestly died happy, cuz this stuff is AMAZING. I don't even need dessert." *sighing at the memory* Only thing I needed was a spoon cuz my poor little fork could not quite scrape every bite of delicious out of that little bowl. Date loved his messy burger. Like gave it a spot in his Top 10. The fries were great, too... I stole a couple of them. I was full from my food, and he was too full to even finish his food, but, we still ordered dessert. *evil chuckle* I had the carrot cake. He had the cheesecake. There is positively no way I had room for anything else in my belly, but that carrot cake - and I have had MANY over the years - was perfection. A giant slice of cream cheese icing-coated perfection. And I am a cream cheese icing fanatic, so like, "icing on the cake"... yeah. Literally. I had to eat it. Date was totally swooning over his giant slice of creamy smooth cheesecake with blueberry compote, but I couldn't even be bothered to taste it (and I LOVE cheesecake) because I was too high on cloud nine to reach down and take a bite. *sigh* I'd definitely go back, and GLADLY pay full price for those dishes. And I'd order both desserts. To go. So I could savor the love for days to come.

text: "I think I get it now. Tucson, that is. We used to come here and not really understand it. But I think we get it now." Confession of one, Britt Daniel, halfway through Spoon's set in the then recently remodeled Rialto a few years back. It's hard not to get Tucson when you step into Railto's historic and hallowed walls that have been updated to a modern indie mecca. Plush black interiors accented with golds that echo its art deco past but beaten into submission by a street music future. An impeccably cared for monument that bares virtually no branding or signs of the deplorable state of the current mainstream music business and its trappings. "You still don't fucking get it!" The inevitable lovingly hostile response to Britt's confession screamed out by one of the indigenous indie smartasses. Just to make it obvious Tucson has some balls. And that it takes more then a handful of one-day stops on 4th avenue to understand it. But in all honesty, you probably could soak the indie scene of Tucson in one day. And Rialto, along with the neighboring Club Congress, is its amazing centerpiece. It's not a hard town to "get". A hipster oasis of cheap booze, character-ridden music venues, any-day-of-the-week bars, and funky shops and restaurants; that doesn't get a lot of credit or ask for it. With Tucson, it's much more of a lead by example sort of thing. You pour money into rebuild a historic theatre because its worth saving. You do it without the sponsorship of a major car manufacturer because you want to cherish the past of your city and want corporate free integrity for the future. You keep ticket prices low and fees sparing or non-existent because you want to support the art scene and build it up rather then gouge people for money. You create partnerships with other indie bars and venues and allow free travel between establishments during shows because you are in the business of entertaining people, not fucking over people with rules. To me, the Rialto says a lot about Tucson, the fellowship of the indie scene there, and its integrity. Boisterous, without being pretentious. Intense, but ironic. Tasteful, but cheap. Communal, but DIY. Experimental, but fun-loving. Always independent.

text: Marly B's extremely negative review of PCS got my attention today so I wanted to write my own review, since I have had the exact opposite experience with this company. I absolutely love this company. I moved to Philly 2 years ago, and before I came here, I sold my car. One of the reasons I knew I'd be able to live car-free was that I knew PCS existed, and that I would have relatively convenient access to a car whenever I needed it. Well, that's exactly what I've gotten. We're still just in the infant stages of what I think will become a very large car sharing industry. And even at this early stage, car sharing programs demonstrate their unbelievable value. My annual transportation costs are FAR lower than they would be if I was a car owner. The true value of PCS is in the minimal annual expense. Sure, they've got an annual fee now. That has apparently annoyed a lot of people. What is it? $120? That's a couple gas refills if you're a car owner. Give them a break. Jeez. I was actually very happy when they instituted the annual membership fee. I WANT this company to succeed, and I recognize that they need a somewhat stable revenue stream, and I also recognize that having a membership fee will tend to eliminate from the program members of inferior quality - deadbeats. The kind of people who are more likely to damage the car, steal shit, etc. It adds just a small bit of exclusivity to the program, which I like. So people don't like the annual membership fee? Okay, well do they like not having to pay over 1000 bucks for car insurance every year? I mean, come on. I'll take that trade any day. Speaking of the annual fee, it used to be a monthly charge to your credit card. I like that they now automatically charge my credit card just once a year. Because I don't like seeing a charge on my credit card every month. It just irritates me. I prefer one annual charge. A few more points about PCS: *Some have complained that the cars are unclean on the inside. Generally speaking, I've always found them to be fairly clean on the inside. Do members really want PCS to vacuum the cars after EVERY use? If so, expect higher hourly charges. Personally, I'd rather have lower hourly charges and the occasional crumb on my seat. *Many of the complaints I've seen are along the lines of "I did something stupid and irresponsible and PCS penalized me for it." Well, ya know, ya might want to stop doing stupid and irresponsible things. If you're relatively intelligent and responsible, you won't have too much trouble. I've never gotten any kind of penalty in the two years I've been a member. *In two years, I've only had trouble with one reservation - I couldn't get into my car. On this particular day, I also had a broken cellphone, which complicated things. Had my cellphone worked, I could have called them and I'm fairly confident they could have helped. Regardless, they refunded my money for this reservation. The folks on the phone are always really nice.

text: Brunchie Bruncherson is back with a review of brunch at The Scottish Arms. (This is not a dinner or bar review, so please note that up front.) And, maybe I should give it another try, but I do not have an endless supply of money, nor do most of us. It is usually a first impression/one try kind of thing with me. OK...so, I REALLY wanted to like this place as did my companions on our recent jaunt to this little Scottish haunt in Midtown/CWE. We are always looking for new and interesting places, and this spot had it all. Interesting decor. No huge crowds. A menu that looked super enticing and would hold our interest. Um...oops. Not so much. Let's start with the food. The menu contains some interesting items that are a-typical of an American brunch which makes things fun. (Like baked apples, oatmeal pancakes, bangers, etc.) Unfortunately, some of the items don't deliver, especially the basic ones. We all tried omelettes, and they seriously lacked some flavor. Eggs are bland on their own, so you need to add, at the very least, salt and pepper. Apparently, they didn't think this was necessary. Note to staff: it was and is. The potatoes served on the side were OK (if they were cooked). The sausage wrapped in rolls were nice. I ordered toast and marmalade, too. The marmalade was basically orange rinds with some gooey sauce. Um...no thanks. For drinks, the coffee was good: not too bitter. Juices were fine. I ordered a bloody mary and was given a glass of just ice and vodka. I had to go into the bar to finish my bloody mary. OK...that is fine with me since I could make it as spicy as I want. But I have about HAD IT with self-service brunch/restaurants! This ain't a work-a-raunt! Restaurant owners: ENOUGH OF THIS! Serve the coffee, make the drinks, make the food, serve the food. Basics. Urgh. So, the food wasn't all that spectacular especially for the price. But, the big downside was the kitchen. We were one of four tables in the dining room, and the bar had a few watching a soccer match. So, the place was not packed by any means. Yet, it took seemingly forever for our food to be delivered. And then, there was a major screw-up in our order. In short, the kitchen did not make two of our four omelettes. Yup, that's right: half the orders. So, two of us ate our bland omelettes while the other two watched us. I guess the kitchen didn't see this as a major problem because other tables were served, time went by, seasons changed, and it took another "forever" for the other two omelettes to come on out. Bad bad bad bad bad. (P.S. I have cooked eggs before. It does not take TEN MINUTES for two omelettes especially when you messed up the order in the first place. Notice Brunchie's internal temperate rising.) OK, so fine. The food came late. The waiter was super apologetic. I'm better. I know the food service industry is hard (especially when customers actually expect you to serve food), so I was willing to let it all pass. I knew what was coming, anyway. The owner or manager would stop by, apologize to the table, and comp one of the meals or both meals. Here they come. Just wait for it. They'll be here any minute now. I mean, of COURSE they will. They comped the friggin' bacon for the table next to ours when it was seconds late; SURELY they will comp some lousy eggs. But, oh no, they did not. Fail. Big time fail. No manager visit. No comp. We paid the full price. Done - two stars it is. Again, I am NOT one to berate restaurants or servers. It is a hard job. There is a lot to do, and customers are super demanding a-holes for the most part. I try to be the best eater out there and be as friendly as possible. But, this was too much. And, no, I will not ask to speak to the manager because that isn't my job. (Maybe there it is since I had to make my own drink.) Instead, I will pay my full bill, tip the waiter generously, and never, ever go back. And, that is where I stand on Scottish Arms. Two stars. Not returning. It really makes me sad, too, because, like I said, I really wanted to like this place.
label: NEG

text: If I could, I'd live at the Apple store. I began my descent into computers at an early age and on a Mac. As I grew older, I became part of the PC population out of being poor and just plain outnumbered. Well, when I started my freelance writing business two years ago, I was determined to do it "right", which meant upgrading my home computer system and rekindling my love affair with Apple. I visited my local Apple store and was hooked! I recently visited to buy an iPhone. Yes, I have the iPhone. At the Marlton, NJ store, folks were camped out on folding lawn chairs during the wee hours of the morning. But when I arrived at 2:00 p.m., when the store closed to ready for the launch, there weren't very many people there: maybe 30 or so. The staff (and security) were friendly, approachable and helpful. I remarked that I hadn't seen people camped out like that since I waited on line for New Kids on the Block tickets when I was 16 and the whole staff broke out laughing. Even John "Mayor Gadget" Street had a catbird seat at another store in the middle of the night. But I decided to shop for a few hours before the reopening (I'm much too cool to sit outside a store for a phone), got ice cream, listened to the Phillies day game on my car stereo, then, joined folks in the line, which by 5:00 p.m. was growing longer. Apple staff arranged for coffee and Panera Bread to offer us free beverages and donuts while we waited! But even with the circus atmosphere (kids scalping their spots in line while local news helicopters hovered above us taking photos) Apple staff was poised, calm and helpful. When I finally picked up my box, I had a staff member offer to check me out using a mini, portable credit card machine! How's that for service? I was talking on my new iPhone in mere minutes. At any Apple store you can peruse and play with any gadget or computer with smart support and without the frustration of the "hard sell." Leave it to Apple to create products that not only are the most usable and glitch-free, but they're also the most stylish and awe-inspiring. I can't take out my iPhone in public without being asked for a look and a tutorial. If it were a man, I'd be jealous! Visit an Apple store. There's a third area Apple location on Gulph Road at the King of Prussia Mall.

text: What an Overwhelming experience being in the Superdome was. Unfortunately, I don't think I was the only one. If you haven't figured it out by now, I was one of the many privileged, yet humbled Hawaii fans that made it out to the 2008 AllState Sugar Bowl. The field was immaculate, the sight of the multi-colored seats and HUGE JumboTron screens were simply amazing! The HP Pavilion (or whatever it's called now) couldn't hold a candle to this place. I've been to The Oakland Coliseum, Candlestick Park, Sam Boyd Stadium, San Jose State, University of Nevada, Fresno State and of course, Aloha Stadium and the Superdome was by far the most impressive all around. One nice perk was the FOOD!!! Besides your usual stadium food, there were Zatarains kiosks serving sausage jambalaya and crawfish meatpies...MMMMMMM!!! Overall, my experience was memorable, to say the least. It was just sad to see our Warriors get their okole's handed to them...

text: I'm so mad Alex M beat me to first to review since this isn't even his CVS it's mine. JERK..... oh sorry, right the review. OK, so this is the CVS in walking distance to my house. Not a bad place for a first, second, or etc. date either. :)

text: House of Wong was always a great spot for dinner when I wanted Chinese food in St. Louis. All of the ingredients are a step up in quality than most other Chinese restaurants you'll try. I always liked their sesame chicken- yummy! The only downsides to this place are the strange hours here (it's been a while but I remember Clayton closing down at 8pm), and seeing my professors here all the time (not good if you just tanked an exam). All in all, a good place to visit in early evening, enjoy some good Chinese food, and avoid eye contact with those who hold your grades in their hands.

text: Maybe I'm too old for this? I went because a friend won a free beer party for 20 friends. The line for the "free" beer was insane and a few people were a little nasty because they had been waiting too long for their beer. It's nearly impossible to move around or get to the bar. The floors are sticky from spilled beverages. Luckily, the wait staff does their best to get around to see if anyone needs to order anything...however, it takes forever because there are few wait staff working. Just be careful, because it's just as hard for staff to move around with their trays full of beverages and you could end up being the unlucky one that gets baptized by a tray of beers. The food is typical bar food, good when your drunk but gross when your not unless you enjoy eating bar food regularly. I found it hard to eat while my eyes and nose were burning from the smell of smoke. The talent was good. At first it seemed a little on the obnoxious side and I thought they were either a good pianist or a good singer but not both. However, there was one guy that was exceptionally talented and I enjoyed everything he played and sang. Nonetheless, it's a great environment for groups...but don't expect to get to know anyone you may not already know because you won't be able to carry a conversation over the noise.
label: NEG

text: I guess it comes down to food being a subjective & relative matter. After hearing about the place, I went down and tried it. I ordered the "Special Pho" (Pho is a good indicator of quality for any Vietnamese restaurant). After tasting it, I have to say it wasn't worth the visit. The flavor of the broth was bland and it didn't come with all the usual meats that would make this "Special". It was definitely below average of all the Pho I've ever tasted (and I've eaten a lot). I've actually made better at home. Additionally, we asked for tea and it turned out the tea was $2.50 for a little pot - another disappointment. My usual dining philosophy is that no Asian restaurants should ever charge for tea or white rice. Overall, with taste being relative, in Santa Barbara, Saigon is probably ok for many people. However, if they opened this restaurant in San Gabriel, Santa Ana, San Jose, or even Northridge, I don't think it would last beyond 2 days. For myself, one visit is enough. But the restaurant is clean and it seems they put effort into making the place look nice. The atmosphere is modern with plants and a cyclo for decoration. The look is tasteful. Too bad the food did not match up to the surrounding. Tip: If you really want good Vietnamese food and willing to drive a little, go to Pho Saigon in Port Hueneme. You'll get more authentic flavors there.
label: NEG

text: The Latest Dish is easy to pass by...it's on a mostly tattoo and piercing block off of South Street, and there's no huge sign or lights to let you know it's there. I like this about the Latest Dish. It's so unassuming that when you eat the food, you're really blown away! Between my boyfriend and I we've sampled a bunch of their offerings. The daily empanada is a sure bet, as is the chicken sandwich. Also wonderful are the organic chicken and the tuna. The drink list has some excellent creative cocktails, along with a substantial beer list and respectable wine offering. This is a great neighborhood spot that serves quality food, unlike some of the other places on South Street. A great place to go with a couple friends, or a casual meal on a weeknight.

text: The meal I had at Katie's Pizzeria was just so satisfying in every way. Anyone else occasionally wake up on a Sunday mid-morning and think a) I need pizza and b) I also need cocktails? No? Alright, well if by chance you do, head to this place. Or you could be normal and crave those things on a weeknight, which also works. Parking here is a little awkward... we parked across the street at the grocery store and had to walk across Clayton Rd. which was interesting, but we made it. The decor of this place is definitely my style... vintage tables and chairs, none matching... a couple locals sitting around reading the paper. It was laid back and filled with all kinds of good smells. Our waitress was energetic and full of suggestions, and let me know they served a fresh watermelon cocktail, so that's what I went with. We actually saw someone cutting up/squeezing fresh watermelon for the drink, and it came with a chunk of it on the side of the glass! Now that's what I call fresh. As Abby S. noted, the salads are beyond delicious. Try the Italian Market Vegetable Chop Salad which is made up of fennel, carrots, zuchinni, parmigiano, pine nuts, canneloni beans and a lemon balsamic dressing. See how the "fresh" trend continues...? For my pizza I chose one that had rich fontina cheese, caramelized onions, speck, and an egg cracked right in the middle. Heaven. Can't wait to go back.

text: Nice little upscale trendy restaurant near Hyde Park. For an appetizer we had the Flash Fried Oysters with boniato potatoes, tamarind chorizo BBQ, chipotle aioli. This was delicious and had a great kind of latin fusion of flavors. I had the peppercorn crusted Filet which was good but not Bern's steakhouse good. It was accompanied with a potato wafer which was at the very least interesting. My wife had the Citrus Sesame Seared Yellow Fin Tuna I did not try, but she was pleased with. For dessert we had the cream cheese eggrolls, which sounds weird but it was so awesome and had a fun presentation. It came with three dipping sauces; chocolate ganache, strawberry cream, and a custard/vanilla one (my fave)??? Overall a good dining experience. Please avoid the italian dishes in this restaurant. text: My number-one favorite Philly restaurant. The food has always been a solid 8 or 9, whether I have been there with just one other person or on the two occasions I have entertained parties of eight or ten. (Unlike most restaurants that put big parties at a huge bare table in the back, we were fit into a cozy alcove where we didn't disturb the other diners, but still felt like we were "in" the same room as everyone else.) I have occasionally wished that the wait-staff were more enthusiastic or engaging, but they have never lacked for competence. I must confess that the Mystery Dinner Theater almost scared me off the first time (I imagined something out of a bad Pocono dinner-theater). I can't say what the show might be like -- I've never been -- but everything I have seen makes Bistro Romano a solid choice, particularly for a romantic dinner for two. text: This restaurant is an original Tucson gem and continues to be very consistantly good. My father told me you will see the owners at a good restaurant every night, standing where they can monitor the food coming out of the kitchen. While I wouldn't say the owner does exactly that, he is there EVERY night - and the quality shows. I actually feel bad for the guy.. but I digress. There is no more charming place to eat in this town than Caruso's patio on a perfect night. My long time favorite dish is Lasagne. Once in a while I will branch out a little and have Lasagne and Eggplant, but a trip to Caruso's definitely has to include Lasagne for me. My wife loves the Veal and Eggplant Parmigiana and their Antipasto salad is delicious. We always get it. I would love the dressing recipe. text: Alright so I listened to my fellow Yelpers and decided on Mema's for lunch today. The ambiance is nice and very themed with a mixture of Mexican and Alaskan (of course) memorabilia scattered throughout the walls. The staff was definitely very friendly and it was a nice surprise to have free refills on my large pepsi. I ordered the nachos (of course) and the my girlfriend ordered the half order of chicken quesadillas. I loved the quality of the food and the fact that they have cheap combo meals available. My nachos were magnificent. The crispy flour shell that they make there is amazing. Think of dark flour chips extra crunchy with a dash of zesty sugar, the taste really stands out. The beans were also very well done, probably the first place I've seen around here with black re fried beans. The chicken itself was good, nothing amazing though, yet my girlfriend really liked it. I prefer my chicken a little more spicy (see:Chipotle). Over all it reminded me of a delicious, local Tampa style Tijuana Flats. Except friendlier, and tastier!

text: After living in San Francisco and San Diego, I returned home to St. Louis expecting a non-existent nightlife. 'Back in the day' of Twist, Fallout and such, there were plenty of gay clubs to hang out, dance, meet friends and more. Over the more recent years, when I have visited St. Louis, The Complex and JJ's were busy and a good time, but didn't really cater to that nightclub experience that Fallout had (as well as the clubs on the West Coast). The interior has the look and feel of a classic South Beach or WeHo club, with booths to chill in, friendly and fun staff, a DJ who knows what it means "to spin". While the dance floor is not large, it has a cozy feel to it that allows for you to interact with others while dancing and share the whole experience. With a a platform box in the middle, friends that love to be the center of attention have their own spot for the duration of the evening.

text: I frequent World Cafe Live, both upstairs and downstairs, often. They usually have great music. The sound is better downstairs, but that's to be expected, since that's where the bigger acts play. The ambience is nice. The servers are pretty attentive for a music venue; I have yet to have a truly bad experience with the waitstaff. Their beer selection is all right. They have a rotating Victory tap and usually a Dogfish Head tap, so I'm pretty happy. They even had Hop Wallop on tap, which is a fine, fine beer. The beer prices are pretty standard for Philly. However, the fancy drinks are pretty ridiculously priced. I once got a Strawberry Shortcake drink, and although it was delicious, it wasn't quite worth $10. Also, the well drinks are $7 or thereabouts, which is pretty outlandish. I think they use middle-shelf liquor, at least, and not Vladimir or Banker's Club. The food is okay, but a little expensive for what they offer. The veggie chili was okay, if maybe a little thick. But $8 for a grilled cheese seems like highway robbery to me. I know I'll be back here, but probably just for beer and music.

text: There are three important words I require any establishment serving baked goods and all-day breakfasts to be worth of: really excellent coffee. Artisan Resto-Cafe has superb coffee and more. Expanded from basically a glorified baker, Artisan offers eggs, Belgian waffles, light breakfasts, sandwiches, and a few burgers and larger meals. The food is extremely fresh - I had a vegetarian omelette and the eggs were fluffy and did not have that oily off-taste that some of the chain breakfast places have. Their signature grilled potatoes are a bit dry, but have an interesting flavour. My friend had an eggs benedict special - the poached eggs were served on turkey, of all things. To finish my meal, I had the bread pudding, which was shaped like a large muffin and served warm with steamed milk. I would come here just for the coffee and that, or perhaps the sticky cinnamon pecan bun, or one of the other mouth-watering desserts. The place has a very artistic feel to it and is relaxed. It gets very busy here on weekends.

text: We went to Gigi's to get cupcakes for a birthday dinner that we were having. By the time dinner was served, 1/2 of the cupcakes had collapsed and were falling over. It was a mess! We were mortified, but had to serve them, because we had nothing else to serve for dessert. When I called the store, they tried to blame us, "we let them melt" or "we didn't handle the box properly", instead of apologizing and offering to make it right. When you are paying the amount they charge for a cupcake, you deserve better! I would never return to this bakery for cupcakes, and I would definitely not recommend it. There are too many other really good bakeries in Nashville, to waste your time and money at this one.

text: Corey T: Best Thai food on the west coast? Surely you are kidding? Ever been to LA's "Thai Town??!" I was pretty unimpressed today. My order consisted of the Pad Kee Mao Lunch Special (Sub. Hot and Sour soup for the Egg Drop soup and Sub. Sticky rice for steamed rice). It took over 1 hr and 15 minutes to get my food, and I was dining alone. Eight people walked in shortly after I did, from the hospital. They ordered food to go, and had drinks while they waited. They ordered after me, and were given all their food and had departed before I received my food. When I assumed my pissed-off-look after about an hour of waiting, the waiter (who I think is the owner) said "sticky rice almost done." I guess this was his justification for how long the food was taking (at that point over an hour). Voracious, of course, I dove into my food when it arrived. The sticky rice was cool to the touch - hmm - shock. I thought that's what was holding up the order!? Shouldn't it be hotter than this!? The Kee Mao was ok - no sight of a red pepper in it - and they use Jalapenos for the heat - not exactly a Thai tradition. I would be willing to give this place another shot to sample more of the menu if I hadn't been lied to. Clearly they cooked the large table's food - then worried about the rest of the restaurant. Sticky rice my ass.

text: I always think of London Drugs as Shoppers Drug Mart on steroids. It's much bigger and offers a huge variety of things. text: Gonna have to give their full detailing services a moderate "meh." The interior at first glance was super clean, but upon further inspection didn't live up to my expectations. Eh, not entirely the case. They also missed some specks of dirt here and there underneath the side mirrors and on the B pillar. Also, I guess their policy isn't to clean underneath the hood/dress the engine or address dirt and filth in the trunk gutter and behind the fuel door. I can't entirely consider that a full detail if they entirely neglect those areas. The entire interior was coated with detailing spray. I forget the exact name, but it was basically on entire interior console, shifter/e-brake, cup holders, armrests, seats, etc. This wasn't a huge problem. It wasn't overly greasy like some sprays but could still be wiped off. So the residue was slight/moderate. And it didn't stain clothing/leave any deposits on napkins I used to wipe it off, or my clothing. Though, considering that, it's kind of a cheap cop out to spray something and leave it with this wet look all over the place. However, it was apparent they'd at least wiped everything down/rid dust and probably brushed seat crevices and HVAC vents prior to doing so. That's good. Whoever detailed my car also never got the message I'd specifically given to the management, to remove a dealership decal from the back of my trunk. Don't know how that didn't happen. I guess maybe they didn't want to risk damaging the paint? They did at least buff the crap out of this one bad scrape I had, just as instructed. Diminished it well enough to my liking, maybe a little too well but I knew there was a risk in that. Other things: I wish they would've told me they'd take all remaining items from door storage, back-of-seat storage, etc and just throw it all into one trash bag. Also, I'm 100% confident at least one personal effect is missing. That's just not cool. Nothing particularly important but it's just the principle of the matter, not so much as even a generic ball point pen, for example, should be missing from my car. I'll probably continue to go here for regular car washes, because there aren't too many hand washes in the city. However, for the $215 (after tax) I paid for this service, I was expecting a bit more. Full disclosure: I used to be a car detailer in a past job. So, I definitely pick up on more than most people and know all the techniques, tools and supplies used.

text: After seeing other bad reviews, I just couldn'tt keep my experience to myself. This place is Atrocious. If that's all you were looking to know, then read no more, but if you are looking to be entertained - then by all means, do read on. This place USED to give the best pedicures. and I USED to be willing to fork over the extra cash for it. No More! Here is some background to preface this review *I live in the city and I wear flip flops Every Day. So my feet get more than their fair share of abuse. *While I bathe and generally make myself presentable to society, I am not what you might consider girlie. I am a very busy woman, and to me these things are nice, but by no means a necessity to life. I am a good human being regardless of the occasionally bushy state of my eyebrows. *The Experience:* Let me now describe for you what I could only call a cursory pedicure that lasted all of 15 minutes (including polish) and that I would not have expected to pay more than $15 ($20 with tip) for; but which ended up costing me a whopping $40. And that I probably could have done my own self for free. This particular day I thought to myself, "self, you are waaaay over due for a pedicure. it would probably be a good idea to treat yourself to the good place, despite the higher price tag." So I walked into Allure, and with a hint of embarrassment, asked for a pedicure. The 10 women who were lounging around doing nothing proceeded to fight over whose turn it was. That should have been my first clue. The woman who led me to the chair seemed nice enough. As with every nail place I have ever been, I warned her that I was ticklish, but that I didn't mind if she didn't mind my hysterical bursts of laughter. All seemed to be going well, and sure enough the minute the pumice stone hit my feet I broke out into fits of loud boisterous laughter which I am known so well for. All of the girls in the salon started to point and giggle (this is totally par for the course and happens everywhere - I am used to it). At this point, the only thing that made me feel slightly uncomfortable was the fact that she kept making what I can only describe as "bedroom eyes" at me which went so far as to include a slight puckering of the lips and sucking in of the cheeks. I thought this strange and it gave me the distinct impression of being hit on (I would have been equally unnerved by had these advances been made by a man or a woman, this scenario isn't exactly primed for romance - I mean, what would you even talk about on the second date?) After 1 or 2 passes of the pumice stone, she placed my foot back in the water and I figured that having seen my feet she realized that they might require some heavy duty artillery. But then the woman did something really quite strange. She rinsed of my feet and started to drain the water. She dried my legs and feet and started to put some lotion on them. She asked me if I shave. I said that I had the day before (there was some stubble, but it wasn't any of her business - I was by no means some wildebeest covered in fur) and jokingly said I didn't feel the need to impress anyone. Her response - raised eyebrows and a guttural sound which I can only classify as chastising in nature. She continued to prep my feet for the polish. I didn't understand what was going on. I kinda tried to tilt my feet to see if I had missed something. But No, the calluses were all present and accounted for. I should have said something then and there. But i think I might have been suffering from a shock related condition. Then, to add insult to injury. She looked up at my face, stitched her brows together, raised her upper lip and asked me when i had last done my eyebrows. I said, Why yes, I am over due, but I can't do it this evening (it was around 5) or my face will be all red. (I have been doing my eyebrows for over 10 years - and owned this face for longer than that - I'd like to think I now how it reacts to things). She continued to insist that this would not happen and that I should have her do them. I chose to drop the subject rather than insult her lest she take it out on the polish she was about to apply. This continued on into an awkward 10 minutes under the dryer not unlike weird silences while on a date you would rather not be on in the first place. (Apparently there was also a shoulder massage involved - though to be honest, at that point, it was so awkward & uncomfortable, I didn't really enjoy it) So the date metaphor was even more apt. So after all this - I would have Still given this place at least 2 stars, for the entertainment value at the very least. had it not been for the fact that the paint job didn't even last 24 hours. I felt Jilted to say the least.

text: Wow... honestly... this is one of the better urban parks I've been to in a long time. We did not make it into the zoo or the native american art museum or the indiana state museum or the NCAA museum but every one of those places looks interesting to visit and we will be back. This is soley a review of the outdoor spaces of White River State Park. An easy walk from any hotel downtown, if you are looking to drive in they have cheap parking for a few bucks right by the visitors center as well as an underground lot. In the Military Park on the other side of the canal from the Indiana state museum you can see a quite and beautiful memorial to medal of honor soldiers. It is worth the 15 minutes to quitely wander and read the names of the men and women that have honorably went above and beyond the call of duty for our freedom. They have an extensive running trail system with very clear markers for distance and the bridges and paved spaces are clear and clean and there is modern art to look at everywhere. There are bikes for rent and segway tours that start here. There is a very nice visitors center with maps of things todo or see all over Indy and they have a great restroom facility. If you wander across the bridge toward the zoo you get a great view of the white river and of the end of the canal system that runs through the north end of the park. You can see IUPUI and the outer edges of the conservatory inside the zoo. I recommend this space to anyone passing through and looking for a break or for anyone downtown looking for something to do. Again I say this is one of the better urban parks I've ever been to.

text: All of that and a bag of chips... Okay, I'm not sure why I wrote that introduction. Well, I suppose I can segue into one illuminating story at this downtown Baggin's. I ordered the Unforgettable Baggin's, a sandwich composed of turkey, bacon, cream cheese, tomato, avocado, and alfalfa sprouts. I also got a drink with that. I handed my debit card to the cashier chick, she swiped it, and just after that moment, I realized that I wanted some chips, too. I quickly try to stop her and ask if I could add a chips to my order. Here's the cool part: she pauses, looks at me blankly and expresses to me that she already ran my card. I then reciprocate in kind by pausing, looking at her blankly and taking my card, which was being extended to me. I'm no master at reading body language, but I'm astute enough to see that this person was in no mood to run my debit card once more to add an order of chips. No "Sure, let me run your card again" or "okay, would you like to pay for that with this card as well?" Nothing but a pause and blankness. Oh, there was silence for a couple of awkward seconds. Granted, this occurred right at the peak of lunch hour as many business and legal types from the downtown area were streaming in, so it was pretty busy. But there were only a couple of people behind me, and there was another cashier manning his station. Needless to say, I just ate my Unforgettable. Speaking of which, the sandwich was prepared well and the ingredients were fresh. Baggin's does deserve some credit for being creative with their sandwiches. While good, however, it was nothing memorable. So while the food at Baggin's is just merely good enough to be forgettable a day later, the service certainly is unforgettable. No offense to anyone who is employed downtown in the finance or legal fields, but perhaps my cashier's eagerness to please is due to having to deal with douche-bag bankers and lawyers all day long. I would go back again some time and offer another opportunity to Baggin's to redeem itself, but I thankfully am no longer serving on jury duty.

text: I went here for dinner with the wife on a Sunday. We were in Nashville for a wedding and wanted to grab something a little nicer than BBQ. It had a 4 star rating on Yelp, so why not! We arrived downstairs, looked over both the bistro and the upstairs menu. We decided to go 'upscale' and be seated upstairs. We were told she could not seat us right now, and it would be about 45-60 minutes. Not a problem on vacation, we went to the bar downstairs and had drinks and an appetizer. I had a Jack/Coke and her a martini. I was impressed by the ice cubes, as they were the nonstandard large size cubes (actual cubes) which decreases the amount of watering down that occurs. We had the duck-fat fried tater tots, and they were fantastic. Three dipping sauces, so it made it feel a little classier than squeezing Ketchup out of a bottle. After about 20 minutes, the hostess came back and said they were ready upstairs. We didn't need the whole basket of tots, so we finished our drink and headed upstairs. Downstairs decor was very cool. Old school styling, subway tile, etc. Upstairs, the decor was very nice, low lighting, very classy with some exposed brick. To my surprise, there were only maybe 10 people upstairs, with seating for at least 50-60. I was very confused at why we had to wait. But figured maybe it was going to be attentive service and they were short-staffed or something. The service was a bit slow to start. They filled our water glasses fairly quickly and gave us menus. After about 10 minutes, he came back to take the wine order. This took a good 15-20 minutes to come back. Then he disappeared again, finally coming back to take the dinner order. Disappeared again... and probably another 20 minutes for our soups to come out. From there out the service was fine, with items coming up properly timed and drinks refreshed. From a food perspective, we both had the tomato bisque, which was very good. We were also brought a small crab and citrus taster which was also very good. This brought our expectations up regarding the upcoming meal. My wife had the roasted chicken with farro and some summer squash. It was pleasant, but nothing to get excited for. She mentioned that she shouldn't have gone with chicken, because who gets excited for chicken? I had a 14oz rib eye, which was recommended by the waiter. It was tasty enough, but a ton of fat. I understand it's a rib eye... but this was a bit over the top. It was cooked properly and was tasty enough, but for almost $30, I was expecting more. It also came in a weird little cast iron pot/dish. The dish was just deep enough to hinder your ability to cut the steak easily. Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. We took a look at the dessert menu, but nothing thrilled us so we got the check. It wasn't bad, $100 for 2 soups, 2 meals, 2 glasses of wine. We were discussing what we thought of the place and both of us said "underwhelmed". We were discussing being spoiled living in Chicago, but I don't know how much weight that holds. I've had amazing dinners in small towns and this just didn't cut it. I'm going with 2 stars, with them getting knocked on service and food. I still don't know why it took 30 minutes (and quoted 60) to get us seated in an empty place? We asked if they were busy and the waitress said "No, we usually book up by 2PM, blah blah blah" adding to the confusion. I just got the impression they were trying to make themselves more exclusive than they are. On food and pricing alone, I would have gone for three. It wasn't bad... but I wouldn't recommend it to a friend. If we had the half-star, MAYBE 2.5... MAYBE. I feel comfortable giving this 2. To be fair, the bistro area has potential. Similar food, but more upscale sandwiches / sides than a standard diner/bar. I would give that a shot.

text: In a world of scarce justice for millions if not billions of people, .05 cents worth (to make) of chips and salsa may not seem like anything, but try telling a man whose beloved wife died that's it's no big deal because thousands of people die every day. I was prepared to write a five-star review of TJ Flats, a restaurant I've been visiting for years, but they cheated me out of my free chips and salsa, which one can win by correctly answering their daily trivia question. The TJ Flats Trivia question of the day was, "Escape artist Harry Houdini died of what causes?" I knew Houdini died from being punched in the stomach and told this to the girl behind the counter. "Yes, but what was the *cause* of death?" I stared at her. "Being punched in the stomach." "No, the medical condition." Fans and friends, I poop you not, the next word out of my mouth was, "Peritonitis." "No," said the girl behind the counter, "it was from a ruptured appendix." The meat in the two tacos I ordered was cold. And the tacos came with chips, the EXACT same chips I would've received free if I'd gotten the trivia question right. But this wasn't about the chips anymore, it was about Justice. How many people know about Houdini getting punched in the stomach? Did you? I considered talking to a manager, but I (used to) frequent the place fairly regularly and didn't want to be known as the "Trivia Chips Jerk Guy" though I act politely at all times. I went home, depressed. I can take a lot of crap from this world, and do. Suffering is universal. But this whole chips affair was like meeting your dream girl and having her fart in your face. On purpose. Later that night I got on wikipedia and discovered that Houdini had died of PERITONITIS resulting from the ruptured appendix. So I was right all along. I seriously considered marching back to TJ Flats with a printout of Houdini's wikipedia article, but finally this seemed as stupid and trivial and insane as the trivia game itself. Imagine Gil Grissom from CSI poring over Houdini's autopsy report with a pretty 18-year-old girl in shorts. Just another Saturday night in Clearwater.

And now, he's open to trying some authentic Italian. Constrained by time we decided we couldn't make it into town for Melograno and so we settled for this Collingswood Italian BYOB. The service was friendly and efficient. The appetizers started the meal well. The wonderful fried calamari came accompanied by the standard cocktail sauce and a light green pesto. Although it was a bit greasy, the light, flaky breading surrounded moist and fresh squid rings and tentacles. The Insalata Saporis was a light bed of fresh greens in a light vinaigrette. The special octopus carpaccio, I think, sat too long in the dressing and was a bit tough. The main entrees for our family spanned a number of pasta dishes and a salmon. The best one was a wonderfully moist flavorful salmon with yummy fried zucchini chips and a bright lightly sauteed spinach. I ordered the interesting red beet, squash and sausage risotto, but it was overcooked, mushy, not creamy and not al dente. I was expecting an interesting combination of flavors with the unexpected pairing of beets and sausage, but there was no real complexity and the flavors did not mesh into something revelatory. Similarly, the duck ragu gnocchi was another interesting rarely seen combination, but the ragu overcooked the duck and masked any of it's flavor and the gnocchi were too large and mushy. The birthday boy's Maine lobster fettuccine in a cream sauce was well balanced dish, with the lobster meat just a tad overdone. Lastly the daughter's pearl pasta with shrimp was too salty with the shrimp way too overcooked and reminded me of the smelly preserved dried shrimp that my mom cooked - and didn't like. On the whole, it was a so-so meal, with the execution way off. I liked their dedication to authenticity and the interesting ideas on the menu. Would like to return to try again, hoping that Sunday night is when the owner-chef is off.
label: NEG

text: The Muse is one of the few 'all ages' venues in Nashville, and is also one of the worst places to see a show in town. I'm not sure if the former causes the latter, but hanging out with angry looking high schoolers definitely does not add to my enjoyment there. Maybe if I was my defiant 15 year old self again and wanted to hang out somewhere that would scare my parents into soiling themselves if they knew. But only just maybe, because I can still think of better places to do that around town. The Muse is located in a seedy part of town, and when I say seedy I mean that it is literally sandwiched between the largest porno store in town and a highway exit ramp and underpass. If your social circle is in need of dirty drunken bums, creepy porno store visiting middle aged men or snarky, under aged kids, then the Muse has you covered. The sound is pretty crappy, but most of the bands that play here can typically be fit into the hardcore/metal/screamo category with a few exceptions. I guess when most of the music is indistinguishable from itself you don't really need superior sound quality. Because the Muse is an all ages place, there's no smoking which is great, but there's also no booze. So if enjoying a drink while watching live music is your thing, you're definitely going to want to go elsewhere. The place itself is small, dark and dirty, though I've heard rumors they've been trying to clean themselves up recently. Due to the types of shows that play here, the crowd ranges from people standing stoically fixated on the performers to people moshing and flailing about wildly, with there never really being a happy medium. I myself like to enjoy the crowd enjoying the show, it adds to the experience for me, and its hard to do that here. One positive thing is that you get a lot for your money here if you really want to break it down. Tickets for shows here tend to run less than $10 and there is usually at least 3 or 4 bands playing on one bill. Add that to the fact that you won't be running up any bartabs, and you've got yourself a pretty cheap evening. The only good thing about the Muse being located next to Interstate 40 is that it is pretty easy to find, and convenient to leave when you're ready to bounce out of there. The parking lot is pretty small, and I don't suggest leaving anything of value in your car. There's nothing really else around the area to go to besides the porno store and its not a safe area to walk around in especially after dark so I wouldn't recommend exploring the surrounding area or even showing up here by yourself.

text: In the span of a 15 minute train ride, PATCO made me vow to start saying my prayers again every night, and possibly even start hitting Sunday mass again. Let me explain. Last Friday evening around 5:30, I boarded a westbound train with two other people. The train car was surprisingly empty, but I made a mad dash for the only seat that had a sports page sitting on it. Just as I started to get into the Flyers' injury updates, the lights went out. This seemed odd, but the train was still moving so I didn't think much of it. We went underground in Camden, and the darkness in the tunnels was quite spooky. As we approached the first underground station, the train slowed, but did not stop. Same with the second. So the lights were out, we weren't making stops and no announcements were being made. As we made our way out of the tunnel and onto the Ben Franklin Bridge, I text-messaged my sister about the situation and said that I was a little freaked. As we went back underground in Philly, I thought we would surely stop at 8th and Market, where I was supposed to get off the train. Again, the train slowed but did not stop. At this point, it is safe to say-- I WAS LOSING MY SHIT!!! Worst-case scenarios featuring gunmen and hostage situations filled my head. I abandoned the sports section and made my way closer to the other passengers. A lovely woman by the name of Susan comforted me when I expressed my concern for our safety. For that, I am eternally grateful. When the train started slowing to what appeared to be a stop as we got to the 12th/13th & Locust station, I stood up and announced that I was going to pry the doors open with my bare hands if I had to. Which is exactly what I tried to do-- only, the doors were locked. I felt like I was in a horror movie when suddenly, the lights went on and we could see the conductor walking towards us from the car in front of us, a confused look on his face. He opened the door and said, "this train is out of service!" To which all three of us replied (i.e., screamed) something along the lines of "well then why were we let on to begin with?!" peppered with many expletives (mostly mine). I shakily made my way above ground, grateful to be alive, grateful for the kindness of strangers and grateful that some taxi drivers don't mind driving drunk girls home to Jersey at the end of the night when they decide to pass on the train.

text: I have to concede immediately that I am a passionate fan of Franklin Fountain. I am somewhat fanatical about high-quality desserts, and this is the best ice cream place I have ever found. In response to Julie F: if you really think this unique, homemade ice cream is not worth more than Friendly's, please go to Friendly's so the lines will be shorter at my beloved FF! The atmosphere is carefully cultivated to authentically reflect a 1920s soda fountain, complete with such waifish, anachronistic, mutton-chopped/hairnet-clad staff that you'd swear they stepped out of a time warp. The foot-pedal water fountain outside, retro candy, and antique cash register are undeniably charming. All of that is beside the point, however. The star here is the ice cream itself, which is homemade by FF in small batches. You can taste the difference in the creaminess and flavor of the different varieties, which are clearly made with fresh, high-quality ingredients, yielding the best ice cream I know how to buy. The menu deserves major points for creativity as well, with thoughtfully designed sundae concoctions and old-fashioned sodas and phosphates (although I admit to never having sampled the latter, given my enchantment with the former). They are also happy to let you customize, which recently inspired me to swap Rocky Road for a combo of Peanut Butter and Chocolate ice creams in the Stock Market Crunch sundae, to delightful effect. The homemade peanut butter sauce (I have a jar in my fridge - it will change your life), crunchy salt pretzel morsels, and fresh chantilly made this monster sundae one for the history books. Other favorites: The Franklin Mint, with marshmallow atop refreshing mint chip ice cream coated with hot fudge, and the classic Broken Hearts Sundae with vanilla ice cream, fresh-cut strawberries and vanilla biscuits. I echo the comments on high prices, which seem somewhat excessive, although I always decide it is worth the cost. The service can be a bit lackadasical, but these people are dedicated to a quality product and meticulous, so I have accept it as part of the charm and pretend they just loaded up on Laudanum before stepping into the time machine on their way to work. My only quibble: I wish they would let you combine two flavors in a "size small," because I always want two tastes, but a "medium" is just too big for one girl (most of the time)! Franklin Fountain is unique and wonderful, and not to be missed if you are serious about ice cream.

For sandwiches, I tried the Quban (pork, swiss, mustard, pickles) and the veggie melt. They guy at the counter suggested white bread for the Quban and it was a good call. The bread was sliced thin, and was very fresh with a slight crisp. I thought the sandwich had great flavor and enjoyed every bite. The veggie melt had portabellas and tons of other stuff and was great on the wheat bread. The coleslaw that came it the sandwich was packing serious flavor and seemed fresh and crisp. It's not creamy at all, more tart and acidic. I was able to pick out an intact cucumber slice. I loved the comfortable low-key vibe in here, the friendly staff, and the reggae/ska playing through the speakers. Looking forward to coming back.

text: I might say 3.75, but the owner was super friendly Went here for lunch last Halloween. They had a special where you could get buy one get one free if you wore a halloween costume. Evidently I was the only person who wanted to cash in on this idea. So Papa Roux's is a Cajun joint. The got plenty of cajun favorites from etoufees, to gumbo to po boys. According to my co-worker, the owners of this joint are New Orleans natives, and decided to set up shop in Eastern Indy. AMBIENCE/SERVICE- Can't really comment too much on both as I grabbed take out, but the owner was really friendly. Seating looked decent, and it looks like they encourage their patrons to write on the wall. One other cool thing I saw is that they had a cow bell instead of a "regular bell" to get their attention. MENU- as I had mentioned before, plenty of cajun favorites. Not being too well versed in cajun food, I can't say that they have ALL of them, but they had a pretty nice mix- jambalaya, pork chops, po boys, dirty rice, stews, etc...They also have a number of vegetarian dishes which happen to be healthy as well (vegetables healthy? The hell you say). FOOD- for my buy one get one free I sampled the chicken and sausage stew and a spicy smoked sausage po boy. With each meal you get free sweet tea (until 3pm daily) and I got a side of the parmesan rice. While I can't say much for the parmesan rice, both entrees were indeed tasty. The stew had a nice spice to it- not SO hot, but a nice bite to it. The chicken and sausage were tasty. As for the po boy, I enjoyed that quite a bit as well. I'm normally not a fan of cole slaw, but the sausage and red beans worked really well with the slaw. OVERALL- gotta love the buy one get one free. Even without it, they have daily lunch specials, and most items are no more than $8-10. I do wish they were a bit closer, because I have a Yats down the street from me, and it's hard to rationalize driving past them to go eat here. I would say if you're in the area, check this place out for something different. Is it worth a 25-30 minute drive? If there isn't a yats near you? Yes. Chuck Norris Rating- 1000 years of pain strike!

text: Winston Churchill Square was a major investment by our city that was controversial a few years back, but I can now say dramatically improves the quality of our downtown experience. Churchill Square, since it was revamped, six or seven years ago, has become a hub for summer festivals and activities, including Taste of Edmonton, The Street Performers Festival and other smaller community events. As I write this, I am sitting in Churchill Square. On this glorious afternoon there are small pockets of people everywhere, sitting on the steps, park benches and in umbrella-covered chairs, soaking up the sun and the blues-folk beats of singer Al Brant, who is serenading us on this mid-week afternoon. To cool off, there are people splashing about in the fountains in front of city hall, and from where I'm perched I can see our new modern art gallery, shining in its sinewy metallic glory. There's a City of Edmonton home composting booth set up in the middle of the square and visitors can roll up their sleeves if they want and dig for worms in a pile of fertile soil. I pass, but enjoy the lookie. Things are thriving at Three Bananas Cafe, where business lunches are being conducted on the patio over mouth-watering oven-baked pizzas. I, myself, go for the cup o' grape jello, and enjoy its cool, slippery texture gliding down my throat on a hot summer day in E-town. There aren't all that many in a year, here, so I'm in the perfect place to enjoy it fully. Any spot you can get mini-donuts and kettle corn in the middle of the afternoon is A-OK to me.

text: A year has passed since our last visit to Coquette, but it was definitely worth waiting for . . . The five of us -- back in town for a conference PLUS the French Quarter Festival -- arrived at Coquette only discover that it was "Speciality Cocktail Night," and all their housemade specialty drinks were only $5! We were shown to the upstairs dining room -- something I didn't even realize existed on my previous visit! In contrast to the black-and-white tile floor and pressed tin ceiling, this has a hardwood floor, artwork on the walls -- it's a very comfortable room that felt "private" even in the presence of other diners. We began with cocktails. I had my usual Sazerac (excellent, by the way), while Lynn & Virginia had a "Ponchatoula Punch" (strawberry infused vodka, Amaretto, lemon and vanilla Dry Soda; quite good, a bit like Hawaiian Punch, but without the sweet finish), and Amy & Linda had a "Coquette Collins" (shochu, hibiscus liqueur, ginger liqueur, lemon, soda; light, clean, refreshing). Then, we moved onto a bottle of Champagne (Diebolt-Vallois) as we contemplated our appetizers . . . The Local Green Salad (with candied pecans, red wine vinaigrette and goat cheese) was fresh, flavorful and refreshing. The Pork Rillette (served with cornichons, piquillo peppers, Dijon mustard, and toast points) was one of the very best renditions of this dish I've ever had! The Fettuccine, served with a fresh yard egg, country ham, and fava beans was truly delicious. And the Roast Oysters -- prepared with fennel, Benton's bacon ragout and horseradish -- were just perfect! For our mains, we focused this time on the restaurant's seafood: Arctic Char (prepared with sweet pea risotto, asparagus, and a preserved lemon vinaigrette) was stunning; so was the Alaskan Halibut (with globe artichokes, niçoise olives and fennel), and the Black Drum (served atop shrimp and grits with collard greens) left all of us wanting more! These were perfectly matched with a bottle of the 2007 Domaine Leflaive Mâcon-Verzé. And for dessert? Well, we just had to get their beignets again -- this time paired with chocolate pot de créme and cream -- but we also had their chocolate brownie served with cherry anglaise and their vanilla panna cotta with blood orange, candied fennel and basil. Simply put -- fantastic! As far as our criticism of our previous visit, we never felt rushed or hurried. Indeed, we enjoyed our meal at a peaceful leisurely pace and a great time was had by all!

My friend and I shared the cheese plate which was fine, but aside from the sharp provolone with whole peppercorns (not a favorite) the others - gorgonzola, goat cheese and fontina, are pretty much staples in my fridge. Nothing too exciting, but very reasonable on the happy hour deal. We wanted dinner, but decided to split a bunch of appetizers instead of entrees. We ordered the grilled vegetable platter, calamari, and tuna mango maki roll. The grilled vegetables comes with onions, peppers, zucchini and eggplant. Unfortunately that's all it comes with, so if you're inclined to want to put your veggies on something, a fork is your only option. The flavor was very good, but eating a forkful of grilled onions doesn't do it for me. It did have two pieces of bread with bruschetta on the side, but the bread was really dry, and since it was already topped it didn't help solve the veggie problem. The calamari was fine - a little on the chewy side, but I appreciated the variety of sauces it came with. The maki was not like anything I (or anyone I know) would call maki. text: Philadelphia has a lot of gyms. Now more than ever there are new ones popping up ALL the time...there used to be a World Gym up on Sansom Street where now exists a bathhouse, and once upon a time, I worked there. This of course, meant that I also had a free membership AND since I was the opener on the weekends, I had a key and free reign to workout before or after hours. Still, I had a membership to 12th Street. WHY? Because it is THAT good. These days, one of the places I am employed offers a free membership to PSC Rodin. While this is a nice option to some stale periods in my workout life, I always end up back at my beloved Gayborhood haunt. I have also, in my poorer days, taken advantage of every free and trial membership in every gym in Philadelphia. And still, I remain here year after year. The Sporting Club, PSC, The Westin, Sweat...I will take my Gay Gym over these anyday. Why? Well, let me add up the elements here. 1. Cost. Their regularly running "specials" are low enough in price, and they offer different payment options for easier to hack dues. But their student discounts and special deals with local businesses are amazing. Their price among all gyms, up until recently, was THE LOWEST in the area. (then that $20 a month place opened up - but - no comparison there. 2: Amenities. The offerings here are awesome - Not that I take advantage of all the extras - like Basketball court, pool, dry/steam sauna, sundeck, TONS of classes at all different times (This has actually been steadily improving, too - more classes, different times and days...), A shake bar with many different protein powder options, as well as a bring your own powder option, which is only $2 to make a shake. You can heat up food in the micro, throw something in the fridge for a few hours (not storage, mind you - don't be a tool) Sit on the couches and watch the flat screen - It all feels like home to me. Maybe because I spend too much time there. 3. Maintenence of Facilities. You can actually SEE your membership dollars at work here. New equipment every seaason, speedy repairs on minor glitches, new snack/drink machines, and the cleanliness is unmatched. The only thing missing is the overbearing smell of bleach - because they use some really great solution of Fantastik for cleaning that I actually LIKE smelling... is that weird? I hope it's not weird... 4. Other members. So, I DID mention it's the gay gym, right? That being said, not ALL members are gay dudes. But the ratio is overwhelming and this, my friends, makes working out as a woman VERY VERY comfortable. One of the big issues being a young blonde is having to ignore stares and peacock behavior, and yes, even sometimes COMMENTS, from testosterone overflow. And it makes me want to turn inside out and run. Read: NOT MOTIVATIONAL. But the straight guys here are secure enough in themselves and insecure enough in avoiding the gay mojo that they stay to themselves. Which, really, is where they need to stay. 5. I COULD knock a star off for hours, but I won't. They are as good as any other gym in the city in that arena. Would I like extended hours on the weekends? Sure. But an 8 am opening ON Sat/Sun, and an 8 pm/7 pm closing time, respectively, is acceptable. They are 5:30 am til 11 most every other day (save Friday when they close at 10...Gotta get your party on earlier, right?) 6. Locker cost: Pretty cheap for a year or 6 months - of course the longer you rent one the cheaper, and I get to cram - I mean, store - half my life in one 12x12 cube. 7. Seven points? yes, we are up to 7 points here: The Camac Center in the back of the gym houses pretty much all you will ever need for your life. EVER. Massage, Hair salon, Esthetitian and laser skincare (you know - botox, bitches!), homeopathic services, a kids gym, and oh, who the hell knows what else is back there. Maybe Santaland and a lollipop tree. Next thing you know they will have housing available. 8. Last one - promise. Trainers - tons of them. Swim lessons. Boxing lessons. Freebies on a regular basis (once in awhile an announcement of "we have a few pairs of free theater tickets for this evening - first to come up to member services, gets 2 free tickets!" or free dinners/training sessions/guest passes with your membership, and promotions from local businesses stationed in the lobby. It's pretty great and ties you into a feeling of "community", which is probably the biggest draw for me at 12th Street Gym. I have tried to find better, my friends. I have been high and low - seen good things and bad things, even worked in places where I could have had it all. But I have been a member here for over 8 years. And I have no plans on changing that. Because really, gay gym boys are really really awesome eye candy. Just sayin'.

The rest of the treated area was growing hair the very next day. They advertise that a doctor is there to review all work, but the only person I saw was the girl at the front desk, who also performed the laser treatment. Like I said, she didn't know what she was doing. Although she instructed me to sign off on the paperwork, saying that a nurse had discussed the procedure with me, NO ONE ever discussed the procedure with me and I doubt there was even a medical professional in the office. Be warned! This is an unprofessional, fly-by night operation and they don't care about providing quality treatments to their customers.
