text: The staff at Kunitz shoes are extremely helpful (no sales pressure) and the selection of "comfort" shoes is extensive. Not many stores specialize in comfort shoes (hardly any), even though many of us require them for our daily lives. The shoes are expensive but that is because they are built to protect your feet and last a really long time. My shoes have been all over the world, they have been soaked in water, thrown around in luggage, and have walked countless trails yet they look at feel like new! Most important of all: Not one callous or blister!
label: POS

text: I'm no hipster - not that anything's wrong with that - yet I felt right at home at Hipster Home. I spotted a beautiful, molded wood chair up front, and sat. I took the store in: brightly-lit interior, relaxing music, stocked with a thoughtfully chosen selection of casual-yet-upscale furniture and accessories. Besides table settings and picture frames, I saw crazy, origami-esque metal folding chairs, a digital music iPod speaker platform, and eye-catching ornamental clocks. The average price point might be high for some, but they're not pawning off discount furniture, after all. Still, there were a few sale tags to entice! Dave, the owner, is clearly into wine, sharing bottles with his patrons; I was unexpectedly treated to a wine-tasting. (Sweet glass, too!) If you're seeking wine accessories, they've got those, including quality Riedel merchandise. My favorite item? A wall-mounted wine rack. Not into wine? Dave's always happy to chat and can help you find what you're looking for. Though I had to brave First Friday crowds to get here, it was worth the effort. Armed with a credit card, I secured a few shotglasses along with a "green" greeting card. Browse their wares online, then get your home furnishing on and pay them a visit!

text: This museum could probably be better described as an amusement park. There's a Ferris wheel on the roof (which i didn't get to ride due to some rain! Boo!), a 10-story circular slide, a big thing of *balls* to play around in, a rope swing, and mazes and *mazes* of deep-down caves, sky-high cages and installation art-type things to crawl through! I was told that this museum used to be an old shoe factory. I love factories! They also have an outdoor area where you can cool off ('cause you WILL get sweaty!), eat hot dogs and drink beer. I never thought I'd say this, but... knee pads would come in handy here.... ..as you will be crawling through millions of small spaces :) I had the good fortune of spending a few hours here with some lovely people on July Fourth, 2009, and we lost each other on several occasions, as one of us would inevitably disappear down a rabbit hole! This place reminds me of the movies Edward Scissorhands and The City of Lost Children...such a trippy place! Playing is so therapeutic...I've never been to a museum quite like this and wish San Francisco had something similar. Just think of all the awesome first dates that have taken place here!

Open 7 days a week 9am-11pm. You'd think everything in the Italian Market is closed, but they keep the light on. Other details: Nice Mexican beer selection. Great service. Spotless. Homemade tortilla chips and two kinds of scrumptious salsa while you wait. Tasty carnitas and tamarindo (tamarind drink). Off-the-charts fajitas. Excellent prices. Telenovelas! Free delivery. text: Environment/Service: 3 Stars Food: 2 Stars Booze: 2 Stars Summary: The location is central to downtown and the beer is better than the Ram (doesn't say much), but the food is barely passable. Avoid. Environment/Service: The location is great (for them), with plenty of tables, window views of the downtown street corners and an upstairs area for overflow seating. The service is slow and inconsistent but not overtly bad. Food: Fair to poor in general. The hamburgers are big and obviously frozen and pre-made, their salads are simple and out of a bag, their pizzas are passable, but you will not be impressed by the selection (think Applebees) or the quality. Booze: This is the greatest travesty. You're a brewery, but your beer is bad. Tried several different selections, all were muddy, with strange aftertastes, the Pale Ale lacked any sort of hop backbone and everything seemed to have been made in giant quantities without an eye for the craft or for detail. In any decent craft-brew city in the States (think Boulder or Fort Collins in CO, Seattle WA, Portland/Bend OR), this place would be out of business in a week.

text: One of our tenants had a leaking washing machine that was running water onto the unit below it. Called these guys since they were closest to the area and fast with appointments. They charged $30 non refundable fee for coming out, and if we did work, the $30 would be deducted off of the bill. Jim came around and said the hose was clogged and the transmission was broken. He wouldn't touch the transmission because he said he thought it was under warranty with Sears for 5 years. I asked if he could just drain the hose and unclog it right then, but he was unwilling to since he didn't have the proper tools (a hose clamp) and it seemed like he really did not want to get wet. I told him since the hose was an issue, why not just do it now so I don't have to call back. Jim replied with there was a chance that the trans would be too expensive that I may just want to replace the whole washing machine and if he came around later, the price would reflect the $30 I already paid. He also mentioned that I could tip the Sears person $20 bucks and maybe they'll drain the hose for us. Basically, he was being lazy. I had Sears come by and they said the hose was clogged, had nothing to do with the transmission. Got it fixed at a premium price, but the issue was resolved. He clamped the hose and it was fixed within 20 minutes, plus he didn't get wet. I called back Phil's Appliances to see what recourse I had to getting back the non refundable fee since I was given a bad diagnostics. If Jim just cleared the hose, I wouldn't have to call another repairman. The secretary was super sweet, but then she transferred the phone to another repairman. He wasn't the one who came around so I retold the story. He kept implying that the transmission could still go out in the next couple of weeks, but he was just trying to cover his co-workers incompetence. I asked what I should do, if I would be forced to write a bad review and then that's when the cursing flew in. He swore and swore and then hung up the phone. Unreal. I caught my emotions together and called back and found out that the person I spoke with wasn't even part owner of the business. The secretary then forwarded my number to the actual technician and got a call later from the person who serviced me. He kept asking why I didn't call him instead of the office. He also kept telling me that the transmission going bad was his best opinion. When I asked about why he didn't just use a clamp to cover the hose, he got hissy and kept telling me that was his best opinion to not to touch anything until I got the transmission fixed. Save your time and do not go with these guys for appliance repairs. His best opinion wasn't the correct opinion. If he wasn't lazy and just took care of the hose when he was there, I wouldn't be writing this review. Save your $30 and give it to your 4 year old nephew and ask for his best opinion. At least your nephew will try to fix the washing machine.
label: NEG

text: Everyone knows that the meat is excellent here, but if you're not a huge steak-eater (which I'm not) the salad bar is more than a meal. I've come here before and done the full meat deal, but for someone like me (a petite girl who isn't into steak enough to eat her money's worth), the salad bar at half the price ($25) is totally worth it. I'm not a vegetarian, but I looooooove veggies and Fogo has some of the best, along with small meats, cheeses and breads to round out the meal. Probably the best salad bar I've ever experienced. Asparagus stalks as thick as your thumb, hearts of palm that melt in your mouth, thinly sliced prosciutto, the freshest of fresh salmon, and a giant wheel of perfectly aged Parmesan that you want to dive head first into and just start gnawing. Plus a variety of salads (chicken, mushroom, caesar), fresh baked bread, and all the typical salad ingredients. Everything is amazingly fresh with servers constantly bringing out new and replacement dishes. I doubt anything sits there for even an hour. And the service was no less stellar for me, the salad bar patron. Fogo is truly a topnotch establishment. Bonus - they brought out a complementary slice of chocolaty fudgey mousse cake for my bf's bday. That's not so special in and of itself, but we didn't even tell them it was his bday... they noticed a birthday card on the table, asked who's it was, and promptly brought out the cake. Bravo! I always applaud cake.
label: POS

text: This place DOES live up to the hype. The Paesano was everything I had hoped it would be. The brisket on it was amazing and the bread was nice and fresh. The egg, cheese and peppers rounded it out perfectly and made it just messy enough to give it some street cred. The Panelle was good too, the chick pea pancake was really good, and it was served on a flat bread type wrap, the perfect sandwich for my little lady. I was a bit disappointed by the Crispelle, it was too mushy and filled with apricot jam, it wasn't what I expected. If in the Italian Market defiantly stop here for lunch, but skip the Crisplle, and walk down Christian street to Isgo's Pastries for some amazing desserts.

text: Decided to hit Joe's up for some breakfast - especially after seeing their ad on TV. I ordered the veggie omelet and the BF ordered the pancake sandwich. Pretty simple breakfast fare that went horribly awry! The waitress, bless her soul, was doing the best she could - I think there was a combination of a language barrier and her being new and unfamiliar with the menu. When she brought out our meals, the BF realized his eggs were scrambled not over-medium, as ordered. The waitress apologized and took the plate back, leaving my omelet and no utensils for me to eat with. No biggie, I sat and waited for the corrected eggs to arrive and decided to pick out some of the crispy potatoes on my plate. Waitress comes back with not only the corrected pancake plate but a new omelet for me - OK, whatever! The BF said that the waitress then took my original omelet and gave it to someone else! (So sorry, to the recipient!) Anyway, to get down to the basics of why I gave Joe's one star: - Veggie Omelet was completely inedible! Didn't even look like an omelet, more like a scramble. Eggs were overcooked, veggies were sub-par and frozen. - Potatoes or their "home fries" were greasy and old and new potatoes were mixed together. Some mushy and some super raw. - In the end, they still didn't cook the BF's eggs correctly. The came out over-hard, not over-medium. (As Gordon Ramsey says, "if you can't cook a simple egg, you might as well get out!") - And the clincher, the breakfast cost $30! As others have pointed out, you don't expect gourmet quality food or linen table clothes at a diner. But what you do expect is good food at a reasonable price! For the prices, Joe's could and should be serving fresh ingredients, cooked and prepared well. There really is no excuse! Sorry, have to throw this parting shot in: The woman's bathroom was hideously dirty!
label: NEG

text: We went on a Monday, so no crayons, w/butcher paper, no lights in the backyard. But it wasn't crowded and we got our food quickly. Our server recommended the coconut shrimp, and I'm so glad we took his recommendation. They were fresh and delicious. The shrimp are delivered fresh every day and prepared on-site. No frozen coconut shrimp here! We ordered homemade ginger brew, which was thick and pulpy with fresh ginger. It was quite strong and spicy--not for the faint of heart. If you can't handle a lot of ginger, stick to the bottled ginger soda. For dinner, I got the escovish fish filet. It too was hot, peppery, and strong with vinegar. I hiccuped for a while after the first bite (spicy food does that to me), but it was great. I've has escoveitched fish before, but this was not as wet. Just different. The side dishes of Jamaican cabbage and rice & peas were so good! Coconut milk in the rice makes all the difference, I think. My friend got the jerk chicken (dark meat) which was also delicious. There was a lot of meat on that plate for a leg and thigh combo! The sauce was thick and tasty, sweet but spicy. We also shared some 'greens, greens, greens,' and I'm glad we did. Collards, spinach, and calaloo with coconut milk is a combination made in heaven. By the time we finished (yes, we ate it ALL) our generous portions of dinner, we had no room for dessert. Our server told us they bring the desserts in from Jamaica. They had lemon cake, rum cake, chocolate cake, and more. Next time I'll remember to bring half of my food home and save room for dessert.

text: The "Don" is a big pink palace. It's very much like the Royal Hawaiian or the Beverly Hills Hotel. It was a WWII hospital and it's a national landmark. It's really gorgeous. I mean, how can you resist a pink, beachside hotel--literally steps from your room is the quiet private beach, warm Gulf waters, smooth sand. Lovely. Too bad I was here for a work conference. Bah humbug. I somehow lucked out and got a little suite for my stay. It was lovely. Bathroom was very long and narrow, which was kind of weird. The water pressure was amazing though. I like a nice stream of water and not a trickle, so I was pleased. Room service is good. Didn't eat in any of the restaurants. They just built a spa and my co-worker said it was great. Note, that MF is correct...nothing is within walking distance. If you only want a pool, the beach, a spa, a retreat, than this is a lovely spot. If you want something happening, go elsewhere.

text: Fairly subpar in a city with many other sushi options. The uni was awful here - either extremely not fresh or sprayed with Windex-flavored juice. I ordered 5 rolls, Agedashi tofu, and ice cream mochi (3). Everything that looked interesting seemed to include avocado and cucumber, which could be acceptable but not particularly creative. Flavor was lacking in every roll unless doused in medium grade wasabi. The pumpkin roll was an interesting creation but still lacking in much flavor. The fish wasn't particularly fresh but not terribly old either. On the plus side, the Agedashi tofu was fantastically prepared and presented very well. The mango mochi was an unusual offering with an excellent wrap and flavorful ice cream. The green tea and red bean mochis were less pleasant and I felt they had freezer burn. Service was reasonable, water was refilled constantly. Décor very simple and not distracting. Agadashi tofu win. Mango mochi win. Everything else, not so good. Cheers.

text: There are a few reasons I've been going to this pub lately: it's on my way home; it has a big patio facing west with hours of afternoon sun exposure for tanning (with sunscreen, of course) while I enjoy a pint or two with friends; the poutine is cheap, cheese-bathed and delicious (even if it's not real cheese curds, just mozza) and there is free Internet. Yes, I love being able to put my feet up and chill out while still staying connected via Wi-Fi. You never know when the urge to Google will arise. Standard basic fare. We were pleased with the basics and will probably try the whole fried fish next time and branch out a little into some of the less basic dishes. Drink orders were the sangria soda and homemade lemonade, which was not too strong, definitely fresh, and had subtle hints of some other flavors. Wasn't quite sure what it was. But it's not standard lemonade. I love steak tacos, but few places do them well, so I usually opt for carnitas. --- will definitely go fully steak next time I'm here. Delicious. Took a menu. text: Five stars it is. Not because I enjoyed myself... but because I know that next time I will. Yes - of course I'll explain. After years of admiring the old Oyster House decor (which I miss) on my way to Nodding Head - I finally had reason to step inside. We were waiting for a large group, so my gf and I passed the time at the over crowded bar - but a glorious 30 minutes it was. Good bar tender, hand pumped selections on the beer menu... and a find drink menu. I was very impressed - and VERY much looking forward to my meal. Our crowd showed and then we were seated. Then this amazing bread and menu showed up. For a while I just couldn't decide what I wanted - but the server was very helpful with that. I ended up in two directions ordering. First - My gf, her brother and I ordered several types of oysters apiece off the raw bar. Second I got the grilled salmon. I was even more looking forward to my meal. The raw bar was great. I wish I had sat at the actual bar with access to more variety on the hot sauces - but overall it was the first raw bar I've enjoyed eating from since I left New Orleans. All I wanted in life was for that amazing fish to hit the table in front of me. But then something awful happened. The fish was ok. Just ok. It wasn't bad... mind you - if maybe a little dry. But just ok. Problem was that by the time I had the fish... after the great bar and raw bar... my expectations were set too high. I also tried the scallop pan roast my gf got and was disappointed... but that may have had more to do with the amazing scallops I had just had from my Aunt during the Garry Maddox bbq challenge the weekend before. So why 5 stars? Because next time I am gonna go back, sit at the bar near that hand pump with that bread and get a salad and a half dozen shooters then attack the raw bar like it's my job. You people will find me crying with glee in an alley... and I know it. So rather than give it four now - I'm giving it the revised five I know it will get from me in a few weeks.

text: Regency is a little out of the way for most city dwellers, but it's worth the stop. The interior isn't as cozy as some other spots I have been to, but it still doesn't take away from the charm of the place. Lots of seats abound, with a large couch near the entrance. The place was nicely decorated, with a few paintings on the wall. Some of which I think were for sale, but sorta pricey and just okay. The menu has lots to offer. They have breakfast in the morning, with breakfast sandwiches and oatmeal and such items. There are hot and cold sandwiches, salads and lots of pastries which are made daily. I haven't had much of the food, except for the pastries, which I can say are delicious. The coffee and specialty coffee drinks are pretty good, they take their time to make it right. So on that, service was great. Everyone was nice in general. The place doesn't get that busy. The word must not be out that there is free WiFi there. text: To help appreciate the Santa Barbara Courthouse, go to some other city's courthouses. Probably you'll see some crappy, utilitarian, 1970s building, 50% of the reason people shudder when they get a summons for jury duty. During the hot days, the architecture keeps the building cool. The Sunken Gardens are lovely and a host to many events (currently this summer UCSB are screening Universal Monster Movies!). And the view from the Tower is one of the best of Santa Barbara. text: I had my heart set on a custom dress for my wedding. The perfect stitch seem to provide quality dresses at affordable prices. Sadly, my wedding dress ended up being my biggest regret. I contact TPS about five months prior to my wedding and asked if they could make a dress for me. I sent sketches and pictures of what I wanted and was told it wouldn't be a problem. At my first consultation my measurements were taken and Melissa also offered to make me a custom corset "with the same lace material as my dress" it was going to cost $125 but she promised it would be an heirloom. My wedding dress was suppose to be around $600 after two "consultations" I finally saw an outline of the dress (cotton mock, not the real thing) and realized it wasn't the right form. In order to change it to what I originally wanted she charged me an additional $250. I paid because it was a month away from the wedding and I was still hopeful that the dress would look beautiful. Two weeks before the wedding I still hadn't even tried on the actual dress. The day before the wedding I finally got to try on the dress but there were still alterations that needed to be made. That's right--I didn't get my wedding dress until the DAY of my wedding. She also had her assistant call to complain that I had "waited too long" to pay my final $125 (even though the dress wasn't even near finished). Melissa made snide comments at my mother because she didn't start to cry when I tried on the dress (probably b/c it looked BAD and my mom was pissed). Finally, on the day of my wedding I went to get my dress. I did a final fitting w/the corset she had made...the corset was too big. She tried to pin it up so that it would fit that day but it provided NO support. It was basically as if I was braless. And the promise that it would be the same lace as my dress was not true. She used completely different material. And to top it off, the "hooks" she used were just thread so no surprise it broke before I even got to the venue and was able to wear it, it was basically useless. The dress itself looked like cheap lace, it was rough and looked horrible. I was embarrassed to wear it but had no other options. It's taken me over a year to write this because it makes me sick to my stomach to think about how horrible I looked and felt. Additionally, Melissa was very condescending and unprofessional. If I could change anything about my wedding experience it would be the dress. Truly, I would have been happier finding a dress at any other store. AND this wasn't a "you get what you pay for situation"--I spent almost $1000 on this attire and that is poor quality that I received. Maybe you need to her friend to receive good service... PLEASE if you must have a custom gown--go somewhere else! And have an airtight contract of services and a plan B.

text: I live just a few blocks from the Memphis Taproom and I am so glad that they have become part of the neighborhood. My husband and I heard rumors before they opened and were super excited. I don't eat red meat so I can't tell you from personal experience. Their salads are fantastic and are usually more than enough for a meal for me. Their suicide rings are amazing and more than enough for a few people to share - and hot hot hot. I could go on and on about the food but I won't - everything has always been spectacular. I think what they really need, though, is an extensive martini list. That way they could make use of all of those tasty vodkas. Next time I come to town, I hope they'll stock some Krol vodka for me, because that stuff is the best. There will be a next time, oh yes.

text: We have been in search of a home in St. Petersburg and I have been amazed at the wide variety of reactions we have had when speaking with realtors about this. I phoned Marilyn Voorhies about a home that she had listed to see if the owners might consider leasing the home (a strategy that has worked well in the past to locate homes that my be available). She replied with a curt, "no, sorry." When we told her, "we are looking for a 3-4 bedroom home in Old Northeast or nearby neighborhoods," and asked if she knew of anything, she responded sarcastically, "Oh really? Well good luck with that!" and promptly hung up. I was so bowled over by this rude response, I felt compelled to write a review on Yelp. Conversely, I spoke with Alona Dishy and Catherine at Vann Zimring who do not typically work with renters, but very kindly suggested a few promising properties after I contacted them with the same inquiry. Regardless of whether a potential client is renting or buying, it never hurts to just be kind and help if you can. You never know when that renter may turn into a buyer as we will soon.

text: I've lived in the neighborhood for 3 years. They have the location and they use it to their advantage. The place is dirty most of the time and the owner is a jerk. if you try to complain about the quality of the food or the overpriced beer, he will have an excuse for you. Don't even think about using the bathroom unless you don't mind port-o-potties. It's as if they don't realize that they have competition and the people in the neighborhood surrounding them have choices and money to go elsewhere.

text: Craig was our private chef for a 3-day business retreat for 15 people. He served us breakfast, lunch and dinner, plus everything in between. Summary: AWESOME The food was just great. Thoroughly enjoyed (and devoured) by all guests. Highlights included a fantastic Mexican chicken salad, incredible homemade potato chips, and some great hearty sandwiches that even the biggest eaters couldn't finish. He is a magician with fish! Where Craig probably best excelled was reading the mood of the crowd. Everyone always congregates in the kitchen, and he was great at adding to the conversation and knew when to step away as well. Though we laid out a thorough menu plan, he continuously gauged the mood and appetite of the group to modify what and when we served. He was tremendously flexible in modifying the menu and how he served it (both casual and formal meals), which couldn't have been easy with a big crowd and working 12 hours day to keep us fed. He was also very cost conscious and came in exactly where he said he would, with few leftovers and no one ever going hungry. The service was stupendous, and somehow the kitchen was always spotless. No one ever washed a single dish. Craig and his team also did a great job handling those with dietary restrictions, whipping up great creations many of the meat-eaters started to crave as well. We had a tremendously successful event, and the Practical Chef was a huge contribution factor to things going so well. A+ job! Thanks Craig!
label: POS

text: Red Lobster. Red Lobster. Send Lobster Right Over. Where is the Red Lobster of my youth? The all-you-can-eat snow crab legs. The deliciously buttery cheese biscuits. The crisp, fresh salad. The crowds. OK, maybe not the crowds. I don't usually choose to go to RD. My parents are usually the ones who want to go there. But I went here last night with the wife and kids. I don't know if it's the economy or what but it was unusually dead. Every other time I've visited this particular location, it was at least a half hour wait to get a table. We were lured in by the promise of delicious, endless shrimp. Just a few points: 1) Endless shrimp ain't so great. They tend to be tiny, cast off pieces that aren't considered worthy of making it to the big leagues. 2) They were "temporarily" out of the shrimp alfredo. Maybe it was wanting what you couldn't get, but that sounded like the most appetizing of the 5 different varieties. 3) Everything seemed sticky. It might have been the diners who were there before us, but even the dessert menu felt like it a 2 year old drooled all over it. The biscuits came out flat. At least they were hot. The salad didn't seem as fresh and crisp as it usually is. All the food was overly salted. I tried to stay away from the water...I really did. But the saltiness of all the shrimp forced me to down a few glasses of water. I probably wouldn't have eaten much more what I did (I'm not telling how much I actually did eat) but still, if it were a bit tastier, I might have been able to stomach a bit more. I've saved the best thing for last. Our waiter was incredible. I know it wasn't crowded but he was attentive and very outgoing and energetic. Oh and one last thing. The kids' meals stink. If it's not fried, it's not anywhere near appetizing. The fish and the grilled chicken were flavorless. My kid wouldn't touch them and he's usually a great eater. Boy, I hope the economy picks up so more people can go out and get the salad turnover higher so we can all get fresher food.
label: NEG

text: Sandwiches have always been delicious, and the sweet potato fries are great. The shakes and smoothies leave a little to be desired, but prices are reasonable for the quality. text: I heard plenty of good things about this place so I'm not quite sure whether Viet Kitchen has switched owners, chefs or management but this place pretty much bombed in my book. Banh mi was ok at best, I've had better. I don't know what it was but the hoagie was definitely lacking something that I've seem to have found quite often in others. I noted a huuuuge red flag when they brought out my cha gio and gave me a small bowl of DUCK SAUCE. Yes, you read that correctly. They did not provide me any nuoc mam to dip my rolls in, but instead they gave me duck sauce which also tasted like apple sauce with salt. How lovely. It was the same with my friend's order of goi cuon (summer rolls)- they brought out peanut sauce with the order but the nuoc mam was no where to be found. This sure as heck isn't customary for Viet cuisine. Also, I've gotta note that my cha gio (spring rolls) were definitely not traditional viet spring roll- they were small for their size and looked pretty out of the freezer. I'm pretty much planning on avoiding this place for a long while and I'll probably avoid Viet Kitchen even if it happened to be the last Vietnamese restaurant in the philly area- that's how disappointed I am with the establishment.

text: I grew up in Hawaii. Then my family moved to Japan. And I've hit more sushi restaurants in Vegas and LA than I thought possible. I've been to some with more creative menus, some with maybe better ambiance, and some with some tasty food (always a nice touch...), but this place...it's definitely better than what some have called "Santa Barbara's best sushi. I'm going to plan a trip up the coast from OC just to time it right for a crazy dinner here. This place has insane food. I'm usually "roll guy," even if that means soy paper wrapped hand rolls. I like the creative rolls, but there's so much good stuff here on the menu, I only got to one roll (Eskimo roll...I like salmon and this had it--quite good). I don't see it on their online menu, but get the Rock Shrimp Popcorn (or something like that)...and ask for extra sauce. Perfect amount of spice in there. I wanted to dip whatever I could find in that sauce. I was almost grabbing edamame from the neighboring table as a conduit for that sauce. Local's Only--yes, I've seen others review it and they nailed it. This thing is amazing. Yeah, it's on fire (what your trendy, loose sleeves/cuffs, btw), and has some crazy scallops concoction on risotto. My friend ordered the "Chef's Special." Didn't see that on the menu...but I'm going to try to sound cool and order that again when I go there next time. It was gooooood. I hope my friend goes next time, too (and pays), b/c this stuff...although good, would have garnered that 5th star from me if it were maybe 20% cheaper. Value? Actually, yeah...so I guess I shouldn't complain. I need to get back soon because there are about 20 rolls on that menu that looked worth trying. And I need more of that sauce.

text: So, positives and negatives: Positives: Decor is nice, very well appointed and nicely done It is quiet as you get into the inner sanctum of the restaurant It is upscale but not stuffy The Margaritas were good, especially as I am not a Margarita fan. I must say it was refreshing, and did the job of getting me slightly intoxicated while not having an overwhelming taste of tequilla The Ceviche was good The guacamole was good The bad: The main entrees were bland and did not have much snap or flavor. the shrimp were overcooked, the meat was flavorless, like it was frozen and thawed in water, the rice was red but tasted nothing like it had tomatoes or any chile in it, even though it smelled of tomatoes and peppers. The entrees were warm. That's just a pet peeve of mine. We were one of maybe 20 people in the restaurant at the time, as my wife and I went for dinner after work. It was not crowded. I do not know why the food was warm. Warm food to me, means it was prepared too far in advance of us being ready. The Nicolatas in the salad tasted like it came from a can. It had no texture, was awefully briney, and had no flavor, versus some mild flavor. and it was slimy. Like thick korean Seaweed used in soup, but the seaweed has flavor and some texture. I remember Cactus as being subtle, but this was just bad. The Filet Mignon was not a Filet, it was a poor cut of tenderloin masquerading as a Filet Mignon. It lacked the flavor or tenderness of a Filet Mignon. The low star count is due to the quality of food versus price of food ratio being off. I don't like spending 30 a plate for mediocre mexican food, that is not as good as the lunch truck I can go to and spend 6.00. The entree was just that unappealing, and we go out to restaurants for the food, not the atmosphere. There are other places I like to go for that, but I don't expect to find good food at those places. I do expect good entrees at a formal sitdown resturant. Would I go back, yes. I would go for a drink and appetizers after work with some friends. I would not see myself going there for a main course sit down type dinner again. The interior is nice, well done, and a pleasant place I could sit, drink, and have some side dishes. If it was a Tapas type place with no main course/entrees, I would give it 3 stars. Again, even with the entrees, the quality to price ratio is off, but I guess the ambience helps to off set that. They should either change and be a Tapas bar or make better quality main courses.
label: NEG

Salt n' Pepper is open pretty late. Overall, recommended.

text: "Lorenzo's Trattoreeeeeeah" with a THICK Italian accent is how I always read it in my head... no I'm not racist, it's just more fun that way. I would say though that it was a bit heavy; after a few slices, it was difficult to fully enjoy the rest. I'd definitely recommend this restaurant for those who want a peaceful night on The Hill with some good pizza. I'll have to update again if I ever go back to try their pasta dishes.

text: I found Zavino to be sort of well, average and while I think it has some merits Stella is a much better choice for high end pizza, bang for your buck and overall experience. text: My mother and I were in Tampa last weekend and this was the first place we dined. I found out about Oystercatchers from restuarant.com. We LOVED it!! From start to finish, our meal was relaxed, delicious and a true dining experience. We started with three different kinds of raw oysters from their raw bar. The oysters are served with a house-made cocktail sauce, horseradish and a red wine vinaigrette- I put all three on mine at once and MMMMMM, awesome. This was my first time having raw oysters and I'm now in love. Deeply, deeply in love. I fear they may not be as good back home in MN, but I'm keeping my fingers crossed. For entrees, my mom and I shared a wood-grilled black grouper, wood-grilled sea scallops and had lobster tails added to each of those. Both were served with orzo pasta and vegetables. The sides were good and fine (I actually found the orzo to be very creamy and perfectly cooked and a nice break from the seafood-fest). The grouper...oh my goodness, the grouper! I'm drooling now just writing about it. This was my first time having grouper (lots of firsts for me at this meal) and I am just as in love with it as raw oysters. The scallops were cooked perfectly and were quite large. The lobster tails were seasoned very well; the only problem was they were a bit on the cold side when we received them- we weren't sure if it had anything to do with the draft coming from the window we were sitting by, so we didn't say anything to our server as it didn't matter that much- it was still quite delicious!! I just dipped mine in the melted butter and enjoyed. There were four sauces served with the seafood- a chili jam, mango chutney, key lime caper butter and scotch bonnet tartar sauce. I didn't try the chutney, but found the other three to be great. The chili jam was very flavorful, but was almost too powerful of a flavor to go with fresh seafood (almost seemed more appropriate for a less "American" dinner). The keylime caper butter and scotch bonnet tartar were my favorites; I can safely say that my mom and I didn't leave hardly a drop of either! Neither overpowered the seafood, they just added to the deliciousness of it all. Desert- my mom is a huge key lime pie fan and she found theirs to be spot on. She doesn't want it too tart or too sweet; she said it was neither- a perfect balance. She also mentioned how flavorful and fresh the raspberries served on the side were. I had a bite of her pie and also found it to be tasty. My desert, however, was the queen @#$% of all deserts- the gourmet Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup!! Hooo boy, this was awesome!! Phyllo dough cup, peanut butter custard/mouse/something, chocolate sauce, crushed peanuts and carmelized bananas on the side. MMMMMM-MMMMM!!! I'm a huge peanut butter cup fan and this just took the combination to the next level. I also have to mention that our server, Mike, was fantastic. He offered great suggestions, answered our questions knowledgably and kindly and had an all-around pleasant demeanor. He checked in just enough, wasn't pushy about anything and really contributed to the overall dining experience. Thanks, Mike! You rule! The ambiance of the restaurant was very nice. I tend to like darker, mahogany-type joints, but I didn't mind the white, crisp, clean decor of the restaurant. It felt cozy and being right on the bay made for an excellent view. If I'm ever in Tampa again, there is no question that I will dine at Oystercatchers again.
label: POS

text: This is like my last desperate pizza place that I call to deliver because I forget how boring the food is and and I'm too lazy to go from Brewerytown to Luigis (which for some reason doesn't deliver .5 miles away). I still order from here, and for the most part everything is just mediocre. From the subs to the poppers its all just bland. The pizza crust reminds me of the prefab ones you can buy at the supermarket and the slices are usually very greasy. One time I went there to get a cheesesteak (much better than their pizzas) and a girl complained because there was glass in her sandwich. Despite all this, for some reason, I still order food from here. Why?
label: NEG

text: I imagine this place could potentially be worth the stars everyone else is giving but on my initial encounter, they're fortunate to get the second star. I went for dinner to celebrate an occasion for my girlfriend's co-worker. They were supposedly given ample notice to accommodate the party. The (lack of) service certainly was not prepared. Everything felt ok at first. We ordered our food, and everything just went downhill. We waited, as a group, for about 45 minutes before anyone got their appetizer. After about an hour, people were finally getting their entrees. About an hour after the first entree was served, the last one was served. It appeared the kitchen was cooking per couple instead of lumping things together to maximize time. Service on a Friday night was oober slow. They had one waitress for the place, knowing there was going to be a big group of us. I think they even had one of their kitchen staff come out to serve dishes as well. Bottom Line: THEY DID NOT PREPARE FOR A LARGE GROUP. Not to mention, the food was more of a lunch menu than a dinner really. I would imagine that's how this place would thrive. I felt forced to choose something that wasn't too lunchy for dinner. Perhaps if I care to venture back for lunch, I may update. However, my return looks unlikely.
label: NEG

text: I came here for dinner a while back and had a nice meal. I opted for two small plates instead of a main entree. The first was a spinach salad with toasted pine nuts and strawberries in a lavender vinaigrette. I've never had this combo before and it was simply fresh and tasty. My next course was the mushroom ravioli sauteed in a butter sauce. I found this small plate to be the perfect size (about 7 ravioli). The flavors of this dish were delicate, subtle, and smooth. I would like to come again and sample their other dishes! The interior of the restaurant is dim with colorful paintings and mirrors. They make most of the tiny space they have. It's a pretty cosy place. One thing I must say is that their dessert is lacking. We ordered the bread pudding which was too dense and bland. I hope that gets resolved soon.
label: POS

text: This place has the potential to be a great place to go "where everybody knows your name" kind of place... I love going to places and being greeted by name... to be known as a regular. Comfortable bar, comfortable seating, more-interesting-than-average staff and amiable owner. It is beyond Karaoke, it is a piano bar. If you wanna get up and sing, they let you. The staff performs between serving tables, but I've not been when it has been busy, so they get to sing a lot. If you're a customer and get to sing; watch out, you might be asked if you want a job as a singing waitstaff ;-) A great place for a celebration or dinner... I wish the food was a bit more extraordinary. I know people who've worked there, and how it can be a crazy busy place (especially around St. Patrick's day), but it needs the support of locals to thrive, and to do that it needs to improve the food and professionalism, without losing the personal touch that makes it fun to go there and hang out. It is a bit expensive to just go after work to meet up with friends for a happy hour type of thing; and I don't think that is the customer they're going for -- but perhaps making it a bit more casual to capture that crowd would increase its visibility, bring more people in and more importantly... keep them as regulars. In the meantime, I'll be remembering it more often as a place to go -- it is still a quiet place to be able to have a comfortable conversation, a drink, and fun with the staff.
label: NEG

text: My favorite Vietnamese place in town. 9 out of 10 times I go there I'll get a #51. I highly recommend it to anyone trying Vietnamese food for the first time. I also recommend trying the Vietnamese Iced coffee. The service is acceptable, not the best in the world. Watch out for water refills and splashes everywhere! A very popular lunch destination between the hours of 11am and 1pm, busy, noisy, lovely.

text: Visiting from Washington and heard Juds was the place of the one pound burger. No way-Im not going to be able to take down a 4 inch frisby-that burger could feed a family. I did have the Bacon-Cheese burger and small fires. This was probably the best burger I have ever had and the french fries were awesome and unique. The help was friendly and it was busy-the burger was hot-very hot- the fries were hot- very hot. Really a great burger and fries for under 8.00. Ill be back...

The menu on the board is organized by meat or veggie sort of and the menu you get to look at is organized by type of dish (chow fun, lo mein, etc.). I'm pretty much a fan of Golden Bowl. My friends go every weekend almost. They're most definitely Golden Bowl's biggest groupies. The staff know us pretty well. My friends usually get the same thing every time, but whenever I want to get something different, the staff is pretty friendly to suggest something.

text: Ate here for a tennis team dinner and it was very good. we had to wait about 45 minutes for a table on a friday night with a party of 10. the restaurant is small and has an outside eating area that almost doubles the capacity. excellent thin crust pizza! we ordered two thin crust. one with pepperoni and mushrooms, then one with pepperoni, onions, sausage and olives. i didn't get a chance to try the thick crust, but it looked very good. the thick crust had pepperoni, sausage, green peppers and onions. from what i heard, the thick crust is very filling. definitely recommend this place.
label: POS

text: I went in, and my first impression was that it looked a lot like Baja Burrito in Berry Hill. Hmm. There was no line, so I went right up to the counter, and the kitchen layout was the same. Knowing that if there was a connection, I changed up my order. I got beef instead of chicken, got a "chipotle" tortilla. I got a medium hot sauce; I even asked for extra cheese, again, hoping it would add flavor. Unfortunately, just like at Baja Burrito, there was just no flavor at all. I ate the whole thing, and it was like eating just the rice, beans, and a plain tortilla. I don't see how they can take fresh vegetables, spices, loads of cheese, and grilled beef, and somehow turn it into British food: a flavorless pile of mush. It's a shame that there's not a Chipotle, or perhaps some sort of local place like Mr. Burrito Fresh isn't in Franklin, because they would kill. It's not bad, but it's nothing like the good stuff you can find elsewhere.

text: Let me start by saying I consider myself a sushi snob. I've had all the best sushi in New York, LA, San Francisco, Seattle and Las Vegas and i've tasted every type of raw fish you can imagine. My buddy has been taking us to these all you can eat sushi spots in Reno for years (Sushi Club, Sushi Pier, Sushi Pier II, the one inside Atlantis) and of them all, Sushi Moto is the best. The fish quality is always amazing, the staff is helpful and courteous, the music is top notch and the decor is fun and funky. The menu for the all you can eat is very extensive with probably forty items you can select from. The Sushi Club used to be my favorite before it changed owners. ______ Update: Went back to Sushi Moto yesterday and once again, the food rocked! $21.95 for All You Can Eat Sushi and they definitely came out with the short end of the deal. I am not an Uni fan, but it's on the AYCE menu if you're daring. The Spider Roll was not great. If you can get in with the guy in the doo rag, ask him to make you the Sushi Moto Special Upside Down Shrimp. Or try the Hamachi. So gooooooooooood!!!

text: Amazing scotch selection. It's a nice uptown bar. There's a pool table out back, and the guy who plays piano is pretty decent. This is a more laid back mellow bar.

text: I make my family eat here every time we go to St. Louis. The beer is great, the food is great, and I'm always so stuffed by the end of the meal I have yet to try the sticky toffee pudding that everyone swears by. I guess I'll have to go back again. Also, the artisan cheese and fruit tray is excellent.

text: In the world of super-sized movie theatres, Harkins in South Tucson really is the shining star of theatres. Off I-19, the facility is easy to find and finding your movie won't require a GPS. The staff is really helpful, always lending a hand with movie questions or the location of your flick. The restrooms are fairly clean and were well-stocked with paper towels and hand soap. The concession stands have a wide variety of movie food - popcorn, candy, sodas and plenty of other high-fat munchies. The theatre also was tidy, and the sound was incredible. For a good flick, this 18-screen in the desert is a winner.
label: POS

text: Really. What can I say? This is an institution on its own level. If you're AT ALL snobby, even a closet-snob: don't go here; you won't like it. If the thought of sharing a ridiculously cheap drink with a Tulane Law student sitting to your right, a palpable stripper to your left, some individuals of questionable character in the background, and possible illicit substance use occurring somewhere in the vicinity appeals to you - you will be fine. Walking into this place is kind of like crawling through a magical, bacchanal wardrobe out of some seedy-after-midnight-version of the Chronicles of Narnia. Some say that it only appears at night when you're drunk, but I will just go ahead and say I've seen it sober. Nevertheless, the feeling of excitement and anticipation that overcomes you when you see the lucent glow of the giant christmas wreath hanging on its door as you near the premises is indescribable. Don't listen to the ignorant, snobby elitists: go ahead and sit on the couches - you won't get crabs. Do it, venture in - and don't be scared. It may be slightly intimidating at first, but you'll feel quite at home in no time. Grab a seat, sit back, and lose your sense of lucidity in a place where time, perhaps even the outside world itself, just doesn't matter. At some point it will hit you, the sun is shining and a new day has dawned over the bayou - at that point the choice is yours: accept defeat and go home, or order a bloody mary. Thank you, Snake & Jakes.
label: POS

text: My favorite little cafe (just on the outer cusp of the Quarter) to just hang w/o obnoxious crowds all over you and use the internet. Opens early. Friendly, cool staff. Tasty breakfast. Offers other snack, coffee and hell they even have a full bar.
label: POS

label: NEG

text: This is one of my go-to places for a good grilled cheese! They make it big, and greasy. Pros- Seated promptly, friendly service, and pretty clean (I mean, there has to be some amount of a heavy, greasy, sticky feel to the place to make it enjoyable as a 50's diner). They give me a pretty big helping of sauteed mushrooms that I like to top my sandwich with! The mushrooms are a little more watered down than I'd like, but still good. Cons- More often than not you wont get a juke box seat. And if you DO get a juke box seat - more often than not the thing will be out of order. Which you will find out AFTER you have already deposited several coins in an attempt to get it going. If feel like that's one ot the main reasons you would visit Mels! Also, they tend to skimp on the yummy fries. But I would suggest this place to anyone who is craving grilled cheese or a milk shake..... or fries..... that they don't give very much of.
label: POS

text: Paradigm's decor is modern chic; more often than not, the patrons match. I've never had to pay cover here (unsure if they ever charge). The venue space isn't huge and it can get crowded fast, especially around the bar. As the night goes on, folks will distribute more, moving to the dance floor. As you may have heard, the unisex bathrooms have see-through doors which fog when you lock them. It's a good policy to lock the door when weeing, unless you like it when people accidentally (or "accidentally") follow you in. Friday night, the talented Aiden Scott (http://www.djaidenscott.com/) played hip-hop and funky house. He was so freaking kickass that my friends are STILL telling me how great he was. He kept everyone dancing from 11 PM to 2 AM. (Saturdays there's no DJ, but the place pipes music to keep loungers entertained.) Our server (Stephanie) was friendly and down to earth. While we were moving about, she asked if we wanted our drinks brought to the table or bar. She even suggested a tasty shot for our group. At the bar, bartenders Rory and Nani (sp?) served us. Nani offered a shot with Jameson, sour mix, and lime juice, which wasn't half-bad. Rory made a sweet pineapple upside down cake shot. Recommended as a nightspot (but not a restaurant) - check it out!
label: POS

text: I took my elderly friend there for dinner tonight, and was definitely disappointed. At first glance, I was impressed due to the decor and the size of Azie. However, the service was SO slow! It took ages to order and for each course to arrive. We were left with the impression that they were stalling to make the place appear busier. My friend ordered a Stoli on the rocks, which took 15 minutes to arrive. This is not because they were just busy: Our booth was facing the bar, so I could see the bartender and servers just hanging out. Then we ordered our entrees, which were ridiculous in terms of the length of preparation time and value for money. (A side note here: I live downtown and go out frequently, so I am comparing my experience with many other restaurants in various price ranges.) My friend's sea bass came out first, and it looked really good, and she really enjoyed it. The fish was $28, which I feel is on the higher side, but not too bad. My friend is 88 and a slow eater, and she was more than halfway finished before my sushi arrived. The waiter didn't even come over in the meantime to apologize for, or even acknowledge the delay! Speaking of my sushi, it left much to be desired. The $10 Azie roll was tiny, about an inch in diameter. The vegetable roll was good, however I am used to the sushi rolls being cut into 6 pieces and there were only 5 pieces of the vegetable roll, each under 1/2 inch thick. Basically, I'd say that the sushi is too expensive to be worth going back, and the service was so slow I'm not sure I have the patience to go back.
label: NEG

text: Beware that they use extra small to-go containers so the portions you get are much smaller than average. I took a regular sized container there and they said they would have to charge me more to use that one. I refuse to be overcharged for under portions of food....I will not go back! Also they are expensive for a food court joint. Be ready to spend about 10 bucks or more for an under portion meal with drink and still be hungry after your done eating.

text: I ate here Saturday night. It was no problem getting a last minute reservation at 7:30. I can understand why. It wasn't bad by any means, but it also wasn't a place I will make a return to. It was just blah. I tried the hand roll chef's selection. It was 3 different hand rolls that were ok. Nothing special. One was tuna, one salmon and one yellowtail. They did serve a generous portion of fish in all the sushi dishes, which was nice. The spicy tuna roll was the best thing we had. The worst thing was dessert. We had the molten chocolate cake which was a cold chocolate cake. This didn't make much sense to me since the definition of molten is warm/hot. Service was ok. I guess nothing really stood out. They didn't have many interesting rolls or entrees. Some of the things were on the spendy side while there ordinary rolls were quite reasonable. I would rather go to raw, zento, uzu, pod, or morimotos any day before zama.

PS: Don't forget your popped collar when going to this chachi infested meat-head bar.

text: As another person put it, the food here really is what you can expect from a chain restaurant. I went here for a birthday party (not mines, thank goodness) with about 8 other people. We shared a couple of appetizers, including a spring roll type with avocado in it. Not bad, considering deep fried things hardly ever go wrong. Got a couple of drinks, basically got what every other chain restaurant makes, premixed mixers tasting really artificial with just a little bit of alcohol. On to the entrees, I got a seafood pasta dish which was okay until I found a chunk of beef in it. I don't eat beef, or any other red meat or chicken, at that. And dishes should never be cross-contaminated like that. I flagged down a waitress, and she wasn't sorry about it. She took it and later some manager type person came and asked me to tell him what was wrong. He said things like this "should not happen" - well right! they shouldn't! but he wasn't exactly sorry either. They obviously comped my dish, but for the rest of everyone else's stuff, consisting of either deep friend appetizers or pasta ala oil, the charge came to be much more than it was worth. The only halfway redeeming quality of this restaurant is obviously the cheesecakes. Which are pretty good and packed well to-go, since we didn't want to spend anymore time there.

text: My boyfriend and I went there for my birthday. We had spent the weekend up at Hearst Castle and drove back to LA. We stopped in Santa Barbara and found this place The food was decent and a bit more what we like, but we both decided it was not the best. It was kind of bland. I blew out the candle and pushed the plate to the edge, the waiter came back and said you do not like, and I was like no. He said he would let me choose another dessert, and so I did. It was unfortunate. :( Overall it was a good ambiance, but its a "you experience it once, and that's all you need."

I tried ebi; then California roll; and then the rest is history. A friend of mine recommended Mikado saying it was probably the best sushi place he has ever eaten. What did I know? I had nothing to compare it to. So I tired it and I was hooked. The display of items, the cleanliness of the restaurant, the variety of choices-Japanese, Chinese and ever "ese" you could imagine; plenty of seating, friendly waitstaff ..all in one place and all at a reasonable price for all you can eat. Lunch prices during the week are $15.00 for all you can eat; Dinner is $26 during the week and slightly more expensive on the weekends. They also have reduced children menu prices. So bring your appetite without breaking your bank...this is definitely one to experience.

The place was also much nicer than I expected; glad we had decided to dress up! I had the caesar salad and it was great (and huge). For an entree I had the bistecca steak with a potato gratin and asparagus. Everything was perfect, and the portions were large enough for me to be enjoying everything again tonight. The steak was the most expensive thing on the menu - $16.50, so their prices are very reasonable. The service was very good as well; we were in the back corner but weren't ignored. I would highly suggest Luciano's as a great place to go out with friends as a slightly upscale place without the cost. (Also, be forewarned: they do not accept Mastercard.)

And that's just the wine... In the mood for some delicious cheese and meat plates? Perhaps a yummy gourmet cupcake? How about a goat cheese, sundried tomato and pesto torte??? You can get all that and more both dine in and to go. Jill has a lovely, intimate space where you can enjoy a glass of wine and a munchie plate with friends or your significant other. There's also always great local art on the walls, fun weekly events (like FREE wine tastings at 5 pm every Tuesday) and always something new for you to try!

text: This was my third experience at a brazilian steakhouse. Having been through the experience before, I was definitely excited to try Fogo de Chao. To start, the salad bar was much smaller and had less variety than other places I have been. This is not to say it was bad, just that it didnt live up to expectations of similar restaurants. When the meat finally started coming, the first few pieces were delicious. Then we waited. And waited. And waited. I think that the room is beautiful but it is shaped strangely for this restaurant. We were tucked away in an alcove where I dont think the gauchos could see us. At other places, I have had a line of gauchos standing by. Here, we had to actually ask for more of them to come by. It kind of diminished the thrill a little to have to "order" the food. Isn't that what the green button is for? When we finally had more meat on plate, this is when the disappointment really started. No matter what the type of meat was, it was charred on the outside and rare on the inside. I usually prefer my steaks cooked medium, and I understand that this isn't cook-to-order, but I would say the majority of people do not like meat that is cool to the touch and bleeding. All told, I was really excited to have a gluttonous feast of meat on a sword. The lackluster salad bar, the slow service, and the raw meat, however, made this an underwhelming experience.
label: NEG

text: AAA (the American Automobile Association) is a great organization. I've been a member for a long time, and I don't plan on changing that now. Still, I've long been disappointed with the competence of the customer service representatives they employ. This goes both at the High School Road location in Indianapolis and at the Mission Valley location in San Diego. In a word, these people are often idiots. I could go on for days with examples and anecdotes, but allow me focus on just one as a representative case: Last Thursday, I went to the Hoosier Motor club desk and asked for a map of New Orleans. Not surprisingly, they had a map from the "Vicinity Series", which shows the area around the City, but not a detailed city map of New Orleans itself. This is understandable. I'm sure this isn't exactly a common destination; and so AAA can be forgiven for not having every map of every city on hand. But here's the kicker: When the idiot who was 'helping' me said "I'm sorry sir, but we don't have that map available." I responded by asking "Thanks. But do you mean that you don't have it here, or do you mean that AAA doesn't make it?" Reflect on that for a moment: This is a simple question. But it has important consequences: If AAA makes such a map, but the HS Road location simply doesn't have one on hand, I can order one online or get one from a AAA location in the city of my destination. But if AAA doesn't make it at all, I have to follow a very different course of action -- namely, getting a non-AAA map of New Orleans when I get there. But really, seriously, no exaggeration: This ever-so-friendly-and-smiley waste of oxygen couldn't understand the crucial difference. Apparently, subtleties like "Do you have it?" versus "Does it exist?" are lost on the imbeciles who work at AAA. This isn't the first time this has happened. And this isn't the first time that my attempt to ask such a question resulted in a waxing poetic about the likelihood that, yes, somewhere on the planet, I'm sure you can find a map of just about anywhere ... but my question is, can you find one at a AAA? AAA desk people also seem to lack an even basic understanding of simple geography. Listen, geography isn't a necessary skill for ALL professions: I don't require it of my barber, my doctor, or even a nuclear physicist. But let's face it, travel advice is part of what AAA does. And if you don't have a brain and don't know even the basics of which cities are where, you should work at Trader Bucks.
label: NEG

text: The beer selection was good and the ambiance was nice, but the food was an utter disappointment and deal breaker. I ordered the twice fried chicken based on all the hype, and all I could taste was salt with some honey glaze. Think KFC thighs dipped in salt and refried with honey on top. The fries (although salty) came with a curry ketchup mayo sauce that was very good. The beer and fries are the reason I'm giving 2 stars instead of 1.
label: NEG

text: I am not a fan of C'est Cera. Maybe my perception is wrong but I do believe that this boutique caters to older women. Most of the tops, jackets and pants I picked up from the rack looked too matronly. text: Down a long drive off a country road in Chalfont, stepping foot into Illg's Meats is like being transported to 19th century Germany. The shop is a must-go if you are a food nut. Besides having an absolutely mouth-watering selection of top-quality fresh meat and cheese products, they also have a tremendous assortment of food stuffs ranging from what seemed like 19 different kinds of sauerkraut, imported chocolates, breads, preserves, spices and seasonings, etc. Being a German meat shop, a large contingent of their product is pork. The loin, smoked meats, scrapple, and wurst I have gotten from Illg's have all been phenomenal. Illg's Meats is where I always go to get a nice big bone-in shoulder roast for my special pulled pork. They also do have beef and poultry products but my personal experience is only from having bought pork products from their store. And if you're searching for that hard-to-find smoked tongue, headcheese, or bloodwurst, Illg's is the place to go. Another great thing about Illg's is that although they do have a commercial distribution side of their business--which undoubtedly is their primary revenue stream--they are very responsive to requests from the individual consumer. Whether you need 50 lbs of bacon for your restaurant or just a half pound of smoked pork loin, Illg's will take care of you all the same. In a time when most people buy their meats wrapped in plastic and styrofoam by some guy in a factory two and a half weeks prior, I am always pleased to go to Illg's where the employees know and understand their product so well. They will not only help you select the best cut for your intended use but they are always quick to offer advice on how to best prepare and cook your meat. It is also important to note that most of their products are "all-natural" without the associated "all-natural" price tag that you find at, say, a Whole Foods. A fresh cut of meat that was slaughtered the day before and has never spent time in the freezer really does taste better. Chalk one up for the independent butcher. During the holiday season, Illg's is especially neat. At that time of year, Illg's will outfit their store with decorations and have a few tables set up that they pile high with all kinds of German Christmas knick-knacks and treats. When I stopped in the week of Christmas one time, the place was absolutely packed--there must have been 30 people squeezed inside the little storefront. Many of the customers crammed into the little shop that day were speaking German amongst themselves, as well as with Illg's employees. [Some advice: if you plan on going to Illg's for that special cut of meat for a holiday meal, do yourself a favor and call 2 or 3 days in advance so they can set aside your product and you won't have to wait in line. They don't have a constant supply of animals all the time, so when they run out, that's it.] It's great to still have an independent family-run butcher shop around. Illg's offers top-notch product at a very good price and the service has always been great. Definitely worth a visit.

text: My job sends me to a new convention center roughly once per year, and the Pennsylvania Convention Center is one of my faves, for sure. The PCC was recently refurbished, and the investment shows. Most convention centers look like giant concrete warehouses, but the PCC has oodles more charm than that. Coming in from the main entrance from Market St, you're greeted by the absolutely massive and breathtaking "grand hall" with what looks like a wire roller-coaster suspended overhead (alas, it's just some artwork). This room is a dramatic backdrop to an otherwise utilitarian space. On the other side of the hall is an escalator up to the main convention space. Lots of rooms here with excellent acoustics. The exhibition space is at the back, with several football fields of real estate in which you mingle with various vendors, chat up poster-presenters, hand out business cards, and do whatever it is what conventioneers do... What's more interesting than the PCC is the location. It's literally perched *above* the Reading Terminal Market, so a quick trip downstairs provides easy access to countless lunch opportunities. As a bonus, it's located on a Blue Line subway stop and is a short walk to just about everything Center City has to offer. (You'd think that locating your city's convention center close to downtown would make sense, but too often it's located out in the boonies. I'm looking at you, Boston.) Unfortunately, the staff here was useless at helping me find anything. What else is there to say? Oh -- there's a Dunkin Donuts in the lobby. Yaaaaaaaay.

I ignored it until my family came to visit me and said that they *had* to see it. I'm so glad that we did. The mosaics, the architecture, the life-size replica of the Pieta, the basement museums...they're jaw-dropping. Breathtaking. I can't really express anything else about it other than to say GO. I mean, the Pope visited; if it's good enough for him... My stepmother said that she's been to Italy multiple times and never saw a church as beautiful as the Cathedral Basilica. It really is a treasure, inside and out. Bring a camera and be sure that you catch a guided tour--it makes an impressive establishment even more so.

text: I hate to be so harsh to a local landmark, but time and again Hannegan's has earned my distrust. I've eaten there quite a bit because I work nearby and I keep thinking it can't be as bad as I remembered. It's so deceptively appealing on a nice early summer day to sit outside and enjoy the ambience of the Landing. Do not fall into this trap! The service ranges from not good to mediocre on almost every occasion I've been there. The servers mostly neglect to fill your glass and it takes a long time to get the bill. Today's experience was actually the best service I've had there, but alas... ...no service could make up for the food. My Greek salad was knife-cut and had obviously been sitting around, as the edges of the lettuce were all brown. Too bad they didn't bother to wash the lettuce (!) before cutting it up, because I kept getting mouthfuls of grit. A Greek salad generally comes with Feta crumbles, which this one did, but...either the Feta was moldy or else they mixed in some bleu cheese, which I hate. Either way, I avoided it. And the pit-filled kalamata olives. And the dressing was just incredibly....greasy. I've had a lot of meals here in the past and none are consistently good: too salty, served cold, bread sometimes stale, meat too fatty. The only thing I've had that is consistently good is the tortilla soup, which is just the right mixture of spicy and tomato with plenty of corn in it, but even that is served warm instead of hot. It was a beautiful day and we were in a hurry, so we gave it one more shot. We're both sorry. I understand that the dessert is good. If you're stuck on the Landing and everyplace else is too crowded, maybe a bowl of tortilla soup and a dessert here would suffice.

text: A particular morning found me a dejected, poor, unfortunate soul with no promise of fortune and no care in the world. So I wrangled up my favorite Bay Area heathens, Dusty Muffins and Winnie Bago. "We need a change," I urged. "We need to kick these small town blues and dive deep into the heart of something sinful, degenerate, and downright depraved." With a nod and a sock, Dusty mounted his hog and tossed us eagle monogrammed leather jackets. "Lasso up your gumption, Sharon and Winnie, we're hightailing it to the biggest little city in the world." And so we descended upon the Peppermill. Italian busts, Julius Caesar, a bronze fountain in the swimming pool, poolside pina coladas, flatscreens in the bathroom, and more bikers than you could fit in a sombrero. We were slingin' 5 dollar chips with reckless abandon, chumming up to the dealers, and striking gold. Our money won was twice as sweet as money earned. When you're in Reno, there's just no reason to leave the Peppermill. It's got more class than Venice. Just like taking an Italian voyage to the Bahamas. That or straight to hell.

text: Definitely sub par to Pat's steaks. I tried both in a row, and there were a few things about Geno's that I was wary of from the start. The cheesesteak - not worth the time I spent waiting in line. The bread was correct (Philly bread that was so soft w/o falling apart), but the meat, which Geno's brags is better quality, was very chewy and had been fried in long strips. This means that when you bite into it, your teeth won't always cut the chewy meat properly, and you will end up dragging out a large piece of meat. I much preferred the meat at Pat's where they chop up the meat into small pieces and fry with oil. text: Mother's Restaurant is a place that every city deserves to have, but only New Orleans is lucky enough to have. Mother's is a gem and absolutely worth trying anytime you visit The Big Easy. Mother's is located in a historic building that is (conveniently) across the street from the W Hotel on Poydras. Your going to wait in a line, probably outside in the heat, no matter what time of day you go - so just prepare yourself. We managed, so will you. As soon as you get inside, start checking the menu so you are ready to order. Because once you get near the counter the action begins and everything moves fast. Everything on the Mother's breakfast menu is done just right. I recommend Ham & Cheese, with a homemade biscuit & some southern grits. Then add a cup of red beans & rice or jambalaya on side - you don't want to leave without trying it. Aside from the great food, the restaurant and staff are totally are worth the trip. Their system for delivering your food is one I've never experienced anywhere else. You order at counter and when you pay they write something the copy of the receipt they keep. Then you find your own table from an array of rooms. Then you wait a little bit. When they serve your food, you'll see the description (of you) they wrote on your receipt at the counter. Our group had "blue shirt", "stripes" and "moustache". The servers just weave through the restaurant until they find someone matching the description on the receipt. Not the most efficient system, but seemed to perfectly fit New Orleans - and it added a humorous element to the experience. Best time to try Mother's: breakfast, brunch or early lunch. It will cure even the meanest New Orleans hangover.

text: When I was a kid, I lived in a secluded area of the suburbs. We had 4 or 5 parks nearby, but no kind of commercial business in comfortable walking distance. Ardmore and Cityline were nearby but both a hike on foot. How I longed for a McDonalds or a 7/11 to be a block from my house. I was envious of friends who could see a Wawa from their bedroom window. To think, that I could have a Slurpee by just walking across the street was mind blowing for me. Sure, the world opened up for me when I started riding my bike alone and then when I got my license, but it was still a hassle. Now Im grown , and I live in an area where I can see the hustle and bustle of the commercial area, right from my front steps. One of the places I can see from my place, is the Hot Spot Diner. Sometimes I go to Hot Spot alone for breakfast. Its real good, as far as diners go. For about $10, I get a heaping plate of breakfast food ( bacon omelette, sausage, homefries, toast, coffee). Its always served fresh and quickly. The service staff (almost all middleage women who between taking orders and bringing out food must flirt with the many elderly gentlemen in the place) are always friendly and efficient. They seem to know when you want to chat and when you dont. As many diners are, HS is run by greeks and it shows from the panoramic photos of greece on the walls. It always seems clean and well run and theres always the same hostess/cashier at the door (does she ever take off?!) A quick note for families. Diners are great places to take the family. I have very picky kids but at HS, theres always something they want and they are giddy when they realize they can have pancakes for dinner. Sometimes when we come as a family for dinner, im also tempted to get my omelette meal but the words Reuben and Patty melt usually extinguish that pipe dream. Its cool that I can almost see my place while eating at HS. Would it have been good enough for me as a kid? No, its way too boring. I would have needed something where candy, fast food or toys were involved. And I have to say, that now, as an adult, being so close to the stores is not as cool as I thought it would be. Id much rather be back to where I was near 4 parks and 0 stores. But I guess thats life.

text: 4 stars on the Reno scale. I wasn't really expecting much from this place but it wasn't bad. I got salad which was decent enough. I got the balsamic vinaigrette dressing. It came on the side in like a tiny like jug. It had all kinds of herbs in the bottom flavoring the vinegar and oil. I had never seen that before, nice touch I thought. The steak came with vegetables and a choice of potato, I chose baked. The waiter brings the food on a cart and dresses the potato at the table, another nice touch. I don't normally get sucked in by that kind of thing but here I just fell for it. The veg was haricot vert and carrots, steamed I think, with some butter maybe. That was the only weak link in my meal. The steak was very good, very tender and cooked just the way I wanted. The potato was huge and satisfying. The GF had clam chowder instead of salad. I found it way too thick for my taste. She had mashed potatoes instead of baked. Those were not good. They were piped onto the plate with star-shaped piping tip and set up like a mound of spackle. They tasted OK, but the texture was awful. Overall I have to say that I was very happy with the meal here. The wine list had enough selections by the glass. The staff was incredibly welcoming, helpful and friendly. That 4 stars is on the Reno scale. Lots of casino restaurants have awful food and this place seems to being doing their best to buck that trend. In the bay area I would give them 3 stars. If I ever go back to Reno and stay in one of those 3 hotels, I'll be eating here again.

text: Another BBQ place in South Philly is always welcome; there's a general shortage of good BBQ in the city, and when you get the craving for it, nothing else will do. I think Percy Street has a lot of potential, but it's not yet my cup of tea. The atmosphere is great- long wooden tables and chalkboards, exposed beams and big windows, very casual and relaxed. Love the paper towels at the table, you'll need them. Drinks, especially their cocktails, are solid- the Jack & Ginger is a perfect summer refresher, and they don't skimp on the alcohol. Service was fast, efficient and pleasant. Unfortunately, it's the food that felt lacking to me, and this place is a restaurant. The mac and cheese was the shining star of the meal; hot, cheesy and delicious, with toasted cheddar breadcrumbs on the top adding to the texture. It's well worth using up two of your sides in a combo to get it. The greens were good if not great, and the coleslaw was refreshing but not memorable. It's the presentation and whole setup of the meats that is a little off: meats arrive sliced (ours were oddly lukewarm) and wrapped in butcher's paper, with a side of white bread and sliced raw onions. We were told this was "in case you want to make a sandwich." First, if I wanted a sandwich, I'd have ordered a sandwich- like the ones already on the menu. I had no desire to assemble my own, especially with such lackluster bread and toppings. Secondly, while the brisket was tasty (but dry), the pork belly was ridiculous. Floppy, tasteless slabs of pure fat. A little different from what I'm used to, to say the least. In the end, I think this restaurant and I just have an ideological difference on presentation, and the acceptability of Wonder Bread appearing on a twenty-dollar platter. It's their right to disagree- they do have a lot of other good things going on, like the drinks, mac and cheese and dessert- the apple cobbler was wonderful, gooey and warm and packed with fresh-tasting, sugary apple goodness. I may not be back here for dinner, but dessert beckons.

We told the staff that it was there and that it would probably relieve itself either on our table or on one of us. Eventually it relieved itself on our table.
