That is just called poor customer service. She basically just lost out on selling about 8 scones (in two minutes). Instead, he went to Bongo Java. Eh, no need to patron this place that doesn't care enough about its patrons to open the doors just a few minutes early. Lame.

text: I love this place! If you're lucky, you can find designer brands at a reasonable price before someone else snatches it. The other day I spotted a beautiful Kenneth Cole winter coat, but I didn't have enough money for it.

text: There are several signs of a good motorcycle shop: First, the majority of the staff actually ride, and actually participate in the riding community they sell and service. Secondly, they should never be open on Sunday. Thirdly, they should be prepared for whatever you can possibly and realistically throw at them. On these points and many others, Reno Cycles does and well deserves the title of "motorcycle shop." I can say that I've had nothing but overall positive experiences here. From the first quarts of oil purchased with a free weather report and where to expect to ride safely (it was the middle of winter and yes, I was riding), to their first St. Patrick's Day run, to their head mechanic digging through scrap parts after the shop had closed to find me a much-needed kickstand spring (and not charging a dime).

text: I live in Wawas in general. This one is disgusting though. The people who work here are slow as molasses. The lady's behind the sandwich counter take no pride in making their sandwiches.

There is one called the Joon roll that they have since renamed, sorry don't remember the new name but the perfect combination of sweet and spicey. The friendliest service, both the wait staff and especially the chefs. The only reason this does not get 5 stars is I have had Masaharu Morimoto serve me at Nobu years ago in NYC and that is a whole other level of sushi.

And they use these blue cups that make it look like they've given you alot, but it's all smoke and mirrors. You'll see what I mean when you try this Yogoratino.

text: Definitely a more casual and more appropriately-priced Brennan's creation (esp. considering the location), but no creativity was lost in putting together the menu (which can vary). Our server was fantastic- knowledgeable, friendly, and really let us relax on a busy Saturday night. We started with the corndogs which I probably could have crafted an entire meal out of - large tiger shrimp lightly battered/fried with tasso and topped with a spicy pepper jelly butter. From there I had the Turtle Soup which is easily a top 3 in the city. My wife had the pecan spinach salad which I thought was tasty and a good portion for $8.50. Muscovy Duck was my entree and was simply divine. The wife had the Blue Crab Pound Cake as her entree and I must say, it was pretty interesting - not as a meal, but certainly something I would order again to share with another couple- it could almost be a dessert it's so sweet. We can't wait to go back and try the shrimp and grits - which looked amazing. We're knocking off a star as I felt the interior was a little 'worn' and dated - it reminded me a little of a casino from the 90's that looks like it could use a good renovation. That may seem harsh, but for $25-$30 entrees, one expects either a nicer interior or dimmer lighting (and fewer kids).
label: POS

text: Yes, I've had better but when you want no-nonsense, regular old sushi and you are on a budget then this is the place to go. If you want zen-inspiring decor and designer rolls go elsewhere. The staff is always pleasant / accomodating and the sushi chefs put out the food at a reasonably good pace.

text: There are reasons Asian Fusion has a bad reputation-- it's unoriginal, inauthentic, overpriced, and tastes mediocre at best (why is it always so sweet/tangy?). And as much as I wish there was a less harsh way to say this, the food at Bobo fits all of those descriptors. The sauces don't stick to the noodles, and the flavors are either too strong or muddled to the extent that you can't taste the individual ingredients. The atmosphere is nice, but I think that it's borderline pretentious for a place that serves mainly noodle dishes. Most of the dishes use Asian ingredients but they somehow wind up tasting more like microwave dinners than genuine ethnic foods. In the end, the recipes and environment are just really lacking in integrity.

The only drawback to this is that the place can occasionally become chaotic and the service tends to lack during these times. Otherwise, fantastic!

text: Step right in to the travesty known as The Gallery and brave your way into one of the crappiest Kmarts ever! Wait, I can't even remember when Kmart was anything but crappy. It was the first place I ever had a job way back when and it was terrible then. And this was way before they had any financial woes to speak of. But THIS Kmart - in The Gallery - brings new meaning to depression mingled with thoughts of suicide. Could they have staffed this place with anything other than the walking dead? Why the hell is it split betwen two floors when the main one seems more than sufficient enough to hold everything a "regular" Kmart does? Did they just want to punish customers with double the crap? Does a dump like The Gallery even need it? It's a classic case of retail insult to injury. If you're used to those one-story Kmarts, this one can be a pain in the ass to find what you're looking for. While the frosting was pretty good, the cake was dry and bland. Certainly not a memorable cupcake experience (and the same can be said for the other flavors I sampled). I'd like to give the bakery two stars because their cookies were wonderful, and I'd go back for the oatmeal raisin alone, but the service was less than friendly, so I'm leaving the one star rating. My friend and I split an app of grape leaves, which were excellent as well. She had the greek salad with lamb and she said it was so good, she is a very light eater and she ate most of it. The salads are huge, thus the price tag. It was well worth it.

text: Va-nes-sa! Va-nes-sa! Va-nes-sa! Today I got a haircut at Underground with Vanessa K and the experience has led me to join Yelp, just so I could share this gem! Decently priced for delicious hair. I live in San Francisco and am just down for the summer in Santa Barbara. After trying 4 salons in San Francisco, I did not find a fit and kind of gave up looking for a stylist. Thus, I walked in today with long, strait and hungry hair that has not seen scissors for (gulp!) 1.5 years. In comes Senior Stylist Vanessa. She Heard what I wanted, asked some Good questions and permission to show me a few tricks. Vanessa set the tone with Goals for our session. During the perfect shampoo and scalp massage (which I am a sucker for), she allowed me time to relax into it. While rinsing, she inquired as to the products I use (Aveda) and gave some helpful feedback about how they were drying my hair. The cut was quick, decisive. My limp hair started to breath on its own after only a few snips. All the while, she was gently educating me on quick, professional styles and how to transition between different looks with a demonstration. She put on some magic thickener and then I got the blow out of my life. Like 'Victoria-Secret-Schwooping-Hair-With-A-Built-In-Fan' blow out. All the while, she was showing brush techniques, informing me about quick alternatives through easy conversation. I walked out with the best cut and most wearable cut of my life and bumped directly into a man walking on the street and the interaction went as follows Me: "Excuse me." Him: "Do you know how gorgeous you are?" Me: "Thank you." (Because it the best hair day of my life!) Him: "No, seriously." So, I walked home instead of biking with my helmet, threw away my BioSilk (as recommended by Vanessa) and wrote to you Yelpers. Go!
label: POS

text: I had a good time playing at Circus Circus this week. I enjoyed a nice session at Super Jackpot Party, and also played in their daily hold'em tournament ($18 buyin, 14 crusty characters and ESPN wannabes). Everyone was very nice and it was a pleasant way to spend an hour or so. They wouldn't even let me lose! I came in second. Circus Circus has improved their buffet significantly. It's still not quite as good as the El D, but it's competitive. One thing that blows the El D away is that they have an Asian soup bar where a guy lets you pick your ingredients and construct your soup. Then, just like in a fast food Thai noodle place, he simmers the ingredients, adds broth, and boom. The won tons were beyond horrible, but the veggies were all very fresh and the broth was heavenly - just like San Francisco soup broth! Extra points for also having Sirracha.

text: Such an enjoyable dinner! The opera-singing waitstaff were amazing! The Italian food was delicious as well (not the best I've even had, but certainly more than respectable). I enjoyed the Frutti di Mare which was quite good, except for the calamari which was a bit chewy. One of my friends had the Caprese Salad and said that the mozzerella was some of the best they've had. I did feel the food was a bit overpriced--but if they channel the profits back to supporting the working opera singers, I'm all for it. I loved the overall restaurant atmosphere including the singing. I could see if being cute for special events--while we were there, they announced a couple's anniversary and had them share a dance in the middle of the restaurant floor. It was easy to get to, being so close to Broad, but parking in South Philly is always an adventure. We lucked out with a spot just a couple blocks from the restaurant. I believe the valet parking is currently $10 which isn't bad at all. All in all, a fabulous dinner experience that I would certainly recommend for a fun evening out.

text: let's be clear about something: i don't like the 50s. when i think about the vestiges of that chrome cut, lassie-loving, segregated, dolled-up, suburban, blackandwhiteleaveittobeaver, toothpaste hugging, fake-smile-toting fucked up shtick, it generally makes me cringe. yes, this is a generalization. and yes, it's not exactly fair. but hell, like nearly all things bad (stalin, hitler, dave matthews band, tv shoppping channels, malls, orlando, and the like excluded), there is a silver lining. for me, that's a pretty short list, and three of them are actually, literally silver: toasters, airstream, and diners. yes, silk city certainly has a bit of this silver shtick going. but it's a good shtick. and it's shtick with at least a play way from true shtick. and it's also pretty tasty shtick....and there's beer. embracing the best of the 50s shtick, silk city celebrates the diner, the airstream form, and has toasters, meanwhile accessorizing these staples with the following wonderful elements: beautiful waitstaff, a side-bar lounge done up sleek and dark, great bathrooms, great tunes bouncing from motown to beebop to rock, booth seating, and, most importantly, liquor and beer. good beer. like southhampton and troeggs and more on the ol' tap (done up sweet goldchrome style), and the duvel and such standards in the bottle. unexpected and delicious. the food is also pretty kick ass for the price. meeting some friends here for dinner on a swing into town, and trying not to gawk at the service staff too much, we happily devoured some spot-on spice-battered calamari, heaps of fries, unanimously satisfying sandwiches (my beersoaked pulled pork sandwich with mustard and kraut was pretty goddamn huge and amazing), and some of the best wings i've ever had, done up in a cilantro-lemongrass-chile sauce that had me dipping my fries in to soak up the afterburn. for 15 bucks, that's pretty sweet. so sweet in fact, that we came back the next morning for some wake-up coffee, breakfast, and a drink or two. and, of course, to stare and talk shit. sure enough the place was bumping again, but no wait for the counter. so it was easy enough to saunter on up and take down a salmon/goatcheese/arugula omelette, some hash, some pancakes, and some sweet broke yolk before hitting the road. all that was missing was a bit of salt. oh. and that really cute bartender from the night before. anyway, i hope to come back here soon sometime not so far away when i can check in on the biergarten in the works. and make proposals with my eyes....

text: Through my insurance and a lot of research I decided to get an Ob/Gyn that was affiliated with Barnes Jewish and had a relatively small practice (2-3 doctors). I found West End Ob/Gyn and got an appointment with Dr. Rosanna Gray-Swain. She is really sweet and attentive, our first meeting went well, she explained a lot of things about pregnancy, delivery, the hospital, etc. She works with Dr. Turner who has more experience, but Gray-Swain's credentials are also excellent. So overall I think they are good doctors, but I was ticked off by a lot of other things. On my second visit, I waited a good 50 minutes to be seen, after I went it, I did see Gray-Swain on her desk but then the nurse informed me that she had to go for a delivery and Dr. Turner would see me. She was okay, did not ask questions, just listened to the baby's heartbeat and literally only spend 3 minuted with us. It was annoying. That was my last visit there. I now switched hospitals and doctors. Their stuff is not the friendliest... their conversations with each other I thought were inappropriate, I don't like it when nurses who treat me that have weird easily visible tattoos on their bodies, some of them have these odd looking long colorful nails (you know which ones I am talking about, right?). Their office is nice and clean, location is fine, they are in a brand new building close to Barnes. I am not sure if it's because they are associated with Barnes and it's more of an inner city hospital, they obviously have a lot of inner city patients and that's fine, but if you have to listen to "ghetto talk" (if I can call it that) the whole time you are waiting to be seen... I'd rather really go somewhere else. I am not trying to be judgmental, but really if you are looking for a nicer, more pleasant office and staff, go somewhere else... and unfortunately I would have to say chose someone that is not affiliated with Barnes. Even though it's a big hospital and one of the best in the country, unless you have a specific condition, don't go there. It is too busy, the delivery floor and baby unit is packed with students... No one needs that...

text: Some investigative Yelping: I had an Arrogant Bastard, a Sam Adams Winter Lager, and a Manhattan. The bartenders consistently under-poured on the pints throughout the night for my friend and I. We are talking about 7/8ths inches lower than the rim on each glass. ( I know it was 7/8ths of an inch since my thumb is measured as such). I went home and it turns out on an American pint glass--16 ounces, which is what my beers were served in, 7/8th of an inch from the rim translates to 2 ounces of liquid. TWO OUNCES. That, friends, is 12.5% unpoured undrunk yet very paid-for beer. At four and five dollars a pint, that is more than a dollar's worth of precious ale that I did not get to touch my lips to. And the beer still had a decent head, so it wasn't like it sat around too long after it was poured. It wouldn't have been so bad if my complaint was corrected, or even just fixed on the second pint. Not so. So that was the Platonic form of Lame Itself. Then, since I am considerate and wanted to give the bar one more chance, I ordered a Manhattan. Now I know the International Bartender's Association official recipe for a Manhattan. It calls for it to be served straight up, and with a cherry. So does Mr. Boston's guide to Bartending. Well, I got a rocks glass full of ice and watery Manhattan less cherry and seemingly devoid of bitters. Rubbish. C'mon folks, The King of Cocktails wasn't even made right here. I also don't understand the infatuation with several huge televisions on all walls of bars. This place exemplifies that model, however. Do we really need to be surrounded with replays from high school football games from the night before? High schools from other states? Can we not talk to one another at bars? This may be a complaint with the notion of sports bars, but I wasn't expecting it from a professed Pub and Grille. Grille with an E ought denote classy, not Class 3A sports highlights. While their tap list is certainly much better than most, I don't know if it is worth it. Smoky atmosphere too, if that is a problem for you. Not so much for me, but I know this worries some folks. Their Spinach & Artichoke dip was good, but not great. The restrooms were very nice though, with complimentary mints.

The food was fairly solid, but I didn't like how they did not shred their beef--they would serve enchiladas or tacos with these big chunks of unchewable beef--unwieldy and unappetizing! My son recently developed a thing for chicken chimichangas, his favorite in SB/Goleta being the commendable offering from Altamiranos in Old Town. Rudy's was worse than mediocre. A chimi, as you probably know, is a deep-fried burrito garnished with guac, sour cream and lettuce. At its best, it is a crispy, cheesy, delightful mess of calorie-laden goodness. Rudy's version was a soggy, barely-fried, lukewarm log filled with flavorless stewed chicken and beans. A pile of sour cream, and a few shreds of cheese and lettuce sat forlornly next to the sodden log in the styrofoam container. Yuck! My son ate about a third and then gave up. My daughter had the chicken taquitos which were 2 small corn tortillas deep fried with chicken inside, a tiny container of guac on the side. They were acceptable, but at $4.25, way over-priced. Rudy's has a nice salsa bar with 4 or 5 varieties ranging from mild to spicy, as well as chopped cilantro, onion, pickled onions (nice), and refreshing whole radishes. It would be nice to get a complimentary basket of chips when you eat there, but instead they give you a small handful as a garnish for most dishes and charge $2-$3 dollars more if you want a basket. text: Where do I start? Every once and while my fellow Yelpers and I disagree . For the most part I've found the reviews reliable - so much so that my team has learned to use yelp as a resource and that's how they picked up on the Stockyard for a group dinner That said, I could not disagree more strongly with the other reviews on this one. The Stockyard is a classic case of a restaurant surviving purely on its historic reputation. We had a large group - so let me begin at the beginning... While I expect a high-end steakhouse to be pricey - I also expect to "get what you pay for". The wine list was not a good start. The wines I recognized were priced 4-6X retail. When we have a significant size group I try to target wines in the 50-80$ range. Thats a real challenge at the stockyard. Precious few decent wines in this range. We went with a Malbec that I know sells for about $20 a bottle retail - $80. Also got a white -- which was a bit more reasonably priced - $65 and surprisingly good. We did the "seafood" appetizer - again, family style due to group size. I was surprised that they didn't cut the fried lobster tails into bite size portions a bit awkward to share. No real complaints here, but it wasn't superb either. At this point i am still thinking "expensive but average steakhouse". But then we got to the main course - and the hustle. Our main waiter launched into a description of the available entrees to the group, including - much to my dismay the description of limited number of American "kobe" filets. In a group this size, I'd want a heads up that he was offering $90 filets BEFORE people start to order. This was followed by an offer to each table (unknown to me) of a 2lb lobster add-on for each. He later claimed he asked first on this - but he did not come to me and i was clearly acting in the capacity of host. Talk about cranking up the bill... All of this - while disconcerting and annoying - is still somewhat "forgivable" when you get a really outstanding meal and service. Nothing could be further from the truth. To a man (or woman) our group was disappointed in the quality and preparation of the entrees - including the kobe which was described as bland and a bit chewy. My porterhouse was undercooked, non-prime beef and clearly not the size stipulated on the menu. I am no steakhouse novice. I know what to expect and this was clearly far below my expectation at a third of the price -- I could have gotten better at Outback. Based on conversation, I was clearly not alone in this opinion. Additionally, a number of people had to wait extended time for entrees while others ate. Lobsters - while large, should have been pre-cracked so inexperienced diners wouldn't struggle so much (and not overcooked). Overall, our price per person was outrageous, the food average, and the approach to draining our pockets insulting. If you want a good meal in Nashville look to the west end near Vanderbilt. Some great places... but Stockyard is the kind of place that makes "overrated" seem like a compliment.

text: First of all, people need to STFU about "authentic" it's a hack phrase that doesn't mean a damn thing. Every village in said country has a different idea of "authentic" and as with almost any foreign food you would not like the actual authentic gopher guts in cactus-armadillo sauce. Secondly, chorizo will ALWAYS be good no matter who makes it. It's salty, fatty, pork. I love it, I've never had bad chorizo anywhere. But that's like adding butter to anything--it's automatically good. I must be seriously not understanding Philadelphia tastebuds because this place is pretty mediocre leaning on bad. La Lupe appears to be in a good location, with opened garage door indoor seating. The prices seemed reasonable and they had a few extra than usual tacos. I was feeling good, until I got the chips and salsa. Most Mexican restaurants take the 10 min to make their own chips. Not so. This place had cold bagged chips pretending to be homemade. Alright, I eat bagged chips at home, no big deal, right? I was eagerly awaiting my big bowl of salsa, when the waiter plopped some IHOP syrup dispenser on the table. No joke, they keep their disgusting salsa in syrup containers in the beverage fridge. Their salsa has no chunks of any kind, it is completely blended and obviously from a jar. It's slimy and thin, with no flavor other than slightly salted baby food. The only way to save it was to mix Yucateca with it, which luckily they have 2 bottles of. Salsa aside, maybe the food is good. Between 2 people we ordered six tacos at $2.50 each--Barbacoa, Enchilada, Steak, Chorizo, Al Pastor, Grilled Pork. The tacos were presented in a gyro-like cone with onions, lime, and a tsp of guacamole. The shells were very thin and flour based rather than corn. They were decent, but I suspect they were also prepackaged. The meats were fairly average, but i couldn't tell any of them apart, and neither could the waitress. The Al Pastor would have been ok, except for the bad quality pineapple which was mushy and disgusting. The meat seemed to be mostly trimmed of fat (although I still found some chunks), but decent fat-content for a Mexican restaurant. The saving factors were the Barbacoa (goat meat) and Enchilada tacos. Both are taco types I don't see in many places, and they were executed fairly well. The goat was tender and well cooked, and the enchilada was nicely flavored. The tacos were just ok, but it's not worth going back. I can't get over that they could not even provide me with half-way decent salsa! Perhaps everything had to be mild and flavorless due to its proximity to the tourist locations of Pat's and Geno's, but this was not nearly as flavorful as Mexican food should be. Bottom line: Never trust a Mexican place that doesn't have salsa! Pros: Hmm...they have goat meat? Cons: Salsa, chips, tortillas

text: So many good memories at this place, only to be ruined by my latest visit. Let's backtrack a little. I'll tell you about my first few experiences at Tiffin Inn. Not much has changed since, and it's kind of nice to go to a place like Tiffin Inn. The first time I went was post-K by about two years. Places still closed at 10, and my naive self walked into this place probably 25 min. shy of when they were going to close. It was completely empty, but it was after a show. I may have still been slightly inebriated (how I made it from HoB to Kenner is BEYOND me). But I remembered getting a bacon waffle. Which was a waffle with bacon bits in the batter, and then two strips of bacon atop the waffle. I was struck with wonder at the amazement of such an idea. Sweet....savory...salty....perfect. At least that's how I remembered it. But every time I came back, the bacon waffle was less and less delicious. So I tried other options, like the chili omelette (do not get this it is disgusting, and not in a good way. The chili is not only canned, it is some of the worst canned chili I'd ever had, mixed with poorly (or overly) cooked eggs). The corned beef hash disappoints too. The signs were present that this place just clearly wasn't worth it, even if you're drunk (that's why there's Danny & Clyde's, but alas that's another story). So why come back? Well, every time I would go to Tiffin Inn, there was always this ominous looking manager/boss-man who looked like he was in the mob or something. (I know, I shouldn't judge a book by it's cover or a person by their demure). He always looked pissed off and ready to hurt someone. Then one night, my friends and I were at the Tiffin Inn after a show, and my friend says to me, "I wanna talk to that guy." And I told my friend, "No way dude! That guy's crazy! He's probably got all kinds of connections you don't wanna know about!" Well, lo and behold that didn't stop my friend. So my friend says to the manager, "Excuse me sir, how big are the silver dollar pancakes?" The manager comes over, looking kind of pissed. Looks like he's about to go off on us, and just when I expected the worst, he joked, and said to us: "As big as your face!!" Turns out, the manager was one of the coolest dudes I'd ever met. He told us of how he was a famous Lebanese movie star, but came to America to start a new life because he played just a little too much Baccarat. He was apparently to play in some local short film where he plays the role of "BIG DOG". (It exists, I tell you- the guy even has an IMDB). Speaking of which, he tells us his name is Pierre Daher. So we go home and google him, and the first few hits are pretty............interesting. Every time I came back, Mr. Daher made it such a pleasurable dining experience. Every time except the most recent time when he wasn't there. Then I woke up and realized that I was being fed garbage, and that the drive to Kenner just was not worth it anymore (sorry America's city!). Sigh, I had such warm memories of this place, but let's be honest the food sucks, and with Pierre gone, I guess the service does too.

We arrived at the restaurant around 7:30 pm - certainly not late, but past the "dinner rush." The place was probably 3/4 full, but the hostess told us that no tables were available and asked if we'd mind waiting at the bar until she had a chance to clear one. No big whoop in my opinion, so we sat down and looked over the wine menu. First impression was that for a restaurant called Wine Thief, their wine menu was pretty weak. By my count they are the Baskin Robbins of wine bistro's having 31 different wines on the menu (which, according to our bartender, weren't even all available that night). 31 bottles is a fine selection of wine, I guess... I am not sure if I expected more wines, or if the wines they had just didn't impress me. Anyway, we both had a glass of the 2008 Conquista Malbec which was sublime. Time ticked by, we each ordered another wine, and then another... next thing we knew 40 minutes had gone by and we still didn't have a table. After asking the hostess if she'd found a table (mind you, this is a small place, so I don't know where the tables were hiding) she hastily wiped down a table that was next to the bar and had been empty since we arrived. Both my wife and I have worked in food service, so we know how much that job sucks so we let that slide. Heck, if my only complaint was that I had to sit at the bar (and subsequently have 3 glasses of wine before dinner), the evening would have been great. Sat at the table for about 5 minutes before I was able to catch the attention of a waiter (everyone working that night was avoiding eye contact with the patrons - not just our waiter, and not just my wife and me... none of the waiters were paying attention to the "cues" of the patrons). We had had ample time to look over the menu while at the bar, so we ordered our appetizer (the cheese plate) and entrees (two New York Strips, medium, Au Poivre) all at once. Cheese plate arrived a few minutes later. Was thoroughly un-impressed. There were four or five, very small, cheese selections... hardly enough for one person. When asked, the waiter knew nothing about the different cheeses, which was disappointing as I always enjoy getting a lesson on where the cheese came from, etc. The selections weren't bad, but all seemed to be middle of the road flavor wise, and because of the small portion size, definitely not worth the $12 price tag. Steaks arrived a few minutes after we'd cleared the cheese plate. We both cut into our steaks to find that they were not undercooked, they were still raw. Don't get me wrong, I love a pink center with my steak. These bad-boys were RED... and cold. I got the hostess' attention and asked if the chef could throw them back on the grill. She politely took the plates and brought them back a few minutes later... still significantly under cooked/ almost completely pink (we ordered medium, remember)? I pointed out that they were still under cooked (which she agreed and appologized for) but told her we'd just take them as-is because it was getting late at this point and we were paying our babysitter by the hour. At this point the hostess asked if there was anything she could do to make it up to us... Nice enough, sure, but when I waited tables, I wouldn't ASK if there was something I could do to make up for a mistake, I just did it. She should have comped us a drink, or written off the crappy cheese plate. Anything to make me think that she actually cared about our service. I know that in some restaurants wait staffers aren't empowered to make that type of decision. If that's the case at Wine Thief, my complaint is with the management, not the hostess. Anyway, I told her no, we were fine, but ordered a Vesper half hoping she would get the hint and volunteer a free drink for me (no such luck). Apparently, while listed in the cocktail menu, this particular cocktail seems to have never been ordered at that bar before because the bartender brought me a rocks glass full of vodka with a lemon twist in it. No gin, no Lillet... Luckily I like vodka. After I finished my drink, we asked to get our meals wrapped up, paid our bill (even left an ok tip knowing how hard waiting tables is) and left... I probably could have made a fuss, and some folks reading this might think I shouldn't have left without getting something taken off the bill, but I didn't mind paying full price for the meal because I knew that I could doctor up the steaks, and that I'd eventually get around to writing this review... and these final words: While I hate taking shots at someone's business/livelihood, I was thoroughly disappointed by, and do not recommend Wine Thief.

text: Can't say enough fabulous things about Vincente's. They used to be located in Wilmington, in Independence Mall, but he moved to Glen Mills for a little while, and now he's down on Kirkwood Highway. Yay! The restaurant is owned by Vincente, who is this adorable old Italian guy who has been running this restaurant for almost 50 years, I bet. He is AWESOME. I go to this restaurant just to see him, he is simply that cool. The dude is a freakin' institution. Anyway, when you first walk in, you'll be asked if you want a paper menu or "the walking menu." For the love of God and all that is holy, get the walking menu! The walking menu is simply this: Vincente himself comes to your table and asks you what you're in the mood for. Steak? Pasta? Seafood? Chicken? (I picked steak.) Then he asks what kind of steak you like. Prime rib? Filet? Something spicy? (I picked something spicy.) He asked me if I liked bleu cheese, and I said, "Amen, brother." So he said, "One steak au poivre!" and the waitress next to him jotted it down. The guy has this schtick down to a science. It is a script he's been reciting for 50 years. Listen to this man, he is a pro. He asks if you want some soup. He tells you the soups. We go for the minestrone, and we are very very happy. Then he asks if you're in the mood for salad. You are an idiot if you say no. You must get the Caesar salad, even if you hate Caesar salad. Trust me. I normally don't care about a Caesar salad either way, but dude, you will lick the plate and beg for more. What makes this Caesar salad special is the fact that he makes it tableside, in a wooden bowl he's been using for 50 years. Yes, he uses raw eggs; just suck it up and live on the edge, fer cryin' out loud! Then... he takes a little bowl of grated parmesan cheese and picks out a cheese wad that invariably forms... and then he flicks the cheese wad into the wooden bowl with a teeny spoon. Yeah, OK, no big deal. Then he takes 10 steps back and flings again. He shoots! He scores! Then he walks *clear across the room* and this 75-year-old guy whips a cheese wad right into the bowl. It is amazing. And if he misses you don't even care, because he is just so awesome and warm and terrific. And yes, the salad is absolutely, unspeakably delicious. Fresh, crisp, amazing. The steak au poivre arrives and it is melt-in-your-mouth perfection. That is all you need to know about that. One friend gets gnocchi and is sent to heaven. My boyfriend gets a chicken thing and he is doing the happy-food-dance. To finish off the night (because you haven't eaten quite enough yet), they'll present you with a dessert menu. We opted against dessert (we were full); however, we chose the "Cafe Diavolo: Coffee of the Devil!" Which is basically a ton of booze set on fire with a splash of coffee in it. Again, he makes this elaborate concoction table-side, and it is a delight to watch, as this schtick too is well-practiced over 50 years. It tastes great, and it will get you snockered. So be sure to linger a bit so you're OK to drive home. I guarantee you'll be saying "Cafe Diavolo: Coffee of the Devil!" for a month after you leave this place. Please go there before Vincente is no longer there. I'm telling you, you will not regret it. It is .0001% cheesy, and it is .00002% campy. Go with it. Feel the love. Bask in the history and greatness of this man. He will flirt with the ladies in that grandpa way, and you will LOVE it. If you've got any Italian in your lineage, you will be convinced you're related to him. When you're there, you're family. Please be aware that it ain't cheap, but then again, you are spending a good chunk of time there (think 2.5 - 3 hours). For two people, it was just over $115, I think. But it is worth every penny. This is my mom talking: Don't be a slob when you go there. Look nice, be respectful, and remember your manners.

text: This all started this a bid on Priceline. I wanted to get away with my wife for our anniversary and selected a resort in Tucson for $80 and won the Loews Vantana. You will pay $9 for parking weather you park yourself or valet. Internet is $11 and cell service is sketchy at best around the resort. The first night we had the basic room and it was nice a clean. It was very noisy as all the rooms around us were full with families with kids. The bed was quit hard and we did have a problem with the shower head as the pipe was leaking and the ceiling was falling apart from water damage. The next morning my back was completely gone from the bed so I called the front desk and they upgraded the room to the top floor with a view. Unfortunately the bed was the same and by Sunday I was searching for a chiropractor. The shower was perfect and the tubs are huge! Big enough to hold 4 adults easily. We went to the spa on Saturday which was pricey and we ate at the restaurants every meal which are very overpriced but the food is good. Get the table side guacamole at the Flying V. Its worth it. After we came home I happened to look at my bill and found they had double billed me for the spa. Since both my wife and I spent a few hours there it happened to be very pricey and they automatically roll in 20% for gratuity. The problem is they ran my card twice! So far I have been calling the spa, customer service and accounting daily and we are going on a week without a response or getting my money back. If you call the spa they give your information to accounting. If you call customer service they give you information to accounting. If you call accounting all you get it a message line to leave your information. After a week of doing this I would just be happy for a call back. Overall if you are looking for somewhere to stay in Tucson, look for something else and save you back and the headaches.

text: Eating dinner at Mangia on Saturday night was a surprisingly pleasant experience! Unlike many of the prior reviews indicated, Mangia has now gone smoke free - high five to them! I have been here many times in the past, but just for drinking because this place was disgustingly smoky before. So bad that you would go home and your purse/wallet would reek of smoke. It was pretty gross. So of course I never thought to actually eat here until now. Once I found out that Mangia went smoke free (via a few smart yelpers - thanks for the heads up!), I figured it would be nice to try their food, as I know they make their pasta right here in St. Louis. Actually, they make their pasta right next door to my apartment so it would be rude NOT to eat here! Getting a table at 7:30 on a Saturday night wasn't a problem, which is too bad. I'd heard that they've lost some business since going smoke-free. Ah well, it's going to take time for people to realize that the food here is actually very good. And it didn't smell bad inside at all. After eating tacos all day, I had a serious craving for pasta. And Mangia's pasta is damn delicious. Usually when I order pasta it's in a heavy cream sauce (and yes, I realize that it's not good for me at all but I do not care!) and theirs hit the spot. My glass of wine was so-so and the pour wasn't terribly generous, but that's OK 'cause I wasn't really here to drink. I did try dessert, too, and it was also OK. It was a flourless chocolate tort with a little raspberry sauce on the side. It was good, but nothing terribly special. But really folks, if you are in the mood for some hearty pasta, Mangia should be your next meal. Let's show this restaurant some love since they went way out of their comfort zone to save the health of STL customers.

text: The Orchard is located @ 97 Styers Lane, Langhorne, Pa. 19047. They are NOT affiliated with the market at Styers. Drive down Styer's Lane to the center of the farm for all farm activities and products. Remember the down to earth activities we used to do as kids? This would be a great way to show a kid how it's grown, farmed and let them enjoy a couple hours seeing and doing all of this. Right now you can pick corn for 20 cents an ear! If they pick it, it is more, if I have the time, I do pick my own. Today I filled several bags with corn, plums, peaches, tomatoes and some peppers. I also stocked up on some fresh herbs. You know it's fresh and right from the farm or orchard. I visit Styers a lot and I pretty well know exactly what they have and when. Strawberries, late May thru mid June. Cherries, early June to late June, Plums mid-July, right now they are so plump and sweet! Peaches, mid July to mid September, Blackberries late July/ August, Pears mid August to early September, Grapes, late August thru early Sept. Apples, August thru early November and Apricots early July to Mid July. They also have nectarines in August to early September. For vegetables, and I will not give time lines, because you know them or can pick up the phone and call ahead. Asparagus, some of the best heirloom tomatoes, cukes, a variety of peppers including hot peppers, eggplant, summer squash and zucchini. In the fall and winter months, until everything is picked and sold, you can also get acorn squash, spaghetti squash, butternut and some odd ones that I have yet to try. They also sell a huge variety of farm grown herbs, like dill, basil, sage and mint. But if you are looking for a particular one, chances are you will find it here.

text: Again, people argue back and forth as to where you can get the best Mexican food in Tucson. It's kinda like arguing about which politician is most corrupt in Washington; Tucson is frankly a Mexican food mecca. Now, each restaurant has a distinct feel, distinct styles, and I often change which restaurant I take my visitors and friends to based on their individual tastes and wants. After all, if you're going to visit Tucson you want to have a good meal. La Poca Cosa comes to mind, or Mi Niditos, but my goto for showing non-Tucsonans how varied and diverse Mexican style food can be is Guadalajara Grill. Of course there is the standard Mexican food fair--burritos, tacos, enchiladas, but what makes Guadalajara unique is the diversity dishes. You can order anything from a molcajete bubbling with peppers and carne asada to the standard Tres Amigos, all with fresh in-house-made tortillas and at-the-table made salsa. Because my family and friends trek from the Midwest, they are often floored by how varied Mexican food can be from what they know, especially the seafood dishes which are pretty fantastic. Seafood in the desert? Yeah, the Baja is only 3-4 hours away. If you want more than just a meal, Guadalajara sports a meandering mariachi band, and they will come to your table to ask if you'd like a song. Many amors and corazons later, your date or family will be laughing and having a good time. If you want some margarita, they are strong and cheap on certain days so swing by, only complaint there is a little salty (but I like salty margaritas). I highly recommend Guadalajara.

text: I didn't realize how much take-out Chinese joints from south Jersey had spoiled me until recently. Peking Wok has been the go to for Chinese for my family since moving to this side of town. Before that, it was another dependable restaurant. Most places don't equal the Wok, but they're all better than you'll find in, say, New York, at the same or better prices. (as far as my experiences go) Every Friday in my parents' house is take-out night, and Peking Wok makes a lot of pretty pennies off my family every few weeks. They know my dad. We're pretty sure business has been handed down to the next generation recently. At least, I'm pretty sure, because their once awesome house fried rice has upgraded to heavenly house fried rice and now also contains egg, the one ingredient I've missed in all my fried rice for the past ten years minimum. Fried rice, you see, is very important. It's your base. And if it's that skimpy yellow stuff they sell you in New York with a few scrawny sprouts, a couple pieces of pork, well then, you've been had. You might as well not order the stuff and stick with the free white rice. It's healthier for you anyway. No, fried rice should be packed with Stuff and colored Brown--you know, as if it were, er, fried? Then you're free to top with your choice entree. I can vouch happily for any of the following: sesame shrimp (comes with broccoli and stuff; we fight over the last two shrimp), beef w/ scallops (also vegetables (fer reelz) and quite yummy), beef with broccoli (different sauce). Lemon chicken; not dry, delish. Dumplings; also way better than generic New York take-out and larger in size. Mu Shoo Pork; comes with fresh pancakes and excellent, cold sauce, though not good to reheat. Lo Mein is lo mein; can you screw up lo mein? Of course, there's none of this free soda or arbitrary container of pineapple wedges they have going on here in New York. But this is suburbia; they probably assume household pantries are stocked with soda galore. And Peking Wok is too legit to give you free stuff; maybe they'll deliver hot tea if you ask nicely. http://www.mountlaurelmenus.com/menus/peking.htm

On a recent weeknight, my dining companion and I were the only ones there. Our waiter, while very nice, was over-attentive (perhaps out of sheer boredom), asking us frequently if everything was "ok." Fried calamari were heavily fried and greasy, but tasty. Steak "medallions" tasted like a Lean Cuisine I could microwave. Lukewarm and lacking sophistication. They came with an avalanche of mashed potatoes. Way too big a portion, and the potatoes were too hard. Vegetables were decent. My dining companion seemed to enjoy the lamb, which came with the same side dishes. Bread pudding was "interesting," but I can't tell if that was a good thing or not. Rarely have I ordered bread pudding that was an actual "piece of bread." The reviews in the paper said it was good. It consisted of a large piece of challah bread, warm and soft, drowned in what seemed like a pool of butter. It tasted more like french toast than dessert. I asked the waiter what the sauce was made of, and he sheepishly said something about a rum "reduction," but I'm not even sure he knows. The prices here are fairly steep for such mediocre food, but there is potential for better. The one bathroom I saw was "iffy" and you had to pass by an open kitchen to get there. Once done, our waiter asked for our names and seemed genuinely thankful that someone had come by to eat. He said business had been "good" since a move from Germantown. He said the owner was sitting at the bar downstairs and would be sure to thank us on the way out. We never saw him. Either way, the food was forgettable and I probably wouldn't return, though I'm told the brunch is good. Roxborough desperately needs some good restaurants. I hope this one gets better with more time.

text: I've been driving up and down Delmar for over a year and looking for a reason to stop in at this interesting looking restaurant/store. I read a very positive article about it in the Ladue News this morning and my wife and I decided we were going. I see that other reviewers have had a very positive experience but mine was somewhat less so. First, when we got there, there is no indication that you have to walk to the rear of the restaurant, place your order at a counter and then seat yourself. We waited a few minutes near the entrance for someone to assist us and none of the staff at the restaurant suggested we walk to the back and order our food. Eventually we figured it out and walked to the back. When we got to the counter, the young woman behind the counter did not acknowledge us or invited us to place our order....she just stood there....I initiated the conversation and asked about vegetarian options....there was something on the counter called a Torte Rustica (sp?) that looked delicious and the young woman explained that it was vegetarian and not vegan which demonstrated that she was knowledgeable about the issue (I appreciate that). I ordered it with a side salad. My wife ordered chicken salad. I ordered a diet coke and the woman asked me to go get it for her from the nearby cooler so she could ring it up. If she had taken two steps (literally), she could have done it hersefl. My wife ordered a Latte and the woman behind the counter handed us a number for us to put on our table so they would know where to bring the food out. We sat at our table for a few minutes which seemed like a long time without the Latte so I walked back up to the counter and found it sitting there. Apparently, you are responsible for picking up your coffee but they bring the food to you. They did not tell us that and it would have not been a problem if we had known to hang out by the counter while they made the Latte. A few minutes later, the server brought our food. They correctly brought the chicken salad but the server was carrying two Torte Rustica's. She gave me the one without the salad by mistake but I didn't recognize that when she put it down....after a moment or two, I did realize it and flagged down the waitress. she said she had inadvertently given my plate with the salad to a different table and I had someone elses. She took the plate on my table and went over to another table and did a switch. To be honest, I think the proper thing to do would have been to bring me the missing salad. There is a little "yuck" factor in getting food that has been on someone elses table that you don't know. While the flavor was very good, the Torte Rustica was barely warm. As I was eating it, I realized that I had little bits of paper in my mouth. I turned the Torte over and there was parchment paper from baking it stuck to the bottom in a few places. I just peeled it off and finished eating it. It was pretty tasty. My wife said her chicken salad was excellent. The server who brought our food came back and thoughtfully picked up the dishes we were finished with and then began refilling the small vase on our table with the silverware rolled up in a napkin for the next guests who would sit there. I appreciate her picking up the dishes but perhaps she could have waited until we were finished or had left before restocking the table for the next people. Though there were small problems with the food, it wasn't enough to keep us from coming back. Now that we know how things work there, our next visit should be much smoother. However, in my mind, the real issue was the detached attitude of the staff. Everyone there is very young and could use a refresher course in customer service. The staff at this restaurant reminded me of the bored/lightly trained college students that used to staff the restaurants in the community where I went to school. No one was rude to us but the lack of hospitality was obvious. If you look at my other reviews, I'm not a stickler for service....just the lack of it at this restaurant made it stand out. We are going to go back because the food is good. Sure hope the staff seems more interested in us when we do return.
label: NEG

text: I am going to go against the grain a bit here, but Five Guys is not that great. I think that the reason that Five Guys is so popular has more to do with lowered expectations than actual quality. Let me explain. I think over the past few decades we have been exposed to enough terrible hamburgers and fries from fast food establishments and lousy restaurants that our expectations of a good burger have been lowered so far that a passable hamburger seems amazing in comparison. That is exactly what Five Guys has, a passable burger. The fries are good and of course they are fresh, but aren't fries supposed to be fresh. I suppose this is why the "craft" burger has taken off all over the city and across the country. When people forget that a product is supposed to be good you can get away with charging a premium for anything that is above average. That get's me to my other point. After all is said and done, with fries and a drink, Five Guys is a $10 meal. There are dozens of places in Nashville that have excellent burgers for around $10. Hell I rarely walk out of Gabby's for more than $8 and that is a far superior product in every way. Most of the sports bar's and pubs in the area have Burgers for less than $10 so I don't really get it. Overall, I think that Five Guys is okay, but they are not particularly special or particulary a good value. Long live the era of low expectations.

text: I was warned by my wife not to bother with Mama Louisa's -- But I thought she was just being snobby. I took her Mom for dinner tonight and I wish I had listened to my spouse (who's out of town.) The Italian Wedding Soup probably came out of the Godfather #1 catering truck - weird pieces of supposed sausage in a salty broth - my sodium level spiked immediately. The salad bar was well described by Veggie Girl - a real mess. The "Italian" dressing and pasta salad jacked up my already elevated sodium level even further. The bread sticks were buttery and yet more salt. Does this place cater to a large crowd of smokers with no taste buds? We waited forever for our Joe's Special (Mom) and my two meat pasta plate: a couple of meatballs and a sausage over tomato sauce and linguine pasta. Where do I begin? The meatballs were "juicy" and just tasted awful. The sausage was dry. The pasta looked like it had been cooked once, then flash-frozen in a plastic pouch, then microwaved and plopped on my plate. It had that kind of dried out, extremely white color around the edges that you see in microwave lunches. In fact, I've had better pasta in microwave lunches. The tomato sauce was kind of sweet in a sickening kind of way - no real spice, garlic, well... flavor! The waiter, Jason, was just obnoxious -- at our table asking how things were going while I was having soup & salad but never again while we where waiting an extremely long time for our main meals. In fact, he sat at the bar hanging out -- when he finally checked our meals were ready. I think that was supposed to constitute as good service in advance of our wait. From their web site (http://emol.org/mamalouisas/), bright green like my face after eating the slop they served up: "serving the best in homemade Italian cuisine." And further, they apparently, since 1956, "been among one of the top restaurants in Tucson." Ummm... according to whom? Again, I should have listened to my wife and simply suggested somewhere else for dinner with Mother-in-law. Live and learn and pass the Maalox.
label: NEG

text: Not only is Bevo Mill a consistently great place to dine, it's a St. Louis landmark as well! As the story goes, Bevo Mill was built by August Busch Sr. so that he had a place for lunch. He built himself a decadent private room to dine in so as to get away from work for a bit. The name came from Busch's non-alcoholic beer of the same name that was being sold during prohibition, and was a combination of the Slavic word for beer "pivo" and the English word "beverage." Ok, now on to the review - There aren't many cooler looking places to eat at in St. Louis, so it's worth a visit for that fact alone. Add to that scrumptious food and you've got yourself a winner. There's a reason this place has been here since the early 1900s! The food is phenomenal! Their specialties are favorites of mine, and this is one of the only places that I will eat a pasta with cream sauce. Typically cream sauces can be clotted or really oily, not so here. If you're willing to be adventurous, try the German rabbit [Hasenpfeffer] and you'll be delightfully surprised. What's great is that the service is just as spectacular as the surroundings. I can't find a negative thing to say about this place.

text: We wanted meat. So we were walking down Stearns Wharf looking for meat. After the unfortunate turn of events at a seafood eatery, I was no longer adventurous to get a second helping of subpar seafood eats, even if we were seated on the dock. I know. I give up easily. But hell, it was July. There's no "r" in it to remind the fishes and sea creatures to taste scrumptious even if they're in the vicious hands of subpar food makers. So I ordered the opposite of seafood-----a pastrami dip au jus. It was massive. It came with fries and coleslaw. It was so big, I actually lost my appetite just looking at it. Thankfully, the fries and coleslaw were filling and yummy. So I ate them first. I ate this entire meal @ three different times. Lunch, and as left overs, for dinner and brunch. Yep, the sandwich was that big. Sat outside. I swear a couple of pigeons tripped over my head as they flew in and out. There were peanut shells scattered about. However, I didn't see anyone eating peanuts. I supposed they also serve as a double purpose: a snack for pigeons. I was not concerned about bird poop because of our unpleasant experience prior to Longboards. I figured good karma will shift back to our side this time around. The service was ultra friendly. I really appreciated this since pretentions were getting on my nerves lately. Great breeze. Lots of sun. Service is fast. Bathrooms clean. Prices are very reasonable. Hanging out with friends and family would be good here. There's a bar inside. Place not so crowded (at the time). If you're into simple, uncomplicated sustenance. Try this joint for size. Lots of tourists, but that's okay. I was one too.

My only complaint is the prices aren't always "Secondhand" prices, but I found some rare british gastronomy, african cuisine, appalachian cuisine, as well as "On Food and Cooking" on the shelves- pretty great selection! Sure the place is not very organized, but they do have a computerized inventory if you know what you want already- definitely a great bookstore of Reno/Sparks, not to be missed.

I love the cheap aviators I've gotten here that I don't have to worry as much about breaking or losing, though I've got hundreds of glasses anyways. It's also a cheaper source for those wierd alligator heads that I was once really obsessed with, haha... I bought up all sizes of them, along with claws and such and gave them to everybody the first time I visited New Orleans and also got enough to mount as showpieces throughout my home. I got over that, but it's always fun to look for random bargains on misc. stuff that you may not want. That's why I loved the La Brea Circus (Bargain Circus in L.A.) and still love browsing Big Lots for randomly sweet items. It's not the place to look for the quintessential NOLA historic pieces or authentic anything, but it has its place with some randomly cool junk! text: My parents are retired and have a pretty strict budget, which is why they were so excited to find the rates of Avania Inn so affordable. However, after being at the hotel for one night they were informed the power was going to be turned off for the entire second evening of their stay. The hotel gave them a very small "discount" on the room for the second night and 2 candles that barely provided enough light to move around the room. My dad is 80 years old and has Parkinson's Disease and due to the immense amount of energy it takes to get around my mom thought it was best to just stay put since changing hotels would be so difficult for my dad. Had I not been 6 hours away I would have driven there, packed them up and found them a hotel that was not going to overcharge them to stay in a dark room with no electricity. My parents take one vacation a year and Avania managed to put a damper on it. When I was attending college in Santa Barbara my parents would stay at this hotel, but it was under different ownership. Some things are beyond the control of the hotel (I imagine they could not turn the power on if they wanted to), but it would have been kind of the hotel staff to offer to help identify and/or move to a new hotel for the evening. One would think that upon seeing a couple that clearly has limited mobility they would offer some extra support, or at least more than 2 candles to ensure that my dad could see on his way from his bed to the bathroom in the middle of the night!

text: My boyfriend took me here recently for my birthday dinner, and it was truly a wonderful experience. After going there, I can definitely understand how popular it is regardless of what time of the day. The interior is wonderful - dark wood floors and furniture highlighted with creamy linens. It can feel a bit crowded when its full, but not uncomfortably so. The kitchen is also partially open to the dining area, with a bar right there (ideal eating location in my opinion), and the bar itself is on the side, partitioned off from diners. The food is delicious; it was very hard to choose only a few, especially since they offer so many traditional spanish tapas. The full entrees seem unnecessary compared to the tapas since we weren't even interested in them. We had: Escalivada: Roasted Peppers & Eggplant, Cippolini Onions & Confit Tomatoes (really good, but would skip next time) Morels Salteados: Morel Mushrooms, Thyme & White Asparagus (exquisite - its small, but very memorable) Grilled Baby Squid (simple but cooked to perfection, they were amazingly tender) Arroz de Langosta: Lobster Bomba Rice with Clams, Lemon Zest & Golden Pea Shoots (MmmMmm gooooood) Pimientos de Padron: Fried Peppers, Sea Salt & Salbitxada (delicately spicy - a must) Piquillos Rellenos: Crab-Stuffed Peppers (If you get one dish, this is the one. Amazingly good) Olas de Chocolate: Godiva Liqueur Cake, Chocolate Mousse, Milk Chocolate Ice Cream (definitely for the chocolate lover, and surprisingly large compared to the tapas) Banana Torrijas: Crispy Spanish Bread, Carmelized Bananas, Maple Syrup Ice Cream, Banana Anglaise (TO. DIE. FOR. If you like bananas, that is) We also each had a glass of sangria; I had the tinto, which was incredible and lived up to the ones I've had in Spain, while my boyfriend had their seasonal bianco with mint and mango, which he loved but was too sweet for my taste (weird, because I'm the one with the sweet tooth). The portions are smaller than some might expect, especially with some dishes, but for the two of us those 6 plates, two desserts, and sangria was perfect - however, it does leave a substantial bill at the end of the evening. However, we both agreed (especially me since I didn't pay ;D ) that it was completely worth it. And the service was spectacular, we had a very attentive, informed waiter. This is truly one of Philly's top restaurants.
label: POS

text: The Regency Cafe is a welcome addition to Lansdowne's business district. For many years we've been lacking a unique, casual bistro where you can simply enjoy a coffee and read a paper (or iPad, or whatever the kids do these days). Regency is all that and more. It's become the best lunch spot in the entire town. Not content with the diner options provided by other Landsowne mainstays, Regency offers up a great selections of salads, soup, and gourmet sandwiches. I particularly enjoy the Lansdowne Farmer's Market Salad, and the grilled vegetable sandwich has always been good. The coffee is good, and they have a large selection of flavored drinks (I like the honey steamer myself). They also keep a selection of newspapers for those who haven't forgotten the pleasures of daily print news. The Regency is located right next to Cinema 16:9 and the work-in-progress that is the Lansdowne Theater. These three establishments will make Lansdowne Ave an exciting place to watch over the coming years,

text: I was shocked to see what a dump the city of Reno is. We were on a trip to Tahoe and decided to drive to Reno for a day. The casinos are old, smelly, and run down. This place has definitely been hit hard by the economy, and it's not holding up well at all. My husband almost got mugged in the bathroom of a casino, we saw a man let his pants and underwear practically fall to the ground while crossing the street, and I've never seen more desperate looking homeless people in my life. And there are plenty of homeless people in the downtown area of my city. Something about being homeless in Reno seems a lot worse than being homeless somewhere else. As for what Rory X. said about my review...I've traveled quite a bit, and have never seen a city more decrepit than Reno. text: We went on one of their summer Monday theme nights ... fried chicken ... need I say more? The evening started with a gathering outside among Greg's "urban garden," where we were offered several wines to taste, along with bruschettas with goat cheese and blueberries. I don't typically eat much cheese, but I figured this was the place to try it, and it was delicious The sweetness of the blueberries with the salty/creamy of the cheese was sooo good (and I don't like cheese, I had to keep reminding myself). Then we moved indoors for dinner, which was served picnic style, with the food on platters in the front of the restaurant, and diners sitting together among four long rows of tables. It made for a very fun and relaxed atmosphere, and husband and I very much enjoyed talking to another couple during the meal. The fried chicken was the obvious star here, marinated in buttermilk, breaded and seasoned, then fried in cast iron pans ... can it get any better than that? It was perfectly moist, with a thick crispy skin ... I could've had a whole plate just of that skin and been happy. The sides included a cheesy potato salad that was also good, just a little too cheesy for me, and a cucumber tomato salad, and all kinds of other things that I now forget. Dessert was strawberry shortcake with homemade whipped cream ... and great combo of rich and light, the sweet berries against the sharp buttermilk shortcake. Greg Hardesty clearly loves food, and loves the people who loves his food. I look forward to more inspiring and inspired dinners in the future.

text: Reno was pretty much an Indian Food wasteland until Indian Garden opened. The last good Indian restaurant had closed a few years prior. So I was a happy customer here until India Kabab and Curry opened and I started going there, mainly getting my Indian food fix with a lunch buffet. The owner of Indian Garden also owns the Spice Rack on Kietzke at Vassar and I ran into him there. He remembered me and mentioned he hadn't seen me in his restaurant in a long time. So I decided to give Indian Garden a try again. The food was excellent. I got the option that lets me add an entree with soup and appetizers. The kabob and tandori chicken served as an appetizer were excllent. Nicely cooked and spiced. The rogan josh for the entree was also excellent, although I seemed to have gotten a little less lamb than when I used to eat this dish before. I love naan and that's always a treat. I had two disappointments. The Mulligatawny soup was not very spicy. That was always a highlight when I ate here before. One my first times here it was awesome and there was a hot British gal and Ameircan guy sitting at the next table. She started commenting on how good the Mulligatawny soup was and when he didn't adequately affirm it she turned to other diners, including me, and asked our opinions. I guess I have to ask for the spicy version next time. Also the mango ice cream was more like lce milk with lots of emphasis on the ice. It was frozen rock solid and seemed to have freezer burn. All in all it was an excellent meal and I've been remiss in not trying Indian Garden more often.

text: So, I took my mom here so she could use a Groupon that I purchased a couple of months ago. The Groupon was for a 50 min. facial or massage. My mom opted for the facial, which was also supposed to include an eye treatment. Anyway, last week, I called and made an appointment for a 50 min. facial and the staff person on the phone told me to arrive 10 min. early so she can change. I've been to spas before and 10 min. seemed a bit short but I took her word for it and we got to the spa at the right time. My mom changed and we were taken back to the waiting area where she was told to wait for her esthetician and in the meantime, to fill out a form specifying any special needs (i.e. skin conditions, sore muscles, etc.). By the time the esthetician came to get her, it was already 20 min. into her appointment time. (At least 15 min. of us being ready and waiting for the esthetician to show up). About 25 min. later, my mom comes out and says she is finished. 25 minutes! Half of the time that was paid for. Now, I understand if a client is late for spa treatments, the person's time gets cut down accordingly in order to accommodate later appointments. In this case, we were not late but the esthetician was. I told the receptionist, hoping that she would either correct the situation or allow me to speak to management. I already paid for it through Groupon so I honestly wasn't sure what the protocol was for subpar service. She told me that she has no way of knowing what time my mother actually went back for her facial and that if we had a problem, we should talk to the woman who provided the treatment. So, we spoke to her and she immediately became defensive. First, she said that most ppl don't need a 50 min. facial because their skin just doesn't need that much work---so 25 min. was all that my mother needed. (Then why advertise a 50 min. session?) She condescendingly asked if either of us had even ever gotten facials before and said that she provided a really good service for the Groupon price and that we were actually getting a bargain anyway! Then she changed her story and said that she came out late to get us because usually, clients are late (doesn't mean we were though). Then, she started talking about how she was so tired and had clients back to back. She even went so far as to say that we got wrong information from the woman who booked the appointment---but that is still the fault of the business and not the customer. I think she expected us to fold and just leave. In the end, all I really wanted was some of the money I paid for the Groupon, to be refunded---I just wanted to pay for what we got and nothing extra...I really wasn't looking for anything else. But she did go ahead and give us a gift certificate for a massage at a later date. Overall, I found the experience a bit stressful. If she had offered a discount or something in the beginning, instead of becoming defensive, it would have been much better and easier for all of us. In her defense, I do have to say that these types of issues are something that salon management should take care of, not the beauticians. The beauty treatment staff should only need to concentrate on providing the service. Management needs to have some mechanism to deal with issues like this or better train their beauticians to do it.

text: Husband, Toddler, and I stopped in here yesterday for a treat, and unfortunately we fall into the ranks of Yelpers that find this place vastly overrated. The atmosphere is pretty fancy for a bakery, which I guess is supposed to help justify the prices you are about to pay for cupcakes. Toddler was VERY excited to pick out her cupcake, a process made even more lengthy by the fact that they kept pulling trays out of the display to fill a large order in back. Not a huge deal, but something that made me feel like they don't much care about the customers in-store...I think they probably make most of their money on outside orders, which would explain a lot of the problems previous reviewers have had with the customer service. But this would all have been forgiven if the cupcakes had been good. I had the Dark Night, Husband had the Red Velvet, and Toddler had the "Bugs in Mud." Three very different cupcakes, and yet somehow they all managed to taste the same. The Dark Night had little chocolate flavor, and certainly not the deep, rich flavor of dark chocolate. Regarding the resort, I should note that we are not gamblers, so this review is based solely on the "hotel" part. First off, the room looked like it was last renovated in 1981, despite the signs claiming "Renovated Rooms Fall 2010!" I half expected to find Burt Reynolds from the Smokey & the Bandit era hiding in the closet...but that didn't happen, because there was no closet. There also wasn't a full-length mirror or a refrigerator, and the clock wasn't even set to Daylight Savings Time. The carpet was dirty and frayed, the wood furniture was scraped to pieces, and I don't think the bedspread had been washed since the Carter administration. The bathroom was gigantic -- probably half the size of the room itself -- but I don't know why, since all it housed was a small tub/shower, one sink, and a toilet. The rest was just empty space (not even any extra counter room). When I showered, I had to ignore all of the hair that didn't match mine or my companion's, and when I was finished, I had to use a hand towel as a bath mat since there wasn't one. The bath towel I used smelled as fresh as a chain smoker hanging out at a truck stop, even though we requested a non-smoking room. The room itself was positioned in a prime spot: right next to the beautiful parking deck. This was especially awesome when, at various points throughout the evening, car alarms would go off, setting off a chain reaction. Every couple of hours there would be four or five car alarms screeching right next to our room. It didn't really matter much, though, because there wasn't much sleeping going on: the bed and "pillows" (I use that term loosely) felt -- and smelled -- like laundry bags stuffed with old socks. Before the concert, we stopped at Aura Lounge to have a drink, because we got a "2 for 1" discount card at check-in. We ordered two glasses of olive juice (we said we wanted "vodka martinis," but apparently that phrase means "olive juice" at SL; suffice to say that I hadn't eaten much all day, drank the whole thing in about 10 minutes, and didn't feel a thing). They were listed in the menu at $9. When we tried to use our coupon -- which had a photograph of 3 martinis on the front -- the server said we couldn't use it for martinis. Huh? Then the bill came in at $24. That's some expensive olive juice for Reno, Nevada! The server was sweet, though, and it wasn't her fault, so we just paid up and left, feeling nickel-and-dimed within an inch of our lives. We self-parked in the adjacent deck, which thankfully was no hassle. We paid for it in the "resort fee," but it was only $7, which is cheaper than most overnight hotel parking. The best part of our experience at SL, aside from the concert itself, was driving out of that parking deck. We definitely WON'T be back.

text: The best bowl of pho, fo sho. Between Reno and SF, it even edges the SF Tenderloin pho joints, which many consider the best on the West Coast. The only downside I can possibly see to going here (aside from the bullshit nitpicky "our table wasn't wiped down properly" reviews also seen here) would be the menu is somewhat limited besides the pho bowls. You have a few appetizers, and maybe 10-15 noodle dishes, including vegetarian options, but the pho is definitely the strong point. I stick to the #1: beef balls (they're just meatballs, not bull testicles btw. duh!!), well done brisket, tendon, tripe, and shitloads of noodles in that cure-all broth, with the side dish of mint leaves, fresh jalapenos, and bean sprouts. Head-sized bowl going for a competitive $5.95. Don't order anything else unless you're sharing or taking some home. All the meat is incredibly fresh and flavorful, and with the jalapenos and a couple scoops of the red chili sauce the broth is a great sinus cleanser. If you do decide to get crazy, treat yourself to a couple of spring rolls stuffed with shrimp, lettuce, bean sprouts and sliced pork. And, of course, the peanut sauce to dip 'em in. These muthas are the diameter of Andre the Giant's finger, you could actually make a meal of two spring rolls. That's just the appetizer. For big appetites and pho purists, I've probably hit 15-20 pho places between Reno and SF and again, 777 comes out on top every time. I kinda liked the old cramped location a little more, when inebriated it resulted in some interesting social interactions around the counter area. Damn you bitch who burned down the Mizpah Hotel!!! If I ever get off that #1 order, I'd probably go for the seafood pho. If the freshness and quantity of meat in the #1 is any indication of how they'd load up that seafood, it's worth a shot. I'll post if I try it, but with the #1 I'm stuck in the "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" mentality. Takeout is interesting btw: they give you the raw meat separate from the broth. Once that broth gets boiling it only takes about 5-10 minutes to cook the meat, that brisket is sliced so thin and perfect you could "flash boil" it for like 2 minutes and have it medium-rare, mmmm....
