text: Been here four times, enough to be able to write a review. And I'm actually a big fan of Bridge, but I nearly withheld one star because I think the prices are too high. Don't get me wrong - Bridge has it all. Atmosphere, good food, and a phenomenal beer and wine selection. I have tried (on the recommendation of the servers or bartenders) five new beers and two new wines here and loved them all. I just wish it was a little easier on the pocketbook. One of the beers I like costs $11/bottle! I can get it in the store for six, but I guess you're paying (almost double) for the excellent ambiance, the company, and the ability to sample. Ambiance they have: The decor is unique but not intimidating. The bar downstairs is always crowded but not in a noisy frat-bar way; and upstairs are well-spaced tables and a wonderful comfy-chair area that overlooks the street through a big picture window. (It feels like someone's awesome loft living room.) Food: I've had chicken nachos (a special item, not always on the menu), an assortment of dips, and soft pretzels; friends have had the smoky strip club. Everything is great and obviously put together with great care and understanding of balance (textures, flavors) and presentation. People rave about the poblano queso but I thought it was just ok. The tapanade was great, though - really, really great. So was the flatbread it was served with. Elegant touch: Individual carafes of chilled water for each table, without ice cubes in them. THANK YOU! I need cool water to drink with my beer, and I hate places that tip the pitchers on their side so your glass gets filled with ice and about two sips of water. And thank you for letting me serve myself, so I don't have to wait, thirsty. (Not that waiting for service really happens here; even at its most crowded, the servers have been attentive but not hovering.) Beer & Wine: Don't be afraid to tell the bartender what you like and ask for suggestions. I'm a picky drinker and they've been right on the money every time for me. That's the great thing about a place like this, where everyone obviously knows their stuff: You can order your old faithful favorite, or you can expand your horizons. All in all, a great place to hang out with friends who take food & drink seriously. Just be prepared for a bigger-than-usual hit on your wallet. Bridge is a special occasion drinking place, for me.

text: I had a horrific experience at Firewaters and will NEVER go back. After my Saturday night wedding reception, several of us wanted to continue celebrating for a few more hours and we decided to come to Firewaters. I'm 30+ years old, as is my husband, and I was still in my wedding dress when we arrived, but the bouncer turned us away since my ID was somewhere back at the hotel (I didn't carry my driver's license on my wedding day). I was CLEARLY not under 21, but the bouncer was on some petty power trip. Whatever. After going back to the hotel for my ID we returned to Firewaters, which may have been our biggest mistake. The bouncer was as much of a jerk when we came back with the ID as he was when he turned me away. Once inside, the place was loud, crowded and the floors were sticky. They did have a decent beer selection, and after getting a pint of my favorite brew, I began to enjoy myself a little. We were able to grab a small table in the back while we celebrated some more. We didn't have table service and instead had to go to the bar for our drinks, which was fine. But at one point, one of the staff came by and cleared away dishes and my husband's $20 half-empty bottle of Chimay! We turned our backs for a minute, and the beer was gone. Irritated, we decided to leave. As we walked toward the hallway-like exit, one of my friends was assaulted by one of the patrons sitting at the bar. He just reached out and grabbed her crotch. The bouncer did nothing about this, despite standing very nearby and hearing the commotion, so my friend's husband took matters into his own hands. The night ended so badly that I will never go back to this place again. So, although the beer selection is good, the staff don't always let you finish what you've purchased. Babysit your beer, or it may be cleared away before you're finished with it. And the security at the establishment are a joke... more concerned with carding people who are obviously not underage than they are with preventing the sexual assault of their guests by drunken patrons. As if that wasn't enough, they have these obnoxious billboards that encourage you to "Drink your date pretty"... turns my stomach every time I see them.

text: Freshberry is a copycat company jumping on the yogurt bandwagon craze largely started by Red Mango and Pinkberry. "healthy" nonfat yogurt with fresh fruit toppings, a trend that came from South Korea (koreans prefer less sweet desserts, so the yogurt was traditionally more tangy than sweet and creamy). Freshberry's yogurt tastes just like plain old fashioned soft serve yogurt, not the newer "healthy" active culture yogurt that's so trendy right now. They do offer more variety of flavors and toppings (they also offer the candy toppings). They don't offer my favorite topping, mochi balls (but I think they will as soon as they find a supplier, as they've indicated they keep getting asked for it). I thought the yogurt was too sweet and too soft, not cold enough. It came out of the machine sort of half melted and didn't hold a stiff peak like I prefer. Positive notes. It's bright and clean inside and the staff are extremely friendly and helpful. also, a note on the "healthy" claims. A 4oz serving is over 100 calories. I believe the smallest serving is over 4oz, largest one well over 3x this. add on 10-100+ calories per topping. (candy toppings generally add on the most, and fruit varies greatly) and you're looking at 400 calories easily even with the smallest serving on the menu. So be careful and enjoy as a treat, not as a healthy snack. They also aren't rated for the live probiotic cultures that are promoted in the product.

Nonetheless, the food is what keeps us coming back. text: Friends wanted to get together for dinner last night - spur of the moment and casual. They had been to Bowman's and wanted to show us. We crossed over the free bridge into New Hope and travelled down the road passing all the usual New Hope restaurants. A few miles down on the left was Bowman's. What a surprise - Valet parking!!! I was caught off guard thinking "valet parking at a supposed casual place"? Sure thing. We were a party of 5 (4 adults and one 11 year old). We were quickly seated. The inside is like a pub...bar area and then two other dining room spaces. A decent size restaurant. We went on a Friday night and at 7 pm we didn't have to wait for a seat. However, by the time we left - the place was packed (maybe at 9:30 pm or so?). They have live entertainment. They had a guy on piano with a good audience sitting around him requesting songs. The crowd was an upscale crowd - I would think 40 years of age and older. The food was inexpensive and they had a good menu of American fare. Our table shared Bruschetta, Fried Mozzerella and Fried Zucchini. For dinner I had crabcakes which were good. My husband had the meatloaf and our friends had fish & chips, etc. This place is just so comfortable inside. Service was quick and attentive. I really loved this place - its always refreshing to stumble upon a new place and really like it. We will definitely go back! If you are spending the day in New Hope - if you want a place for dinner that is just down the road from the craziness of New Hope at dinner time - drive down to Bowman's. Plus, in the summer - there is a barge that sets off fireworks on the Delaware River at 9:30 each Friday weather permitting. As we were driving back home to NJ - the fireworks just started and it was a great ending for the evening. FYI - the free bridge and Lambertville Stations restaurant lot was PACKED with people. We just drove by and watched! Enjoy!

text: OMGsh we had a blast here! On a recent business trip we decided to try Niche after Michelle did a little research on local restaurants. The plan was for us to split the salad and dessert and then Michelle would order an entree. And oh was the plan successful! The salad was yummy mixed greens with a light vinaigrette. Michelle had the scallops and she said they were delicious! I had the steak and it was also delicious! Well, we both finished a VERY good portion of our meal so that tells you how delicious it was! text: I visited on a Sunday evening with a friend on a gluten-free diet. I saw a lot of good reviews on here so I was pretty excited. And I wasn't disappointed at all. It's a cute, cozy place. It was strange to eat them in a restaurant when I've cooked them oh so many times at home, but they were delicious nonetheless. I am curious to know what kind of cheese they use. My friend and I both got the arepas. After reading the description of the Pernil- slow roasted pork marinated in orange juice and cooked with olives and grilled onions- I had to taste it. My friend got the La Selva, an eggplant, mushroom, spinach, etc deal. I absolutely loved mine. And even though my friend is mostly vegetarian, I told her it was necessary she try it and she loveeeeed it as well. They look small on the plate, but I was stuffed and stayed full for a long time. We finished the meal with the Venezualan version of flan, I believe casuella? It was great. Very rich and did not have the bitter sauce that normall accompanies flan. All in all, great time. The service was fine, nothing too great, but nothing lacking. I loved the family atmosphere and that the owner was there talking to tables. I'll definitely be back.

text: Mamma's was the perfect evening to celebrate both the end of my exams AND my birthday. Unfortunately, the combination of the free-flowing wine and limoncello and the fact that I had hardly eaten anything due to the stress of that day, I can only comment on the first half of the evening. We came in, late and flustered, and sat down to antipasti and bread and a full glass of red wine. Now there are few things that make me happier than wine and bread and olive oil, so you could have stopped the whole thing right there and I would have been totally happy. But wait, there's more! The soup was kind of a franco-italian version of mazoball or wonton soup - egg crepes in a chicken broth. Quite good, but I went easy on it in preparation for the next courses. The pasta trio was pretty good, the rose sauce in my opinion the best of the three. I ordered flounder, in a light egg batter with lump crabmeat for my entree, which was light and delightful, though the sides left something to be desired. Luckily, there was still dessert coming, and at this point I wasn't caring about anything at all. One decaf cappuccino, some chocolate cake and too many shots of limoncello, lemon cream and blackberrycello later I stumbled out the door, happy as a clam. Though this was not haute cuisine, it remains a tremendous dining experience, certainly worth the money. Mamma knows what she's doing.

text: I want to give this place one star purely based on service, but the food was actually pretty good, so two. When you walk into the place, it's like stepping out of a time machine. The atmosphere is reminiscent of an old school supper club, complete with the musty smell not unlike my grandparents' basement. It was actually very cool. Live smooth jazz playing, cozy booths. But since our group was from Chicago/St. Louis, we wanted to sit outside and enjoy the warm weather. The host accommodated us on the cute patio and we were set. Our server seemed to be relatively attentive, and we thought he was trying to be cute when he continually made comments about how crazy we were for sitting outside. He even resorted to giving us menus and saying, "I'm waiting inside, wave at my when you're ready." OK, it was warm, but like high 70's. Give me a break already. We started with some drinks. I had the Martinez, which is similar to a manhattan, and my friend had the pear martini. Both were very good, nice mixture of flavors and not too sweet. The second round was a champagne cocktail (way too sweet for my taste) and a wedding cake martini. The wedding cake martini was creamy and delicious. For my entree, I had the shrimp and grits. The sauce was perfectly spicy and flavorful. It was also a nice touch that the shrimp were served with the head on, but with the shell removed. I hate pulling legs off my food when it's covered with sauce. I was very happy. An all around great meal. And then the fun came to an abrupt halt (sound of the screeching of a needle on a record). The bill came and we wanted to put our charges on 3 cards. I know it's a pain, but our server actually threw a tantrum, complete with whining and complaints that they are so slammed inside. So, as we were looking at all the empty tables inside, we finally relented and narrowed it down to two cards. First of all, if that was slammed, whatever do they do during Mardi Gras? Second, even Applebee's will split your check. That kind of behavior is totally unacceptable for this caliber of restaurant. We were going to stay for another drink, but our server pretty much killed our good time. Boo on him, we won't be back....ever again.

text: Came here for a Sunday brunch, while on visit in Santa Barbara. I'm from SoCal, but have been living in NorCal so long that I sometimes go for really long stretches forgetting how much I love sunshine and real beaches. The Boat House is right on a beach that's framed by rocky cliffs, that's filled with puppies and their owners (it's dog-friendly!), and that seriously sparkles with daytime surf. This helped snap me out of a long NorCal spell, reminded me of just why I'll probably never truly, truly be able to call myself a Bay Area girl; and, along with the fact that it offers al fresco dining and wall-to-wall windows inside so you can fully appreciate all this while you eat, earned Boat House its first three stars from me, easy. It's like they say: location, location, location. But that's not all Boat House has got going for it. It gets another star and a half (yeah, I really want to give it a 4.5) for its friendly staff, quick service, and yummy breakfast food and cocktails. I got the Signature Breakfast with a mimosa; my friend got the Chilaquiles, corned beef hash, and a blood orange margarita. They weren't knock-your-socks off amazing, but boy were they yummy. The total damage for all that was about $60-- a pretty decent price for this kind of Sunday bliss. After all that, the hypnotic ladies' room tiles (seriously, if you go, make sure to check these out!) and our Dennis Franz sighting (he was having breakfast with his family) were just icing on the cake.

text: I had THE WORST service experience of my dining career at this restaurant. It's been about a year and a half since I had my lovely experience, so maybe the service is better, but I will never go back. Now, the story: We arrived and there was a wait, no big deal, so we decided to wait in the bar. The service in the bar was fine and the hostesses sat us as soon as they could, no complaints with these aspects of the service. However, I cannot say the same for our server once we sat down. She came and took our order and then everything went downhill. I had ordered an appetizer to share with one of my friends, we expected the service to be slow, but we never received our appetizer or saw our server. We asked the woman who brought our pizza, I'm assuming the food runner, and she had no clue, our server didn't come back after we had asked. We decided to ask one of the hostesses where our server was as we had no idea what she looked like. After all, we had only seen her once. Finally, our server came back to our table. She was clueless as to the fact that we didn't get our appetizer then proceed to launch into a speech where she called the chefs/cooks in the kitchen "RETARDED" and explained that we should really come back on a Tuesday or Wednesday because that's when they are okay. (Really? You can only eat at this restaurant 2 out of the 7 days in a week?) This was quickly followed by "and don't ask the host staff anything because they're retarded too". All 5 of us at the table were completely shocked by her speech, I would think the owner would be mortified to know that these were the explanations given by one of his staff members. Then after the appetizer STILL didn't come, we again had to flag her down to tell her that we simply didn't want it anymore (assuming she had put the order through in the first place). She came over to our table with an empty, dirty glass from another table. When she left the table, she left the dirty glass sitting right next to me. At this point, I really thought that maybe I was on some sort of TV show where they test your patience. The manager came over and gave us free dessert, blah blah blah. As we were getting ready to leave, we all decided that we were still pretty disturbed by the whole "retarded" speech so one of the members of my group decided to let the manager know why we were not leaving a tip. He took the check over to her while the rest of us waited by the door. As we were waiting, our server walked by a few times and then finally came up to one of us and asked if she had given us our bill. SERIOUSLY? This is the most clueless server I have ever met, with absolutely ZERO people skills who should never be waiting table because she can't seem to figure out which way is up or down. Because of this ridiculous experience, I am giving BJ's 1 star, if I could give it 0, I would. The food really wasn't very impressive and the service was beyond horrible. I guess it's not fair to judge an establishment based on one employee, but I really can't bring myself to go back.

text: Before the flagging begins, Id like to slap it right out on the table. 1.) Ive never actually bought anything at Hipster Home. - not that I wouldn't. Its awesome stuff. I just am very cheap and not at all stylish and aesthetic. My own style screams frat boy goes to Kmart. 2.) I'm personal friends with the owners, Dave and Lindsay. Therefore, take this glowing review with a grain of salt, but keep in mind that Ive been friends with them, and have visited Hipster Home for over a year and I'm just now reviewing it. They don't need my great review because their business speaks for itself. They have specifically stated that they don't want great reviews from friends that aren't valid. This one, however, comes from the heart. Lets begin with Pheonixville. Ive lived in the greater Philly area for all of my life, long enough to see the next "IT' neighborhood, rise out of the ashes. In the 90s, it was Manayunk. I would say now, as the first decade of the new millennium comes to an end, its Pheonixville. Its such a cool place, all the glitz of being the Main Line, without the pretentiousness. It seems to be a tight knit community, where the inhabitants really want to see each other succeed and they work in unison. There's a real feeling of community here. Located a few doors down from the historic , Blob filled Colonial theater is Hipster Home. Its a very inviting place in an inviting town. The laid back atmosphere really pulls you in, and the eclectic household items, along with the proprietors , keeps you there. Dave and Lindsay know how to treat their customers. Actually, there is no customer vibe here, only friends. Dave treats everyone like a friend whether he has known them for 15 years or 15 minutes. Its really good business. There is no sales pressure, they are just genuinely happy to have you in there store. Its almost surreal, to go on a Friday night, where the wine and music are flowing. Its a trip to see people walk into the store as patrons and morph quickly into party guests. Having just bought a home, I'm looking forward to finally breaking my Hipster Home cherry, and buying something cool for it. If I had the money, Id go to town in here. Not to say that the wares at HH are expensive, I'm just at a point where even a cutely named bookcase at Ikea causes budgeting woes. So please do yourself a favor and check this gem out. And don't forget to tell them The Dribbler sent you! This may not get you a 10% discount (although mentioning Yelp might...) but at least they will have time to put some plastic covers over the couch.
label: POS

text: Does this restaurant even need any more reviews? Everyone says it's awesome. It *is* awesome. Most of the menu rotates. But there's beef rendang every day. Beef rendang is beef that is cooked very, very slowly in coconut milk and in its own rendered fat until the meat melts in your mouth and the remaining liquid is a thick, rich sauce. My other favorites are the lamb stew, which falls off the bone, and the rich, savory tempeh. If you like satay, get five skewers of beef or chicken satay, plus rice, for five bucks. There are a lot of interesting-looking fried items on sale, but the only one I ever tried I didn't care for. I thought it was greasy and had been sitting around too long. That's the one and only thing I've ever eaten at Hardena that I didn't like. Everything else has been a winner. Despite the scary descriptions, it is a fine place to take kids. The kids won't mind the décor. And nobody will care if they spill rice on the plastic-covered tables. Addendum 2010-05-24: Hardena no longer looks like an abandoned mini-mart. The outside has pretty new paint. They have a sign that does not involve movable black plastic letters and does not advertise 7-Up. The interior has been rearranged to open up more space, and decorated. There are new tiles in the bathroom. And they still have the best food ever! Addendum 2011-08-13: A rice plate with three dishes is up to $7 now. It's still one of the best deals around and the food is still superb. Addendum 2016-09-22: Hardena has not gotten any worse. It is still one of my favorite restaurants in Philadelphia, worth a special trip to visit.

text: Anyplace that serves up a martini called "Wedding Cake" has my vote! Anyway, The Porterhouse does not have this problem! I've never had a bad meal here, and have tried just about everything, except the seafood. My PIC (Partner in Crime), however, has eaten the seafood and loves it! A few favorites: The Ham & Havarti, the black bean soup, the smoked chicken spring rolls. OMG - The Kentucky Derby Pie (pecans and chocolate) is TO DIE FOR. Seriously awesome. And if you like bread pudding - there's is fab - homemade! Also to note - the pasta dishes are always wonderful too. You know how often you order pasta and the noodles are limp and pasty? Not so here, it's always wonderful! One thing that didn't please us - the Creme Brulee - it tastes like vanilla pudding with a sugary coating. But - that's the only criticism! Love the bar area - there is a wall of windows which brightens the place up. (I love a lot of light). Upstairs, the whole back wall is all window, which overlooks fields and is scenic in all seasons! Love it! ***note, they are closed on Mondays!

The cheese was entirely too stringy, and although it said it was made with Gruyere, I would like to challenge them on that. I couldn't even get myself to swallow 3 spoonfuls. text: I would LOVE to give Seven Stars a 5, and it nearly earned it too! If you are interested in sushi, they have an in house chef that prepares a varied menu of both cooked and raw. They even offer a sushi boat for 2 people (50$). The Chesapeake roll (12$), which I have ordered twice now, well let's just say I swear on it's deliciousness. Overall, in both take out and dining in the sushi gets a full 5 stars. text: The food quality is okay, but I do not like the lack of transparency in how they charge for food nor their prices--gave the impression of dishonesty. When we went there in Jun 2010, the lady working there showed us the food on the small buffet, but I noticed they did not display what the buffet price was. When I asked her, she said it was charged by the pound and she would weigh our plates after we choose our food. When I asked what the price was per pound, she mumbled something about $7 or $8 per pound (I asked my wife later and she also did not hear a clear price). We sat down and ate and the food was decent. However, we were annoyed that this is a buffet, and they charged $10-11 for a one-time plate, so it is overpriced when compared to all other Indian buffets we've been to in other cities that are 'all you can eat' with prices between $7-9 for lunch (and some of those buffets were magnificent in comparison to this one). Also, the naan bread (normally part of other buffets and plentifully supplied) was an extra $1-2 and was brought out on a small saucer with 4 small pieces. I also wondered if they scammed their customers by not advertising clearly a price for the buffet anywhere, not telling you a clear price per pound when asked (not sure if they vary it on the spot depending on what they think you can pay), using a scale where the weight read-out only faces the cashier (and not the customer--like in grocery stores and delis) and wondering if they are charging us for the weight of their plate and not just the food you're there to eat (since their plates have a little heft to them and also go on the scale for weighing). This small business was a case study in how not to treat your customers in terms of pricing and services provided. They arranged everything in the transaction to their advantage and have neglected showing their product's value to the customer.

So I had a few bites here and there, and was pleasantly surprised. They WERE amazing. After everyone finished their entrees, our server offered us a dessert menu, making sure to mention that strawberry shortcake is also available for the evening. I'm a sucker for a good strawberry shortcake and thought I could tolerate a few bites. However, when it showed up, I couldn't resist and uncomfortably pigged out. Oh, it was worth it. If you don't go for anything else go for the strawberry shortcake. Who knows how long it will be on the menu! Even though I guess it wasn't... Here's what it came down to: with one entree, a beer, and a dessert, the bill came to like $50 with tip. Most of the time, I get furious paying that much for food I know I can make myself at home. What I liked about Cochon is we walked out of there feeling like our money went somewhere good. I could NOT have made the stuff at home (except maybe the strawberry shortcake, but it was only like $7 anyway). It was not a waste of money. That means a lot these days. I plan to go again, and I plan to bring my appetite with me! If you have guests in town who want to experience some good local dishes, this is the place to go. text: Beer and wine sales tax ripoff: The Red Robin chain has decent, but overpriced, burgers. Their "unlimited" steak fries come-on is a ruse. I ordered a 20 oz mug of beer, which my check priced at 5.99. I've asked several bartenders at other places about this way of charging tax for alcohol, and all say they've never heard of it being done that way. text: Good, bad, both... I went here for the first time about 2 years ago while in town and ended up eating here 3 times (2 lunches and a dinner). I thought it was really really tasty. They had a great bread pudding, great sandwiches, great burgers, etc. The service was also really quick and servers were nice. I just went back to Nashville for a car show and convinced my parents to go for dinner one night. Apparently they changed chefs or the chef changed menu items or something, didn't really know exactly what the server said. We started out with the spinach artichoke dip which wasn't horrible, but it was really runny. For our dinner, we ordered pork chop, brie salad, and chicken sandwich. I had the sandwich and I ordered a side of the spicy chipotle mayo with it. They did not lie about the spicy part of it!!! It was good, but my mouth was on fire while I was eating it. The sandwich tasted like a chicken sandwich that you would order from any restaurant, nothing special about it, but no complaints either. The pork chop was full of fat, and nowhere near the cost. The salad had really runny dressing and when asked for a side of dressing (twice), it never came. Every time we had an issue that the server knew about, he disappeared and didn't reappear until the problem was fixed which was fine except that he would disappear for 10 minutes at a time while everyone's drinks would be empty (and with that spicy chipotle mayo, you need a full glass at all times). At this point, my parents had no clue why I told them we had to go there, but we stayed for dessert because my mom loves bread pudding when it has chocolate chips instead of raisins, which they have. We also ordered carrot cake and chocolate cake. The description of the chocolate cake said something about it being chocolate cake with chocolate icing. When I got my "chocolate cake", it was not cake, it was mousse. I never would have ordered it had I known that. I took a bite thinking maybe it had cake somewhere, but it didn't, it was just mousse. The carrot cake was small and round and 90 percent frosting. There was approximately 2 spoon fulls of actual carrot cake hidden under tons of frosting. When the server came back and saw that I only took one bite of the chocolate "cake", he said yeah, our chef changed it today (thanks for the warning), but I will take it back since you didn't like it. This was very nice considering that I didn't even ask him to do that, but he never offered me another dessert, just took it back. It is fine, I didn't need the calories anyways. Our bill was around 100 bucks for 1 appetizer, 3 meals, and 2 desserts. Overall this 2nd experience was nowhere near as good as the first, but the bread pudding is still delicious so I would maybe go back for just that. They are getting ready to do a major remodel so hopefully after that they will work on getting their food back to being good!
label: NEG

text: Talking about disappointment...I love good BBQ, and really look around the city to find something authentic, not drowned in sauce covering the real taste and flavor of the meat. I first asked my server what style of BBQ they serve, and whether it was beef or pork ribs. After a deer-in-the-headlight look, she said she didn't know, but I can ask the bartender. So I did. Funny, I got the same response "Umm, I'm not sure, let me get somebody who knows." After another 5 minutes a woman comes out to tell me they are pork ribs. I asked if they were St Louis or Memphis style, and if they were rubbed. I can still hear the crickets! So seeing as these employees have no clue as to what food they serve, I figured I'd stay with what they advertise as good texas beef brisket. The brisket was ok - not great - but very dry and didn't have that traditional smokey flavor one gets from eating real 'cue. Having lived in the South for 11 years, 3 years in Mississippi, and 2 in North Carolina, I am very familiar with the territorial battles of good BBQ. If you make decent BBQ, it should be succulent, moist and very flavorful, without sauce. Unfortunately, I had to hit mine with sauce to flavor it up - and the sauce was average at best. Ratings for Food: Beef Brisket - 1.0 stars because it was a decent portion, but would have been lower if the sauce wasn't there. There is NO PERSON IN THEIR RIGHT BBQ MIND WHO WOULD EVER "BRINE" THEIR BEEF BRISKET !!! Thats sacriligious, and just proves that "chefs" should stay in French cuisine instead of monkeying with the oldest recipe known to mankind for curing, preparing, and smoking meats properly. Didn't try the ribs or the pork belly sammich - so I can't comment. Maybe if I hear decent reviews I'll try, but I doubt it. Side Dishes: Very average - not to hard to make Kraft mac-n-cheese. Service: 1 star - Really bad. How can you work in a BBQ joint and not know what you serve?!?! How does it take 3 different people to ask one stupid question - beef or pork ribs....aint that difficult people. Pay attention to your trade, or know your own menu. That tells me they weren't trained or have poor management - especially when the manager decided not to come over and say anything as he watched me ask three different people the same question and nobody could answer - my guess he didn't have a clue either. It was 6PM on a Thursday, and I was one of 5 people in the place - I would think sitting at the bar I would have better, more informed employees who know how to do more than fill a mason jar with beer. Can't say I would recommend this place or ever go back. Waiting to find a "real" authentic BBQ joint in Philly who knows the difference between pork and beef.
